verdict.rationale: The separation is a Scheme of Arrangement demerging the "Clinical Services" undertaking of NH Integrated Care Private Limited (NHIC, a wholly owned subsidiary) — 9 clinics in Bengaluru and 1 in Hosur — into the listed parent Narayana Hrudayalaya Limited (NHL) on a going-concern basis, while the Narayana Aarogyam care-plan vertical stays behind in NHIC and the IRDAI-regulated insurer Narayana Health Insurance Limited (NHIL) remains a separate reporting entity. Management's stated reason is cost and overhead duplication: Sandhya J said the clinics' residual losses were "mainly because of the corporate overheads that are being incurred to sustain the integrated care infrastructure," with the combined clinics-plus-insurance drag flat at roughly INR 66 crore in FY26 despite the first cohort of clinics breaking even in the modelled 18 months. Viren Shetty framed the demerger as letting the clinics share corporate resources with the parent rather than carry a standalone cost base — "a few of the corporate overheads can be worked in a way that we share resources with the parent and we'll be demerging the clinic business into the core" — and in Feb 2026 as being "better able to manage the synergies and costs between two entities," so the margin dilution "should minimize over the coming quarters." The second rationale is measurement and reporting: clinics are an acknowledged feeder for the hospitals (domestic inpatient referrals replacing lost Bangladesh/international volumes, and a funnel into One Health/insurance plans), and as doctors, manpower and expenses get shared across hospitals and clinics in the same cities, "it will be harder for us to say what is attributable to clinic alone and what is not," so from FY27 the clinic business is rolled into the hospital P&L as "its best reflection of the contribution to the performance of those hospitals." A corollary benefit management cited is cleaner disclosure of the insurance arm: once integrated care merges into NHL, NHIL's profitability is reported separately rather than netted against clinic burn in a single "integrated care" line. Mechanically it is cost-free to shareholders: because NHIC is a 100% subsidiary, no shares are issued, there is no change in share capital or shareholding pattern, no SEBI/BSE/NSE no-objection was required (Regulation 37(6), intimation only), employees transfer on terms no less favourable, and NHIC's sole secured creditor's (HSBC) charge over the demerged undertaking moves to NHL. The only cost called out was one-time transaction expense — "legal stamp duty and other costs" sitting in FY26 India overheads, said to normalise next year. No investor, lender or partner was identified as having demanded the separation; the pressure visible in the calls is analysts repeatedly asking why clinic/insurance losses were not falling and when breakeven would come.
verdict.evolution: Through the Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) and Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) calls there is no mention of any demerger — management discussed only the INR 450 crore earmarked for clinics and insurance (INR 100 crore capital into insurance, INR 150 crore into clinics by Q1) and cash burn trending down. The Board approved the Scheme on December 12, 2025 and filed it with NCLT Bengaluru on December 17, 2025, and it was first explained to investors on the Feb 17, 2026 call as "merging it into NHL" to manage synergies and costs, with Sandhya confirming integrated care would merge into NHL while insurance would be reported separately. By the May 26, 2026 call the language hardened to "demerging the clinic business into the core," with FY27 guidance that clinics would be reported inside the hospital business and merger-related stamp duty/legal costs flagged as one-timers. Procedurally it ran from the Feb 13, 2026 first-motion order to near-unanimous approvals on April 2, 2026 (equity 99.9999% in favour; secured and unsecured creditors 100%) and NCLT sanction delivered October 30, 2026 (order uploaded November 4, 2026) with an Appointed Date of April 1, 2025.

points.point: Viren Shetty ties the demerger directly to stripping out duplicated corporate overhead by sharing resources with the listed parent, in answer to why clinic/insurance losses stayed flat.
points.quote: What we are doing is a little bit of consolidation and a few of the corporate overheads can be worked in a way that we share resources with the parent and we'll be demerging the clinic business into the core that should help with a lot of that.

points.point: Sandhya J identifies the residual loss as corporate overhead for the integrated-care structure, not clinic-level losses, since the clinics set up two years earlier had already broken even.
points.quote: the losses that you' re seeing are mainly because of the corporate overheads that are being incurred to sustain the integrated care infrastructure.

points.point: The analyst framing that prompted the demerger answer: clinics-plus-insurance losses stuck at about INR 66 crore in FY26 despite expected maturity-driven decline.
points.quote: If you look at the clinics and insurance losses, it has remained flat around INR 66 crore s loss in FY 26.

points.point: Measurement rationale: shared doctors, manpower and expenses across hospitals and clinics in the same city make standalone clinic attribution impossible, so clinics are reported inside hospitals from FY27.
points.quote: But going forward, it will be harder for us to say what is attributable to clinic alone and what is not simply because a huge amount of the manpower and expenses and doctor talent will be shared between the two.

points.point: Explicit reporting change effective FY27, justified as the truest reflection of what clinics contribute to hospital performance.
points.quote: So, from this year onwards, FY27, the clinic business will be rolled in with the overall hospital business because that is its best reflection of the contribution to the performance of those hospitals.

points.point: Sandhya flags unquantified one-time merger costs (legal, stamp duty) inside FY26 India other expenses, which is why operating leverage did not show at 18% of revenue.
points.quote: In addition, there are some one -time costs in there because we are going through a certain merger process.

points.point: Strategic justification for keeping and expanding clinics: they are the sole driver of domestic referrals that replaced de-emphasised international revenue and the entry point for One Health insurance customers.
points.quote: Ever since we took a call on improving our domestic focus and deemphasizing on growing international revenues, the clinic business has been the sole driver of the increased referrals to our hospitals from the cities in which we operate.

points.point: First investor-facing explanation of the transaction, framed as managing synergies and costs across two entities and reducing margin dilution over coming quarters.
points.quote: We are balancing out the scope of expansion of our clinic program across the country and merging it into NHL.

points.point: Viren links the merger to minimising the dilutive impact of the clinic build-out on reported margins, while confirming continued investment in clinics across core geographies.
points.quote: So, we're better able to manage the synergies and costs between two entities. So, the diluted impact should minimize over the coming quarters.

points.point: Sandhya separates the two legs: integrated care (clinics) merges into NHL; the insurance company stays a separate reported business.
points.quote: Integrated care will merge into NHL. The insurance business we will continue to report out separately.

points.point: A disclosure benefit management expects: post-merger, insurance profitability gets reported on its own instead of being blended into the integrated-care loss line.
points.quote: Once the merger happens, we will report out the profitability of the insurance business separately.

points.point: The transaction perimeter: Clinical Services undertaking of NHIC — 9 Bengaluru clinics plus 1 Hosur clinic — transferred to NHL as a going concern, with Appointed Date April 1, 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the demerger of the Clinical Services (as defined in the Scheme) undertaking of the Demerged Company, comprising 9 clinics located in Bengaluru and 1 clinic in Hosur, into the Company on a going-concern basis.

points.point: What is left behind: the Narayana Aarogyam care-plan vertical continues inside NHIC, which retains its "Remaining Undertaking" and its own assets and liabilities.
points.quote: to demerge the clinical services as defined in the scheme of NHIC ('the Demerged Undertaking') into the Resulting Company, while continuing the Narayana Aarogyam Vertical within NHIC, on a going concern basis

points.point: No dilution or consideration because NHIC is a 100% subsidiary; share capital and shareholding pattern of the listed company are unchanged.
points.quote: As the Demerged Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, no shares shall be issued by the Company as consideration pursuant to the Scheme and, accordingly, there will be no change in the share capital or shareholding pattern of the Company.

points.point: Light regulatory path: as a wholly owned subsidiary demerger, only intimation to the exchanges was required rather than SEBI/NSE/BSE no-objection certificates.
points.quote: in terms of Regulation 37(6) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with the applicable SEBI Circulars, no No-Objection Certificate from the Securities and Exchange Board of India, National Stock Exchange of India Limited or BSE Limited is required for the Scheme, and only an intimation to the said Stock Exchanges is necessary

points.point: Employee protection: clinic staff move to NHL without break in service and with provident fund, gratuity and superannuation balances transferred.
points.quote: all employees of Petitioner Company No.1 engaged in the Demerged Undertaking shall become employees of Petitioner Company No. 2 with effect from the Effective Date, on terms and conditions no less favourable than those on which they were engaged by Petitioner Company No. 1, and without any interruption in service.

points.point: Lender treatment: HSBC, NHIC's sole secured creditor, voted for the Scheme and its charge over the demerged clinics shifts to NHL.
points.quote: It is further submitted that the charge in favor of the said Secured Creditor pertains to the Demerged Undertaking and hence shall be moved to Petitioner Company No. 2.

points.point: Stakeholder approval was effectively unanimous at the April 2, 2026 NCLT-convened meetings — equity holders 99.9999% in favour, with secured and unsecured creditors 100% in favour.
points.quote: the concerned stakeholders consented with 100% voting in favour, thereby approving the Scheme with the requisite majority.

points.point: No charter change was needed because NHL's existing objects already cover clinics and polyclinics, supporting the view that clinics belong in the parent.
points.quote: The clinical services undertaking, being the Demerged undertaking under Clause 1.6 of the Scheme, is squarely covered by the existing objects clause of petitioner Company No.2, and accordingly, no alteration to the said Objects Clause is required

verdict.what_management_expects: For NHL: lower duplicated corporate overheads, less margin dilution from clinic cash burn, shared doctors/manpower leverage, and clinics reported inside hospitals from FY27 as a referral feeder. For NHIC/NHIL: a cleaner structure where the Aarogyam vertical stays behind and insurance profitability is disclosed separately. No consideration, no dilution; one-time stamp-duty/legal costs normalise next year.
verdict.gaps: No quantified synergy or overhead saving, no clinic/insurance breakeven date, no tax treatment, no NHIC pre/post financials, no stated cost of the scheme.

verdict.rationale: Management framed the separation as the core of "Vedanta 2.0": breaking one monolithic diversified natural-resources company into five independent, sector-specific pure-play listed companies — Vedanta Limited (residual: Zinc India/HZL, Zinc International, Copper, Ferrochrome/FACOR, Nickel), Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd, Vedanta Power/Talwandi Sabo Power (merchant power), Vedanta Oil & Gas/Malco Energy (Cairn), and Vedanta Iron & Steel — so that each could "chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors" rather than being valued as a conglomerate (Apr 2026, Apr 2025: "pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility"). The stated problem was that a single balance sheet and single capital-allocation process blurred very different businesses: Zinc India at 56% EBITDA margin and $959/t COP, aluminium at 38% margin, versus a Copper trading business running ~1% margin, and a power business that wants to add 10–12 GW. The fix was a capital structure "architected with precision… aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company": of $5.5bn net debt (group leverage 0.95x), $3.5bn goes to Aluminium (1.3x), Power sits at 4.7x on long-dated PFC/REC paper, Vedanta Limited keeps ~$1bn (0.4x), while Oil & Gas is nil-debt and Iron & Steel carries no more than $0.2bn. Specific frictions the split removes: the Copper brand fee drops from 3% to 0.75% on ~$3.1–3.2bn of revenue (~$65m, +2.25% to EBITDA), taking Copper margin from ~1% toward at least 5% in FY27; the dividend policy moves from "prescriptive" to "descriptive", from rule-based (minimum 30% of profit) to principle-based, and the mandate to upstream Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months falls away; Ajay Goel also called it "an opportunity… from taxation viewpoint" via recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation. Third parties shaped the terms: lenders demanded debt allocation be "broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC"; the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT over ~$512–520m of disputed dues and was satisfied only by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full alleged claims, with any arbitration outcome ring-fenced to Oil & Gas; creditor SEPCO was settled in full for ₹660 crore "as part of demerger proceedings… paving the way for a proposed demerger process", and a ₹1,248 crore cash-backed bank guarantee was lodged with NCLAT over the TSPL power demerger. Management also pointed to equity-side demand — "many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table" of the de-merged entities as a fresh deleveraging avenue for VRL's remaining $4.7bn. Three months after listing, the Board extended the same logic to a second, vertical separation: ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft of surplus real estate (22 assets, only ₹1.26 crore of FY26 turnover, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share for every 20, because the portfolio was "historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub-optimal visibility… and value realization."
verdict.evolution: The demerger was already a live execution item by the Feb 2025 call (Jan 31, 2025), where Ajay Goel flagged the Feb 18 shareholder/creditor meetings as "the important stage of execution"; on the Apr 2025 call (Apr 30, 2025) Deshnee Naidoo recast it as creating "pure-play entities" under Vedanta 2.0 with completion guided for September 2025. It then slipped repeatedly on legal and stakeholder hurdles — Aug 2025 (Jul 31, 2025) disclosed the NCLT second-motion part-hearing of July 2 with the next date Aug 20, an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power order, and the MoPNG objection; Nov 2025 (Oct 31, 2025) resolved SEPCO for ₹660 crore and MoPNG via a Vedanta corporate guarantee, guiding to a final Nov 12 hearing and five listings by FY26-end. Jan 2026 (Jan 29, 2026) reported NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power on Jan 9, 2026) and shifted the detail toward mechanics — bank NOCs conditioned on debt allocation, recast balance sheets, tax structuring — targeting Apr 1 effectiveness; Apr 2026 (Apr 29, 2026) set the record date at May 1 with mid-June listing, 4 extra shares per share, and added two new rationales not previously spelled out: the Copper brand-fee cut to 0.75% and five independent dividend policies. By the Jul 30, 2026 filings the plan had extended beyond the original five, with a sixth vertical split of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1:20.

points.point: The demerger was already at the shareholder/creditor-vote stage, pitched purely as investor value unlock, with no operational rationale given on this call.
points.quote: On the demerger front, we are in the important stage of execution , the shareholders and the creditors meeting scheduled on Feb 18th. This transformative step is poised to unlock significant value for our investors.

points.point: First explicit statement of the design goal — pure-play entities for strategic focus and operational flexibility — inside the Vedanta 2.0 ambition of a $100bn critical minerals, energy and technology powerhouse; completion then guided for September 2025.
points.quote: We are making good progress with our demerger plan, aiming to create pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility.

points.point: A shareholder (Ashish Kejriwal, Nuvama) pressed that mining leases — Sijimali bauxite and the coal blocks held under Vedanta Limited — must first be transferred to Vedanta Aluminium before the split can complete; management confirmed a parallel approvals plan.
points.quote: Ashish, you are right. This is part of the overall approvals that we have in our sight.

points.point: Execution stalled in two forums at once: the NCLT second-motion petition was part-heard on July 2 with the next date Aug 20, and NCLAT granted an interim stay on the TSPL power demerger order, backed by a ₹1,248 crore fully cash-backed bank guarantee over the SEPCO creditor matter.
points.quote: Separately, the NCL AT has granted an interim stay on TSPL, our power demerger order by NCLT, with the next hearing scheduled on 4th August.

points.point: The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT, questioning whether the demerged, standalone Cairn oil & gas P&L could absorb disputed dues if arbitration went against Vedanta — i.e. a regulator worrying that separation strips a weaker entity of parent support.
points.quote: In the last NCLT hearing, they did express concern about the payments of any of the disputed dues that may become payable by Cairn in case the ongoing arbitration ruling, as we have all learned now, comes in their favor.

points.point: A long-standing SEPCO creditor dispute was settled in full for ₹660 crore (part of ₹1,547 crore of net exceptional items that quarter) explicitly to clear the path for the scheme.
points.quote: As part of demerger proceedings, a full and final settlement of Rs. 660 Cr has been done with SEPCO , thereby resolving a long -standing dispute, paving the way for a proposed demerger process.

points.point: MoPNG's objection — over roughly $512–520m of alleged claims — was resolved not by cash but by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full extent of the claims, so the demerged oil & gas entity would not carry the obligation.
points.quote: Their concern has been taken care of by us providing a corporate guarantee from Vedanta.

points.point: Five simultaneous listings by FY26-end were framed as the vehicle for sharper strategic focus, with Goel adding that it unlocks "focused value across our five verticals".
points.quote: This will set the stage for the listing of all five demerge d entities by the end of FY '26, enabling greater strategic focus and enhanced value creation for all stakeholders.

points.point: After NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power order Jan 9, 2026), the rationale was stated as three things at once — sharper strategy, stronger standalone balance sheets, faster growth — with Q3 results already reported under Ind AS 105 demerger accounting.
points.quote: This marks a defining moment in our journey, one that empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value.

points.point: Lenders drove the capital-structure design: debt allocation across the five entities had to be agreed with banks before they would issue no-objection certificates, with $6.7bn of Vedanta India consol net debt split by asset ratio and each entity's own cash-generation and debt-servicing capability.
points.quote: When we went to the banker seeking NOC, in that case, debt allocation was broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval.

points.point: Goel named taxation and deleveraging as further gains — recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation per entity — alongside the intent to make oil & gas and iron & steel debt-free, funded partly by the ₹3,000 crore HZL OFS.
points.quote: One thing I can confirm to the entire audience and to the stakeholders at large, that demerger in fact, becomes an opportunity across the areas.

points.point: Final articulation: five sector-specific pure-play companies whose purpose is independent growth paths and dedicated thematic investor bases; record date May 1, 2026, one Vedanta share yielding four additional shares, listing targeted by Q1 FY27 (mid-June).
points.quote: This will entail creation of five independent sector -specific pure -play companies, allowing each company to chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors.

points.point: Debt was matched to each business's earnings power and growth stage rather than split pro-rata: Oil & Gas nil debt, Iron & Steel under $0.2bn, Aluminium $3.5bn at 1.3x, Power 4.7x on 7–10 year PFC/REC paper, Vedanta Limited ~$1bn at 0.4x, against group leverage of 0.95x.
points.quote: The de -merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.

points.point: A concrete economic benefit of unbundling: the brand fee was re-benchmarked per entity, cutting Copper's rate from 3% to 0.75% on ~$3.1–3.2bn of revenue (~$65m), lifting Copper margin from roughly 1% to at least 5% in FY27, while the other entities stay at 3% (fixed to FY29).
points.quote: So the brand fee for copper from the current 3% will go down to 0.75% and that alone from India's viewpoint means higher EBITDA by 2.25%.

points.point: Each of the five boards gets its own dividend policy; Vedanta's shifts from rule-based (minimum 30% of profit) to principle-based, and the obligation to pass through Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months is removed.
points.quote: Currently, Vedanta's policy on dividend is more prescriptive; it will become more descriptive.

points.point: Separation creates a new deleveraging route for VRL's remaining $4.7bn: differentiated capital structures that anchor investors can enter at the entity level, on top of the ~$400m brand fee and 4–5% dividend.
points.quote: Now as we de -merge all the five companies, additionally we'll have the optionality of a differentiated capital structure and in that case, many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table , and that will be additional avenue for de -leveraging.

points.point: M&A governance was redrawn around the split: each CEO is mandated to grow organically on their own 2x/3x plans, with cross-sector or out-of-portfolio acquisitions sitting at a new holdco with its own M&A team and the Chairman.
points.quote: Holdco will be set up to make sure there is some visibility of capital allocation across all 5 businesses, but also with its own M&A team to start looking at some of these opportunities.

points.point: The May 16, 2026 cost-apportionment filing fixes the five resulting entities and their relative weights: Vedanta Limited 52.34%, Vedanta Aluminium Metal 7.15%, Talwandi Sabo Power 12.23%, Malco Energy (oil & gas) 21.49%, Vedanta Iron and Steel 6.79% — one share of each per Vedanta share, effective/appointed date May 1, 2026.
points.quote: In accordance with provisions of the Scheme, Resulting Companies issued and allotted 1 (One) fully paid -up equity share of each Resulting Companies for every 1 (One) fully paid -up equity share held in the Company

points.point: On July 30, 2026 the Board approved a sixth, vertical separation — surplus real estate (22 assets, ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft, just ₹1.26 crore of FY26 turnover, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share per 20 — because the assets sat embedded in the operating business and were under-utilised.
points.quote: The real estate business is currently embedded within the operating business and the real estate portfolio has been historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub -optimal visibility of the real estate business segment and value realization.

points.point: The real estate scheme's stated aim mirrors the five-way logic — a pure-play platform with its own management, capital structure and investor base, potentially consolidating real estate from other group companies (Meenakshi Energy, Incab) and claiming a value-creation opportunity of over ₹30,000 crore on ~130mn sq ft.
points.quote: To unlock the inherent value of the Real Estate Business, enable focused development, exploit the growth potential of the Real Estate Business and attract a distinct set of investors and strategic partners aligned with real estate and infrastructure development, it is proposed to consolidate the Real Estate Business of the Demerged Company under an independent, dedicated entity.

points.point: The Q1 FY27 filings present the completed demerger as having validated the thesis: combined market cap of the resulting companies up over ₹71,000 crore in one quarter, and ₹225.50 at announcement (Sep 29, 2023) versus ₹932.05 combined on listing day (June 15, 2026).
points.quote: Vedanta’s  demerger is unlock ing significant shareholder value, with combined market cap of resulting companies growing  by over ₹71,000 crore  in the 1st quarter .

verdict.what_management_expects: Five pure-plays each chasing its own growth and thematic investors; debt matched to earnings — Oil & Gas nil, Iron & Steel <$0.2bn, Aluminium 1.3x, Power 4.7x, Vedanta Ltd 0.4x; Copper brand fee 3%→0.75% lifting margin ~1%→5%+; independent dividend policies with HZL upstream mandate dropped; tax efficiency from recast balance sheets; anchor investors entering entity cap tables to deleverage VRL; real estate platform targeting ₹30,000 crore+.
verdict.gaps: No per-entity EBITDA/valuation targets, no quantified stranded corporate or listing costs, no reason the other four brand fees stay at 3%, no real-estate monetisation timeline or revenue model.

verdict.rationale: Triveni Engineering & Industries (TEIL) is carving out its Power Transmission Business (PTB) — the Mysuru high-speed/turbo gearbox and incubating defence-products business — into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd (TPTL), a then-wholly-owned subsidiary, via a composite scheme that also amalgamates the 61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL) into TEIL; management's stated purpose, repeated almost verbatim across calls, is 'value unlocking' and later 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies'. The implicit problem is the conglomerate mix: PTB is the one segment with predictable, high-quality economics (FY25 turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, PBIT margin >34%; H1 FY26 PBIT ~36%, one quarter at 41%; Suresh Taneja in Jun 2026: 'we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT'), while sugar and distillery are price- and policy-regulated commodity businesses whose margins collapsed in FY25 on a 69 bps gross-recovery fall, red rot/pest damage, ₹300/MT UP cane-price increases and frozen ethanol prices — exactly the asymmetry investor Bharat Shah (ASK) pressed management on in Feb 2025. Separation also funds and showcases PTB's own growth programme: board-approved capex in three tranches totalling ₹340 crore (₹231 crore spent to 31 Mar 2026, of which ₹78 crore on the defence facility), lifting gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ~₹700 crore of output by September 2026, against a global high-speed/turbo gear market management sized at '$650-$700-odd million', a Swiss subsidiary (Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, bought by TPTL in FY26), AVL qualifications with global OEMs, and exports targeted at 'more than half' of original-equipment sales; Tarun Sawhney said TPTL is 'armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more'. Crucially, TEIL deliberately retains ~30% of TPTL rather than a clean split — investor Resham Jain (DSP) challenged this as re-importing a holdco discount — because, per Sawhney, the defence business is being incubated and 'in establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important', plus the view that the earlier Triveni Turbine separation 'was actually quite a positive one'. Preparation was operational as well as legal: systems, CRM, SAP HANA/ERP migration, digital-twin and smart-factory work so TPTL could 'hit the ground sprinting' as a standalone, with separate board meetings and separate earnings calls promised for TEIL and TPTL from Q1 FY27. The scheme was approved by shareholders/creditors in December 2025, sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad (orders 7 and 18 May 2026), effective 19 May 2026, with scheme appointed date 1 April 2025 and demerger appointed date 1 April 2026; shareholders receive 1 TPTL share of ₹2 for every 3 TEIL shares of ₹1, and ICRA reaffirmed TEIL at AA+ Stable, 'lifting it from its previous under watch status'. Water/wastewater, sugar, distillery and IMIL/IMFL stay with TEIL, which keeps the residual cash flows the board said it would run workshops on to evaluate deployment options.
verdict.evolution: The composite scheme was approved by TEIL's board on 10 December 2024 and first discussed on the Feb 5, 2025 call, where Sawhney framed it purely as 'value unlocking', defended the ~30% retained stake on defence pre-qualification/balance-sheet grounds against Resham Jain's holdco-discount objection, and guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year'. Through May 28, 2025 and Jul 30, 2025 the plan was unchanged but stuck at SEBI ('following up continuously with SEBI', possibly '+30-odd days'), with separation still expected in Q4 FY26/early CY2026, while Resham Jain asked for granular PTB disclosure 'given that this is going to get separately listed' and the board began workshops on what residual TEIL would do with its cash. By Nov 7, 2025 the stock exchanges had issued observation letters (BSE 7 Aug, NSE 11 Aug 2025), NCLT-convened stakeholder meetings were set for late November/early December, and TPTL had acquired the Swiss entity; on Feb 2, 2026 management added the second rationale — 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' — reported December 2025 shareholder/creditor approval, a February NCLT hearing, and said 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies'. On Jun 4, 2026 Sawhney confirmed NCLT approval (19 May 2026 effective date), the two record dates, restored AA+ rating and guided to TPTL listing 'by the end of August' with separate calls for both entities; in fact the demerger record date was 22 July 2026 and TPTL's 10,47,54,338 shares only began trading on BSE/NSE on 12 October 2026, with cost of acquisition split 86.60% TEIL / 13.40% TPTL.

points.point: First call after the 10 December 2024 announcement; the scheme is presented as two linked steps — amalgamating the 61.77%-held listed subsidiary SSEL into TEIL and vesting the Power Transmission Business undertaking into wholly-owned Triveni Power Transmission Ltd — with value unlocking as the stated board motive.
points.quote: I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.

points.point: Resham Jain (DSP) objected that TEIL retaining ~30% of TPTL recreates the Triveni Turbines-style holdco discount and is not a clean value unlock — the clearest instance of an investor shaping the debate on structure.
points.quote: It seems that Triveni Engineering will still be holding 30% stake even after demerger. So why such structure, if the value unlocking has to happen, it should have been a clean structure where Triveni would not be holding anything otherwise, the same Holdco discount will be applicable to the Power Transmission business once it gets demerged.

points.point: Sawhney justified the retained stake on two grounds: the Triveni Turbines precedent was positive, and the co-located defence business needs group balance-sheet backing to win pre-qualifications and bid — i.e. a clean split would handicap defence.
points.quote: The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.

points.point: Bharat Shah (ASK Investment Managers) framed the underlying investor problem the separation addresses: PTB is the one predictable, compounding business while the rest of the portfolio produces erratic outcomes, making long-term valuation of the whole impossible.
points.quote: If you look at the composition of various businesses that we are in, barring the Power Transmission business, which is relatively more robust, predictable economics and predictable outcomes over a period of time, brick-by-brick being built.

points.point: The same board meeting approved an incremental ₹60 crore capex to lift gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ₹700 crore by September 2026, sized against a global high-speed/turbo gear market of roughly $650-700 million — the growth case the separate listing is meant to fund and surface.
points.quote: The Board has confidence that we need ₹700 crore worth of capacity as we start off 2026-27.

points.point: PTB's FY25 numbers were the evidence for separate valuation: turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%), PBIT margin above 34%, order booking over ₹475 crore and record Q4 revenue of almost ₹140 crore — growth without margin dilution.
points.quote: And the PBIT grew by 18.4% to ₹126.8 crore with PBIT margins in excess of 34%, which is a very much in line with our long-term average.

points.point: Resham Jain asked for far more granular PTB disclosure — customers, industry mix — explicitly because it will be separately listed; management accepted, showing investor demand driving pre-separation transparency.
points.quote: So I would request maybe if you can start giving more colour on the Power Transmission business from like what kind of customers you are targeting ?

points.point: The plan was unchanged in substance but stalled at SEBI, with timing guided to Q1 of the next calendar year / Q4 FY26 and possible slippage of about 30 days; separately the board said it would run workshops on how residual TEIL would deploy its cash flows post-demerger.
points.quote: We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.

points.point: Stock-exchange approvals were in hand and the NCLT process had begun with stakeholder meetings scheduled for late November/early December 2025; in parallel TPTL acquired 100% of Triveni Power Transmission GmbH (Switzerland), building the export engine inside the entity being demerged.
points.quote: The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT.

points.point: Management for the first time stated both objectives together — unlocking value and driving operational efficiencies — and confirmed December 2025 shareholder/creditor approval with a further NCLT hearing in February 2026.
points.quote: Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.

points.point: Standalone readiness was being built deliberately — skills, systems, CRM, smart factory and SAP HANA migration — so TPTL could run as an independent company with TEIL-level efficiency from day one.
points.quote: A lot of systems work is being done as we speak to let them hit the ground sprinting, frankly speaking, and have the same kind of efficiencies that we've had at Triveni Engineering and any of the other businesses that the company has run.

points.point: Scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval; appointed date 1 April 2025 for the scheme and 1 April 2026 for the demerger, with the SSEL record date on 3 June 2026 and TPTL listing then guided for end-August 2026.
points.quote: I'm delighted to inform you that the composite scheme of arrangement is effective from the 19th of May, 2026 after the approval of the NCLT.

points.point: A lender/rating-agency consequence: ICRA removed the rating watch tied to the scheme and reaffirmed TEIL at AA+ Stable, which management called a return to Triveni Engineering's historically highest rating.
points.quote: I am very proud to announce that post the scheme having been approved, ICRA has reaffirmed our long-term credit rating as AA+ Stable, lifting it from its previous under watch status.

points.point: TPTL carries its own funding capacity for the ₹340 crore capex programme (₹231 crore incurred to 31 March 2026, ₹78 crore of it on the defence facility; ~₹109 crore left, ~40% of it defence), which supports ~₹700 crore of gears output excluding defence.
points.quote: Of course, as power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.

points.point: Independent listing is now named as the explicit strategic objective of the Power Transmission segment, alongside export-led growth, the Swiss subsidiary, oil-and-gas pump/compressor qualifications and compressor test rigs.
points.quote: Within the Power Transmission Business, our strategic push to clearly move towards, of course, the independent listing of TPTL.

points.point: Post-separation governance was spelled out: separate Q1 FY27 board meetings, separate published results and separate earnings calls for TEIL and TPTL — the disclosure separation investors had asked for since mid-2025.
points.quote: I do want to assure all those on this call and other investors of Triveni Engineering that the end of August 2026 will probably be after our Q1 board meetings for TEIL as well as TPTL, and we fully intend on publishing our results in the papers and on our web pages and holding earnings conference calls for both companies so that our shareholders are fully knowledgeable about the progress that the businesses have made in Q1 of FY27.

points.point: Asked directly whether demerger changes PTB margins, Group CFO Suresh Taneja pointed to continuity of the ~35% PBIT profile, with FY26 order book just under ₹500 crore (+25%) and aftermarket at ~40% of gears sales supporting it.
points.quote: So far, we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT. I think the same trend is expected to continue in future also.

points.point: The demerger consideration ratio: TEIL shareholders receive one ₹2 TPTL share for every three ₹1 TEIL shares held, with the demerger record date fixed at 22 July 2026 (filing dated 11 July 2026).
points.quote: For every 3(three) equity shares of the Demerged Company with a face value of INR 1 each held in the Demerged Company, every equity shareholder of the Demerged Company shall, without any application, act or deed, be entitled to receive 1 (One) equity share of the Resulting Company with a face value of INR 2 each, credited as fully paid up on the same terms and conditions of issue as prevalent in the Demerged Company

points.point: The SSEL leg: eligible SSEL shareholders received 100 TEIL shares of ₹1 for every 137 SSEL shares of ₹10 on record date 3 June 2026; 14,65,048 TEIL shares were allotted on 9 June 2026, SSEL was dissolved without winding up, and ₹12.25 lakh of fractional-entitlement proceeds were distributed on 9 September 2026.
points.quote: Accordingly, as on May 19, 2026 ie Effective Date (as defined in the Scheme) the Amalgamating Company has merged with the Amalgamated Company in accordance with Part III of the Scheme and the Amalgamating Company stands dissolved without being wound up, without any further act or deed.

points.point: Actual separation completed well after the end-August guidance: TPTL allotted 7,34,54,338 shares to TEIL shareholders on 28 July 2026, ceasing to be a subsidiary and becoming an associate, and 10,47,54,338 TPTL shares began trading on BSE (544824) and NSE (TRIVENIPT) only on 12 October 2026. Cost of acquisition was split 86.60% TEIL / 13.40% TPTL.
points.quote: Accordingly, the equity shares of the Company shall be listed and admitted to dealings on BSE and NSE with effect from October 12, 2026, as per the details set out below:

points.point: TPTL was set up with its own full management slate on 28 July 2026 — Dhruv M. Sawhney as Non-Executive Chairman, Tarun Sawhney as Vice Chairman & MD for five years, a dedicated CFO, Company Secretary and eleven designated senior management personnel including a separate Defence Design and Defence Business Development leadership — evidencing the standalone-operating-company rationale.
points.quote: Mr. Tarun Sawhney (DIN: 00382878) as Managing Director (designated as Vice Chairman & Managing Director) and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company for a period of five years and subject to approval of the shareholders.

verdict.what_management_expects: TPTL: independently listed, ~35% PBIT margins sustained, own cash flows funding the ₹340 crore capex to ~₹700 crore gears output plus the defence facility, exports above 50% of original equipment, global AVL access; TEIL's retained ~30% preserves defence pre-qualification credibility. TEIL: sugar, distillery, water retained, AA+ Stable restored, investable cash flows, separate results and calls for both.
verdict.gaps: No quantified value-unlock or target valuation, no PTB standalone balance sheet/debt split, no rationale for the 30% stake size, no explanation of repeated timeline slippage.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the demerger of Sammaan Finserve Limited's (SFL) entire NBFC lending business — the 'Demerged Undertaking' — into its parent Sammaan Capital Limited (SCL), leaving SFL as an empty-of-lending vehicle for a strategically distinct new business. The binding trigger management cites is regulatory: when RBI granted SCL a fresh NBFC-ICC certificate of registration on June 28, 2024 (N-14.03624) on its conversion from an HFC, RBI directed that no other entity in the group may hold an NBFC-ICC/HFC CoR within a prescribed timeline, and SCL had been running on an RBI dispensation for an NBFC owning an NBFC that Gagan Banga said 'is not a structure which will be long term enabled' (May 2025). The original plan had been the opposite — in Q2 FY25 SCL recreated SFL as a standalone affordable-housing/micro-LAP lender, transferred ~₹3,000 Cr of common legacy book from SFL up to SCL at arm's-length fair market value (bids invited from third parties, advisers Deloitte, BDO, CAM, IndusLaw), ran ~₹4,000 Cr of credit cost through SFL's P&L leaving only ₹25 Cr net NPA there, and brought ~₹2,500 Cr of the fair-value discount into SCL as a general provision buffer (total imputed provisions ₹9,575 Cr, ~30% of the legacy book) — explicitly so SFL could be monetised, since 'peer companies in this space typically trade at valuations of more than 4x their net worth' against SFL's ~₹3,000 Cr net worth, ₹6,100 Cr retail AUM, ₹2,900 Cr own book and seven co-lending partners. By Aug 2025 the decision was to sell a stake in SFL to a 'rating accretive' strategic partner within 9 months, with independent leadership, branches, tech and people, and a Deputy CEO hired for SCL. IHC's ₹8,850 Cr preferential allotment for 41.2% (announced Oct 2025) changed that: Banga said in Nov 2025 the Finserve strategy 'is still something which is being planned out with the investor,' and by Feb 2026 the plan had flipped to merging SFL's lending business into SCL — 'post the announcement of the proposed preferential allotment to IHC, this was the next logical step' — consolidating lending and distribution so SCL alone offers the full mortgage-backed suite (prime home loans ₹30 lakh, LAP ₹75 lakh, affordable home loans ₹15 lakh, micro-LAP ₹25 lakh) and later widens beyond mortgages, with the AIF platform (~₹6,200 Cr lent, top 8 cities) kept as the wholesale/credit vehicle. Management also said the merger was tactical for approvals: it 'is facilitating an expeditious approval from both the RBI and SEBI' for the IHC preferential issue and open offer. The Scheme adds that SFL is 'contemplating entry into a new industry, namely the insurance broking and insurtech business, which is strategically distinct from its existing NBFC operations,' needing a dedicated management and operational structure, and that SFL will prospectively house other financial services under IHC's guidance; SFL's listed NCD holders get 1:1 SCL NCDs on identical coupon, tenure, ISIN, redemption price and security, and since SFL is a wholly owned subsidiary no shares are issued as consideration.
verdict.evolution: Aug 13, 2024: Banga flags a 'completely new corporate structure,' six small subsidiaries being merged and fee-based businesses identified. Nov 15, 2024: SFL is made the designated vehicle for the incubated Smart City/affordable line, the common legacy book is transferred to SCL, a 'clean separation of the business' is declared and SFL is framed as a quick monetization tool at >4x book, while Banga notes the RBI forbearance on an NBFC owning an NBFC; Feb 11 and May 16, 2025 add FY27 targets for SFL (AUM ₹15,000 Cr, disbursals ₹9,000 Cr, 4-5%+ ROA, ~14-15% ROE) and the admission that the dispensation 'will not be long term enabled,' with de-subsidiarisation or listing as options. Aug 13, 2025: a formal decision to bring a 'rating accretive' strategic equity partner into SFL within 9 months, with full isolation of people, tech and distribution; Oct 31, 2025: after the IHC deal is announced, the SFL strategy is put on hold pending the investor's views. Feb 4, 2026: direction reverses — SFL's lending business merges into SCL as 'the next logical step' after IHC, helping expedite RBI/SEBI approvals, with SFL kept alive for other financial services; the Scheme (board approval Dec 31, 2025; RBI no-objection May 7, 2026; NCLT first motion June 12, 2026; shareholder approval 99.97% on Sept 10, 2026; second motion admitted Sept 21, 2026) grounds it in RBI's one-licence condition and SFL's planned insurance broking/insurtech entry.

points.point: First signal of a structural redraw: six small subsidiaries being merged and fee-based businesses identified, with a new corporate structure to be unveiled with Q2 FY25 results, shaped by RBI and other stakeholder feedback.
points.quote: We would also like to unveil a completely new corporate structure they have as part of the Board outcome gathered that we are merging six of our smaller subsidiaries.

points.point: SFL is converted from a mirror image of the parent into the designated vehicle for the Smart City affordable line, after a deep scrub leaving just ₹25 Cr net NPA in SFL and the common legacy book (~₹3,000 Cr) consolidated into SCL.
points.quote: Sammaan Finserve Limited is now going to be our designated vehicle for pursuing a new line of business, which we had been incubating for the last 2 years under the Smart City program.

points.point: The separation's stated purpose is a clean split of processes, systems and focus between SCL's prime housing/urban MSME book and SFL's new line, aiding shareholder transparency, regulatory compliance and the eventual partner search.
points.quote: We've also been able to achieve a clean separation of the business.

points.point: Valuation arbitrage is given as an explicit motive: affordable-housing peers trade above 4x net worth versus SFL's ~₹3,000 Cr net worth and ~₹5,000 Cr AUM, making SFL a quick monetization tool.
points.quote: Peer companies in this space typically trade at valuations of more than 4x their net worth.

points.point: Asked by Prithvi (VicAsset/Oaktree) about monetization, Banga names the regulatory constraint — RBI's forbearance for an NBFC owning an NBFC — and says SCL must de-subsidiarise at an appropriate time in consultation with the regulator.
points.quote: As far as the monetization plan is concerned, we are extremely mindful of the fact that there is RBI forbearance, which is there where an NBFC is owning an NBFC.

points.point: Pressed by Niraj Chhajer (Pransh Capital) on whether RBI requires dilution and on the 12-month dispensation expiring June 2025, Banga confirms the two-NBFC structure is not sustainable, with de-subsidiarisation or listing as optionality once SFL hits ₹10,000 Cr AUM.
points.quote: There is RBI dispensation that we currently enjoy as far as an NBFC owning an NBFC and that is not a structure which will be long term enabled.

points.point: A formal decision is taken to induct a strategic equity partner into SFL within about 9 months, requiring complete isolation of SFL's tech, people and distribution plus organisational restructuring and a Deputy CEO appointment.
points.quote: We would be looking to, over the next 3 quarters, bring in into Sammaan Finserve, a strategic partner who is rating accretive.

points.point: The partner's purpose is credit-rating uplift: a reputable equity partner would be rating accretive for SFL (then ~₹7,121 Cr balance sheet, ₹3,071 Cr net worth) and rub off positively on SCL's own rating and cost of funds.
points.quote: The arrival of a new equity partner with a strong market reputation should be rating accretive for the Sammaan Finserve entity and should also have a positive rub-off on Sammaan Capital.

points.point: After IHC's ₹8,850 Cr preferential allotment for 41.2% is announced, the SFL plan is suspended pending the incoming promoter's views; SFL (₹6,200 Cr AUM) stays a small-ticket mortgage player for the interim.
points.quote: The strategy around Finserv, the subsidiary in light of this investment is still something which is being planned out with the investor.

points.point: Direction reverses: SFL's lending business will be merged into SCL, consolidating lending and distribution so SCL offers the full mortgage suite (home loans ₹30 lakh/₹15 lakh, LAP ₹75 lakh/₹25 lakh) and can later widen beyond mortgages.
points.quote: To start off, in this quarter, one of the major developments was the announced proposed merger of our subsidiary, Sammaan Finserve into Sammaan Capital.

points.point: The consolidation is framed as the direct consequence of the IHC transaction rather than a standalone idea, replacing the earlier plan to sell a stake in SFL.
points.quote: Post the announcement of the proposed preferential allotment to IHC, this was the next logical step.

points.point: A tactical approval motive is stated: simplifying to one lending NBFC helps secure faster RBI approval for the preferential allotment and SEBI approval for the open offer, with both IHC and SCL engaged with regulators.
points.quote: We believe that the proposed merger of Sammaan Finserve, is facilitating an expeditious approval from both the RBI and SEBI.

points.point: SFL is deliberately kept alive as the forward vehicle for non-lending financial services under IHC's guidance, while the AIF platform (~₹6,200 Cr lent, good investor returns, top-8-city experience) remains the wholesale credit platform.
points.quote: Sammaan Finserve as a company will continue to exist and whatever other financial services we propose to offer in due course of time, under the guidance of IHC, would be housed prospectively under Sammaan Finserve.

points.point: The Scheme's legal rationale is RBI's one-licence condition attached to SCL's June 28, 2024 NBFC-ICC certificate of registration (N-14.03624) issued on conversion from a housing finance company; the demerger transfers SFL's NBFC business to SCL on a going-concern basis to comply.
points.quote: While issuing the CoR, RBI directed SCL to ensure that no other entity in the group shall hold CoR as an NBFC-ICC/HFC within the prescribed timeline.

points.point: Benefit one is scale and capital consolidation of both entities' lending activity into a single platform, with stated synergies, pooled resources and knowledge, a more diversified product suite and improved scalability, funding access and long-term credit growth.
points.quote: Entire NBFC Business activities of SCL and SFL shall be consolidated into a single entity, with a wider and stronger capital and asset base, having greater capacity for conducting its operations more efficiently and competitively;

points.point: The other half of the rationale is SFL's planned entry into insurance broking and insurtech — needing a focused management and operational structure, justified by industry growth, broking-channel dependency, digital disruption, favourable regulatory reform and investor interest.
points.quote: SFL is contemplating entry into a new industry, namely the insurance broking and insurtech business, which is strategically distinct from its existing NBFC operations.

points.point: Capital allocation is explicitly split: SCL optimises capital toward lending, provisioning and regulatory buffers while SFL deploys resources to product development, platform enhancement and digital innovation, improving transparency for shareholders, lenders, rating agencies and regulators.
points.quote: SCL will be able to optimise its capital allocation towards lending, provisioning and regulatory buffers, while SFL will deploy its resources towards product development, platform enhancement and digital innovation.

points.point: Creditor protection is the stated reason no meetings were needed: SFL's listed NCDs transfer to SCL on identical terms 1:1, no shares are issued as consideration since SFL is a wholly owned subsidiary, and employees transfer with continuity of service.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme, the NCDs of the Demerged Company shall be vested with the Resulting Company on the same terms, including the coupon rate, tenure, ISIN, redemption price, quantum, and nature of security.

verdict.what_management_expects: SCL: all NBFC lending in one entity, wider capital and asset base, full mortgage suite, scalability, better funding access, capital to lending and provisioning buffers. SFL: clean vehicle for insurance broking/insurtech and other IHC-guided financial services, resources to product, platform, digital innovation. Both: simpler structure, easier compliance, cost rationalisation, clearer transparency for lenders, rating agencies, regulators.
verdict.gaps: No deadline date for RBI's licence condition, no insurance-broking capital, licence or revenue numbers, no explanation of dropping the rating-accretive partner search, and the May 2026 call never mentioned the scheme.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is the green mobility (electric-vehicle fleet) business — Refex Green Mobility Limited (RGML), a 100% subsidiary of Refex Industries (RIL) running B2B employee transportation and B2B2C fleets (~1,300–1,400 EVs across Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai) — which is being carved out into a separately listed Refex Mobility Limited (RML) via a composite scheme: first RGML merges into RIL, then the Mobility Undertaking is demerged from RIL into RML with mirror 1:1 shareholding (appointed date 1 April 2025). Management's stated reason is that mobility attracts a fundamentally different investor base: Dinesh Agarwal said on the May 2026 call that 'the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited,' and the scheme documents add that the risk, competition, financial profiles and return ratios of Ash & Coal handling are 'distinct' from green mobility, and that mobility can attract its own investors, lenders and strategic partners. The second problem it solves is the drag on consolidated earnings: in Q1 FY26 green mobility ran at a minus 50% segment margin, pulling consolidated PAT down to INR20.4 crore against INR33 crore standalone, and investor Narayana on the August 2025 call called this 'a miscalculation in your capital allocation,' to which Anil Jain replied 'Point well taken.' The green mobility losses were large and recurring — a PBT loss of roughly INR13.9 crore in Q1 FY27 alone and INR38.2 crore of segment EBIT loss in FY26 — because EMIs start the day a vehicle is bought while 100% utilisation takes 6–9 months. Separation also moves the mobility balance sheet out of RIL: Agarwal confirmed about INR220 crore of net assets transfer to mobility and Anil Jain said 'all the debt etc. will also move to that entity,' leaving RIL as a focused ash & coal handling (plus wind, via Venwind) platform where 95–100% of standalone revenue comes from ash and coal. Lenders were an explicit gating item — in January 2026 the company was 'waiting for some final NOCs from the lenders' before the scheme could be filed. Management frames the outcome as 'sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery,' with RML free to pursue an asset-light, clean-fuel, enterprise-led growth strategy independently; it had crossed INR100 crore of revenue in three years and is described as 'in the path to profitability.' Because RGML is wholly owned and shareholding mirrors across, no valuation was required and no cash consideration is paid — one RML share of INR2 for every one RIL share of INR2.
verdict.evolution: Through FY25 there was no separation plan at all — on the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 calls management defended diversification as 'optimally diversified,' and the Apr 24, 2025 call offered only a narrower fix: exiting the Bengaluru airport EV taxi contract to save INR6.82 crore of annual fixed cost and refocus on B2B/B2B2C. The idea surfaced as a capital-allocation complaint on the Aug 13, 2025 call, when an investor confronted management with mobility's minus 50% margin and the standalone-versus-consolidated profit gap, and Anil Jain conceded the point and promised to 'rework' the business; the Board approved the draft composite scheme on Sept 22, 2025 (RML incorporated Sept 12, 2025) and it was announced on the Nov 6, 2025 call as a two-step scheme to 'unlock focused value creation,' with no valuation needed and a 6–7 month estimate. By the Jan 21, 2026 call the plan had hardened into numbers and dependencies — INR220 crore of net assets and the mobility debt moving across, lender NOCs pending, mobility reclassified as discontinued operations, completion guided to end-April — and it then slipped repeatedly: BSE/NSE observation letters came on Mar 16, 2026, the NCLT application on Mar 26, 2026, and on the May 27, 2026 call Agarwal reset guidance to another 75–90 days, blaming only court timelines ('from our side, 100% of the all compliances is done'). Shareholders and creditors approved on Aug 5, 2026 (99.999% of equity votes in favour), but the Oct 28, 2026 press release still showed NCLT hearings underway with the next hearing on Oct 28, 2026 — i.e. roughly a year of regulatory drift against the original timeline.

points.point: Before any demerger was contemplated, the fix proposed for mobility was operational pruning — exiting the Bengaluru airport B2C EV taxi contract to cut INR6.82 crore of annual fixed cost and refocus on B2B/B2B2C, with the fleet having grown from 24 vehicles in March 2023 to over 1,300.
points.quote: The withdrawal of service from Bangalore Airport will help us save an annual fixed cost of INR6.82 crores and other variable expenses pertaining to the operation over there.

points.point: Management disclosed green mobility's segment margin at minus 50% while power trading was also negative; this quantified the drag that the separation later addresses.
points.quote: The margin for coal and ash handling is roughly about 11.77%. Refrigerant gas has been 0.9%. Green Mobility has been minus 50%.

points.point: An investor (Narayana, TrueWealth Advisors) directly attacked the capital allocation, pointing to standalone PAT of ~INR32 crore versus consolidated PAT of ~INR20 crore because of mobility and wind losses, and asked why the company did not just focus on the coal business.
points.quote: And you are making nearly 50% losses on mobility segment and your wind energy is also in loss. It seems to be there is a miscalculation in your capital allocation, sir.

points.point: Anil Jain accepted the criticism and committed to reworking the business, explaining the structural cause of the losses — EMIs begin on vehicle acquisition while full utilisation takes 6–9 months, so a growing fleet is permanently loss-making at the consolidated level.
points.quote: Point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses to ensure that we remake them profitable, sir.

points.point: First formal announcement on a call of the two-step composite scheme — merger of RGML into RIL, then demerger of the Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a new separately listed Refex Mobility Limited — framed as unlocking focused value creation.
points.quote: On this note, I would like to briefly mention that the de-merger of Refex Green Mobility Limited from Refex Industries Limited is in progress through a composite scheme comprising two steps. That is, first the merger of RGML into RIL, followed by a de-merger of Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a separate listed entity called Refex Mobility Limited, in line with our strategy to unlock focused value creation for all our stakeholders.

points.point: Asked by Smit Jain (KTech Family Office) what valuation had been ascribed to the mobility vertical, the CFO said none was needed: RGML is a 100% subsidiary and shareholding mirrors across, so value discovery is left to the market post-listing; filings with BSE/NSE were done and NCLT next, with a 6–7 month estimate.
points.quote: As per the company and the process of merger and demerger process there is no valuations requirement to be done since the company holds 100, it is a 100 subsidiary and a mirror shareholding will happen, all the shareholder of Refex Industries Limited will be same shareholding as per the scheme which has been disclosed there.

points.point: Lenders were the binding constraint on filing the scheme — the company was waiting on final no-objection certificates from them, with completion then guided to end-April 2026.
points.quote: On the demerger, I think we currently are waiting for some final NOCs from the lenders.

points.point: The separation is explicitly a balance-sheet separation as well as an operational one: mobility's debt travels with it into the new entity, giving RML independent liberty to run its own business.
points.quote: Once it is demerged, the Refex Mobility will run as a separate entity where it will have more liberty to do its own business and also it will have its own, all the debt etc. will also move to that entity.

points.point: Quantum of the carve-out: in answer to Vivek Joshi asking what share of consolidated net assets moves to mobility, the CFO put the figure at INR220 crore, and confirmed RML will be 'a parallel separate listing completely.'
points.quote: Rs.220 Crores.

points.point: The clearest statement of purpose on any call, in answer to a shareholder (Maya) asking how the demerger creates value: the EV/sustainability business needs a different investor base than Refex Industries, and the structure is meant to unlock value for shareholders, with mobility itself 'in the path to profitability.'
points.quote: The purpose of the demerger is because the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited.

points.point: Management's statement of the expected benefits for each side — independent operation with dedicated strategic and financial focus, sharper operating focus, clear capital allocation and value discovery — alongside mobility crossing INR100 crore of revenue in three years on an asset-light, clean-fuel, enterprise-led strategy.
points.quote: Post completion of the demerger, the mobility platform will operate independently with a dedicated strategic and financial focus. We believe this structure will create sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery for all the stakeholders.

points.point: Timeline slippage was attributed entirely to the NCLT calendar, not to the company — BSE and NSE approvals obtained, NCLT filing done, courts in summer vacation until 1 June, 75–90 days more expected; compliance 100% complete from Refex's side.
points.quote: Yes, sir. It all depended on the court time and other process. But from our side, 100% of the all compliances is done.

points.point: The filed scheme's rationale rests on business dissimilarity: ash & coal handling and green mobility differ in risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios, so housing them together obscures both.
points.quote: The nature of risk and competition, financial profiles and return ratios involved in the Ash & Coal handling business of RIL are distinct from Green Mobility Business presently undertaken through its wholly owned subsidiary RGML.

points.point: The scheme names the external constituencies the separation is meant to serve — a distinct set of investors, lenders and strategic partners for the mobility business — which is the written counterpart of management's 'different set of investor' remark on the call.
points.quote: The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.

points.point: Listed benefits include an independent global-scale mobility company, greater management focus, independent collaboration and expansion by each entity, letting investors choose exposure by risk profile, and — most concretely — separate access to debt and equity markets.
points.quote: Enabling focused and sharper capital market access (debt and equity) and thereby unlocking the value of the Green Mobility Business Undertaking and creating enhanced value for shareholders.

points.point: Consideration mechanics: no shares are issued for the RGML merger (investment cancelled, wholly owned), and the demerger pays RIL shareholders in RML shares on a 1:1 basis, with RML's existing 50,000 shares held by RIL cancelled; RML to be listed on BSE and NSE; appointed date 1 April 2025.
points.quote: 1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Share of Rs.2 each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted as fully paid up for every 1 (One) Equity Shares of Re. 2 each fully paid up held in the Demerged Company.

points.point: Stakeholder approval was overwhelming at the NCLT-convened meetings of 5 August 2026: equity shareholders 99.999% in value in favour (7,91,07,251 votes for versus 603 against), three secured creditors representing 47.2% of INR158.91 crore of secured dues voted unanimously in favour, and 37 unsecured creditors representing 6.1% of INR347.68 crore voted unanimously in favour.
points.quote: Based on the above, the resolution approving the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement has been "unanimously" voted in favor by all the Secured Creditors of the Company.

points.point: Green mobility was reclassified as a discontinued operation pending the scheme, quantifying the drag it removes from RIL: consolidated discontinued-operations loss before tax of INR52.96 crore in FY26 and INR13.94 crore in Q1 FY27, with green mobility segment EBIT losses of INR38.24 crore in FY26 and INR13.61 crore in Q1 FY27.
points.quote: The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on September 22, 2025, had approved the draft Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement amongst Refex Green Mobility Limited ("Transferor Company" or "RGML"), Refex Industries Limited ("Transferee Company" or "Demerged Company" or "RIL") and Refex Mobility Limited ("Resulting Company" or "RML") and their respective shareholders and creditors, under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the rules framed thereunder ("Scheme"), subject to receipt of requisite regulatory approvals, as may be applicable.

verdict.what_management_expects: For RIL: a focused ash & coal handling (plus wind) platform, mobility's ~INR220 crore of net assets and its debt off the books, better earnings quality and 15–18% EBITDA margins. For RML: independent operation with dedicated strategic and financial focus, its own investors, lenders and strategic partners, separate debt and equity market access, asset-light enterprise-led scaling toward profitability, and market-led value discovery via 1:1 mirror listing.
verdict.gaps: No standalone funding plan, margin targets or profitability date for RML; no valuation or asset/debt split detail; no reason given for merging RGML into RIL first.

verdict.segment_name: Green Mobility (labelled "Electric Vehicle" in FY2024 and FY2025 segment tables; "Green mobility" from FY2026) — Refex Green Mobility Ltd. / Refex EV Fleet Services Pvt. Ltd., the Demerged Undertaking transferring to Refex Mobility Limited
verdict.measure_notes: Revenue = consolidated 'Segment Revenue (Net Sales/Income)' per Ind AS 108 note; no inter-segment split is disclosed, so it is the segment revenue as reported. Operating profit = 'Segment Results' i.e. EBIT before other income and exceptional items (finance cost, other income and tax are unallocated at company level, not by segment). No segment-level PAT, EBITDA, depreciation or tax is disclosed anywhere on these pages. FY2026 figures are from the consolidated note where Green Mobility is classified as a discontinued operation.
