verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not a pharma business at all: it is the Life Sciences business and the Digital Innovation business of Arco Lab Private Limited, Strides' wholly owned Global Capability Centre (GCC), carved out into a new wholly owned subsidiary, Pivot Path Private Limited, under a Sections 230–232 Scheme of Arrangement, and then majority-sold. Management's stated reason is that this unit — built inside Arco Lab across life sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, and technology-enabled operational services — outgrew its captive role: 'As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.' The filings name four problems the separation solves: supporting its next phase of growth, serving global customers effectively, building agentic-AI platforms, and enabling access to external capital — none of which a cost-centre inside a pharma manufacturer can fund or staff. The numbers cited are modest and explain why it is not core to Strides: FY26 revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) — just 3% of Strides' turnover — with EBITDA of ₹169 million, net worth of ₹100 million standalone (0.3% of Strides' net worth) and ₹360 million consolidated (1%). Ascent Capital (through Ascent Growth Trust) with co-investor Vintage Classic Limited values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300 million post-money; Strides realises ~₹1,000 million (₹750 million at closing, ₹250 million on the first anniversary), keeps 19.95%, and Ascent injects ₹500 million of primary capital, leaving Investors 65.05% and a 15% ESOP pool, with Pivot Path reclassified as an Associate. Badree Komandur frames it as Strides' repeatable playbook — 'Strides' proven capability to identify, incubate and scale high-potential businesses' — that 'unlocks value for Strides, provides Pivot Path with the resources to scale independently, and allows Strides to retain meaningful participation in its future success,' while also 'strengthens the Company's balance sheet.' No investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the pull came from external life-sciences customers and from the incoming financial investor, whose rationale (per Raja Kumar) is to pair 400+ subject matter experts with technology and agentic AI in 'core, non-discretionary segments of the pharmaceutical industry.' Pricing rests on an independent valuation by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, and the deal is declared not a related party transaction and outside Regulation 37A.
verdict.evolution: The idea does not appear in a single one of the thirteen earnings calls; it exists only in the filings, which reference an intimation of May 15, 2025 for the Arco Lab–Pivot Path scheme, with an Appointed Date of April 10, 2025 — i.e. the carve-out was in motion for more than a year unmentioned. NCLT Bengaluru pronounced approval on May 18, 2026 (the same day as the Q4 FY26 board meeting whose call, on May 18, 2026, discussed only US/ex-US growth, margins and deleveraging), the order hit the NCLT portal May 20, 2026, the certified copy arrived May 25, 2026, and the Scheme became effective June 1, 2026. Only on June 27, 2026 did the plan's second leg surface: the board approved selling a majority stake to the Ascent Capital consortium, converting what the Scheme had set up as a wholly owned subsidiary into a ~20%-held Associate. The nearest the calls come is context on the earlier OneSource/softgel playbook — Arco Lab named as the wholly owned subsidiary parking the OneSource stake (May 22, 2025 call) and the ₹78.8 billion returned to shareholders via that demerger and listing (July 29, 2025 call).

points.point: The separated business is Arco Lab's Life Sciences business plus its Digital Innovation business, demerged into Pivot Path under Sections 230–232, with Appointed Date April 10, 2025 and NCLT approval pronounced May 18, 2026.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab’s Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the “Demerged Undertaking”) into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder (“Scheme”).

points.point: The stated purpose of the carve-out is growth capacity, global customer service, agentic-AI platform building and access to outside capital — things it could not do as a captive GCC unit.
points.quote: To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital, the business was carved out into Pivot Path pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in May 2026.

points.point: The trigger was external demand: a unit originally serving Strides internally began winning third-party pharma and life-sciences customers and became a standalone platform.
points.quote: As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.

points.point: Strides positions it as a repeatable incubate-and-unlock model rather than a disposal of a problem asset, keeping economic participation.
points.quote: The transaction reflects Strides' strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth.

points.point: Scale cited: FY26 revenue ₹1,447 million (3% of Strides' turnover) and EBITDA ₹169 million; net worth ₹100 million standalone (0.3%) and ₹360 million consolidated (1%) — small enough that it is clearly non-core.
points.quote: For FY26, the carved-out business reported revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) and EBITDA of ₹169 million, demonstrating its operating scale and growth trajectory.

points.point: Economics: ~₹2,300m post-money valuation, ~₹1,000m realised by Strides (₹750m at closing, ₹250m after one year), ₹500m primary infusion by Ascent, Strides left at 19.95% with Investors 65.05% and a 15% ESOP pool.
points.quote: The transaction values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m on a post-money basis, enables Strides to realise ~₹1,000m while retaining a ~20% stake, and includes a primary capital infusion of ₹500 million to accelerate Pivot Path's next phase of growth.

points.point: Badree Komandur's framing of the three-way benefit — cash and balance-sheet strength for Strides, independent scaling resources for Pivot Path, retained upside.
points.quote: This transaction unlocks value for Strides, provides Pivot Path with the resources to scale independently, and allows Strides to retain meaningful participation in its future success.

points.point: Accounting consequence: Pivot Path drops out of consolidation and becomes an Associate; the deal is declared non-related-party, priced off an independent SEBI-registered merchant banker valuation.
points.quote: Upon completion of the transaction, Pivot Path shall be reclassified as an Associate Company.

points.point: The incoming investor's rationale: 400+ subject matter experts applying technology and agentic AI to compliance, digital transformation and drug safety in non-discretionary pharma spend.
points.quote: Pivot Path brings deep domain expertise across the core, non-discretionary segments of the pharmaceutical industry, capabilities that have been rigorously honed within the Strides stable.

points.point: The Q4 FY26 call, held May 18, 2026 — the very day NCLT pronounced the Pivot Path order — never mentions Pivot Path, Arco Lab or any carve-out; the three-year strategy is described purely in pharma terms.
points.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have been very clear on our priorities, geographical diversification, profitability and balance sheet strength.

points.point: The only call-level support for the value-unlocking logic is the OneSource precedent, cited as the company's demonstrated way of returning value to shareholders.
points.quote: And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.

points.point: Arco Lab — the entity Pivot Path was later carved out of — is discussed on the calls only as the wholly owned subsidiary holding the residual 1.6% OneSource stake, with no hint of a services business inside it.
points.quote: So we retained this in Arco Lab, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Pivot Path: ₹500m primary capital, resources to scale independently, serve global customers, build agentic-AI platforms, access external capital and Ascent's expertise, plus a 15% ESOP pool. For Strides: ~₹1,000m realised (₹750m at closing, ₹250m at one year), a strengthened balance sheet, and a ~20% associate stake retaining upside. No margin, focus or re-rating claims are made.
verdict.gaps: Calls never mention Pivot Path or Arco Lab's demerger. No use of proceeds, no reason for selling majority rather than listing, no customer, employee or related-party-pricing detail.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is the hospitality business of Prestige Estates Projects Ltd., housed in subsidiary Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited (PHVL), out of the listed real-estate development parent. Management's stated reason is capital, not distress: Irfan Razack said hospitality is where "a lot of capex will be required," that the currently trading hotel assets are already "booming" and throwing "positive numbers from all the assets," and that there is "a huge pipeline of new assets which are either under planning or under construction or approval" that "will definitely require fresh spending" — "hence an IPO will be the need of the day." The demerger-plus-IPO is therefore framed as giving "additional bandwidth to grow the hospitality business," i.e. a dedicated capital pool for a capex-hungry annuity business instead of funding it from the developer's balance sheet. The only parent-side numbers given are balance-sheet ones: management guided that by end-FY2025 cash flows would be "pretty robust" and debt would fall — clarified as debt-to-equity, not absolute debt — helped by land already paid for at Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel turning into positive cash flows. The push came from the sell side and retail holders asking for updates and for a shareholder quota in the IPO (Kunal Lakhan, Rajeev Venkatesh); no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. A related theme is staying within core competence — on data centres, Zayd Noaman said operations are "completely different, and it's not our expertise," preferring build-to-suit (NTT) and partnerships. The structure ultimately executed was a subsidiary IPO: PHVL filed a DRHP on April 24, 2025, then withdrew it on September 25, 2026 "on account of strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions," with a fresh DRHP possible later.
verdict.evolution: On the May 2024 call the hospitality demerger was already "a work in progress" and management committed to the direction — demerger then IPO — on capex and growth-bandwidth grounds. By the October 2024 call it had moved only to the structuring stage: "too early," with Board approval and the appointment of bankers still ahead, and the retail-quota question deferred. The filings then show execution and reversal: a PHVL DRHP dated April 24, 2025, withdrawn on September 25, 2026 for strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions, with a possible refiling subject to market conditions and approvals.

points.point: Asked for an update on the hospitality demerger, Irfan Razack confirmed it was under way and endorsed the direction as the right one.
points.quote: That's a work in progress and I believe that that's the way to go.

points.point: The core driver given is the capital intensity of hospitality — the demerger plus IPO is meant to create headroom to grow it, since trading assets are performing and a large pipeline is in planning, construction or approval.
points.quote: And once we do the demerger and we do an IPO that will give us additional bandwidth to grow the hospitality business because currently the hospitality business is booming and we're getting positive numbers from all the assets, current assets which are trading and we do have a huge pipeline of new assets which are either under planning or under construction or approval.

points.point: The new pipeline needs fresh money, which management said makes the IPO necessary rather than optional.
points.quote: So all this will definitely require fresh spending and hence an IPO will be the need of the day.

points.point: Parent-side context: land already funded at Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel turns into cash inflows, supporting deleveraging through FY2025 — clarified as debt-to-equity, not absolute debt.
points.quote: So we believ e that the debt levels for the end of financial year 2025 of course there'll be blips up and down quarter -on-quarter, but the cash flows will be pretty robust, and we will try and bring down the debt level from what it is today.

points.point: Five months later the transaction was still only being structured, with Board approval and banker appointments yet to come — so no terms, ratio or timeline were available.
points.quote: It is too early right now. We are in the structuring process.

points.point: A retail shareholder asked for a reserved shareholder quota in the hospitality IPO; management deferred the decision to a later stage.
points.quote: So maybe how much will be the retail quota for the existing shareholders, we'll figure at that point of time once we -- more advanced.

points.point: On data centres, management drew a competence boundary — it will sell land and build to suit (NTT) but not operate — consistent with housing operating-intensive businesses separately or with partners.
points.quote: So with that, we'll build some expertise, but the operations of a data center are completely different, and it's not our expertise.

points.point: The separation was executed as a subsidiary IPO: Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited filed a DRHP dated April 24, 2025 with SEBI, NSE and BSE.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that our subsidiary, Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited ( “PHVL ”), filed a Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated April 24, 2025 (“DRHP ”) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI ”), the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited (“Stock Exchanges ”).

points.point: On September 25, 2026 the PHVL board withdrew the DRHP, citing strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions — no further rationale was disclosed.
points.quote: However, the board of directors of PHVL has decided to withdraw the DRHP on account of strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions, pursuant to its resolution dated September 25, 2026 and corresponding communication dated September 25 , 2026 made to the book running lead managers to the Offer .

points.point: The listing is deferred, not abandoned: PHVL may refile a DRHP later, conditional on markets, approvals and other considerations.
points.quote: Additionally, PHVL may consider filing a fresh draft red herring prospectus with SEBI in the future for an initial public offering of its equity shares in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, subject to suitable market conditions, receipt of requisite approvals and other considerations.

verdict.what_management_expects: Hospitality: demerger plus IPO gives bandwidth and fresh equity for heavy capex on its pipeline under planning, construction and approval, while trading assets already give positive numbers. Parent: cash flows from Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel land bring debt-to-equity down by FY2025. No margin or valuation targets stated.
verdict.gaps: No hospitality revenue, EBITDA, keys or capex numbers; no debt quantum, scheme rationale text, entitlement ratio, asset-debt split, lender or partner consent, valuation, timeline, or what "strategic considerations" meant.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.
verdict.evolution: These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

points.point: The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.

points.point: The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India.
points.quote: The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.

points.point: MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering.
points.quote: As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.

points.point: Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals.
points.quote: During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".

points.point: The Board meeting of 3 February 2026 — the same meeting that approved the first post-demerger results — approved a new standalone factory at Pune, the capacity leg of the separation.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. on February 03, 2026, has approved the setting up of a new factory /plant at Pune, Maharashtra.

points.point: Management re-stated the ACES strategy (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF, defined through 2028) explicitly because the company is now separately listed and needs its own growth and profitability narrative.
points.quote: I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and make our business more profitable.

points.point: The structural case for separate industrial management: industrial runs on small lot sizes and channel flexibility unlike automotive — the Pune TRB example raised capacity from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces, cut cost ~18% and improved changeover/flexibility 20% and new-product lead time 35%.
points.quote: Flexibility, which is key, which is industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels, which means we can switch between one product and another because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller.

points.point: A concrete problem the focused, localized entity solves: segments previously abandoned on cost/margin grounds — wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors — are being re-entered via localization, including a 32.5 crore tractor OEM win and ZF/Suzlon wind orders that drove 91% QoQ wind growth.
points.quote: The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we are now getting back into it.

points.point: Residual entanglement with the automotive entity persists: SKF India (Industrial) manufactures for SKF India Automotive (~4% of FY26 sales), pays royalty/trademark (up ~INR 60 million QoQ) and a transfer-pricing margin on services, and SKF India job-works for it until the new plant starts.
points.quote: We are , till that new plant comes up , comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.

points.point: The one-off separation charges continued into Q4 FY26 at INR 183 million, so reported PBT of 9.5% was 11.5% adjusted (versus 13.1% adjusted in Q3), with the remaining gap blamed on OEM mix (OEM up from 46% to 50%) and full bonus accrual.
points.quote: In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.

points.point: Margin roadmap post-separation: back to ~13% once demerger costs end around end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 through localization, operational efficiency and S&A leverage, with 16-18% only an aspiration held back by OEM mix, competition and depreciation from the new plant.
points.quote: So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.

points.point: Standalone capital plan: INR 800 crore+ capex FY26-27 to FY29-30, a large part for the new Pune plant plus DGBB and TRB channel additions (the INR 350-400 crore earlier flagged), operational mid-2028 and fully ramped by end-CY2028, with growth of ~8% in the interim.
points.quote: So, on capex, the overall plan for the between FY 26, FY27 to FY 29, FY30, we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant which we are in the process of setting up.

verdict.rationale: HEGAM's separation is the "Composite Scheme of Arrangement" among HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly HEG Limited, the Demerged Company), HEG Limited (formerly HEG Graphite Limited, the Resulting Company) and Bhilwara Energy Limited (the Transferor Company): the legacy Graphite Undertaking — the graphite electrodes business, plus the overseas investment and the assets and liabilities of the TAWA power plant — was demerged into the Resulting Company on a going-concern basis with mirror shares issued to HEGAM shareholders, while Bhilwara Energy Limited was simultaneously amalgamated into HEGAM. As the filings present it, the purpose is to put the mature, cyclical electrodes business (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore, H1 FY27 ₹1,207.36 crore and PAT ₹192.33 crore, carrying ₹4,419.21 crore of segment assets and ₹1,245.85 crore of liabilities) in one listed vehicle, and leave HEGAM as a "technology-led, globally competitive advanced materials platform" spanning anode materials (TACC), graphene (HEG Graphene Materials), battery energy storage (Replus Engitech, 74% held) and green power. The amalgamation of Bhilwara Energy brings 278 MW of debt-free hydro (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW of wind into HEGAM, which the CFO says "provides a sound financial foundation for the Group" with "stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore" annually — i.e. the hydro cash flow and the ₹1,322.84 crore cash pile now sit against the heavy new-materials capex rather than against electrodes. The problem it solves is capital allocation and identity: HEGAM's board on 3 November 2026 approved a revised Phase-1 anode cost of ~₹2,350 crore (20,000 MT, COD June 2027, 61% built), a ₹1,606 crore Phase-2 to 44,000 MT by March 2029, a ₹475 crore crucible plant for "backward integration" and cost optimisation, and a ₹500 crore 500 MTPA graphene plant — none of which belong on an electrode balance sheet. The company also altered its main object clause to insert "Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material" (CIN changed from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290) and implemented an ESOP of up to 98,93,970 options, so each entity can be objected, incentivised and financed on its own. Leadership was split along the same line: Ravi Jhunjhunwala moved to Chairman, MD & CEO of the demerged HEG Limited (graphite), while Riju Jhunjhunwala leads HEGAM and has now taken the chair of MPCL and AD Hydro. A lender appears in the record on the power side: CYHPL bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025 and intends to merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself "for consolidating the hydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank."
verdict.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts were supplied, so the sequence can only be traced through filings: by 19 January 2026 the Scheme was already public enough to warrant an investor "Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement," and the 49% MPCL buy-out from Statkraft (SPA 9 September 2025, closed 17 November 2025) had pre-positioned the hydro assets. Shareholders approved it at the NCLT-convened meeting on 5 May 2026 with requisite majority; the NCLT Indore Bench sanctioned it on 13 August 2026; the board fixed 1 September 2026 as Effective Date (Appointed Date backdated to 1 April 2024) and allotted the new shares on 7 September 2026, lifting paid-up capital from ₹38.60 crore to ₹65.96 crore. Only after effectiveness did the plan visibly widen from "separate graphite" to "build out advanced materials": the 3 November 2026 board added Phase-2 anode (44,000 MT), crucibles, graphene, an ESOP and the new object clause, while on 29–30 October 2026 the object-clause CIN change was registered and HEGAM had to publish the unlisted Resulting Company's results on its behalf pending listing.

verdict.rationale: Management presented the separation as a focus-and-investor-base argument, not a rescue: India Glycols was running four structurally different businesses under one listing — Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC, including the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals JV into which IGL sells ethylene oxide), Potable Spirits (country liquor/IMIL plus IMFL, with the Amrut and Bacardi tie-ups), Bio-Fuel/ethanol-ENA sold at government-administered prices to OMCs, and Ennature Biopharma (thiocolchicoside, nicotine, nutraceuticals) with biopolymers. On 4 February 2025 the board approved splitting these into India Glycols (chemicals, glycols, bio-glycols, new specialties, industrial gases, plus the Clariant JV), IGL Spirits (spirits + bio-fuel/ENA) and Ennature Bio Pharma (biopharma + biopolymers), all three to be listed via the NCLT route. CEO Rupark Sarswat said the purpose was to run the companies differently with much more focus and to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors have different appetites; CFO Anand Singhal listed the benefits as independent growth for each business, reducing the risk of one business affecting the others, unlocking value by drawing focused investors, and clearer focus leading to improved management and resource allocation — while insisting the structure would not unduly increase the cost base. Scale was quantified with 9MFY25 numbers: chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 178 cr at 14.9% (against FY24 BSPC Rs 1,626 cr, Bio-Fuel Rs 512 cr, Potable Spirits Rs 5,575 cr gross). Capital allocation was the hard constraint: big capex was frozen until after the demerger, long-term debt was pre-allocated with the SBI-led consortium (about Rs 500 cr chemicals / Rs 700 cr liquor out of Rs 1,200 cr in May 2025, restated to Rs 600 cr / Rs 800 cr out of about Rs 1,400 cr in November 2025), the Rs 467 cr preferential allotment at Rs 915/share in November 2025 went entirely into prepaying debt, and the credit rating was parked on watch-list with no upgrade possible until the demerger completed. Management simultaneously defended keeping bio-fuel with spirits rather than with chemicals, arguing captive multi-feedstock ethanol/ENA gives backward integration, quality control, scale and resilience even if it dilutes percentage margin, and that plant proximity and the EO-to-JV link preserve synergies. By FY26 the residual chemicals business was pitched as under-earning for want of focus and in-house cost streamlining, with the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 expected to make the chemicals entity debt-free. The scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad on 17 July 2026, became effective 1 September 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2026), with IGL Spirits and Ennature Bio Pharma listing and trading from 2–4 November 2026.
verdict.evolution: First disclosed on the 6 February 2025 call as a composite scheme that also folded promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings into IGL so promoters would hold IGL directly; by the 21 May 2025 call it was accompanied by a Rs 500 cr/Rs 700 cr debt split, and the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the KHL amalgamation to pursue the demerger alone. The 11 August 2025 and 18 November 2025 calls hardened the mechanics — three named entities, capex deferred to the post-demerger companies, debt restated to Rs 600 cr/Rs 800 cr, and a Rs 467 cr promoter-and-associates preferential issue to cut debt — while an investor on the August call openly questioned demerging a unit in degrowth. The 12 February 2026 call added that the credit rating would stay on watch-list and no sizeable capex would be sanctioned until completion, and the 18 May 2026 call was spent waiting on the NCLT hearing of 21 May. Shareholders (4,42,48,625 of 4,42,48,626 votes) and unsecured creditors (100% by value) approved on 24 March 2026; NCLT sanctioned on 17 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026, record date 2 September 2026, with trading in both new entities from 4 November 2026.

points.point: Rupark Sarswat first unveiled the three-way restructuring, initially to sit inside the IGL group before listing.

points.point: The core stated reason: different businesses need different strategies and attract different pools of capital.
points.quote: And also, to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments.

points.point: CFO Anand Singhal framed one benefit as ring-fencing contagion between segments (relevant given Ennature's margin collapse and the chemicals/EO price squeeze).
points.quote: Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others.

points.point: Anand gave the pro-forma 9MFY25 size and margins of each proposed entity — chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6%, spirits+biofuel Rs 1,628 cr at 14.4%, Ennature Rs 178 cr at 14.9%.
points.quote: IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin.

points.point: Anand confirmed the NCLT route, a 12-15 month timetable, 1 April 2026 appointed date and listing of all three entities.
points.quote: So, this demerger will be effective from 1st April, 26 and all the three companies will be listed on the stock exchange.

points.point: Investors pushed on listing of the biggest piece, noting over 75% of the business would sit in IGL Spirits.
points.quote: Sir, my first question regarding post restructuring, more than 75% of business comes from IGL Spirits. Is there any plan to list that entity?

points.point: Lender involvement: working capital and term loan allocation across the three companies had to be negotiated with the SBI-led consortium and was not yet confirmed.
points.quote: Rohit, regarding the working capital allocation to each Company and the term loan allocation, we are talking to the term lender, mainly the State Bank of India, who is the leader in our consortium banking.

points.point: Rupark stressed the split must not create duplicate overheads; corporate resources would stay shared with an allocation mechanism.
points.quote: The principle of demerger to start with is to continue to run the businesses under one umbrella, but differently as in separately from a strategic perspective, but not unduly increasing the cost base.

points.point: Asked by Saket Kapoor whether clubbing government-priced bio-fuel with liquor would dilute the IMFL valuation, Rupark defended it as backward integration, quality control and scale.
points.quote: Well, percentage margin is one factor, but the overall profitability and resilience of the business also improves.

points.point: First debt allocation disclosed: Rs 1,200 cr long-term debt split roughly Rs 500 cr to chemicals and Rs 700 cr to liquor, with annual repayments of Rs 150-160 cr (spirits) and Rs 90 cr (chemicals).
points.quote: Just to brief you as of now position, we are having about INR 1,200 crores long-term debt in the books of the company, out of which about INR 500 crores will go to the Chemical division and INR 700 crores will go to the liquor division.

points.point: Rupark restated the rationale and the exact clustering — spirits with ethanol/bio-fuel into IGL Spirits, chemicals with the Clariant JV, Ennature with biopolymers.
points.quote: The idea is that different investors have different appetites for different kind of businesses.

points.point: Growth capex was explicitly deferred to the post-demerger entities; FY26 limited to rollover and Rs 40-50 cr maintenance capex.
points.quote: And after the demerger, the separate companies will think over the CapEx.

points.point: Investor pushback: a long-term shareholder challenged unlocking value by demerging a unit whose net margin had fallen from ~33% (2021) to ~2.4%.
points.quote: We are planning to unlock shareholder value by demerging our business units when there is extreme degrowth in that business.

points.point: Entity-level debt restated: of about Rs 1,400 cr long-term debt, Rs 600 cr to India Glycols and Rs 800 cr to IGL Spirits, with the Rs 467 cr raise plus Rs 180 cr scheduled repayment cutting both proportionately.
points.quote: INR 600 crores in India Glycols and INR 800 crores in IGL Spirits.

points.point: The Rs 467 cr preferential issue at Rs 915/share to promoters, friends and relatives was earmarked entirely for debt reduction ahead of the split.
points.quote: So, this is the update, and the money which whatever we will receive out of this preferential will be utilized for the reduction of the term loan.

points.point: Rupark tied the restructuring to the broader strategy of focusing on bio-based ingredients and consumer/lifestyle value capture.
points.quote: And one of the outcomes of that is in the last few years and now once again, how we've been reorganizing and restructuring our businesses to bring the necessary focus.

points.point: Rating agencies had placed IGL on watch-list because of the demerger; no upgrade (and hence no full benefit of the Rs 582 cr debt reduction) until completion.
points.quote: So, you will not find the rating improvement till our demerger happens.

points.quote: Apart from this, we are not having any big size capex. And any capex will be undertaken only after the demerger.

points.quote: Now, there is, if you look at EBITDA without adjusting the other income and probably some streamlining that is required in-house, we will start to see that the quality of the Chemicals business is probably going to be better than this going forward.

verdict.rationale: Critical premise correction: in these documents JSW Energy is not separating a business of its own — it is the Resulting Company receiving a business, and the separation is GE Power India Limited (GEPIL) demerging its boiler (pressure parts) manufacturing undertaking, centred on the Durgapur plant, into JSW Energy under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act and Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act, with an Appointed Date of 1 July 2025. GEPIL's stated reasons are to let it focus on strategic growth areas and its services growth strategy, streamline the Retained Business and cut costs, ease local approvals versus other transfer routes, and unlock value for its own shareholders while letting them stay invested in the demerged business via JSW Energy shares (10 JSW Energy shares for every 139 GEPIL shares, adding only ~48.4 lakh shares and diluting promoters from 66.53% to 66.36%). JSW Energy's reasons are vertical integration and supply-chain de-risking: management said repeatedly that boiler-turbine-generator (BTG) supply had become 'a big constraint for the industry' after roughly 18 months of heavy thermal bidding (11.6 GW of state thermal bids in H1 FY26, 12.8 GW in 9M FY26 against a 97 GW national addition plan to 2032–34), and that the prime reason was to guarantee timely boiler supply for the 2x800 MW Salboni Phase 1 (₹16,000 crore, PPA fixed charge ₹3.65/unit, 48–54 month PPA clock) plus the second 1,600 MW at Salboni, the KSK Mahanadi 1,800 MW brownfield units and future 800 MW projects. Specifics cited: the Durgapur facility comes with established technology, engineering team and people, pressure parts made in-house with non-critical parts outsourced; nameplate capacity 'as is' of 1.1 GW (about 1.3 boilers of 800 MW a year), expandable with de-bottlenecking and minor investment to 2x800 MW i.e. 1.6 GW, to be benchmarked against the Toshiba JSW Chennai 2x800 MW turbine-generator line. Paired with raising the Toshiba JSW Power Systems JV stake to 10.7% from 2.4% and the 2x800 MW STG order placed with TJPS, management said this gives 'full control over our build-out' and thermal capacity at 'one of the lowest capital costs in the industry'. The Scheme also promises economies of scale, cost efficiencies, control over critical components of thermal assets, and increased production capacity for future thermal projects — the mirror image of JSW Energy's decision to pause its solar module plant, where supply-chain de-risking was no longer needed.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced publicly on the Q2 FY26 call (17 Oct 2025), where it was listed as one of three strategic developments — a Scheme of Arrangement with GE Power India to acquire its boiler manufacturing business — and management, pressed by Mohit Kumar and Atul Tiwari, framed it as BTG supply-chain security for Salboni and sized it at ~1.5 boilers of components a year (board approval was 18 Sept 2025, Appointed Date 1 July 2025). By the Q3 FY26 call (23 Jan 2026) it had become part of a two-pronged plan with the Toshiba JSW 2x800 MW STG order, with the Durgapur plant 'expected to be fully with us by June or July of '26' and boilers to be made there for captive requirement only. On the Q4 FY26 call (11 May 2026) it was restated as de-risking the thermal supply chain, 'expected to be consummated within the next two quarters', and by Q1 FY27 (22 July 2026) management said completion was due that quarter, raised its TJPS stake to 10.7%, revised the plant's nameplate to 1.1 GW going to 1.6 GW, and declared thermal growth 'fully de-risked'. Approvals then followed: BSE/NSE observation letters 1 Apr 2026, NCLT-convened shareholder and creditor meetings 20 July 2026, NCLT sanction 1 Oct 2026 and certified copy received 13 Oct 2026.

points.point: The separation is GEPIL demerging its boiler pressure parts business to JSW Energy; for JSW Energy the stated purpose is entry into boiler pressure parts manufacturing in line with its energy-portfolio expansion.
points.quote: the Demerger provides an opportunity for the Resulting Company to enter into boiler pressure parts manufacturing business in alignment with the long-term vision of expanding into energy portfolio and extending footprint in a highly competitive and fast growing business

points.point: The Scheme's core industrial logic for JSW Energy is vertical integration: owning a dedicated boiler pressure parts plant instead of depending on third-party BTG suppliers.
points.quote: the Demerger will also result in vertical integration by securing a dedicated manufacturing facility for boiler pressure parts and reducing dependency on third-party suppliers

points.point: Synergy claim: scale economies, cost efficiency and control over critical components across existing verticals and ongoing/upcoming thermal projects, plus capacity for future thermal build-out.
points.quote: Demerger will create significant operational synergies within existing business verticals and across ongoing and upcoming thermal power projects, leading to economies of scale, enhancing cost efficiencies, and improving control over critical component requirements of thermal power assets

points.point: GEPIL's side of the rationale: sharpen focus on services/strategic growth, streamline and cut costs in the retained business, ease local approvals, and unlock value for its shareholders who stay invested through JSW Energy shares.
points.quote: the Demerger is the most optimum manner in which the Demerged Business could be transferred to the Resulting Company as it aids in unlocking and creation of value of the Demerged Business for the shareholders of the Demerged Company and giving them the flexibility to stay invested in the growth journey of the Demerged Undertaking.

points.point: Consideration is paper, not cash: a share entitlement of 10 JSW Energy shares per 139 GEPIL shares, taking JSW Energy's share count from 1,83,34,82,736 to 1,83,83,19,245 and promoter holding from 66.53% to 66.36%.
points.quote: 10 (ten) fully paid up equity shares of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted for every 139 (one hundred and thirty nine) fully paid-up equity shares of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each held in the Demerged Company

points.point: First disclosure on a call, listed as one of three strategic developments of the quarter, justified by in-house technology and people for equipment manufacturing supporting the thermal expansion plan.
points.quote: Acquisition of GE Power India Ltd.'s Boiler Manufacturing Business: We have entered into a Scheme of Arrangement with GE Power India Ltd. to acquire its boiler manufacturing business. This acquisition significantly enhances our in-house capabilities with both technology and people which is very critical for equipment manufacturing and supports our thermal power expansion plan.

points.point: Sharad Mahendra named the specific problem: 18 months of heavy thermal bidding had created constraints on timely BTG supply against PPA timelines, and the prime purpose was securing boilers for Salboni; critical pressure parts to be made in-house, non-critical outsourced.
points.quote: And lastly, our strategy was to ensure the timely supplies of the boiler for our, especially the Salboni plant which we have PPA which we have signed.

points.point: Capacity sizing given to Atul Tiwari — roughly 1.5 boilers' worth of components per annum, with an 18-month build cycle, matched to the 2030 Salboni PPA commissioning deadline.
points.quote: So effectively, you can say once the plant is fully functional, it will give a material worth 1.5 boilers, you can say, per annum this will be giving.

points.point: Boilers for the 3.2 GW Salboni site will be made captively at Durgapur once the plant is in hand by June–July 2026, with capacity to be increased as required.
points.quote: So we will be making these boilers for our captive requirement in Durgapur only, which has a capacity of almost about 1.5 boilers of 800 -MW -- 1.5 boiler equivalent material to manufacture.

points.point: Paired with the Toshiba JSW 2x800 MW turbine-generator order, the GE boiler plant is presented as removing the industry's biggest execution bottleneck and as the precondition for bidding further thermal capacity.
points.quote: Because now we are secured from the material supply point of view, supply chain security with the acquisition of GE boiler plant and placing the Toshiba into -- with Toshiba JSW. So we are secured in terms of the suppliers of BTG, which has been a big constraint for the industry.

points.point: Restated as one of two deliberate supply-chain de-risking steps for thermal, with completion guided to within two quarters.
points.quote: As we have informed, in parallel, we have taken strategic steps to de-risk our thermal supply chain through the strengthening of the Toshiba -JSW joint venture for turbine generators, and the acquisition of GE Power's boiler business, with the latter transaction expected to be consummated within the next two quarters.

points.point: With the TJPS stake raised to 10.7% from 2.4% and the GE boiler deal due to close that quarter, management declared thermal growth fully de-risked with full control of the build-out and among the lowest capital costs in the industry.
points.quote: Combined with our ongoing acquisition of GE's boiler business, which we look to complete this quarter, we have now fully de -risked our thermal growth ambitions — giving us full control over our build -out, for both our current projects and future opportunities.

points.point: Revised plant economics disclosed: Durgapur's as-is nameplate is 1.1 GW (about 1.3 boilers of 800 MW a year), rising with de-bottlenecking and minor investment to 1.6 GW, benchmarked against TJPS Chennai's 2x800 MW line.
points.quote: That has a nameplate capacity as of now, as is where is basis is 1.1 GW, means if we say 800 MW boiler, it can make 1.3 boilers in a year.

points.point: Process milestones: BSE and NSE observation letters on 1 April 2026; shareholders approved on 20 July 2026 with 99.9999% of 1,65,22,85,927 votes polled in favour (1,143 against) and unsecured creditors 100% in favour on ₹1,938.13 crore of debt; NCLT sanctioned the Scheme on 1 October 2026.
points.quote: This is to inform you that the NCLT, has sanctioned the Scheme vide its order dated 1st October 2026 ("Sanction Order").

verdict.what_management_expects: For JSW Energy: vertical integration and fully de-risked BTG supply, full control of its 800 MW build-out, Durgapur capacity rising 1.1 GW to 1.6 GW, economies of scale, lower capital cost per MW on Salboni/KSK, ready-to-use assets with technology and people. For GE Power India: sharper focus on services, a streamlined lower-cost retained business, and value unlocked for its shareholders via JSW Energy shares.
verdict.gaps: No boiler-business revenue, EBITDA, purchase price, IRR or standalone financials on calls; no justification of the 10:139 ratio; no explanation why JSW Energy itself would separate anything.

verdict.segment_name: GE Power India boiler manufacturing business (boiler manufacturing unit, Durgapur, West Bengal) — referred to in the documents as the Demerged Undertaking / Demerged Business / boiler pressure parts business
verdict.measure_notes: No profit or revenue line exists for this business in the supplied pages. The only segment disclosure in these documents is the Group's two reportable Ind AS 108 segments — Thermal (Grey) and Renewables (Green) — reported as 'Segment revenue (Revenue from operations)' and 'Segment results (Profit/(loss) before tax and finance costs)', i.e. segment EBIT before finance costs; the boiler/pressure-parts business is not a reportable segment and is not shown within or separately from them. Entity-wise tables in the quarterly presentations give Revenue from Operations and EBITDA (including other income) for major entities only, and no GE Power India / boiler entity appears in them.

Annual Report 2026 — page 320 (FY2025 comparatives: Thermal and Renewables only; no boiler business)
Annual Report 2026 — page 117 (acquisition of GE Power's boiler manufacturing business described, 'currently underway'; no financials)

latest_quarter.source: Presentation Nov 2026 — page 34 (entity-wise revenue and EBITDA for Q2 FY27/H1 FY27 list no boiler or GE Power India entity)

verdict.not_found: All figures. Pages carry no revenue, operating profit/EBITDA, EBIT or PAT for the boiler/pressure-parts business — only a narrative that the GE Power India Durgapur boiler acquisition is underway (AR2026 p117).

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is HUL's Ice Cream business — the Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum brands — demerged into a new listed entity, Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL), under a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai (orders dated 30 October 2025 and 6 November 2025), effective 1 December 2025, with KWIL listing on 16 February 2026. The Scheme's stated benefit is the 'creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream business's distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential' — i.e. the structural argument is that ice cream does not fit HUL's FMCG operating model. The financial case management gave on the calls is size and dilution: Ice Cream is 'roughly 3-odd percentage of our business' and 'makes low single-digit margin', below the HUL average, so CFO Ritesh Tiwari guided that removing it adds 50–60bps to reported EBITDA margin on top of the 22–23% guidance (later restated by Niranjan Gupta as a 50bps benefit, giving an implied 22.5–23.5% band). FY26 also showed the category's volatility — Ice Cream 'declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition' in the September quarter — reinforcing the seasonality/operating-model argument. Mechanically it was a two-step process: demerger completed in the December quarter with Ice Cream reported as a discontinued business, then listing in Q4 FY26; shareholders received 1 KWIL share of Re.1 for every 1 HUL share (2,34,95,91,262 shares allotted on 1:1), with cost of acquisition apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL. The December quarter reported PAT of Rs. 6,603 crores (up 121%) included a 'one-time non-cash gain arising from Ice Cream demerger', and HUL flagged it would lose PLI benefits that had flowed through the P&L via Ice Cream. By May 2026 Priya Nair framed it as portfolio rotation — 'strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio' — while explicitly keeping Foods (Tea, Coffee, Horlicks/Boost, Kissan) 'outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction that we have done'.
verdict.evolution: In the Apr 2025 call (24 April 2025, FY25 results) it was already an in-flight action — 'progressing on track with regulatory requirements', completion expected by end of FY26 — the original announcement rationale sitting in earlier calls not included here. By the Oct 2025 call (23 October 2025) the plan was firmed and quantified: demerger in the December quarter with Ice Cream shown as a discontinued business, listing in Q4 FY26, ~3% of business at low single-digit margin, 50–60bps reported-margin accretion, plus the admission that Ice Cream had declined on extended monsoon and GST transition. In the Feb 2026 call (12 February 2026) it was done — demerger completed in December, KWIL listing announced for 16 February 2026, a one-time non-cash demerger gain in reported PAT, and the guided EBITDA band reset to an implied 22.5–23.5%. By the May 2026 call (30 April 2026) it was cited retrospectively as one of the portfolio actions improving HUL's growth mix, alongside Minimalist and OZiva.

points.point: The Scheme's stated rationale is a focused, separately listed ice cream company with management flexibility suited to the business's own operating model and market dynamics.
points.quote: Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential

points.point: Mechanics: 1:1 entitlement of Re.1 KWIL shares to HUL shareholders on the 5 December 2025 record date; 2,34,95,91,262 shares were allotted and cost of acquisition was apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL.
points.quote: for every 1 (one) equity share of face value of Re. 1/- fully paid up held in HUL, 1 (one) equity share of face value of Re. 1/- credited as fully paid up in KWIL

points.point: At FY25 results the demerger was already in motion, with regulatory work on track and completion targeted by end of FY26 — no fresh rationale was restated.
points.quote: The demerger of Ice cream business is progressing on track with regulatory requirements, and we expect it to be completed by the end of financial year 2026.

points.point: Ritesh Tiwari quantified the dilution being removed: Ice Cream is about 3% of HUL's business at low single-digit margin, running even below that in FY26 because of monsoon and investment.
points.quote: Ice Cream, as we had called out even earlier, it's roughly 3-odd percentage of our business. and the business makes low single-digit margin.

points.point: The margin benefit was sized at 50–60bps on reported EBITDA, explicitly because Ice Cream earns below the HUL average — on top of the unchanged 22–23% guidance.
points.quote: Coming to EBITDA margin, Ice Cream demerger is expected to result in an improvement of 50-60 bps to the reported margin as Ice Cream business operates at a margin lower than HUL average.

points.point: The category's volatility was on display in the quarter being separated, and the process was described as two-step: demerger/discontinued-business reporting in Q3, listing in Q4 FY26.
points.quote: Ice Cream business declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition. As you are aware, the Ice Cream demerger process is currently underway.

points.point: On completion, Priya Nair justified it by dedicated leadership and undivided focus letting KWIL chase India's growing ice cream opportunity; listing was set for 16 February 2026.
points.quote: With a dedicated management team and singular focus, we are confident that KWIL is well positioned to capitalise on the growing market opportunity in India and deliver sustained performance.

points.point: Niranjan Gupta confirmed the guidance arithmetic — the old 22–23% band plus a 50bps demerger benefit, i.e. an implied 22.5–23.5% — and reported a one-time non-cash demerger gain inside the Rs. 6,603 crores reported PAT.
points.quote: So, our guided range has been that 22% to 23%. We also outlined that the range, therefore, you will see a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points.

points.point: A year on, the demerger is presented as one of several portfolio-rotation moves lifting the quality and growth profile of what remains.
points.quote: Strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio.

points.point: Asked whether Unilever's global retreat from foods implies more separations, Priya Nair drew the boundary: HUL's Foods (Tea, Coffee, Horlicks/Boost, Kissan) is deliberately outside the transaction perimeter and remains a strategic priority.
points.quote: So therefore that, combined with the opportunities that exist in India in Foods, is the reason why Foods is outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction that we have done, and Foods continues to be a very important area and focus of strategy for HUL.

verdict.what_management_expects: For HUL: ~50–60bps uplift to reported EBITDA margin (22–23% guidance becoming an implied 22.5–23.5%), since Ice Cream, ~3% of turnover, earned low single-digit margins; a better growth mix; a one-time non-cash gain; loss of PLI income. For KWIL: dedicated management, singular focus and flexibility to capture India's growing ice cream opportunity.
verdict.gaps: Never explained: original announcement rationale (older transcripts omitted/scanned), KWIL standalone financials and capital structure, Unilever's global ice-cream separation, and whether any investor, lender or partner requested it.

verdict.segment_name: Ice Cream Business (reported as 'Discontinued Operations' in the FY2025-26 segment note; Demerged Undertaking demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited, KWIL)
verdict.measure_notes: Revenue = 'Segment Revenue from Discontinued Operations' (segment revenue; note states there are no intersegment transactions, so effectively external). Operating profit = 'Segment Results from Discontinued Operations', i.e. segment result = profit before other income, finance costs, exceptional items and tax (EBIT-type, not EBITDA). PAT = 'Profit/(Loss) for the year from Discontinued Operations'. FY2026 figures cover only part of the year (Kwality Wall's ceased to be a subsidiary / demerger effective 30th November, 2025), and FY2026 PAT of 4,407 is dominated by the one-off positive impact of the Ice Cream demerger accounted per the approved scheme, not by trading profit; FY2026 PBT before exceptional items from discontinued operations was (135). No separate Ice Cream disclosure exists for FY2024 — it sat inside the 'Foods & Refreshment' segment.

years.source: Annual Report 2024 — page 213 (ice cream reported only within 'Foods & Refreshment'; no separate figures)
Annual Report 2026 — page 229
Annual Report 2026 — page 229

verdict.not_found: No Ice Cream quarterly revenue/margin in any presentation (only 'demerger completed, KWIL listing underway'); no FY2024 ice-cream split; no EBITDA, assets or capex for the undertaking.

verdict.rationale: Gabriel is not divesting anything — the separation runs the other way: promoter holding company Asia Investments Private Limited (AIPL) is carving its "Automotive Undertaking" out of itself and vesting it in listed Gabriel India, after first absorbing fellow-subsidiary Anchemco India by amalgamation (Appointed Date 1: 1 April 2025; demerger Appointed Date 2: 1 April 2026), while AIPL retains its own Gabriel shareholding and ANAND's separate management-services wing. What moves across is Anchemco's business (brake fluids, radiator coolants, diesel exhaust fluid/AdBlue, PU and PVC adhesives; ~INR330 cr sales, ~12% EBITDA; Tata Motors, Daimler, Mahindra) plus AIPL's stakes in Dana Anand (25.1%; ~INR2,700 cr revenue, 16% EBITDA; axles and driveshafts), Henkel Anand (49%; ~INR900 cr, 26% EBITDA, ~60% return on equity; BIW and NVH) and Anand CY Myutec (76%; >INR200 cr, 12% EBITDA, 22% ROCE; brass/steel synchronizer rings and aluminium forging). The stated purpose is to convert Gabriel from a "mono-product suspension company" into a diversified, technology-driven mobility solutions provider, mitigate concentration risk (2-wheelers were ~63% of sales), and make Gabriel the group's growth engine toward ANAND's INR50,000 cr-by-2030 target — the group was ~INR20,000 cr, the four entities ~INR4,000 cr against Gabriel plus Inalfa at ~INR4,000 cr, so roughly 40% of group value lands in the listed company. It is paid in paper, not cash: 1,158 Gabriel shares of Re 1 for every 1,000 AIPL shares of Rs 10, at a little under 8x EV/EBITDA (KPMG and BDO as valuers, ICICI Securities fairness opinion, JM Financial as financial adviser), so Gabriel "scales up without any leverage or cash outlay," with ~40% EPS accretion claimed (INR7 per share on FY25 numbers) and higher return on equity; promoter holding goes to 63.5% and public to 36.5%. Management said the move answers "repeated queries of investors on product diversification, M&A," and Elara's Jay Kale called it "a long standing wish of investors." The operating logic is cross-selling: push Anchemco's under-penetrated products (where Gabriel admits little market share) through Gabriel's OEM strength and aftermarket network, and feed ACYM's aluminium forging into Gabriel's 2-wheeler and EV franchise (>70% share with EV players). The scheme filed with the NCLT adds the plumbing reasons: eliminate intra-group transactions and consequent "cash flow blockages," rationalize the corporate structure and reduce shareholding tiers, enhance ability to raise funds for future organic and inorganic growth, and position Gabriel as a preferred global OEM partner and a preferred vehicle for future foreign collaborations and US/European expansion.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced as a pillar before it was a plan: on the Aug 2024 and Oct 2024 calls management kept M&A as one of four strategy pillars and said it was in "advanced stages" on inorganic pursuits, delivering the MMAS asset purchase announced at the Jan 2025 call ("M&A is not an event... it's a journey"), and confirming in May 2025 that the next product addition "would be inorganic." The composite scheme was unveiled at a dedicated business update call on 1 Jul 2025 with the Chairperson present, sized at four entities and 10-12 months to approvals. Through Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 the story shifted from rationale to process — pro-forma numbers withheld pending approvals, stock-exchange NOC received, NCLT first-motion hearing in early January 2026, order end-January, restructuring costs flowing through other expenses, while in parallel the Inalfa JV was recast to 65:35 after PN3 rejection and new JVs (SK Enmove, Jinhap) were added. By the May 2026 call the scheme had shareholder and NCLT approval and became effective 22 May 2026 (now branded "Project Rise"), with consolidation promised from Q1 FY27 and management stating a "complete intention" to bring further group businesses into Gabriel — which it then did via the HL Mando Anand, HL Klemove and Faurecia seating transactions.

points.point: Before any scheme existed, management framed the group's partnership/inorganic route as the way to hit Gabriel's vision, with M&A one of four pillars alongside domestic dominance, exports and technology.
points.quote: Mumuksh, our approach towards the partnership piece remains where it is. We are looking at inorganic pursuits in order to achieve our vision.

points.point: After the MMAS (Motherson Marelli) asset purchase, Jaggi said consolidation would continue and more opportunities were already being evaluated — the bridge to the group-asset transfer.
points.quote: So, see, M&A is not an event, right? It's a journey.

points.point: Management committed to adding at least one more product in FY26 and specified the route would be inorganic, not organic product development.
points.quote: So, this -- adding new product would be inorganic.

points.point: Chairperson Anjali Singh announced the composite scheme as a corporate-structure realignment making Gabriel the group's growth vehicle and platform for long-term value creation, against the INR50,000 crore 2030 group target.
points.quote: This scheme of arrangement marks a meaningful step forward in realizing our group's strategic vision, realigning the corporate structure to unlock synergies and enhance our competitive edge.

points.point: The core investor-facing rationale: moving mature promoter-held JVs into the listed company answers shareholders' long-standing demands for diversification and M&A, and does it without debt.
points.quote: By consolidating mature ventures under Gabriel's umbrella, we enhance scale without incurring additional debt, addressing investors expectations around diversification and M&A.

points.point: Jaggi quantified the financial case — no leverage, no cash outlay, ~40% EPS accretion on current scale, and greater capacity to fund future organic and inorganic growth.
points.quote: This helps Gabriel scale up without any leverage or cash outlay, accretion of EPS has been already explained by the Chairperson. We are looking at a 40% on a current scale basis and the enhanced ability to raise the funds for future organic and inorganic growth.

points.point: Diversification is explicitly about de-risking single-product dependence and getting direct access to global partners (Dana, Henkel, CY Myutec) for co-developed technology.
points.quote: Through this scheme, we aim to enter new product segments to mitigate concentration risk for direct alliances with global partners to co-develop advanced technologies and leverage synergies through scale and shared resources.

points.point: Group CEO Goyal sized the transfer: group ~INR20,000 cr, the four entities ~INR4,000 cr, Gabriel plus Inalfa ~INR4,000 cr — about 40% of group value consolidated into the listed entity, with Dana at ~INR2,700 cr/16% EBITDA, Henkel ~INR900 cr/26% EBITDA, ACYM >INR200 cr/12%, Anchemco ~INR330 cr/12%.
points.quote: So that takes care of almost 40% value of the group actually, which is being consolidated at the Gabriel level.

points.point: The specific commercial synergy for Anchemco is distribution: its market share is low, and Gabriel's OEM relationships and aftermarket network are the lever to raise it.
points.quote: So we can use the OEM strength of Gabriel, we can use the aftermarket network, which is very, very relevant for business of Anchemco.

points.point: Investors treated the restructuring as overdue — Elara's Jay Kale opened by congratulating management for acting on what he called a long-standing investor wish; Anjali Singh called it a first step, not the end.
points.quote: Yes, good morning and thanks for taking my questions and congratulations team for taking this step, which has been a long standing wish of investors.

points.point: The NCLT-sanctioned scheme spells out the product-concentration rationale: consolidating the Demerged Undertaking (drivetrain/EV transmissions, BIW and NVH, synchronizer rings, aluminium forgings, brake fluids, coolants, DEF, PU/PVC adhesives) transforms Gabriel out of mono-product dependence and into new segments, geographies, aftermarket and railways ranges.
points.quote: thereby transforming the Third Applicant Company from a mono-product suspension company into a diversified, technology driven mobility solutions provider, and reducing the dependency on a single product line by expansion into new segments, geographies, the aftermarket product range and railways product range

points.point: The scheme also gives structural/treasury reasons absent from the calls: killing intra-group transactions that trap cash, collapsing shareholding tiers, EPS accretion, and cost savings from not administering separate entities; AIPL's investment in Gabriel itself is explicitly excluded from what transfers.
points.quote: Eliminate intra-group transactions and consequent cash flow blockages which shall result in streamlined cash flow management and efficient utilization of capital;

points.point: Consideration is pure paper at a defined swap ratio, discharged by issuing Gabriel shares to AIPL's shareholders; 3,35,86,081 equity shares (plus 2 for fractional entitlement) were allotted on 9 June 2026 against the 29 May 2026 record date.
points.quote: "1158 fully paid equity shares of Rs. 1 each of Resulting Company, for every 1000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each held in the Demerged Company"

points.point: Asked whether the four entities' management fees and royalties would also shift to Gabriel, Goyal drew the line: Gabriel takes the manufacturing businesses, ANAND keeps the services arm — i.e. the separation is of operating assets, not of group service income.
points.quote: Gabriel is a manufacturing company. Gabriel is a business company, so nothing is changing for the Gabriel. And ANAND has a separate wing for providing services.

points.point: Management reiterated the strategic frame while declining to share H1 numbers for the four entities pending regulatory approvals, saying they continue to outperform the market.
points.quote: I think initially earlier also, we made a statement and we continue to maintain the same statement that Gabriel is a growth future for the ANAND Group, and that strategy continue basically.

points.point: CFO Srivastava tracked approvals — exchange NOC obtained, NCLT first-motion hearing in early January 2026, order issued by end-January, on original timeline; restructuring costs were being booked in other expenses against milestones.
points.quote: So on the scheme of arrangement, we received the NOC from stock exchange and post that, we filed our application to NCLT.

points.point: Jaggi confirmed completion: shareholder and NCLT approvals obtained and the scheme effective 22 May 2026, with residual formalities to close by mid/late June and consolidated reporting ("Project Rise") from Q1 FY27.
points.quote: So, I would like to update you all that the composite scheme involving the amalgamation of Anchemco India Private Limited into Asia Investment Private Limited followed by the demerger of automotive undertaking into Gabriel India has now received key shareholder and NCLT approvals.

points.point: Goyal confirmed the scheme is only stage one — all remaining group businesses are intended to come into Gabriel, and JV partners are not an obstacle; the HL Mando Anand (28.99%), HL Klemove and Faurecia seating deals followed.
points.quote: And as far as with respect to bringing other businesses into the Gabriel fold, as I said in the past, there is a complete intention to bring all those businesses into the Gabriel brand and again, I can't commit any timeline because it's too early to comment on any transaction.

verdict.what_management_expects: Gabriel: diversified multi-product portfolio, more balanced PV/CV mix, ~40% EPS accretion (INR7/share on FY25), higher ROE, improved margins, scale without debt or cash outlay, better fundraising ability, cross-selling via its OEM and aftermarket networks. AIPL: fewer shareholding tiers, simpler structure, no intra-group cash-flow blockages. Partner JVs continue unchanged; ANAND keeps its separate services wing.
verdict.gaps: No lender involvement, tax treatment, or why minority stakes (25.1% Dana, 49% Henkel) can't rise; no per-entity quarterly financials until Q1 FY27; valuation multiple's basis unexplained.

verdict.segment_name: Automotive Undertaking of Asia Investments Private Limited (AIPL) — the "Demerged Undertaking" under the Composite Scheme of Arrangement (Anchemco India Private Limited business + investments in Dana Anand India Private Limited, Henkel ANAND India Private Limited and ANAND CY Myutec Automotive Private Limited)
verdict.unit: ₹ crore (constituent-entity annual tables); ₹ million (constituent-entity quarterly/half-year data)
