verdict.rationale: There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the only stated reasoning is in the Regulation 30 filings, where management frames the separation as an internal group restructuring that splits the AI/technology business from the VFX/post-production services business. The entity being separated is Prime Focus Technologies Limited — renamed Brahma AI Services India Limited — together with the Metaphysic assets (Metaphysic Limited renamed Brahma AI Services UK Limited, DAX Cloud ULC renamed Brahma AI Canada Inc., DNEG Creative Private Limited renamed Brahma AI India Technologies Private Limited); the stated purpose of the March 30, 2026 steps is "internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under the Company's vertical 'Brahma'", which the company says "is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams", and the April 1, 2026 steps are to "streamline the business operations". Mechanically the separation runs both ways: pure software/IP moves up into Brahma (proprietary software assigned from Brahma India to Brahma AI ME Ltd for INR 75.2 Crores, and from Prime Focus Technologies Inc. for USD 3.44 Million), while the people-and-services tails move back into DNEG — the TCS business and Restoration business sold as a going concern by slump sale to DNEG India Media Services Limited for INR 26.5 Crores (FY25 turnover INR 102.62 Crores, 2.85% of consolidated turnover; net worth INR 23.86 Crores, 2.38%), and all of Prime Focus Technologies Inc. (the US services arm, revenue sliding from USD 13,459,863 in FY23 to USD 10,589,160 in FY25) sold by Brahma India to DNEG S.a.r.l. for about USD 21 Million. The holding structure is then re-pointed: DNEG S.a.r.l. sells 100% of Brahma India (its own 92.23% plus the residual 7.77% from other holders) to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey, for USD 90.09 Million, so the AI business sits under a separate Jersey holdco that is 90.20% held by Double Negative Holdings Limited — i.e. roughly 9.8% outside equity already sits at the Brahma level, which is the only structural hint at third-party participation. Management stresses this is not a divestment and not a court scheme: "the sale is outside the scheme of arrangement. Regulation 37A is not applicable", and "PFT US and Brahma India will continue to be part of the group and will continue to be step-down subsidiaries of the Company". It is also explicitly cashless at the parent: the conversion of Brahma India's inter-company loan and optionally convertible redeemable preference shares in PFT US into equity "does not involve any fresh infusion of capital by the Company or Brahma India". By the time shareholders ratified both transfers as material related-party transactions at the September 30, 2026 AGM, the same notice also carried an increase in authorised capital from 85 Crore to 100 Crore shares and an enabling resolution to raise up to Rs 3,000 Crore via QIP/ADR-GDR/preferential/rights issue — the clearest signal of what the cleaned-up structure is meant to be used for. No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having asked for the separation.
verdict.evolution: The groundwork predates the Brahma language: in the June 2024 quarter Prime Focus Limited sold its entire shareholding in Prime Focus Technologies to step-down subsidiary DNEG S.a.r.l. for Rs 69,302.55 Lakhs, booking an exceptional gain of Rs 21,621.18 Lakhs (shareholder approval June 6, 2024), and on February 14, 2025 the group acquired Metaphysic Inc. for USD 130 Million settled in subsidiary shares (goodwill Rs 96,942.67 Lakhs, later topped up by Rs 6,399.09 Lakhs), while FY25 also carried Rs 38,017.71 Lakhs of exceptional impairments including Rs 17,574.77 Lakhs of decommissioned intangibles. The July 3, 2025 preferential issue of 46,26,69,444 shares at Rs 120 (Rs 5,55,203.33 Lakhs, mostly a 2,561-for-100 swap of DNEG shares, allotted September 17 and 23, 2025) pulled DNEG up into the listed entity and cut non-controlling interest from Rs 1,28,432.26 Lakhs to Rs 45,713.96 Lakhs — a precondition for cleanly re-sorting the subsidiaries. The split itself then arrives in two board/audit-committee steps: March 30, 2026 (software assignments to Brahma AI ME Ltd plus the TCS and Restoration slump sale to DNEG India) and April 1, 2026 (PFT US to DNEG S.a.r.l.; Brahma India to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey), with the Prime Focus Technologies → Brahma AI Services India renaming confirmed in the May 28, 2026 results. Approval was completed at the September 30, 2026 AGM (resolutions 4 and 5), alongside the capital increase, the Rs 3,000 Crore fund-raise enabling resolution, and Namit Malhotra's move from Non-Executive Director to Whole-time Director effective August 7, 2026.

points.point: Filing of March 30, 2026: the stated reason for assigning proprietary software out of Brahma India and PFT USA into Brahma AI ME Ltd (INR 75.2 Crores and USD 3.44 Million respectively) is consolidation of the AI/technology business under the 'Brahma' vertical, justified on brand value and new revenue streams.
points.quote: The said software assignment forms a part of internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under the Company's vertical "Brahma". This is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams.

points.point: Same filing: the TCS business and Restoration business are sold as a going concern by slump sale from Brahma India to DNEG India Media Services Limited for INR 26.5 Crores, on the identical Brahma-consolidation rationale — i.e. services work is deliberately moved out of the AI entity and into the VFX entity.
points.quote: The said slump sale by Brahma India to DNEG India forms a part of internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under vertical "Brahma". This is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams.

points.point: The March 30, 2026 filing draws the dividing line between the two businesses explicitly: Brahma India is the cloud software platform, DNEG India is the post-production services operation.
points.quote: Brahma India: Provides a cloud-based technology platform for content, workflow, supply chain, and production management for the media and entertainment industry.

points.point: Filing of April 1, 2026: the two share transfers — 100% of PFT US from Brahma India to DNEG S.a.r.l. (about USD 21 Million) and 100% of Brahma India from DNEG S.a.r.l. to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey (USD 90.09 Million) — are presented only as streamlining of operations, with no financial target attached.
points.quote: the following mentioned subsidiaries of Prime Focus Limited (the "Company" or "PFL") have proposed to undertake certain steps for internal restructuring within the group to streamline the business operations

points.point: Management is emphatic that nothing leaves the group and that this is not a demerger or court-sanctioned scheme requiring Regulation 37A compliance.
points.quote: Upon completion of the aforementioned transfers, PFT US and Brahma India will continue to be part of the group and will continue to be step‑down subsidiaries of the Company.

points.point: The restructuring is funded by converting existing intra-group exposure, not new money: Brahma India's inter-company loan and optionally convertible redeemable preference shares in PFT US convert to equity before PFT US is handed to DNEG.
points.quote: It is important to note that the issuance of additional equity shares does not involve any fresh infusion of capital by the Company or Brahma India.

points.point: AGM of September 30, 2026 (Annexure A): the separated AI entity is sized for shareholders — Brahma India FY2025-26 consolidated turnover INR 328.72 Crores (7.03% of group) and net worth INR 278.63 Crores (10.95% of group), versus PFT US turnover INR 99.74 Crores (2.13%) and net worth of just INR 1.04 Crores (0.04%).
points.quote: Consolidated Turnover of Brahma India for FY 2025 -26: INR 328.72 Crores

points.point: The same AGM that ratified both transfers as material related-party transactions also raised authorised capital from 85 Crore to 100 Crore shares and approved an enabling resolution for up to Rs 3,000 Crore of fresh capital, linking the clean-up to a funding event rather than to any disposal.
points.quote: To consider, evaluate and approve the proposal to raise funds of an amount not exceeding Rs.3,000 Crore (Rupees Three Thousand Crore Only) or its equivalent in any other currency through one or more permissible mechanism as may be deemed appropriate by the Board of Directors of the Company ("Board"), by way of issuance of equity shares and/ or debt securities or non -convertible securities and/or other securities including share warrants and/ or any other equity linked securities.

points.point: Audited results of May 28, 2026 undercut any claim that the two businesses are already reported separately — despite the Brahma/DNEG split the group still reports a single operating segment and still describes itself as one integrated setup.
points.quote: The Group is mainly engaged in operating as integrated post-production setup.

points.point: Context for the timing: the FY26 results carry an emphasis of matter on the admitted-then-stayed Section 7 insolvency petition by Raspalfa (formerly Reliance Alpha) for Rs 35,379.75 Lakhs, with the full amount deposited with the Registrar, NCLAT; the underlying Bombay High Court suit was recorded as settled and withdrawn on August 4, 2026, and the group refinanced USD 500 Million of foreign-subsidiary debt to June 2029.
points.quote: Subsequent to year end, the Group has refinanced its debt facilities of USD 500 Mn in its foreign subsidiary tills June 2029

verdict.what_management_expects: Only two stated effects: consolidating all AI/technology under the Brahma vertical to "leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams", and streamlined operations. Structurally, Brahma AI Holdings (Jersey, 90.20% held) gathers the platform and Metaphysic IP; DNEG takes back PFT US, TCS and Restoration services. No margin, capital-allocation or valuation claim is made anywhere in the filings.
verdict.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts on file. Filings give no margin, valuation or synergy numbers, no listing/demerger plan for Brahma, no segment financials, and name no investor, lender or partner as requesting it.

verdict.rationale: The materials supplied do not support a reconstruction of a separation rationale, and I will not supply one from memory. No earnings call passages were included — the "CALL PASSAGES" section is empty — so there is no management commentary, no cited numbers, and no statement of who asked for a separation. The one document provided is not a scheme rationale section either: it is a Viyash Scientific Limited (formerly SeQuent Scientific Limited) stock-exchange letter enclosing a Crisil Ratings press release dated January 16, 2026 withdrawing the ratings on Symed Labs Limited's bank facilities. Crucially, the corporate action it documents is the opposite of a separation: it is a two-step consolidation — Symed Labs amalgamated into Viyash Lifesciences Pvt Ltd (deemed effective for Symed on November 27, 2025), and then Viyash amalgamated into SeQuent Scientific Ltd (deemed effective for Viyash on December 16, 2025), under an NCLT Hyderabad Bench order dated November 18, 2025. The only stated reason for any action in the text is procedural: Crisil withdrew the ratings because Symed ceased to exist post-amalgamation, in accordance with its withdrawal policy. The text does describe the businesses now under one roof — SeQuent, incorporated 1985, an animal health pharmaceuticals company with seven manufacturing facilities globally, five R&D centres and presence in over 100 countries; Viyash, incorporated 2019, a mid-tier API and formulations player with nine Indian plants (~2,000 kilolitre) and one US formulation facility; and Symed, incorporated 1998, with ~50 APIs, four API plants and one R&D centre around Hyderabad, all USFDA-approved and catering exclusively to overseas markets — plus Carlyle's ~53% stake in SeQuent as of March 31, 2025 and its 74% (July 2021) to 100% (July 2024) buildup in Symed. None of that is offered as a reason to separate anything. To answer the actual question, I need the earnings call transcripts and the demerger scheme's rationale clauses.
verdict.evolution: No evolution can be traced: zero call passages were provided, so there are no call dates to sequence. The only dated sequence in the text is the consolidation itself — NCLT Hyderabad order November 18, 2025; Symed into Viyash deemed effective November 27, 2025; Viyash into SeQuent deemed effective December 16, 2025; Crisil rating withdrawal published January 16, 2026. Rating history shows Symed on Crisil A/Watch Developing from October 29, 2024 through October 20, 2025 (previously Crisil A/Stable on August 4, 2023), which is consistent with a pending merger, but no document here explains it.

points.point: The document is a Crisil rating withdrawal, and the stated trigger is a two-step amalgamation (consolidation), not a separation of any business.
points.quote: Crisil Ratings has withdrawn its ratings on the bank facilities of Symed Labs Ltd (Symed), following the amalgamation of Symed with Viyash Lifesciences Pvt Ltd (Viyash) and, subsequently, Viyash's amalgamation with Sequent Scientific Ltd (Sequent).

points.point: The scheme of arrangement referenced was sanctioned by NCLT Hyderabad on November 18, 2025, with effectiveness dates of November 27, 2025 (Symed into Viyash) and December 16, 2025 (Viyash into SeQuent).
points.quote: On November 27, 2025, the amalgamation of Symed with Viyash is deemed effective for Symed, and subsequently , on December 16, 2025, the amalgamation of Viyash with Sequent is deemed effective for Viyash-following the filing of the National Company Law Tribunal order dated November 18, 2025, Hyderabad Bench, sanctioning the scheme of arrangement , with the Registrar of Companies by Symed and Viyash respectively.

points.point: The only rationale articulated anywhere in the text is procedural and belongs to the rating agency, not management: Symed ceased to exist, so the ratings lapsed under policy.
points.quote: Consequent to the amalgamation, Symed has ceased to exist.

points.point: Crisil explicitly frames its action as policy-driven, with no commercial or strategic reasoning given.
points.quote: Crisil Ratings has applied its policy on withdrawal of ratings.

points.point: The businesses now combined are described: SeQuent is the animal health platform, while Viyash and Symed are human-health API/formulations assets — a possible later separation axis, but the text never proposes one.
points.quote: Incorporated in 1985, SeQuent is a leading animal health pharmaceuticals company with a global footprint, presence in formulations and API segments across multiple markets and customers .

points.point: Viyash is characterised as a mid-tier API and formulations player with nine Indian plants (~2,000 kilolitre capacity) and one US formulation facility, mostly USFDA-approved.
points.quote: It has nine manufacturing facilities in India with a combined capacity of ~2,000 kilolitre and one formulation facility in the US.

points.point: Symed's API business was export-only with four USFDA-approved plants and roughly 50 APIs around Hyderabad.
points.quote: All the plants are approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) and cater exclusively to the overseas markets.

points.point: Ownership context: Carlyle-backed Viyash went from 74% of Symed in July 2021 to 100% in July 2024 by buying out the founders; Carlyle held ~53% of SeQuent at March 31, 2025.
points.quote: Global private equity firm, Carlyle-backed pharmaceutical company, Viyash, took a majority stake (74%) in Symed in July 2021 and subsequently increased it to 100% in July 2024, post the acquisition of the balance stake held by Dr G Mohan Rao and Dr Parthasaradi Reddy, founders of Symed.

points.point: The only financials in the text are Symed's Crisil-adjusted standalone numbers — revenue Rs 785 crore (FY2025) vs Rs 709 crore (FY2024), PAT Rs 120 crore vs Rs 101 crore, PAT margin 15.4% vs 14.2%, adjusted debt/networth 0.03x vs 0.18x, interest coverage 36.66x vs 20.81x — none of them tied to any separation argument.
points.quote: PAT Margin % 15.4 14.2

verdict.what_management_expects: Not stated anywhere in the supplied texts. No management expectation for margins, capital allocation, valuation re-rating, focus, debt placement, or shareholder entitlement appears, because no earnings call passages were provided and the only filing text is a rating-withdrawal notice whose sole rationale is Crisil's own withdrawal policy.
verdict.gaps: Everything: no earnings call passages were supplied, no demerger rationale, no business being separated, no management commentary, numbers, investor/lender/partner requests, timelines, synergies, or valuation reasoning.

verdict.rationale: These documents describe no separation, spin-off or demerger — the corporate action is the exact opposite: the amalgamation of the listed subsidiary Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital Limited (AEHL) into its parent Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Limited (AHCL), with AEHL dissolved without winding up and its public holders becoming AHCL shareholders. The two businesses were artificially split by geography: AEHL, BSE-listed since 1995 and 72.67% owned by AHCL, held all Tamil Nadu operations (63 facilities, 250+ doctors, 6,19,800+ patients, 72,500+ surgeries; FY25 revenue ₹397.15 cr, EBITDA ₹123.59 cr, PAT ₹54.65 cr), while every new centre outside Tamil Nadu plus Africa sat in AHCL (288 Indian facilities across 14 states/5 UTs and 19 in Africa; FY26 revenue ₹2,080 cr, Ind-AS EBITDA ₹614 cr, PAT ₹168 cr) — Adil Agarwal repeatedly called it 'a clear demarcation.' Management said the merger solves running two listed companies: duplicate compliance cost (two separate statutory auditors, separate filings), GST tax leakage on cross-charges between the entities, duplicated regional/corporate resource loading, and slow decision-making — plus it delivers 'unified capital allocation' so AHCL's holdco cash can be deployed anywhere rather than AEHL having to fund Tamil Nadu capex from its own accruals and debt (₹85.77 cr secured, ₹44.64 cr unsecured at Dec 2025). The capital constraint was concrete: AHCL had to inject ₹70 cr into AEHL by preferential allotment of 1,32,827 shares at ₹5,270 each to pay for the Cathedral Road flagship, chosen over a loan because, in Adil's words, it avoided 'putting any more stress on the balance sheet at the AHCL level'; that lifted promoter holding in AEHL from 71.9% to 72.7%. The ask came from several directions: AHCL itself had promised in its January 31, 2025 IPO prospectus to explore the merger within three years of listing; analysts (Ankit Shah, Harshal Seth, Varun Hemant, Dishant Jain, Rachna Kukreja) pressed for a timeline on every call; and AEHL minority holders demanded the swap be reworked, arguing 15–17 AHCL shares per AEHL share was fairer than the 23:2 offered, that the fairness opinions came from the same bankers (Kotak, Motilal Oswal) the group had just paid on the IPO, and that AEHL had been kept Tamil Nadu-only and never allowed a rights issue or QIP. Terms held firm: PwC and Bansi S. Mehta jointly valued AEHL at ₹4,942–₹5,262 and AHCL at ₹429–₹456 per share (DCF 50%, market price 25%, comparable-company 25%), giving 23 AHCL shares per 2 AEHL shares — a 15% premium to AEHL's 10-day VWAP of ₹4,554 — leaving AEHL public holders 4.6% of the merged entity, AHCL public holding diluted 67.6%→64.5% and promoters ~30.9%, with post-merger net worth of ₹2,225.44 cr versus ₹1,973.87 cr standalone. It cleared every gate: exchange NOCs (NSE Feb 16, BSE Feb 17, 2026), NCLT application March 4, 2026, shareholder approval July 2, 2026 with 99.97% of votes and 99.96% of public votes in favour, NCLT Chennai sanction September 30, 2026, Appointed Date April 1, 2026 and Effective Date November 1, 2026, record date November 18, 2026, authorised capital raised ₹90 cr to ₹110 cr, at a one-time cost of ~₹80 lakhs.
verdict.evolution: It surfaced as an IPO-era promise: on the maiden call (Feb 17, 2025) Adil said bankers had not yet been engaged but pledged a fair valuation and share swap within three years, 'ideally sooner,' while Ankit Shah asked how much dilution to expect. By May 29, 2025 the group was 'speaking to the bankers right now to decide on which bank,' and on Aug 12, 2025 it was 'under consideration… evaluating this further along with advisors,' with the outer limit cut to 1–1.5 years. The dedicated merger call of Aug 28, 2025 fixed the terms (23:2 swap, ₹70 cr preferential allotment, 12–14 month timeline) and drew sustained minority protest that management logged but did not act on; the Nov 2025 call did not mention the merger at all. Thereafter it became pure process reporting — exchange NOC filing (Feb 4, 2026), NCLT first-motion order and July 2, 2026 meetings with completion guided to Q3 (May 21, 2026) — ending in NCLT sanction (Sept 30, 2026) and effectiveness from Nov 1, 2026.

points.point: On AHCL's first call as a listed company, management said no bankers had yet been engaged on the merger but committed to a fair valuation and share swap within three years, framing it as a duty to AEHL's minorities.
points.quote: So from management perspective, it is our fiduciary responsibility to take care of our minority shareholders in the listed subsidiary, which is why when we get down to this process, we will do a fair valuation of both the entities and based on that fair valuation, we will do a share swap of both the entities.

points.point: Adil spelled out the artificial split the merger removes — AEHL holds the Tamil Nadu network and AHCL everything else including Africa — and confirmed banker selection was underway.
points.quote: Outside of the state of Tamil Nadu, which is Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Punjab, all that happens in the holdco which is Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Limited, including Africa.

points.point: Management flagged that AEHL was carrying the group's largest single capex — the Cathedral Road flagship — on its own books, ₹70–80 crore over and above the ₹310 crore group capex, with AEHL's own revenue only ~₹120 crore.
points.quote: Out of the INR 310, INR 60 crores will be for growth capex, plus newer greenfields. The additional INR 70 crores will be over and above this INR 310 crores, which will be spending for the flagship facility.

points.point: The merger was tied explicitly to the DRHP disclosure, with the timeline tightened from the three-year outer limit to 1–1.5 years.
points.quote: So right now, as we had disclosed in the DRHP Varun, the merger of the listed sub with the hold-co is under consideration. Management is now evaluating this further along with advisors. We continue with the endeavor to complete the merger in outer limit of the next 3 years, but we believe in the next 1-1.5 years, we should be able to get this one.

points.point: On the dedicated merger call Adil gave the full rationale — operational and financial efficiencies, unified capital allocation, a stronger balance sheet and a simplified legal and governance framework — calling it a 'long-awaited' simplification.
points.quote: It will enable unified capital allocation, strengthen the balance sheet to support future growth, and provide a simplified legal, regulatory, and governance framework.

points.point: Asked by Binay Singh (Morgan Stanley) to name the duplicated costs, CFO Yashwanth Venkat listed two separate statutory auditors, GST leakage on inter-entity cross-charges, resource optimisation and filing costs.
points.quote: See, in terms of cost synergies, Binay, the main thing is on the compliance costs. One, currently since we have two companies, in terms of the auditors, we have to have two separate auditors for both the companies.

points.point: The ₹70 crore preferential allotment of 1,32,827 AEHL shares at ₹5,270 each was structured as equity rather than an intercompany loan specifically to avoid loading AHCL's balance sheet, deploying holdco cash reserves instead.
points.quote: We believe that instead of us putting any more stress on the balance sheet at the AHCL level, we feel that this will be a better route for us to do a preferential allotment.

points.point: AEHL minority holders, several of 18–30 years' standing, attacked the 23:2 ratio as unfair on revenue, EBITDA, PAT and net worth, with one (Ankur Shah, Quasar Capital) alleging conflict of interest because the fairness-opinion bankers had just been paid on AHCL's IPO.
points.quote: The thing is that it is completely unfair since I am also in the market since last 30 years. I don't know on what metrics, because we can see topline, EBITDA, PAT, growth, net worth, debt, equity on all parameters, it looks completely unfair.

points.point: Siddharth Chandrasekhar pressed on why AEHL had been confined to Tamil Nadu and never allowed to raise equity, arguing AHCL's faster growth was funded by VC and IPO money AEHL was denied; management replied only that the merger now lets AEHL holders participate.
points.quote: Yes, my question is like why we haven't raised any funds in subsidiary, right?

points.point: Management defended the ratio by pointing to the 15% premium over AEHL's ₹4,554 ten-day VWAP, and listed what AEHL holders gain: pan-India growth, a larger clinical talent pool, a larger cash pool and a bigger market-cap company.
points.quote: The swap ratio implies a 15% premium for AEHL over AEHL's 10-day VWAP of INR 4,554 per share.

points.point: The merger became process reporting: NOC filed with the exchanges, NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings expected two to three months later, with COO Rahul Agarwal guiding completion to Q3–Q4 of 2027.
points.quote: So, quickly on the merger update, right now, we have filed for a no-objection certificate from the stock exchanges.

points.point: CFO confirmed exchange observation letters with no adverse objections in Feb 2026 and the NCLT first-motion order convening shareholder and creditor meetings on July 2, 2026; IR guided completion in five to six months. One-time merger expenses of ~₹80 lakhs hit Q4 other expenses.
points.quote: In May 2026, the Honorable NCLT Chennai bench allowed the joint first motion application and directed the convening of meetings of equity shareholders, secured and unsecured creditors of both companies on July 2, 2026.

points.point: The scheme explanatory statement states the consolidation rationale in four heads — operational/financial efficiencies, integrated capital allocation, simplified legal and governance framework, and EPS accretion from year one.
points.quote: The merger will consolidate the businesses of AHCL and AEHL into a single entity, enabling operational and financial efficiencies through streamlined functions and agile decision-making.

points.point: Valuers PwC and Bansi S. Mehta weighted DCF 50%, market price 25% and comparable-company multiples 25%, valuing AEHL at ₹4,942/₹5,262 and AHCL at ₹429/₹456 per share, on projected FY25–FY30 revenue CAGRs of ~22% (AHCL) and ~20.6% (AEHL) versus an industry 12–14%.
points.quote: 23 (Twenty-Three) fully paid-up Equity Shares of face value of ₹1 each of Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Limited for every 2 (Two) fully paid-up Equity Shares of face value of ₹10 each held in Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital Limited

points.point: Shareholders approved overwhelmingly despite the call-time protest: 95.91% of capital voted, 99.97% in favour overall and 99.96% of public votes in favour (81,138 shares against). NCLT sanctioned on Sept 30, 2026; effective Nov 1, 2026 with April 1, 2026 appointed date and Nov 18, 2026 record date.
points.quote: Accordingly, the Scheme shall become effective and operative from November 01, 2026 (Effective Date), with the Appointed Date being April 01, 2026.

verdict.what_management_expects: For the single surviving entity (AEHL dissolves): EPS accretion from year one; net worth ₹1,973.87 cr to ₹2,225.44 cr; unified capital allocation letting holdco cash fund Tamil Nadu and pan-India expansion alike; lower compliance costs (one auditor, no GST cross-charge leakage, fewer filings); faster, single-board decision-making. AEHL holders gain pan-India growth, larger talent and cash pools, bigger market cap; AHCL promoters dilute ~1.48%.
verdict.gaps: No separation is explained because none exists — this is a merger. Management never justified the 23:2 ratio on revenue, EBITDA or PAT, never quantified the synergies, and never held the promised separate AEHL-minority valuation call.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not contain any explanation by AIIL management of a separation, demerger or spin-off of one of AIIL's own businesses — there are no earnings-call transcripts on file ('no transcripts on file') and none of the nine filings is a scheme of arrangement for AIIL, so no management rationale, no investor/lender/partner demand and no financial targets for such a separation can be reconstructed from them. The only business separation described anywhere in the material is the splitting of a third party, Wind World (India) Limited (WWIL), between the two members of the consortium that acquired it under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016: the filing of July 28, 2026 states that Inox Neo Energies Limited (INEL, the Lead Member) and/or its affiliates would take (i) the IPP and power sale undertaking and (ii) the operations and maintenance (O&M) business of WWIL, while AIIL and/or its affiliates would take 'certain identified real estate / assets'. AIIL's financial commitment for that identified-asset leg was approximately INR 350 crore, which the October 10, 2026 filing confirms was fully remitted to WWIL (net of TDS filed on WWIL's behalf). That filing also records that the scheme of arrangement forming part of the Resolution Plan was NOT approved by the NCLT in its order of July 27, 2026, so the Consortium used the flexibility in the Resolution Plan to adopt a 'Revised Structure' cleared by the implementation and monitoring committee on August 31, 2026; the debt/equity infusion option that was to go into WWIL was redirected to Vibhav Energy Private Limited (VEPL), an implementation entity of the Lead Member and a subsidiary of Inox Green Energy Services Limited, via a INR 100 crore inter-corporate deposit dated September 28, 2026 that converted on October 9, 2026 into 10,00,00,000 shares, or 25% of VEPL on a fully diluted basis. The stated reason AIIL gives for that 25% stake is only that 'the target entity has strong potential for value creation, and it also aligns with our objective of portfolio diversification' — VEPL had nil turnover in FY2023-24, FY2024-25 and FY2025-26 and negative net worth of INR (0.1) crore at March 31, 2026. The remaining filings concern unrelated capital actions rather than any separation: a 4:1 bonus issue (67,93,80,400 shares, out of Rs. 8,880.02 crore of free reserves/premium at September 30, 2025) approved by the board on November 28, 2025 and by shareholders on December 31, 2025; a Rs. 2,450 crore 0.01% NCRPS private placement to promoter Mentor Capital Limited redeemable at a 6.5% IRR over 15 years, approved November 17, 2025; an ESOP Scheme 2025 of 5,00,000 options including for subsidiary employees; a further Rs. 101.625 crore rights-issue subscription in 88.37%-owned ISARC 'to meet its capital requirement for general business operations'; and the NCLT's July 7, 2026 rejection of AIIL's resolution plan for Vas Infrastructure Limited, with the company stating 'there is no impact on the business operations of the Company'. In short, on these documents alone the question's premise — that AIIL is separating one of its businesses — is not evidenced, and the only documented separation is of WWIL's businesses between AIIL and INEL, driven by the structure of a court-supervised insolvency acquisition rather than by any explained strategic or stakeholder pressure.
verdict.evolution: With no transcripts on file, the only traceable sequence is in the filings: the WWIL resolution plan dated February 13, 2026 (addendum May 20, 2026), intimated February 20, 2026, already envisaged splitting WWIL's IPP/power-sale undertaking and O&M business to INEL and identified real estate/assets to AIIL. The July 28, 2026 filing reported NCLT approval of that plan on July 27, 2026 and restated the INR 350 crore commitment. The October 10, 2026 filing then disclosed that the NCLT did not approve the scheme of arrangement inside the plan, forcing a Revised Structure approved on August 31, 2026, under which AIIL's optional infusion went into INEL's implementation entity VEPL as a INR 100 crore ICD converted to a 25% equity stake on October 9, 2026. verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is stated for AIIL itself. For the WWIL split, the documents only allocate assets — INEL's affiliates take the IPP/power-sale and O&M businesses; AIIL takes identified real estate/assets for ~INR 350 crore plus 25% of VEPL for INR 100 crore, justified solely as 'strong potential for value creation' and 'portfolio diversification'. verdict.rationale: The texts provided do not describe a separation, spin-off or demerger at all, and no earnings-call passages were supplied — the CALL PASSAGES section is empty, so nothing can be attributed to management commentary. What the filing text describes is the opposite transaction: a Scheme of Amalgamation in which Cigniti Technologies Limited (the Transferor Company, a digital assurance and engineering / software-testing business using AI-driven Continuous Testing and Test Automation, listed on BSE and NSE) is merged into Coforge Limited (the Transferee Company, an IT and IT-enabled services provider across financial services, insurance, travel, transportation and logistics, manufacturing and distribution, and government). The commercial backdrop given is that Coforge had already bought control before the scheme: by 27 December 2024 it held 54% of Cigniti's expanded share capital, having acquired 72,35,865 equity shares between October and December 2024 for approximately INR 10,239 million, and both boards approved the original scheme that same day, 27 December 2024. Consideration was set by a Joint Valuation Report of PwC Business Consulting Services LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP at a share exchange ratio of 1:5 (one INR 10 Coforge share for five INR 10 Cigniti shares), with fairness opinions from JM Financial Limited and Axis Capital Limited. That ratio was later restated to 1:1 by a Joint Clarification Note dated 13 June 2025 purely because Coforge split each INR 10 share into five INR 2 shares (board 04 March 2025, shareholders 17 April 2025, record date 04 June 2025); the filing stresses the revised ratio is "mathematically and economically equivalent" to the original and conveys no substantive change in value, with Axis (16 June 2025) and JM Financial (19 June 2025) reconfirming fairness, and both boards approving the amended scheme on 06 July 2025. Critically, the extract itself does not reproduce the rationale: it states the rationale "ha[s] been set out in detail in the First Motion Order dated 17 October 2025" and is only "briefly recapitulated herein", and the recapitulation that follows is procedural — incorporation history, registered-office shifts to Gurugram, share capital, exchange ratio, exchange and tribunal steps — with no stated synergy, margin, capital, focus or valuation reasoning. No investor, lender or partner is identified as having asked for the transaction; stakeholders simply voted in favour, and no objections were received from any shareholder or creditor.
verdict.evolution: No earnings calls were provided, so there is no call-by-call evolution and no call dates to cite. The only sequence available is from the filing: board approval of the original scheme plus the 1:5 valuation and fairness opinions on 27 December 2024, after Coforge's October–December 2024 purchase of 54% of Cigniti; the Coforge stock split (board 04 March 2025, shareholders 17 April 2025, record date 04 June 2025) prompting the 13 June 2025 restatement of the ratio to 1:1 and amended board approvals on 06 July 2025; then NSE and BSE observation letters on 17 and 18 July 2025, the First Motion Order of 17 October 2025, stakeholder meetings on 06 December 2025, Chairperson's Reports of 08 December 2025, the Second Motion petition filed 15 December 2025, and admission by the Tribunal on 09 January 2026. That is a change in transaction mechanics and process, not a change in a separation plan.

points.point: The transaction is an amalgamation of Cigniti Technologies into Coforge, not a separation of any business.
points.quote: In The Matter Of Scheme Of Amalgamation Between Cigniti Technologies Limited And Coforge Limited

points.quote: It is pertinent to note that as on 27 December 2024, the Transferee Company already held 54% of the expanded share capital of the Transferor Company, having acquired 72,35,865 equity shares between October and December 2024 for approximately INR 10,239 million.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is stated. The supplied texts contain no management expectations for margins, capital allocation, valuation or business focus, and no post-transaction operating or financial targets for either entity. The filing's substantive assertions are limited to consideration being fair (1:1 post-split, economically identical to 1:5) and procedural compliance; benefits are said to be detailed only in the First Motion Order, which is not included.

verdict.rationale: On the texts supplied there is no separation, demerger, spin-off or carve-out of any Happiest Minds business: the only corporate event is the opposite — Happiest Minds Technologies is being dissolved into ITC Infotech India Limited by merger by absorption, alongside a partial exit by its promoter, so the honest reading for a special-situation investor is a combination plus a de-promoterisation, not a separation. The Board approved on August 31, 2026 a Scheme of Amalgamation under Sections 230–232 whereby Happiest Minds (the Transferor) merges into ITC Infotech (the Transferee), Happiest Minds shareholders receive 25 ITC Infotech shares of ₹10 for every 81 Happiest Minds shares of ₹2, ITC Infotech's shares then list on BSE/NSE, and 'the Transferor Company shall be dissolved without being wound up'; in parallel Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP sell 22.106% of the company (3,36,61,700 shares) to ITC Infotech for ₹1,329.72 crore in two tranches at ₹390 and ₹400 (average ~₹395, against an assessed ₹405), leaving ITC Limited with ~73.4% and public holders ~26.6%, of which Soota keeps ~7.55% as the largest individual shareholder but explicitly 'will not be a promoter.' The separation that management did explain is therefore the promoter's separation from the company: Venkatraman said Soota had 'expressed his intention to pare down his stake in the Company to fund his legacy not-for-profit organizations, SKAN, and also to capitalize his healthcare venture Happiest Health,' and that 'the funding needs of these entities have since then grown substantially' — an escalation from the Aug 13, 2024 call, where Soota said the same purposes but promised not to go below 40% and expected no further sale 'in the next two to four years.' The business case given for the merger is scale and complementarity, not focus through separation: combined FY26 revenue of ₹7,033 crore (Happiest Minds ₹2,315 crore + ITC Infotech ₹4,718 crore), 19,000+ people, 800+ customers, 30+ countries, India's 11th largest listed IT services player, 9,000+ AI-trained professionals, and a geographic mix of ~38% Americas / ~31% Europe / ~31% rest of world versus Happiest Minds' 59% Americas and 8% Europe. Management said the explicit problem it solves is the stranded US$1 billion revenue ambition: Venkatraman admitted 'our goal of our possibility of reaching that goal looked difficult earlier, now but it is very well within sight,' with the target pulled from FY31 to FY28; Joseph framed the industry problem as AI-led spending, outcome focus and accelerating vendor consolidation requiring 'broader capabilities and greater execution scale,' with Happiest Minds strong in AI, digital, product engineering, cloud, data and cybersecurity and ITC Infotech in enterprise transformation, SAP, PLM, Industry 4.0 and industry solutions, almost no overlap in top customers, and a partner ecosystem (Microsoft, SAP, ServiceNow, PTC, Google, Amazon) where a ₹7,000-crore entity matters more. Valuation was set by PwC and Grant Thornton with an ICICI Securities fairness opinion at 15.1x FY26 EBITDA for Happiest Minds versus 13.6x for ITC Infotech — 'reflecting the relative premium that has been attributed to Happiest Minds' — implying ₹6,167 crore for Happiest Minds, ~₹11,920 crore for ITC Infotech and ₹18,087 crore combined. Nobody is recorded as demanding this: no investor, lender or partner asked for a separation; the only pressures visible in the calls are retail shareholder anger at the stock ('we are not happy indeed. So please do something... I request to improve your balance sheet,' Feb 10, 2026) and the promoter's own funding need, while lenders appear only mechanically — the outstanding NCDs are to be redeemed by September 26, 2026 so that 'no new NCDs will be issued pursuant to the Scheme,' and no open offer is triggered because the purchase stops at 22.1%, below the 25% threshold. The earlier, far smaller 'separation' threads in the calls were internal, not structural: a separate P&L planned for the Arttha banking product/SaaS business (May 13, 2025), a standalone Generative AI business unit with its own P&L, CEO and COO, and Happiest Health kept outside the listed company with an IPO Soota said 'could be easily 6 years away' — while the actual legal activity in the period ran toward consolidation, with PureSoftware and Aureustech amalgamated into Happiest Minds (NCLT orders received June 5 and August 18, 2026, appointed date April 1, 2026).
verdict.evolution: The idea first surfaced only as promoter liquidity: on the Aug 13, 2024 call Soota explained a bulk sale to fund SKAN and Happiest Health, capped himself at 40% and expected no further sale for two to four years; on May 13, 2025 and Jul 30, 2025 the $1bn-by-FY31 vision was openly questioned and management said it would 'restate where we stand on that goal,' while separation talk was limited to a separate P&L for Arttha and the standalone GenAI BU. On Feb 10, 2026 an investor put press reports of a Soota stake sale directly to him and he denied any change ('Make no mistake, I am here to completely see it through'), promising instead 'a new trajectory' and a 'secret weapon' (AI First, Agile Always) at Q4; on May 29, 2026 and Jul 28, 2026 management still guided standalone FY27 revenue growth of 12.5% with a 15% FY28 aspiration and said nothing about a transaction. The plan then changed completely on Aug 31, 2026, when the Board approved the Scheme of Amalgamation, the Merger Framework Agreement, the 22.106% promoter share purchase agreement at ₹390/₹400 and even a shift of the registered office from Karnataka to West Bengal, explained on the Sep 1, 2026 special-purpose call; by the Nov 2, 2026 Q2 FY27 release the merger was 'progressing well and remains on track,' with ₹398 lakh of merger costs booked as an exceptional item and the FY28 US$1 billion aspiration restated.

points.quote: We plan to create a separate P&L and invest in market-specific features and go-to-market strategies for India, while expanding internationally into Europe and North America through partnerships and enhanced digital banking capabilities.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation benefits were claimed; only combination ones. For the merged entity: US$1bn revenue by FY28 (from FY31), ₹7,033cr FY26 base, ~18.1% operating margin rising ~100bps via scale, SG&A leverage, utilisation and office consolidation, 11th-largest Indian IT rank, cross-sell across 800+ customers, 38/31/31 geographic balance. For HM shareholders: continued participation plus a premium 15.1x swap. For Soota: ₹1,330cr cash, ~7.55% non-promoter stake.
verdict.gaps: No separation rationale exists. Unexplained: who leads the combined entity, retention/incentives, client overlap detail, AI revenue share, why ITC Infotech, headcount duplication, ₹405-vs-₹395 gap.

verdict.rationale: The supplied record does not contain any statement of why JPPOWER is separating a business, because it contains no earnings call transcripts at all ("no transcripts on file") and no scheme of arrangement, demerger, slump sale or composite scheme document. The only two filings provided are distress/insolvency disclosures, neither of which mentions a separation, a resulting company, a share entitlement ratio, or any business being carved out. The 27th February 2026 filing discloses that National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited, as Trustee of NARCL Trust, acting through its power of attorney holder India Debt Resolution Company Limited, filed a Section 7 IBC application before the NCLT Allahabad Bench at Prayagraj against JPPOWER itself, alleging default of Rs. 511,72,82,207 plus interest and charges, arising from a corporate guarantee JPPOWER extended for Jaiprakash Associates Limited (under IBC); the same dispute was already before the Hon'ble DRT-III, Delhi (disclosed 27th October 2025). The 17th March 2026 filing discloses the NCLT Allahabad Bench's oral order under Section 31 IBC approving Adani Enterprises Limited's resolution plan dated 14th October 2025 (with email clarifications of 5th November 2025) for promoter Jaiprakash Associates Limited, under which JAL's securities will be delisted, shareholders receive NIL consideration because the liquidation value is insufficient to satisfy even secured creditors in full, and all pre-CIRP share capital, convertible instruments, warrants and rights will be entirely cancelled and extinguished for zero consideration on an Effective Date no later than 90 days from NCLT approval. These documents describe a change of control at the promoter level and a creditor-initiated insolvency threat at JPPOWER on a guarantee obligation — not a voluntary business separation. No management named any businesses to be separated (e.g. thermal power, hydro, cement grinding), cited no segment numbers, identified no investor, lender or partner who asked for it, and set out no problems a separation would solve. Any rationale would therefore have to be supplied from outside these texts, which the instructions forbid.
verdict.evolution: The idea does not surface anywhere in the provided record: there are zero earnings calls on file, so there is no call-by-call progression to trace. The only datable developments are the JAL insolvency track — resolution plan filed with NCLT per JAL's 27th November 2025 disclosure, NCLT approval of Adani Enterprises Limited's plan orally pronounced 17th March 2026 (JPPOWER's related disclosure chain beginning 3rd June 2024) — and the guarantee default track, moving from the DRT-III Delhi dispute disclosed 27th October 2025 to NARCL's Section 7 CIRP application against JPPOWER disclosed 27th February 2026. Neither track is presented as, or linked to, a separation of a business.
verdict.what_management_expects: Not stated. The record contains no management commentary on a separation and therefore no expectations for margins, capital structure, valuation re-rating, or business focus at any entity. The only forward-looking content is JAL's delisting, NIL exit price for its shareholders, and extinguishment of its pre-CIRP share capital within 90 days of NCLT approval.
verdict.gaps: Everything: no transcripts supplied, no scheme document, no businesses named, no segment financials, no demerger rationale, ratio, timeline, or requesting stakeholder.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not a listed division but an internal undertaking: under the Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Laurus Labs board on 21 August 2025, the 'Identified Business Undertaking' (Unit-1) of Laurus Synthesis Private Limited (LSPL) — a 100% subsidiary described in the filings as doing Contract Development and Manufacturing Operations (CDMO) for global pharma and biotech — is demerged into Sriam Labs Private Limited, another 100% subsidiary that manufactures Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, pharmaceutical intermediates and allied products, while the 'Remaining Undertaking' of LSPL is amalgamated into the listed parent, Laurus Labs Limited, with LSPL then dissolved without winding up from an Appointed Date of 01 April 2026. The stated reason for the demerger leg is that it 'enables consolidation of like businesses, greater integration, financial strength, and flexibility,' i.e. putting Unit-1's API/intermediate-type activity with Sriam's existing API/intermediate business; the amalgamation leg is justified as consolidation that will 'maximize overall shareholder value,' deliver 'economies in business operations,' 'optimal utilization of resources,' 'greater administrative efficiencies,' let the entities 'raise financial resources on better terms,' fund 'organic and inorganic growth opportunities,' and 'simplify the overall group structure.' The scale involved: LSPL is tiny on equity (paid-up ₹10,76,000 across 1,07,600 shares of ₹10) but carries real debt and payables — 3 secured creditors owed ₹290.43 crore and 76 unsecured creditors owed ₹764.92 crore as at 21.08.2025 (restated as 476 unsecured creditors owed ₹671.47 crore at 30.09.2025) — against Sriam's paid-up ₹14,20,33,630 (1,42,03,363 shares), nil secured creditors and 155 unsecured creditors owed ₹18.05 crore; the listed parent carries 7 secured creditors at ₹1,280.41 crore and 1,039 unsecured creditors at ₹1,830.41 crore. Consideration is shares only at the subsidiary level: Sriam issues 27 equity shares for every 1 equity share of LSPL, and every LSPL share held by Laurus Labs is cancelled with no shares issued by Laurus Labs, so, as the NCLT order records, the Scheme 'does not result in any dilution of its shareholding, including that of its public shareholders.' On who asked for it: no investor, lender or partner is shown asking — the secured creditors of LSPL (100% by value) filed consent affidavits, Laurus's own shareholder and creditor meetings were dispensed with precisely because no shares are issued, and the only stakeholder push visible in the calls was analysts asking about separate listings or divesting divisions, which management declined. Critically, across all seven earnings calls in the window management never once mentions the Scheme; the demerger exists only in the filings, and the quarterly results from Jan 2026, Jul 2026 and Oct 2026 are all 'presented without giving effect to the said merger' pending NCLT sanction.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaced on an earnings call: on 24 April 2025 an investor asked about 'creating value by divesting such businesses as and when they reach scale' and Dr. Chava answered only that the CDMO verticals 'need some time to get to a scale,' and on 25 July 2025 — four weeks before board approval — a direct question on listing divisions as separate entities drew 'We don't have any plans for that.' It appears instead in the filings: board approval on 21 August 2025 (disclosed 21 August and 5 September 2025), petition filed with NCLT Amaravati on 11/13 October 2025, first-motion order pronounced 24 February 2026 dispensing with shareholder and secured-creditor meetings and directing unsecured-creditor meetings for 6 April 2026, creditor approval obtained 6 April 2026, and a further NCLT order pronounced 24 July 2026 directing service of Form CAA-3 notices with the next hearing set for 10 September 2026. Through the 30 April 2026, 24 July 2026 and 29 October 2026 results the only change is procedural — the Appointed Date stays 01 April 2026 and the accounts continue to exclude the merger — while the same period shows separate, unrelated structural moves: a 49% KRKA Pharma JV funded with ₹49 crore in Dec 2025 and up to €9.8 million more approved 30 April 2026, further investment into Laurus Bio, and the voluntary closure of Laurus Generics GmbH.

points.point: Consideration moves only inside the group: Sriam issues 27 shares for every 1 LSPL share (LSPL paid-up is just ₹10,76,000 / 1,07,600 shares), and Laurus Labs issues nothing, cancelling its LSPL holding instead.

points.point: Because no shares are issued by the listed entity, its shareholders' and creditors' meetings were dispensed with and public shareholders are untouched — this is a restructuring, not a value-unlock event for listed holders.
points.quote: The proposed Scheme does not involve issuance or allotment of any shares by the Third Applicant Company, and therefore, does not result in any dilution of its shareholding, including that of its public shareholders.

points.point: An investor had earlier pushed for value creation by divesting businesses once they scale (cell therapy, hospital formulations, crop sciences); management redirected to the CDMO portfolio needing more time, naming animal health peaking around FY27 and crop sciences needing another year.
points.quote: Out of these, I would say we need some time to get to a scale.

points.point: The one separation-like step management did explain was the Eight Roads/Fidelity stake in Laurus Bio — framed as access and bandwidth, not monetisation, at a valuation implying roughly ₹850-860 crore for a business then running under ₹200 crore of revenue.
points.quote: The primary objective for us to bring Fidelity as a partner is to work closely with their portfolio companies across the globe.

verdict.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of Lloyds Enterprises Limited's (LEL) Real Estate Business Undertaking into a new, separately listed vehicle, Lloyds Realty Limited (LRL), carried out inside a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 read with Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013 that the Board approved on 22 December 2025; the same scheme first merges Lloyds Realty Developers Limited (LRDL, Transferor 1) and Indrajit Properties Private Limited (IPPL, Transferor 2) into LEL, so that all realty assets sit in one place before being carved out into LRL. The only rationale management itself states is in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): the merger-and-demerger scheme means 'our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders', set against a realty platform spread across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane with 'nearly 14 million square feet of upcoming projects under development' — i.e. a capital-hungry pipeline that needs its own currency and price discovery. For the parallel group merger the Chairman gives the generic benefits: 'enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders'. The filings show why real estate sat awkwardly inside LEL: for 9M FY26 the Real Estate segment did only ₹53.30 crore of revenue and ₹0.88 crore of segment result (down from ₹11.26 crore) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, while Steel (₹492.80 crore revenue, ₹255.60 crore result) and Engineering (₹795.75 crore, ₹151.08 crore) carried the group, and subsidiary LRDL itself ran a ₹1.26 crore net loss; consolidated FY26 total income was ~₹2,200 crore against ~₹800 crore standalone, with LEL otherwise functioning as a holding/trading company (stakes of ~4.13% in Lloyds Metals and Energy, ~31% in Geomysore, and material subsidiary Lloyds Engineering Works with a group order book of ~₹8,000 crore and 44% PBT growth). No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; the only parties on record demanding anything are the regulators — SEBI, NSE and BSE required LEL to disclose to shareholders the 'Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio', synergies, minority impact and a cost-benefit analysis, plus lender NOCs and 'Conditions imposed by lenders, if any'. The same unlock-by-listing logic recurs twice more in the group: LEWL's absorption of Lloyds Infra, Metalfab and Techno Industries to end 'silos' and create a ₹6,150 crore-order-book design-to-execution entity, and the SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore), where a DRHP within 30 months is meant to 'facilitate independent price discovery', market visibility and access to capital.
verdict.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the idea is traceable only through filings. It surfaces fully formed on 22 December 2025, when the Board approved the Composite Scheme (LRDL + IPPL into LEL, real-estate undertaking out into LRL) and filed it with BSE and NSE the same day; a week later (29 December 2025) the group announced the separate LEWL merger of LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries, and the 9 February 2026 results notes restated the Scheme verbatim alongside a ₹500 crore NCD approval, the ₹361 crore Tata Capital/Bajaj Finance/Jio Credit borrowings and the block-deal sale of LEWL shares to Thriveni Earthmovers. On 15–16 May 2026 LEL received NSE's 'No objection' and BSE's 'no adverse observations' (with LRL's listing left to exchange discretion, an Information Memorandum, frozen shares and a 60-day post-NCLT listing timetable), followed on 18–19 May 2026 by exchange NOCs and CCI clearance for the LEWL merger; by the 9 July 2026 AGM the Chairman described the scheme as approved, an NCLT application filed, and the realty business as one that 'will be listed'.

points.point: Board approval on 22 December 2025 of the Composite Scheme: LRDL and IPPL merge into LEL, and LEL's Real Estate Business Undertaking is demerged into Lloyds Realty Limited; filed with BSE and NSE the same day.
points.quote: The Scheme is filed with Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) & National Stock Exchange (NSE) on December 22, 2025.

points.point: The only explicit purpose management gives for the demerger, in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): a separate listing of the real estate business to unlock value, against a pipeline of nearly 14 million sq ft across MMR, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane.
points.quote: Importantly, as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders.

points.point: For the group merger leg, the Chairman offers only structural benefits, noting approvals from NSE, BSE and SEBI and an application filed with the NCLT.
points.quote: This strategic merger is expected to enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders.

points.point: NSE's 15 May 2026 observation letter confirms the demerger is a route to a new listed realty entity, but conditions it on an Information Memorandum, newspaper advertisement, frozen shares until trading permission, and listing within 60 days of the NCLT order.
points.quote: However, the listing of shares of Lloyds Realty Limited  is at the discretion of the Exchange.

points.point: The parties actually demanding an articulated rationale are the regulators: SEBI and both exchanges ordered LEL to put the need, rationale, swap ratio, synergies, minority impact and cost-benefit analysis in the shareholder explanatory statement.
points.quote: Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio, synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the minority shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme.

points.point: Lenders are referenced only as a consent/disclosure requirement imposed by SEBI — NOCs from lending banks, FIs and debenture trustees, plus any lender-imposed conditions — not as instigators of the separation.
points.quote: Conditions imposed by lenders, if any, may be disclosed to the public shareholders along with the impact of same on the scheme.

points.point: The mirror-image transaction at material subsidiary LEWL (announced 29 December 2025) consolidates LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries into one vertically integrated design-to-execution entity with a ~₹6,150 crore combined order book, ~38.1 crore new shares and equity rising from 147.42 to 185.52 crore shares, appointed date 1 April 2025.
points.quote: By bringing Lloyds Infra, Metalfab, and Techno Industries under one banner, we are eliminating silos.

points.point: The same unlock-by-separate-listing logic is applied to the June 2026 SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore; FY26 turnover ₹816.87 crore, net profit ₹43.42 crore), with a DRHP promised within 30 months of Stage 1.
points.quote: The proposed listing of SISCOL is expected to facilitate independent price discovery of its business, enhance its market visibility and access to capital, and unlock value for all its stakeholders, including the Company as a significant shareholder.

points.point: The filings' own numbers show the real-estate leg was the group's weakest earner before separation: 9M FY26 segment revenue of ₹53.30 crore and segment result of ₹0.88 crore (vs ₹11.26 crore a year earlier) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, with LRDL itself loss-making.
points.quote: We have not conducted a review of the Subsidiary (Lloyds Realty Developers Limited) included in the unaudited consolidated financial results. whose financial information reflects total revenues of <53.30 and total Net Loss after tax of t1.26. crores.

verdict.what_management_expects: For the realty entity: a separate listing of the ~14 mn sq ft Mumbai-region pipeline, 'unlocking its true potential' and greater shareholder value. For the retained LEL group: enhanced operational efficiencies, optimised resource utilisation, a stronger business structure and sustainable long-term value, leaving a holding/trading company around LEWL (~₹8,000 crore order book, 44% PBT growth), Lloyds Metals, Geomysore and SISCOL.
verdict.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts on file; no swap ratio, valuation, debt or asset split for LRL, no margin or capital targets, no timeline, no named investor or lender demand.

verdict.rationale: These texts describe no spin-off, demerger or separation of a business by Max Healthcare Institute Ltd. (MAXHEALTH) — the direction of travel across all eleven disclosures is the opposite: consolidation of subsidiaries into fewer entities, acquisitions (Jaypee Healthcare/Max Noida, Kalinga Hospital Bhubaneswar at ~INR 298 crore for 58.28% rising to 66.34%, Yerawada Properties Pvt. Ltd.) and brownfield/greenfield bed addition (~20% brownfield capacity commissioned in FY26, 500-bed Gurgaon Sector-56, 700-712 beds at Shaheed Path Lucknow for ~INR 1,400 crore). The only business genuinely separated out is small: the Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals, divested for INR 40 crore under a binding term sheet announced on the Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) call and completed in September 2025. Management's stated reason was strategic fit and sub-scale economics, not value unlocking: the two came in as part of the Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and 'had limited strategic alignment' with a strategy 'to focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies'; only Chitta was operational, at ~INR 5 crore revenue and an INR 1 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26, running 26% occupancy on 100 of 200 capacity beds, with no plan to spend on opening the balance 100 beds. On the Nov 2024 call Abhay Soi said of Anoopshahr/Bulandshahr that they were 'not meaningful enough', that no value had been attributed to them in the Jaypee price, and that the choice was between spending CSR time and money on them or wrapping them up. The second, larger strand is internal simplification rather than separation: merger of wholly-owned subsidiaries Alps Hospital Limited with Max Hospitals & Allied Services Limited, and of Crosslay Remedies Limited (CRL) with Jaypee Healthcare Limited (JHL), which management said would 'simplify the holding structure, improve governance and optimize cash flows' and 'reduce our outflow on the acquisition by INR 200-225 crore'; the CRL-JHL amalgamation (NCLT Chandigarh, appointed date October 5, 2024, effective December 15, 2025) produced a one-time tax gain of INR 149 crore in Q2 FY26 (~INR 142 crore net after a ~INR 7 crore Q4 FY26 reversal) against a INR 14 crore stamp-duty provision inside the INR 55 crore of Q3 FY26 exceptional items. Alongside this, step-down subsidiary ET Planners Private Limited was voluntarily liquidated with its entire undertaking transferred to Alps Hospital Limited on a going-concern basis (dissolved March 25, 2026), and MHC Global Healthcare (Nigeria) Ltd — nil revenue, negative net worth of INR 70.89 lakh, -0.0076% of consolidated net worth — was put into voluntary liquidation from January 29, 2026. No investor, lender or partner is recorded in these texts as asking for a separation; no scheme of arrangement for a demerger appears in the filings (the only MOA change put to shareholders, approved October 19, 2026, widens the objects clause to add medical colleges, pharmaceuticals/cyclotron radiopharmaceuticals and food & beverage services — an expansion of scope, not a carve-out). The one business repeatedly discussed as structurally separate — the Partner Healthcare Facility societies (Balaji, Devki Devi, GM Modi, Nirogi, Vikrant) — is being drawn closer, not separated: cash is moved between societies or upstreamed into MHIL via revised medical service fees (e.g. ~INR 25 crore a year at Balaji) because, as Yogesh Sareen explained, 'there is no dividend that can be declared for any society' and upstreaming costs ~25% tax.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 7, 2024 call, where Abhay Soi called the Bulandshahr/Anoopshahr units 'not meaningful enough', said no value was attributed to them in the INR 1,660 crore Jaypee enterprise value, and was weighing whether to keep them or 'wrap it up'; on the May 21, 2025 (Q4 FY25) call the same assets were disclosed as sub-scale (Chitta 26% occupancy, only 100 of 200 beds opened, no plan to open the rest) while a parallel 'simplify the holding structure' programme was announced — Alps/MHASL merger concluded and a CRL-JHL merger filed with NCLT to cut acquisition outflow by INR 200-225 crore. It hardened into a transaction on the Aug 14, 2025 (Q1 FY26) call with a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr for INR 40 crore, and was reported complete on the Nov 17, 2025 (Q2 FY26) call under the heading of streamlining the corporate structure, together with NCLT approval of the subsidiary merger and its INR 149 crore one-time benefit. Thereafter the thread is only tidying-up — stamp duty inside Q3 FY26's INR 55 crore exceptional items (Feb 6, 2026 call), liquidation of MHC Nigeria (Jan 29, 2026) and ET Planners (dissolved March 25, 2026) — and by the May 22, 2026 and later disclosures the narrative is entirely acquisition and capacity addition (Kalinga/Bhubaneswar, Pune, Lucknow Shaheed Path), with no separation plan of any kind.

points.point: First signal: asked whether the Bulandshahr/Anoopshahr units attached to the Jaypee deal mattered, Soi said no value had been ascribed to them and the company was deciding between supporting them or exiting.
points.quote: No, they're not meaningful enough. And we did not even attribute any value to it. We are trying to determine whether we should focus and spend CSR time and money on this or just wrap it up.

points.point: Simplification of the group structure — not separation — is framed as the corporate-action agenda, tied to governance (IiAS 'Next Leaders' recognition) and cash flows; Alps/MHASL merger done, CRL-JHL merger filed with NCLT.
points.quote: On that note, we would like to highlight that we continue to undertake corporate actions to simplify the holding structure, improve governance and optimize cash flows.

points.point: The cash rationale for the CRL-JHL merger is quantified: it reduces the cash outflow on the Jaypee acquisition by INR 200-225 crore.
points.quote: We have also filed an application with the NCLT for merger of Crosslay Remedies Limited and Jaypee Healthcare Limited, which will, in effect, reduce our outflow on the acquisition by INR 200-225 crore.

points.point: Chitta is shown as sub-scale and capital-starved — 100 of 200 beds opened, 26% occupancy on those, and no intention to spend on the rest — the operating backdrop to the divestment decision.
points.quote: Similarly, Chitta Hospital is a 200-bed hospital, but only 100 beds have been opened. And on those 100 beds, we have only 26% occupancy. So, there is no plan to open the balance 100 beds because that will also require some spend.

points.point: The only actual business separation: a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr for INR 40 crore, justified by strategic focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies, with only Chitta operational at ~INR 5 crore revenue and INR 1 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26.
points.quote: As part of our strategy to focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies, we have executed a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals for Rs. 40 crores, with completion expected by September '25.

points.point: The problem the divestment solves is stated as fit, not funding or valuation: the assets arrived with the Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and did not fit the network strategy.
points.quote: These assets were part of the overall Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and had limited strategic alignment.

points.point: Completion is reported under the banner of corporate streamlining, together with NCLT Chandigarh approval of the two-subsidiary merger (appointed date October 5, 2024) and its INR 149 crore one-time benefit.
points.quote: Alongside our expansion efforts, we also streamlined our corporate structure. Divestment of hospitals in Chitta and Anoopshahr was completed in September 2025.

points.point: The cost side of the restructuring: Q3 FY26 carried INR 55 crore of exceptional items, part of it stamp duty on the subsidiary merger (INR 14 crore per the FY26 earnings update, with INR 41 crore for the Code on Wages).
points.quote: During the quarter, there were exceptional items aggregating to INR 55 crore relating to impact of the Code on Wages, 2019 and provision for stamp duty on the merger of two of our subsidiaries.

points.point: The structurally separate Partner Healthcare Facility societies are explicitly being kept inside the network and their cash upstreamed or moved between societies rather than separated, because societies cannot pay dividends and upstreaming costs ~25% tax; Balaji's fee revision alone adds ~INR 25 crore a year to MHIL.
points.quote: No, there is no dividend that can be declared for any society.

points.point: Filing of May 21, 2026 (FY26 earnings update): the subsidiary amalgamation was completed, with the merged entity retaining the Crosslay Remedies name — a consolidation of two legal entities into one, the opposite of a carve-out.
points.quote: Post approval of Scheme of Amalgamation, two WoS i.e., CRL and JHL, have amalgamated effective December 15, 2025 and the name of amalgamated entity has been changed to Crosslay Remedies Limited

points.point: NCLT order of March 25, 2026 dissolving step-down wholly-owned subsidiary ET Planners Private Limited: its whole undertaking was moved up to parent Alps Hospital Limited on a going-concern basis, removing a legal entity rather than separating a business.
points.quote: The entire business undertaking of the company which comprises of all assets, all liabilities, customers and suppliers contracts, service agreements, lease and licenses, employees etc. on a going concern basis will be distributed to its shareholder i.e. Alps Hospital Limited.

points.point: Filing of January 29, 2026: voluntary liquidation of MHC Global Healthcare (Nigeria) Ltd, a non-material subsidiary with nil revenue and negative net worth of INR 70.89 lakh (-0.0076% of consolidated net worth), explicitly with no business or financial consequence.
points.quote: The voluntary liquidation of MHC Nigeria will neither affect any business nor impact materially the consolidated financials of the Company.

points.point: The only structural item put to shareholders (postal ballot results declared October 19, 2026) widens the company's objects into medical colleges, pharmaceuticals/radiopharmaceuticals and food & beverage — evidence that no demerger scheme was placed before members in this period.
points.quote: Alteration of the Main Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association of the Company

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation economics were given, because no separation was announced. For the divested Chitta/Anoopshahr units: INR 40 crore proceeds and exit of a strategically misaligned, loss-making asset (INR 1 crore EBITDA loss). For MHIL: a simpler holding structure, better governance, optimized cash flows, INR 200-225 crore lower Jaypee outflow and a ~INR 142 crore net one-time tax gain, against INR 14 crore stamp duty.
verdict.gaps: No demerger, spin-off, listed-entity separation, buyer identity, Anoopshahr financials, or any investor, lender or partner request for a separation is explained anywhere in these texts.

verdict.rationale: The materials provided do not contain any rationale for separating a business, so no reasoning can be reconstructed from them. The section labelled 'CALL PASSAGES' is empty — there are no earnings call excerpts, no management quotes, no cited numbers, and no named businesses being separated. The section labelled 'SCHEME RATIONALE' is not a rationale section: it is two post-effectiveness compliance reports dated May 11, 2026 (from Paradeep Phosphates Limited's Audit Committee and its Independent Directors) certifying, under SEBI Master Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/POD-2/P/CIR/2023/93 dated June 20, 2023, that proceeds from the sale of consolidated fractional entitlements were distributed to eligible shareholders. What the texts do establish is a combination rather than a separation: under Part II of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Mangalore Chemicals & Fertilizers Limited (Transferor) and Paradeep Phosphates Limited (Transferee), approved by NCLT Bengaluru on September 24, 2025 and NCLT Cuttack on September 26, 2025, MCFL merged into PPL as of Effective Date 2 (October 16, 2025) and was dissolved without being wound up; eligible MCFL shareholders on the October 31, 2025 record date received 187 PPL shares of Rs. 10 each for every 100 MCFL shares of Rs. 10 each, with 22,16,23,331 shares allotted on December 3, 2025, including 23,217 fractional shares held by the 'PPL Merger Trust' (Vistra ITCL (India) Limited as trustee), sold in the open market and distributed on May 08, 2026 (gross Rs. 26,01,427.96, TDS Rs. 11,801.00, net Rs. 25,89,626.96). The word 'Composite' implies the scheme had other parts, but no part describing a demerger, its business, or its purpose appears in the supplied text, which is explicitly truncated. Answering the question as asked would require inventing content, which these sources do not support.
verdict.evolution: No evolution can be traced: zero call passages were supplied, so there are no call dates, no first mention of a separation, and no change in the plan to report. The only dated sequence available is procedural and post-approval — NCLT orders September 24 and 26, 2025; merger effective October 16, 2025; record date October 31, 2025; allotment December 3, 2025; fractional proceeds distributed May 08, 2026; certification reports dated May 11, 2026. A further filing fragment dated October 17, 2025 appears but is cut off mid-address with no content.

points.point: The scheme described is a merger of Mangalore Chemicals & Fertilizers Limited into Paradeep Phosphates Limited under Part II, not a separation; MCFL was dissolved without winding up effective October 16, 2025.
points.quote: Accordingly, as of 16.10.2025, i.e., Effective Date 2 (as defined in the Scheme) the Transferor Company has merged with and into the Company in accordance with Part II of the Scheme and the Transferor Company stands dissolved without being wound up, without any further act or deed.

points.point: Consideration terms: 187 PPL shares of Rs. 10 each for every 100 MCFL shares of Rs. 10 each, with 22,16,23,331 shares allotted on December 3, 2025 to MCFL holders on the October 31, 2025 record date.
points.quote: In terms of the Scheme, eligible equity shareholders of the Transferor Company as on the record date (i.e. October 31, 2025) were allotted equity shares of the Company on December 03, 2025 in the share exchange ratio of 187 fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 10 each of the Company for every 100 fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10 each of the Transferor Company.

points.point: The documents' only stated purpose is SEBI-mandated certification that fractional-entitlement sale proceeds (23,217 shares; net Rs. 25,89,626.96, distributed May 08, 2026) reached eligible shareholders — not an explanation of strategic intent.
points.quote: Based on the above, it is hereby certified that the Company has compensated the eligible equity shareholders by distributing the sale proceeds of the fractional entitlements in accordance with provisions of the Scheme and SEBI Master Circular.

points.point: Judicial approval came from two benches, reflecting the two companies' registered offices (Bhubaneswar for PPL, Bengaluru for MCFL).
points.quote: was approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Bengaluru Bench vide its Order dated September 24, 2025 and the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Cuttack Bench vide its Order dated September 26, 2025.
