verdict.rationale: Eternal is not spinning a business out to the market — it is pulling one together inside the group. On October 21, 2026 the board approved a Business Transfer Agreement to hive off the Going-out India business housed in the listed parent (dining-out plus entertainment ticketing — District's dining-out, movies, events, sports and newer categories like retail stores and activity outlets) to Zomato Entertainment Private Limited (ZEPL), a wholly owned subsidiary, by slump sale on a going-concern basis with its assets and liabilities, for cash consideration of ~INR 130,75,56,871 (~INR 131 crore) valued under Rule 53 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, to close within 30 days of execution. The same day, the boards of ZEPL, Orbgen Technologies (OTPL) and Wasteland Entertainment (WEPL) gave in-principle approval to evaluate how to fold the Going-out India business sitting in those two subsidiaries into ZEPL as well. The sole stated reason is structural: "an overall internal restructuring exercise to consolidate the Going-out India business operating across various group entities, in a single wholly owned subsidiary - ZEPL to streamline the group's corporate structure and achieve operational synergies" — i.e. one business currently fragmented across the parent and at least two WOS gets one legal home. The scale is small and the economics are unchanged: FY2025-26 revenue of the identified business was INR 587 crore, 5.39% of standalone revenue, and net worth at March 31, 2026 was INR 8 crore, 0.02% of standalone net worth; the filing states there will be "no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control" and that the entire economic interest continues to vest with the holding company, and the standalone results note says the transaction has no impact on Q2FY27 numbers. It follows an identical template used three months earlier, when Nugget by Zomato (FY25-26 revenue INR 7.20 crore, 0.07% of standalone revenue; net worth INR 10.54 crore) was slump-sold to Carthero Technologies for INR 35 crore "as part of an internal restructuring exercise to streamline our corporate structure," and sits alongside other tidying — dissolution of dormant Zomato Media (Sri Lanka) and Zomato Internet Hizmetleri (Turkey), and swapping the Adonmo stake into Mygate (~4.4% fully diluted, valued INR 156 crore against INR 112 crore invested in January 2022). The calls supply the only operating logic management has ever voiced for one-business-one-entity: Bistro is "in a separate entity" so "the segregation of accounts is very clear," and Akshant conceded on April 28, 2026 that "our businesses are split across multiple entities, so... it's hard to reconcile our MIS with the way we report it in our audited financials."
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces as a separation thesis on any of the eight calls (Jan 2025 through Jul 2026); what builds instead is a habit of entity-level ring-fencing — May 1, 2025: Bistro "is not part of food... even if it scales, we want to report it separately"; Oct 16, 2025: Bistro losses parked in the 'Others' segment; Jan 21, 2026: District Pass investment pushes going-out losses up with breakeven guided in four to six quarters; Apr 28, 2026: management admits businesses are split across multiple entities and that MIS cannot be reconciled to audited financials; Jul 22, 2026: the same board meeting that hosted the Q1FY27 call approved the Nugget slump sale to Carthero on exactly the "streamline our corporate structure" rationale, and on the call Akshant reiterated Bistro's separate entity and clean segregation. The plan then appears fully formed in the Oct 21, 2026 board outcome: BTA signed for the parent's Going-out India business into ZEPL, plus in-principle approval to subsequently consolidate the Going-out businesses in OTPL and WEPL into the same entity — a two-step sequence, with the second step's "means and manner" still to be evaluated.

points.point: Oct 21, 2026 board approved transferring the parent's Going-out India business, with assets and liabilities, to wholly owned subsidiary ZEPL by slump sale on a going-concern basis; stated purpose is consolidating the business from multiple group entities into one and achieving operational synergies.
points.quote: The BTA and aforesaid consolidation is being undertaken as part of an overall internal restructuring exercise to consolidate the Going-out India business operating across various group entities, in a single wholly owned subsidiary - ZEPL to streamline the group's corporate structure and achieve operational synergies.

points.point: Step two is folding the Going-out India business housed in two other wholly owned subsidiaries — Orbgen Technologies (OTPL) and Wasteland Entertainment (WEPL) — into ZEPL; their boards only granted in-principle approval to work out how.
points.quote: In order to enable this, the board of directors of ZEPL, OTPL and WEPL, have also granted in-principle approval at their respective board meetings held on October 21, 2026, to evaluate the means and manner of implementing the aforesaid business consolidation.

points.point: The business being moved is small relative to the listed parent: FY2025-26 revenue INR 587 crore (5.39% of standalone revenue) and net worth of INR 8 crore (0.02% of standalone net worth) at March 31, 2026.
points.quote: Revenue of the Identified Business for FY 2025-26 is INR 587 crore representing 5.39% of the revenue of the Company on a standalone basis.

points.point: Consideration is cash of ~INR 130.76 crore from ZEPL to Eternal, set under Rule 53 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, with closing within 30 days of the BTA; it is a related-party transaction deemed arm's length.
points.quote: Cash consideration of an amount of ~INR 130,75,56,871/- (Indian rupees one hundred thirty crore seventy five lakh fifty six thousand eight hundred and seventy one only), will be paid by ZEPL to the Company, subject to the adjustments as agreed under the BTA.

points.point: Economic ownership does not move — no change in ultimate beneficial ownership or control, with the entire economic interest still vesting with the holding company; the standalone note confirms no P&L impact for Q2FY27.
points.quote: The proposed transfer is being undertaken as part of an internal group restructuring, pursuant to which there will be no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control of the transferred business, and the entire economic interest therein shall continue to vest with the holding company, and hence would be at arm's length.

points.point: Three months earlier the identical mechanism and wording were used for Nugget by Zomato (FY25-26 revenue INR 7.20 crore, 0.07% of standalone revenue; net worth INR 10.54 crore), slump-sold to wholly owned Carthero Technologies for INR 35 crore to run as a B2B AI-driven support platform.
points.quote: The proposed transfer is a part of an internal restructuring exercise to streamline our corporate structure.

points.point: Management's operating rationale for one-business-one-entity: housing a business separately gives clean, non-overlapping accounts versus food delivery — said of Bistro, the template now applied to Going-out.
points.quote: The Bistro business is also in a separate entity, and so the segregation of accounts is very clear, and there is no overlap with the food delivery business.

points.point: Asked why consolidated and standalone ad spends could not be mapped to District, the CFO conceded the group's businesses already sit across multiple entities, making internal management accounts hard to reconcile to audited financials — the reporting mess the consolidation addresses.
points.quote: That's right, our businesses are split across multiple entities, so generally speaking, it's hard to reconcile our MIS with the way we report it in our audited financials, unless you have more data.

points.point: Kunal Swarup confirmed the parent's standalone ad spend covers food delivery plus only part of the going-out business — largely dining-out — evidencing that Going-out was split between the listed entity and subsidiaries before the BTA.
points.quote: It's not entire District, but only a part of the going-out business. Largely the dining-out business.

points.point: District is operationally distinct from the rest of the group — five categories, dining-out and movies the largest, retail stores and events the promising newer ones, with a smaller, higher-spending customer base and far fewer cities than food delivery or quick commerce.
points.quote: It's definitely a smaller customer base, Garima, for going-out compared to food delivery or quick commerce.

points.point: Going-out losses jumped in Q3FY26 on the unplanned District Pass rollout, but management guided losses down sequentially to breakeven within four to six quarters, and said the FY30 $3 billion NOV target (>30% CAGR) rests mainly on market-share gains in events and movies.
points.quote: Irrespective of that, as we have mentioned in question 13, we now expect the losses to come down sequentially from here towards breakeven in the next four to six quarters.

points.point: District's perimeter was explicitly frozen before the restructuring — no new categories, travel ruled out — and the group's $1 billion FY29 EBITDA target was said to include every business, Hyperpure included.
points.quote: Garima, we have no plans to add any more category to District than what we already have, and travel is not a focus area for us at this point.

points.point: The precedent of keeping new businesses legally and reportably separate even when small was set early: Bistro was deliberately excluded from the food delivery segment and parked in 'Others'.
points.quote: Yes, it is not part of food. It's a totally different business. So even if it scales, we want to report it separately.

verdict.what_management_expects: No financial effect is claimed: only a streamlined group structure and "operational synergies," with ownership, control and economics unchanged and nil impact on Q2FY27 standalone results. Separately for the business itself, management expects going-out losses (INR 55 crore in Q2FY27; INR 292 crore FY26) to fall sequentially to breakeven, ~$3bn NOV by FY30, and inclusion in the ~$1bn FY29 group EBITDA.
verdict.gaps: Calls never mention it. No demerger, listing, value-unlock or fundraising rationale; no investor, lender or partner asked; no synergy quantum, tax effect or ZEPL standalone economics.

verdict.rationale: On the documents supplied, the business being separated is ITC's IT services arm, ITC Infotech India Limited (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary that is to be carved out of the unlisted group structure and listed on BSE and NSE through a strategic combination with listed Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (31 Aug 2026 filing). The mechanics are two-step: ITCI buys 3,36,61,700 shares (22.106% fully diluted) from promoters Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP for ~Rs 1,330 crores cash in two tranches (11.00% at Rs 390/share, 11.106% at Rs 400/share), funded by a Rights Issue of Rs 1,330 crores, after which Happiest Minds amalgamates into ITCI at 25 ITCI shares per 81 Happiest Minds shares (1:3.24) — implying Rs 405/share or Rs 6,167 crores for Happiest Minds and Rs 1,312/share or Rs 11,920 crores for ITCI pre-rights — leaving ITC with ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders ~26.6%, and ITCI listed. The stated problem it solves is sub-scale: management says '> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management office radar' and gives the 'Right to Hunt' and 'Right to Win' large deals, so the combination targets US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis versus ITCI's FY26 IT services revenue of Rs 4,718 crores (PAT Rs 510 crores adjusted, 18.5% adj. EBITDA margin, 13,000+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 14%) and Happiest Minds' FY26 Rs 2,315.11 crores (FY25 Rs 2,060.84 crores, FY24 Rs 1,624.66 crores, 6,500+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 25%). It also fixes portfolio gaps: Americas mix rises from 27% to 38%, BFSI from 12% to 20%, Build:Run moves to 50:50, and Hi-Tech, EdTech and Healthcare verticals plus 800+ clients and 19,000+ professionals are added, against an industry backdrop of a ~$400 Bn AI-driven TAM by 2030, compression of ~$350 Bn of legacy services, cost-takeout deals at 30-40% savings and vendor consolidation. For ITC shareholders the explicitly stated benefit of separation itself is that it 'Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility', alongside ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion and EPS accretion in the first full year. Nobody is recorded as having demanded it: ITCI's board moved under its own 'Orbit Next' strategy, ITC's board merely 'endorsed' it, and the only external party is the counterparty-seller Ashok Soota, who frames it as Happiest Minds finding 'a welcoming new home'; approvals needed are CCI/anti-trust, stock exchanges/SEBI, shareholders, creditors and NCLT, over ~15 months.
verdict.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so the idea is traceable only through filings: ITC had already demerged its Hotels business (visible as discontinued operations with Rs 15,163.06 crores of exceptional items in FY2024-25 and ITC Hotels Limited now an associate), establishing the separation template. The IT separation surfaces fully formed on 31 August 2026, when ITCI's board approved both the 22.106% promoter-stake purchase and the Happiest Minds amalgamation that will list ITCI, endorsed the same day by ITC's board. Housekeeping then followed in the opposite, consolidating direction: on 1 September 2026 step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan Technologies and Cloudlytics were dissolved into ITC Infotech (appointed date 1 October 2024), tidying the entity to be listed, while on 2 November 2026 ITC moved the other way at the parent by absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar) to 'reduce the number of operating entities'. The plan's indicative sequencing was set at board approval in Aug'26, Tranche 1 and exchange/SEBI no-objection around Q3FY27-early Q4FY27, shareholder/creditor meetings Mar-Apr'27 and ITCI listing in Q2-Q3 FY28.

points.point: The separation vehicle is disclosed in the 31 August 2026 filing: ITC Infotech acquires 22.106% of Happiest Minds for cash and then amalgamates it, with ITCI's own shares to be listed on both Indian exchanges.

points.point: The value-creation case for ITC shareholders names independent price discovery as a benefit of having the IT business separately listed.
points.quote: Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility

points.point: Regulation 30 disclosure frames the deal as the execution of ITCI's existing standalone expansion strategy, aimed at a step change in revenue scale and competitiveness.
points.quote: ITC Infotech's 'Orbit Next' strategy envisages rapid global expansion through capability led strategic partnerships.

points.point: The industry slide gives the explicit scale threshold problem the separation-and-combination is meant to clear — being below US$1bn keeps ITCI off large buyers' vendor lists.
points.quote: > $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management  office radar

points.point: Media statement sets the quantified target for the combined, listed entity: US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis, AI-first, with 19,000+ professionals.
points.quote: ITC Infotech (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC Limited and a leading global technology services player, today announced the proposed strategic combination with Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (Happiest Minds) to create a scaled, future-ready, AI-first global technology services enterprise.

points.point: Synergy slide quantifies what the combination is expected to deliver financially: roughly 10% revenue synergies, about 100 bps of margin expansion, and EPS accretion in year one.
points.quote: Expected to be EPS accretive in first full year of combined entity operations

points.point: ITC's Chairman Sanjiv Puri justifies it on complementarity of capability and culture rather than on any investor, lender or partner demand.
points.quote: The coming together of our complementary strengths, deep domain expertise and future-ready capabilities will further enhance our ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions across geographies.

points.quote: We believe that ITC Infotech is the best partner for Happiest Minds to fulfil its destiny and we are pleased that our team will have a welcoming new home .

points.quote: Integrating Happiest Minds' Digital Engineering, Data, AI, and Cybersecurity capabilities with our deep domain expertise, cloud and engineering capabilities will enable us to serve as a full stack AI-led transformation partner.

points.point: At the parent level ITC is simultaneously simplifying in the opposite direction, absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar; FY26 turnover Rs 451.71 crores, total assets Rs 150.07 crores) on 2 November 2026.
points.quote: Result in reduction of the number of operating entities to simplify the corporate holding structure.

points.point: The 1 September 2026 filing shows pre-listing entity cleanup: step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan and Cloudlytics were merged into ITC Infotech with appointed date 1 October 2024.
points.quote: Accordingly, with effect from 1st September , 2026, BTPL and CTPL stand  dissolved without winding up and have cease d to be subsidiaries of the Company.

points.point: Completion is conditional and long-dated — about 15 months — with CCI, exchange/SEBI, shareholder, creditor and NCLT approvals, and the two firms operating independently until then.
points.quote: The compani es expect the transaction to be completed within the next                     15 months and will continue to operate independently until all approvals have been obtained.

verdict.what_management_expects: ITC Infotech: step change to ~US$1bn revenue by FY28 (from Rs 4,718 crores FY26), Americas mix 27%→38%, BFSI 12%→20%, Build:Run 50:50, ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion, EPS accretive in year one, 19,000+ people, 800+ clients. ITC: a separately listed IT platform giving independent value discovery and strategic flexibility, while retaining ~73.4%.
verdict.gaps: No earnings-call transcripts supplied; filings never explain ITC's intent for its 73.4% stake, any ITC-shareholder entitlement, carve-out/dis-synergy costs, valuation basis, or the earlier hotels demerger's rationale.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is Linjemontage i Grästorp AB (LMG), KPIL's Swedish power-grid EPC subsidiary held through Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB (KPTS) — separated not by demerger but by an offer-for-sale IPO on Nasdaq Stockholm (listed 25 September 2026), in which KPTS sold down from 96.12% to 66.45% rather than giving LMG new capital. The trigger management cited on the calls was value crystallisation and cash: LMG had compounded from ~INR1,000 crores revenue in FY24 to INR1,800+ crores in FY25 (PBT INR21 crores to INR70+ crores) to ~INR3,000 crores in FY26 with EBITDA ~INR200 crores and PBT ~INR170 crores (both up over 100%), i.e. SEK1.3bn to SEK3.2bn net sales at a 56.6% CAGR with adjusted EBITA margin rising from 4.4% to 7.6%, net cash of SEK172.1m, ROCE of 48.1% and an order book of SEK4,349m — yet it was only ~11.14% of KPIL's consolidated revenue and ~4.5% of consolidated net worth. Mohnot repeatedly placed the Sweden 'fundraise' inside the same bucket as the noncore exits (Vindhyachal road asset sold January 2026 for ~INR799 crores EV / INR600+ crores net, Indore real estate, Shree Shubham Logistics), i.e. as a source of 'further cash flows' to cut leverage and fund the INR800-900 crores/year capex programme and lift ROCE; the IPO delivered KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at SEK46/share, valuing LMG at SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores). The second problem it solves is that LMG's economics are structurally different from KPIL's: management argued a 6%-7% PBT in a 'mature market' is fine there because 'the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always' — a profile the consolidated KPIL multiple was not reflecting. LMG's own filings justify the separation on strategic grounds: visibility, credibility and brand recognition with customers, partners and employees, transparency, a platform for long-term value creation, a broadened shareholder base, and support for its ambition to lead Nordic power-infrastructure EPC in a Swedish serviceable market growing from ~SEK19bn (2025) to ~SEK31bn (2030) at 11% CAGR (transmission 17%), with ~80% of Sweden's transmission grid over 40 years old and Statnett planning NOK150-200bn of 2025-2034 investment. Pressure came from investors and analysts, not lenders: Carnelian and DAM Capital pushed management on why a T&D business sitting inside a T&D company needed its own listing, while cornerstone demand from Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen (SEK290m) anchored the book; LMG's management/employee shareholders (991,950 shares) sold mainly to repay the financing they had used to buy their shares. KPIL stressed continuity, not exit: KPTS 'indicated an intention to remain a long-term major shareholder', is locked up for 360 days, and LMG remains a step-down subsidiary.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced on the 19 May 2025 Q4 FY25 call, where Mohnot disclosed that the Board had approved appointing bankers and intermediaries to examine 'fundraising options' at Linjemontage — framed alongside the noncore clean-up (VEPL, Indore, Shubham); the 14 Feb 2025 call had contained no such plan, only LMG's record order book of INR3,143 crores. By 8 August 2025 (Q1 FY26) it had hardened into a disclosed 'strategic overview… including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions', and management refused to explain the logic when Carnelian asked why a T&D business inside a T&D company needed a separate listing, even withdrawing LMG margin guidance because the process had started. On 31 October 2025 Mohnot said the path was still undecided but expected 'some light' on valuation in FY26-27, and on 5 February 2026 he said the Sweden mandate was 'progressing well' and should throw off cash in FY26-27; by 15 May 2026 he described it only as 'some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes'. The form was fixed in the filings: KPTS board approval on 9 September 2026, prospectus and SEK46 price on 16 September, listing and ~32.1% offer on 25 September, and partial greenshoe exercise on 23-24 October 2026 leaving KPIL at 66.45%.

points.point: Baseline: no separation plan existed; LMG was simply presented as a record performer, with revenue doubling and an all-time-high order book of INR3,143 crores.
points.quote: LMG's order book is at a all time high of INR3,143 crores.

points.point: First disclosure of the separation idea — the Board approved bankers and intermediaries to study fundraising options at Linjemontage, mentioned in the same breath as LMG's PBT rising from ~INR21 crores to ~INR70+ crores.
points.quote: the Board has also approved appointment of bankers as well as intermediaries to look at fund options, fundraising options in Sweden Linjemontage in the last Board meeting, which we have declared to everyone.

points.point: Formalised as a disclosed 'strategic overview' with an IPO explicitly named as one of the options, and merchant bankers and advisers appointed; LMG had already begun preparatory steps.
points.quote: We have initiated a strategic overview on LMG where various options are being evaluated, including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions.

points.point: An investor (Mihir Manohar, Carnelian Capital) pressed on exactly the question management never answered — why carve out a T&D business that already sits inside a T&D company; Mohnot declined to comment.
points.quote: I just wanted to understand the thought process because I mean, it is also T&D business similarly sitting in KPIL.

points.point: Management explained LMG's different economic profile — lower PBT than KPIL's core but very high ROCE and permanently cash positive — the implicit valuation argument for separating it, with bankers still mandated and the path undecided.
points.quote: As far as margins are concerned, I think that those are mature markets where a PBT of 6% to 7% is very reasonably good because the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always.

points.point: The Sweden transaction was placed squarely in the monetisation/debt-reduction bucket alongside transmission assets, the last road asset and Shree Shubham Logistics, with cash expected in FY26-27.
points.quote: We do not know which options and what timing it exactly is, but we have appointed bankers to look at exploring fund option raising at Sweden also, which I'm expecting in FY26-27 should give us further cash flows.

points.point: Final pre-IPO framing: a 'strategic investment' into the Swedish subsidiary grouped with remaining divestments as free-cash-flow events to strengthen the balance sheet, set against INR800+ crores of annual capex and net debt already down 50% to INR915 crores.
points.quote: We also have some events of free cash flows coming in next year, whether it is through a few more divestments which are left, which might happen either next year or a year after that or whether it is through some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes.

points.point: The 9 September 2026 filing/press release gives the official rationale — standalone visibility, credibility, brand and Nordic leadership ambition — and discloses LMG's scale: SEK3,225m FY26 revenue (~11.14% of KPIL consolidated revenue) but only SEK334m net worth (~4.5% of KPIL's).
points.quote: The Listing is expected to enhance the Company's visibility, credibility and brand recognition among customers, partners and employees, and to support Linjemontage's long-term ambition to strengthen its position in the Nordics as one of the leading EPC providers within power infrastructure.

points.point: Transparency, long-term value creation and a diversified shareholder base are the stated second leg, with KPTS committing to stay a long-term major shareholder (360-day lock-up) and LMG remaining a step-down subsidiary.
points.quote: Becoming a publicly listed company will also provide greater transparency and a platform for long-term value creation, while diversifying the shareholder base.

points.point: Structurally this is a pure sell-down, not a capital raise for LMG: 14,311,620 base shares plus a 2,146,743-share greenshoe at SEK46, ~32.1% of LMG, giving KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at a SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores) valuation and taking KPTS from 96.12% to 66.45% after the partial greenshoe exercise of 1,877,911 shares.
points.quote: The Offering consists only of existing shares and the Company will therefore not receive any proceeds from the Offering.

points.point: Demand was investor-led: Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen cornerstoned SEK290m, while LMG's own management/director/employee holders sold 991,950 shares chiefly to repay the borrowings used to buy them.
points.quote: All individual Selling Shareholders other than Kalpataru Sweden are selling shares in the Offering primarily to repay financing arrangements relating to their respective acquisitions of shares in the Company.

points.point: LMG's standalone financial targets quantify what separation is meant to unlock — revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8% (from 7.6%), net debt/adj EBITDA below 1.0x and a 25% dividend payout — in a market growing 11% CAGR to SEK31bn by 2030.
points.quote: Profitability : Linjemontage aims to reach an adjusted EBITA margin exceeding 8 per cent in the medium term.

verdict.what_management_expects: For LMG: standalone visibility, credibility and brand with customers and employees; transparency; a growth platform and broadened shareholder base; revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8%, net debt/EBITDA under 1.0x, 25% payout. For KPIL: ~SEK711m cash to cut debt and fund capex, value crystallised at SEK2.36bn, retained 66.45% control, higher ROCE and a cleaner noncore-free core EPC portfolio.
verdict.gaps: Calls never explained why a listing over a trade sale, the valuation sought, use of proceeds, dilution to consolidated EPS, or minority/governance terms; management explicitly refused to give the rationale.

verdict.segment_name: Linjemontage i Grästorp Aktiebolag ("Linjemontage (Sweden)" / LMG) — step-down subsidiary within KPIL's Power T&D (EPC) segment; not a separately reported Ind AS 108 segment

verdict.rationale: The separation management explains across these texts is the demerger of the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle ("MFL") western-wear brands business — the Lifestyle Brands portfolio plus Reebok, American Eagle, Van Heusen Innerwear and the exited Forever 21 — into Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), leaving ABFRL with Pantaloons/Style Up-OWND, the ethnic portfolio (designer brands Sabyasachi, Tarun Tahiliani, House of Masaba, Shantnu & Nikhil, plus Tasva, Jaypore and TCNS), luxury retail (The Collective, Galeries Lafayette) and the digital-first TMRW platform. The problem stated is internal competition for capital and attention: the combined ABFRL "had multiple growth opportunities, and we realized at some point of time, that we'll have to capitalize it and structure it differently to pursue independent growth opportunities more aggressively", with Innerwear cited as a business that "will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us" (May 2025). The cash-generative, high-margin brands business (FY25 normalised revenue INR7,830 crores, 16.2% EBITDA margin, 19.3% for Brands, 3,200+ stores) was described as "underleveraged in the combined entity", and Ashish Dikshit said "one of the strategic rationale for the demerger was to leave that cash for allowing that business to soar" — funding a historic 300-plus net store rollout in FY26 that franchisees could not drive in a downturn (Feb 2025). On the other side, a USD 490 million QIP plus preferential issue (promoters paying a premium) was raised to make demerged ABFRL debt-free with INR2,350 crores consolidated cash (vs an earlier INR1,300 crores estimate) to fund the TCNS turnaround, Tasva, Style Up, Galeries Lafayette and TMRW "until they become self-sustainable", with a plan to be free-cash-flow positive in about three years; ABLBL started with INR781 crores net debt (INR700 crores planned opening), repayable in 2–3 years, and was to be "a dividend-distributing company at the earliest appropriate opportunity". Management repeatedly framed the purpose as unlocking value through "2 independent entities" / "two focused fashion power houses", each on its own "distinct value-creation journey", with ABLBL guided to double in scale and expand margins over five years and demerged ABFRL to 3x revenue and 2x margin — the latter mostly from turning currently loss-making TCNS, Tasva and TMRW positive rather than from the already-profitable parts. Mechanics: the demerger was Board-approved 19 April 2024, books separated from 1 April 2024, 1:1 share exchange ratio (1,22,02,94,773 shares), NCLT sanction 27 March 2025, effective 1 May 2025, ABLBL listed 23 June 2025, accounted as a common-control transaction at book values with MFL shown as discontinued operations and a one-time INR97 crores gain from discontinuing inter-division elimination (Pantaloons inventory written up to purchase price). The same "separate and separately capitalise" logic continues one level down at TMRW, created as a standalone company in 2021, funded first by ABFRL (INR770–1,000 crores), then by ServiceNow Ventures (INR437 crores for ~11%, round completed at INR450 crores in Q2 FY26), then INR500 crores of NCDs (INR800 crores cash), explicitly aimed at "its own public market journey as we go forward from private to public". The only separation-type item in the newest filings runs the other way: the Scheme amalgamating wholly-owned Jaypore E-Commerce and TG Apparel & Decor back into ABFRL (Board 5 Feb 2026, NCLT 2 July 2026, effective 1 August 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026) for "simplification of legal & operating structure" and lower administrative cost, with no consideration as the shares are simply cancelled.
verdict.evolution: By the Feb 2025 call (17 Feb 2025, Q3 FY25) the demerger was already Board-approved (19 April 2024) and in execution — "progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months" with the NCLT hearing in the third week of March 2025 — and that call paired it with the USD 490 million fundraise, disclosing the split balance sheets (ABLBL ~INR700 crores opening debt; demerged ABFRL ~INR1,300 crores cash) and the clearest motive statement, that Lifestyle Brands' expansion had been "underleveraged in the combined entity". The May 2025 call (26 May 2025, Q4 FY25) reported completion, restated the rationale as two focused, independently capitalised platforms with explicit five-year targets (ABLBL double scale; ABFRL 3x revenue, 2x margin), and added the Innerwear example of a business that had not got management attention when five or six opportunities competed. The Aug 2025 call (14 Aug 2025) closed the process (ABLBL listed 23 June 2025) and extended the same capital-allocation philosophy to TMRW's external fundraise; by Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 the demerger survives only as base-effect accounting (the INR97 crores gain), separate ABLBL/ABFRL earnings calls, leverage guidance "around 2 to 3" for each fashion company, and subsidiaries told to "fund their own growth" — while the newest Scheme filings (5 Feb 2026 to 1 Aug 2026) consolidate two wholly-owned subsidiaries back in.

points.point: The demerger of the western-wear brands business into ABLBL was in final regulatory execution, with the NCLT hearing set for the third week of March 2025 and completion expected within 2–3 months.
points.quote: First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months.

points.point: The USD 490 million QIP plus preferential issue was explicitly sized to leave the demerged ABFRL debt-free with enough cash to carry its loss-making growth businesses until they stand on their own.
points.quote: The fundraise within demerged ABFRL will strengthen its balance sheet by making it debt-free and leaving enough cash in the books to take care of the growth needs of its businesses until they become self-sustainable.

points.point: Management quantified the split balance sheets: ABLBL to open FY26 with INR700 crores of debt, demerged ABFRL with roughly INR1,300 crores of cash (consolidated net debt was ~INR1,800 crores in January 2025 after INR1,860 crores of QIP money).
points.quote: We expect ABLBL to start the next year with opening debt of INR700 crores, whereas demerged ABFRL will have a likely cash balance of approximately INR1,300 crores.

points.point: The clearest stated motive: the Lifestyle Brands store-expansion opportunity had been starved inside the combined company, and the demerger was designed to leave that business its own cash flows to expand (300-plus stores planned, vs a consolidation year in FY25).
points.quote: We think that's a large opportunity, which was sort of underleveraged in the combined entity. And one of the strategic rationale for the demerger was to leave that cash for allowing that business to soar.

points.point: Asked why capital was raised at the pre-demerger consolidated level and why ABLBL kept INR700 crores of debt, Dikshit said the simultaneous TCNS merger stretched the demerger to 12–15 months, so raising in the combined entity was simply the fastest route; the books of the two companies were separated with effect from 1 April 2024.
points.quote: And that's when we decided to do the fundraise in the combined entity, because that is the fastest way of raising capital at that point of time.

points.point: The purpose was framed as value unlock through two independently viable listed companies, each with its own growth runway and balance sheet.
points.quote: The completion of these steps in the next 2, 3 months will enable us to unlock value through 2 independent entities, both with attractive growth potential and a strong balance sheet through a resilient growth-oriented business model sharpened over time.

points.point: Completion was announced as the creation of two focused entities on separate high-growth trajectories; ABLBL shares were allotted to ABFRL shareholders on the record date and listing was targeted by end-June.
points.quote: We successfully completed the demerger, creating two focused fashion power houses, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, ABLBL; and Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited, ABFRL, both now set on independent high-growth trajectories.

points.point: The sharpest statement of the capital-and-attention problem the split solves, given in answer to a question on why Innerwear had stagnated at about INR500 crores since 2016–17: ABFRL had five or six competing growth opportunities, so Innerwear never got management focus; inside a cash-generating ABLBL it would.
points.quote: ABFRL, the combined ABFRL business had multiple growth opportunities, and we realized at some point of time, that we'll have to capitalize it and structure it differently to pursue independent growth opportunities more aggressively.

points.point: Post-demerger targets were given per entity: ABLBL to double in scale and expand margins over five years off 3,200-plus stores and its own free cash flow (FY25 normalised revenue INR7,830 crores, 16.2% EBITDA margin; net debt INR781 crores to be repaid in 2–3 years; dividends "at the earliest appropriate opportunity").
points.quote: ABLBL, backed by a robust portfolio over 3,200 stores and healthy free cash flows, is positioned to double in scale and expand margins meaningfully over the next 5 years with 300-plus stores already in the pipeline for FY '26.

points.point: For demerged ABFRL (FY25 revenue INR7,355 crores) the target was 3x revenue and 2x margin over five years on INR2,350 crores of gross cash, with Dikshit saying the bulk of the margin expansion comes from turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW from loss-making to profitable rather than from the already-profitable units.
points.quote: ABFRL with a sharpened brand portfolio, a comprehensive diversified play across high-growth segments and a gross cash balance of INR2,350 crores is set to unlock the next phase of growth, targeting a 3x revenue scale up and 2x margin expansion over the next 5 years.

points.point: A mechanical consequence of separation: inter-division eliminations between Madura and Pantaloons stopped, producing a one-time INR97 crores EBITDA gain (inventory written up to Pantaloons' purchase price) that recurs as a base-effect drag in later quarters; ABLBL's INR148 crores of depreciation on discontinued operations was also not charged in consolidated financials.
points.quote: Reported EBITDA includes gain of INR97 crores on account of discontinuation of interdivision elimination post demerger as company's financials get reset to report on independent and stand-alone basis going forward.

points.point: The process closed with ABLBL listed on 23 June 2025, and from Q1 FY26 ABFRL reported only the retained portfolio, with newer businesses already 44% of revenue versus 37% a year earlier.
points.quote: On demerger, as previously communicated, all requisite processes have been successfully completed, culminating in the creation of Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited. The company was listed on the stock exchange on 23rd June 2025.

verdict.rationale: A correction first: nothing in these texts describes ACC separating or spinning off a business — they describe the opposite, ACC itself being absorbed. The Board approved a Scheme of Amalgamation on December 22, 2025 under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013, merging ACC Limited (Amalgamating Company) into its parent Ambuja Cements Limited (Amalgamated Company, which held 50.05% of ACC's paid-up equity as at 31.05.2026), with appointed date January 1, 2026, ACC dissolved without winding up, Ambuja's ACC shares cancelled, and public ACC holders receiving 328 Ambuja shares of ₹2 each for every 100 ACC shares of ₹10 each (valuation jointly by GT Valuation Advisors and BDO Valuation Advisory, fairness opinions from SBI Capital Markets and IDBI Capital Markets, all dated 22.12.2025). The stated reason is that both companies are in the same line of business, so the merger lets Ambuja 'assume complete ownership and direction' of ACC, unify manufacturing and commercial functions, optimise resource allocation and cut the number of entities in the same line of business, pooling financial, operational and logistical resources for economies of scale. On the January 30, 2026 call Vinod Bahety called it 'our defining development this quarter' and the start of a 'unified One Cement Platform' that would accelerate growth, support EBITDA expansion, strengthen operational excellence leverage, improve logistics density and enhance capital efficiency, with value creation framed over 24–36 months; by May 4, 2026 he added 'sharper focus on the operational performance, business synergies and the overall higher degree of compliances.' The concrete problem it fixes is the MSA (Master Supply/Service Agreement) plumbing that already runs ACC and Ambuja as one business while leaving ACC's own accounts distorted: ACC carries a receivable from Ambuja under the MSA and therefore 'will find negative operating cash flow' (May 2026), a ₹3,900 crore inter-corporate deposit at 8% repayable by March 31, 2027 was sanctioned by ACC shareholders on April 1, 2026 to settle it, ₹315 crore of coal sales had to be grossed up at ACC level only and 'nullifies at the consol level' (Jan 2026), consolidated EBITDA of ₹1,060/t exceeded the standalone ₹708 (Ambuja) and ~₹900 (ACC) because inter-company sales are knocked off, and the Q2 FY27 release still says reported numbers 'are not strictly comparable due to the impact of MSA' with Q1 FY27 EBITDA of only ₹457 crore / ₹458 PMT (7.9% margin) attributed to 'higher MSA volumes with Ambuja.' It also sits on top of acknowledged operating problems: ACC's structural cost gap of ₹300–400 a tonne versus Ambuja (no captive coal, power ₹6.10 vs ₹5.30 per unit, WHRS 14% vs 21%), a network Karan Adani said was wrong in both companies — 'It's ACC and Ambuja, both of them had issues' — with grinding units to be shut and moved closer to market, and an FY26 cost of ₹4,400/t against a ₹4,000 target, peaking at ₹4,500 in Q4. Nobody external is named as demanding it: the promoter-controlled Board initiated it, SEBI/NSE/BSE gave no-objection on June 4, 2026 (3 complaints each to ACC and Ambuja, SEBI demanding disclosure of cost-benefit analysis, dilution impact and pending enforcement actions), NCLT ordered meetings on July 29, 2026, ACC shareholders approved on September 29, 2026 with 95.52% of all votes and 84.97% of public votes in favour, and lenders were not involved at all because both companies had no secured creditors, so no lender NOC was required and creditor meetings were dispensed with. ACC is the last step in a sequence — Adani Cementation (effective August 1, 2025), Sanghi Industries (March 12, 2026), Penna Cement (April 10, 2026) — with Orient Cement running as a parallel scheme and completion expected during FY27, subject to final NCLT sanction.
verdict.evolution: Through the May 2025, August 2025 and November 2025 calls there is no merger talk at all: the story is acquisition and integration (Sanghi, Penna, Asian, Tuticorin, Orient), capacity targets moving 118 → 140 → 155 MT, and ACC's standalone cost/EBITDA gap of ₹300–400 a tonne versus Ambuja, with the MSA already shifting profit to the consolidated level. The Board approved the Scheme on December 22, 2025, and it surfaced publicly on the January 30, 2026 call (filed February 2026), where Bahety called the proposed amalgamation of ACC and Orient Cement with Ambuja 'our defining development this quarter' and the beginning of the One Cement Platform, promising EBITDA expansion, logistics density and capital efficiency over 24–36 months. By the May 4, 2026 call the framing had shifted from growth to clean-up: Sanghi and Penna were done, 'ACC and Orient Cement is under process,' the platform was pitched as sharper operational focus, synergies and 'higher degree of compliances,' and it sat alongside Karan Adani's explicit reset — capacity target slipping from FY28 to about FY30, grinding units to be shut and relocated, SLA operators brought in. Execution then ran to schedule on paper — SEBI/exchange NOCs June 4, 2026, NCLT order July 29, 2026, ACC shareholder approval September 29, 2026 (over 95% in favour), ₹3,900 crore ICD in Q1 FY27 to clear the MSA receivable — with completion still only 'expected during FY'27' as of the October 27, 2026 release.

points.point: First public discussion of the scheme; Bahety presents it as the quarter's single most important event and names the five benefits — growth, EBITDA, operational leverage, logistics density, capital efficiency — over a 24–36 month horizon.
points.quote: Our defining development this quarter has been the proposed amalgamation of ACC and Orient Cement with Ambuja Cements.

points.point: The benefit list is explicitly operational and financial rather than portfolio-related, and is given a time frame of 24 to 36 months for value creation.
points.quote: This marks the beginning of a unified One Cement Platform that will accelerate our growth trajectory, support EBITDA expansion, strengthen operational excellence leverage, improve logistics density and enhance capital efficiency.

points.point: Accounting distortion created by running two listed entities under the MSA: ₹315 crore of coal sales had to be grossed up at ACC standalone level and vanishes on consolidation — Rohit Soni confirming it is 'only at ACC level... At consol level, 0, 0, 0.'
points.quote: It is only the grossing up. No impact on the P&L item, right?

points.point: Sequencing update: two acquisitions already merged into Ambuja, ACC and Orient still in process, with the platform now justified on operational focus, synergies and compliance.
points.quote: Successful amalgamation of Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement with Ambuja Cements is now completed, while ACC and Orient Cement is under process.

points.point: The stated purpose of One Cement Platform widens from growth to operating discipline and compliance.
points.quote: The One Cement platform is a strategic initiative and will help to bring sharper focus on the operational performance, business synergies and the overall higher degree of compliances.

points.point: Answering Prateek Kumar (Jefferies) on ACC's sharply negative operating cash flow, Bahety attributes it directly to the MSA receivable from Ambuja and says the shareholder-approved ICD will knock it off — the cash-flow symptom the merger removes structurally.
points.quote: So it's like as a one consol business under the MSA, the receivables are there. Therefore, ACC will find negative operating cash flow.

points.point: Karan Adani says the grinding-unit/logistics network is mislocated in both companies and units will be shut and moved closer to market — the physical overlap a single entity is meant to let them fix (e.g. Bihar served from Chhattisgarh).
points.quote: It's both ACC and Ambuja. It's ACC and Ambuja, both of them had issues.

points.point: Pre-announcement evidence of the same problem: Pathanjali Srinivasan asks why consolidated EBITDA of ₹1,060/t exceeds standalone ₹708 (Ambuja) and ~₹900 (ACC), and Bahety confirms the MSA inter-company knock-off is the reason.
points.quote: Because in consol, the inter sale between the companies gets knocked off.

points.point: ACC's structural handicap versus Ambuja quantified before any merger talk — no captive coal, power ₹6.10/unit versus ₹5.30, WHRS 14% versus 21% — a ₹300–400 per tonne EBITDA gap.
points.quote: Therefore, I said for ACC our primary efforts are to work on the investments and the efficiencies gain on the cost and that will help us to bridge this gap of whatever ₹300-₹400 a ton and come to 4-digits sooner for ACC as well.

points.point: The consolidation logic predates the scheme: the CFO frames the acquired entities (Sanghi, Asian, Tuticorin, Penna, Orient) as delivering synergies ahead of plan under a 'disciplined M&A playbook'.
points.quote: And I'm happy to report that the integration of these assets is progressing extremely well, unlocking the synergies faster than what we expected across operations, logistics and procurement.

points.point: The formal rationale in the NCLT application rests on same-line-of-business overlap and the parent taking full control of a company it already majority-owns (50.05%).
points.quote: As both the companies are under the same line of business, the amalgamation will enable the Amalgamated Company to assume complete ownership and direction of the Amalgamating Company's business for long-term strategic alignment.

points.point: Second limb of the rationale: removing duplicate entities to speed decisions, production planning and operations discipline.
points.quote: The amalgamation will unify manufacturing and commercial functions, optimize resource allocation, and streamline the group's structure by reducing multiple entities in the same line of business.

points.point: Third limb: scale economics and capital deployment as the route to shareholder value, consistent with Ambuja's stated consolidation vision.
points.quote: By pooling financial, operational, and logistical resources, the merged entity will unlock economies of scale.

points.point: Consideration for ACC minorities, with Ambuja's own 50.05% holding cancelled; valuation jointly by GT Valuation Advisors and BDO Valuation Advisory, fairness opinions from SBI Capital Markets and IDBI Capital Markets, all dated 22.12.2025.
points.quote: the Amalgamated Company will issue and allot to the equity shareholders of the Amalgamating Company (other than Amalgamated Company), 328 equity shares of the face value of ₹ 2 each fully paid of the Amalgamated Company, for every 100 equity shares of the face value of ₹ 10 each fully paid held by them in the Amalgamating Company

points.point: No lender asked for this and none had to consent: ACC had no secured creditors, so the SEBI-mandated 75%-by-value secured-creditor NOC was not required and creditor meetings were dispensed with (1,38,007 unsecured creditors, ₹4,950.67 crore, unaffected).
points.quote: The Amalgamating Company had no secured creditors on the date of aforesaid applications filed by it with the Stock Exchanges or even as on the date of filing of the present applications before this Tribunal.

points.point: Shareholders, not lenders or partners, were the gating approval: at the NCLT-convened meeting of 29 September 2026, 144,822,702 votes (95.52%) were in favour and 6,784,657 (4.48%) against, with public shareholders 84.97% in favour; the October 27, 2026 release restates the benefit case.
points.quote: The Scheme secured the statutory majority and requisite public-shareholder approval, with over 95% and 99% of votes cast by ACC and Ambuja shareholders, respectively, in favour.

points.point: The MSA distortion persists right up to the latest reported quarter: ACC's Q1 FY27 EBITDA of ₹457 crore (₹458 PMT, 7.9% margin, versus ₹730 PMT a year earlier) and Q2 FY27's ₹401 crore are footnoted as reflecting 'higher MSA volume with parent Ambuja Cements'.
points.quote: While the reported numbers are not strictly comparable due to the impact of MSA, the underlying business momentum remains encouraging

verdict.what_management_expects: For the combined Ambuja: accelerated growth, EBITDA expansion, operational-excellence leverage, improved logistics density, higher capital efficiency, economies of scale from pooled financial, operational and logistical resources, and a simpler, more agile structure with fewer same-business entities. ACC ceases to exist; its holders get 328 Ambuja shares per 100 ACC shares. Value creation framed over 24–36 months.
verdict.gaps: No quantified synergy, cost-benefit or tax numbers; no explanation of ACC's MSA-depressed standalone EBITDA; no lender, partner or investor demand named; no reason for timing.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these transcripts and filings, APSEZ is not separating or demerging a business, and management never explains one, because no separation exists in the record: the only Scheme of Arrangement here runs the other way, folding a subsidiary in. The Scheme is the amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services Limited (AHSL, the wholly-owned harbour/marine-services arm) INTO APSEZ under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 — intimated by the letter of November 4, 2025, sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench on April 1, 2026, and effective April 21, 2026 when the certified order was filed with the RoC Gujarat; no rationale, synergy, cost saving or valuation argument is given in the filing, and no earnings call mentions it. The only transaction that separates economic interest in a business is the Vizhinjam partial sell-down: a Share Purchase and Subscription Agreement dated June 29, 2026 under which Mundi Limited, a subsidiary of Terminal Investment Limited (TiL, the terminal arm of MSC), takes 49% of Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited (AVPPL) at a total deal value of USD 2.85bn, of which TiL's 49% share is USD 1.397bn — USD 539mn for the stake and USD 858mn on completion of the Phase 2 expansion by December 2028 (total expansion capex USD 1.75bn, capacity 1.6m to 5.7m TEUs, 3.5x; quay 800m to 2,000m; STS cranes 8 to 29). This is explicitly not a demerger or slump sale (both marked "Not Applicable" in the Regulation 30 disclosure): APSEZ keeps 51%, a majority of board seats, and continues to consolidate AVPPL as a subsidiary, so it is a partner-led monetisation of a minority stake, not a separation of the asset from the group. The problems it is said to solve are commercial, not structural — enhanced volume visibility and ramp-up ahead of plan, a higher share of Bangladesh cargo today routed through competing Southeast Asian transshipment hubs, a stronger position on East Africa trade routes, more relay cargo — plus funding: "Transaction unlocks USD 1.397bn for APSEZ's future growth trajectory" against AVPPL FY26 income of Rs 843.19 crore, share capital of Rs 897.00 crore and net worth of Rs 2,813.98 crore at 31.03.26. Who asked: the counterparty is MSC/TiL, a third strategic partnership after Mundra CT3 (AICTPL, 50:50, 3.2m TEUs in FY26) and Ennore (AECTPL, 51:49, 701K TEUs in FY26); no investor, lender or rating agency in these texts asks for any business to be separated, and investors instead asked for, and got, separate REPORTING lines (international ports, marine, trucking and international freight network) plus capital-allocation detail. Management's stated strategic direction across every call is the opposite of separation — integration and consolidation into one "integrated transport utility" with scale, and the only business they declined to own, shipbuilding, was declined on competency grounds, not separated.
verdict.evolution: The idea of a separation never surfaces in the calls: Oct 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025 (May 1, 2025), Nov 2025 (Nov 4, 2025) and the Apr 30, 2026 Q4 call discuss volumes, margins, ROCE, capex and leverage, with no demerger, spin-off or listing of a vertical mentioned. What did evolve was disclosure and structure: at the May 2025 call management introduced separate reporting lines for international ports, marine services and trucking/IFN "thanks to your feedback"; on November 4, 2025 — the same date as the Q2 FY26 call, where it was not discussed — APSEZ intimated the inward amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services into the parent, sanctioned April 1, 2026 and effective April 21, 2026. Only after the last call in this set does a partial separation of economic interest appear, in the June 29-30, 2026 Vizhinjam agreement with MSC's TiL for 49% of AVPPL, which was never previewed or justified on any call in this record. Across the whole window the narrative runs toward consolidation — Ambition 2031, capex first, strategic M&A second, buyback "the last option" — not toward breaking anything out.

points.point: The only Scheme of Arrangement in the record is an inward amalgamation, not a separation: wholly-owned Adani Harbour Services Limited was merged into APSEZ under Sections 230-232, sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench on April 1, 2026, with no rationale stated in the filing.
points.quote: the Scheme of Amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services Limited ("Transferor Company") with Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited ("Transferee Company") under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable all provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, has been sanctioned by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Ahmedabad Bench by its order passed on April 1, 2026.

points.point: The amalgamation completed on filing the certified NCLT order with the RoC Gujarat; the first intimation was a letter dated November 4, 2025, the same day as the Q2 FY26 call, where it was never mentioned.
points.quote: Accordingly, the effective date of Scheme is April 21, 2026.

points.point: The only separation of economic interest is a 49% stake sale in the Vizhinjam port entity (AVPPL) to Mundi Limited, a subsidiary of MSC's terminal arm TiL, signed June 29, 2026 and subject to customary and regulatory approvals.
points.quote: the Company has entered into Share Purchase and Subscription Agreement on June 29, 2026 with Mundi Limited ("Mundi"), pursuant to which Mundi will invest for 49% interest in Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited ("AVPPL").

points.point: Vizhinjam is explicitly NOT being separated from APSEZ: control, board majority and consolidation are retained, and the disclosure marks both "disposal of the undertaking outside Scheme of Arrangement" and "slump sale" as Not Applicable.
points.quote: APSEZ will retain 51% of equity, hold majority of board seats, and will continue to consolidate AVPPL as a subsidiary company

points.point: Pricing and staging: total deal value USD 2.85bn, TiL's 49% share USD 1.397bn — USD 539mn for the stake plus USD 858mn on completion of the Phase 2 expansion by December 2028 (expansion capex USD 1.75bn), against AVPPL FY26 income of Rs 843.19 crore and net worth of Rs 2,813.98 crore.
points.quote: TiL to invest USD 1.397bn, equivalent to its proportionate 49% share of USD 2.85bn.

points.point: The funding rationale is stated as growth capital for the parent rather than any structural or governance problem being solved.
points.quote: Transaction unlocks USD 1.397bn for APSEZ's future growth trajectory

points.point: The commercial case is cargo, not corporate structure: faster ramp-up, Bangladesh volumes currently going to rival Southeast Asian hubs, East Africa routes and relay cargo; it is the third APSEZ-TiL tie-up after Mundra CT3 (50:50, 3.2m TEUs FY26) and Ennore (51:49, 701K TEUs FY26).
points.quote: Higher share of Bangladesh cargo, largely dependent on competing Southeast Asian transshipment hubs

points.point: On the last call before the Vizhinjam agreement, capital allocation was described with no reference to any separation, demerger or value-unlocking structure — organic capex first, strategic M&A second, buyback last.
points.quote: Our priority number 1 is to invest in the capacity expansion and creating new capacities. Our priority for strategic M&A.

points.point: Asked by Pulkit Patni (Goldman Sachs) whether a possible group shipbuilding venture would sit inside Adani Ports or in a separate entity, the CEO refused the business on competency grounds rather than discussing any separate-entity structure.
points.quote: I don't think that's our competency. Our competency is to build the infrastructure ecosystem and to run it efficiently and effectively that's our competency.

points.point: Closing remarks frame integration across ports, logistics and marine as the core competitive advantage — the opposite of a separation thesis.
points.quote: our strength, which is scale, but and which is integrated, right, makes us different than others.

points.point: Even in the quarter when the AHSL amalgamation was intimated (letter of November 4, 2025, the call date), the stated direction of travel was one consolidated global platform, with no mention of the scheme on the call.
points.quote: Looking ahead, we are building a truly global integrated transport platform.

points.point: What investors actually asked for and received was segment-level transparency — separate reporting for international ports, marine and trucking/IFN — not legal or structural separation of any business.
points.quote: As our business evolves, and thanks to your feedback. We are introducing new reporting lines.

points.point: Management repeatedly argued the case for keeping the verticals together, on the grounds that the port network feeds logistics market share — a direct integration argument against carving out logistics.
points.quote: Now what we want to do is use the port's network to increase the market share of our inland logistics and this is where, we are going to focus on capex, on the logistic business

points.point: The founding frame for the period under review is an integrated utility absorbing commodity and geographic risk across one portfolio, which management uses to justify holding the businesses in one entity.
points.quote: During the period, we continued to strengthen our value proposition as an integrated transport utility company with unmatched waterfront to last mile connectivity solutions.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation, so no per-entity expectations are given. For the Vizhinjam 49% sell-down they expect faster ramp-up and volume visibility, more Bangladesh and East Africa relay cargo, and USD 1.397bn unlocked for growth, while APSEZ keeps 51%, board control and consolidation. For the AHSL amalgamation into APSEZ, no margin, capital or valuation benefit is stated anywhere.
verdict.gaps: No rationale for the AHSL merger; no call discusses either deal. Feb 2026 transcript duplicates the Apr 2026 call; Aug 2025 unreadable — those windows unverifiable.

verdict.rationale: The separation on record is the transfer of BlackBuck Ltd.'s Loads Business Undertaking — the freight-matching business comprising the classifieds load board and the full-stack 'Superloads' brokerage — as a going concern, on a slump-sale basis, to BlackBuck Transport Services Private Limited (BTSPL), a wholly owned subsidiary 'engaged in business of Transportation and Storage', approved by the Board on the Audit Committee's recommendation on October 12, 2026. The only rationale management put in writing is operational: 'Restructuring to organize its businesses under dedicated wholly owned subsidiary and improve operational efficiency.' The scale given is small and asset-light: FY26 revenue of the transferred undertaking was INR 887.43 million, 12.6% of the Company's standalone total income, while its net worth at March 31, 2026 was INR 9.88 million, just 0.07% of standalone net worth — so the lump-sum cash consideration, set at the Net Asset Value / book value on the closing date, is immaterial and the deal is a related-party transaction with its own subsidiary rather than a sale of value. It is deliberately structured outside a scheme of arrangement, via a Business Transfer Agreement, so Regulation 37A does not apply, there is no NCLT process, no share-exchange ratio, and 'no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company' — i.e. a ring-fencing of the business inside the group, not a demerger to shareholders. The earnings calls never mention the transfer, but they supply the operating logic the filing compresses: loads is the one vertical booked at gross value, forcing management to invent a 'net revenues' metric in Aug 2025; by Feb 2026 Rajesh Yabaji described core and growth as having 'literally no connection' with 'pretty independent' costs and called Superloads 'essentially a independent business which has basically its losses'; and it was the loss-making, 250-person, hub-by-hub expansion (Bangalore/Hyderabad to 9–14 cities, then 10 more) that was diluting consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin from ~36% to ~31%. It also follows the company's established pattern of parking distinct or regulated businesses in dedicated wholly owned subsidiaries — Blackbuck Finserve (NBFC; INR 140 crore of IPO proceeds plus a INR 100 crore rights issue in Dec 2025) and TZF Logistics (PPI licence from RBI, INR 21.99 crore rights issue in Sept 2026 partly to meet 'regulatory requirements applicable to PPI issuers') — with the dormant ZZ Logistics struck off in May 2026. Nothing in these texts shows any investor, lender or partner asking for the separation; investors asked only for segment-level disclosure, which management repeatedly deferred as 'too early'.
verdict.evolution: The loads business was described on May 27, 2025 as the pivot of classifieds into brokerage (five hubs, playbook-building, 6–8% take rate), and on Aug 5, 2025 it was first reported as a separate 'growth business' line whose gross-level accounting forced the new 'net revenues' metric. On Nov 5, 2025 management went 'aggressive' — four hubs to 14, team from ~50 to ~250 people — and on Feb 5, 2026 Yabaji explicitly framed core and growth as independent businesses with independent costs and independent investment decisions; on May 19, 2026 he conceded Superloads' pace 'could have been much stronger' and declined to split profitability, saying it was 'still too early'. The legal separation then appears with no prior signalling: the Board approved the slump sale of the Loads Business Undertaking to BTSPL on October 12, 2026, with the BTA still to be executed and closing subject to conditions precedent. No earnings call in the 36-month window discusses, previews or explains it.

points.point: Board, on Audit Committee recommendation, approved transferring the Loads Business Undertaking as a going concern to wholly owned subsidiary BlackBuck Transport Services Private Limited (BTSPL) on a slump-sale basis on October 12, 2026; the BTA is yet to be executed and closing is subject to conditions precedent.
points.quote: the Board of Directors of BlackBuck Limited (Formerly known as Zinka Logistics Solutions Limited) ("Company"), at its meeting held today i.e. Monday, October 12, 2026, inter-alia, on recommendation of the Audit Committee, have considered and approved the transfer of Loads Business Undertaking ("Transferred Business Undertaking") as a going concern to BlackBuck Transport Services Private Limited, Wholly Owned Subsidiary ("BTSPL") on a slump sale basis.

points.point: The entire stated rationale is one line: housing businesses in a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary and operational efficiency. No mention of margins, capital allocation, valuation, funding or partner/lender demands.
points.quote: Restructuring to organize its businesses under dedicated wholly owned subsidiary and improve operational efficiency.

points.point: Size of the carved-out business: FY26 revenue INR 887.43 million, 12.6% of standalone total income, but net worth of only INR 9.88 million, 0.07% of standalone net worth — a revenue-heavy, capital-light, gross-booked undertaking.
points.quote: Revenue of the Transferred Business Undertaking for FY 2025-2026 is INR 887.43 Million, representing 12.6% of the Total Income of the Company on a standalone basis.

points.point: Consideration is lump-sum cash at Net Asset Value / book value on the closing date — i.e. no value is being crystallised or marked up; it is an intra-group related-party transfer to a 100% subsidiary, not a sale to a third party.
points.quote: The Company will receive a lump sum cash consideration for the Proposed Transfer, which shall be based on the Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Transferred Business determined as on the Closing Date of the Proposed Transfer.

points.point: Deliberately structured as a BTA outside any scheme of arrangement, so Regulation 37A / NCLT process does not apply, and shareholders get nothing directly — the shareholding pattern is unchanged.
points.quote: There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the slump sale of relevant business undertaking of the Company to its wholly owned subsidiary i.e., BTSPL.

points.point: Pattern of the same playbook elsewhere: the payments entity TZF Logistics got a INR 21.99 crore rights-issue infusion on September 28, 2026, expressly tied to growth and to PPI regulatory capital under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act; the NBFC Blackbuck Finserve took INR 140 crore of IPO proceeds plus INR 100 crore of rights issue on December 15, 2025.
points.quote: Further the investment will also support the subsidiary in meeting the regulatory requirements applicable to PPI issuers under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 and the RBI regulations.

points.point: Loads/Superloads is the only vertical booked at gross value, which distorted the consolidated P&L and forced management to introduce a 'net revenues' metric (gross margin of Superloads added to other operating revenue) — an accounting mismatch a separate entity cleanly isolates.
points.quote: Important point to note is that Super Loads business in an accounting terms happens to be at a gross level, right?

points.point: Management already treated loads as a standalone, loss-making business with no cost or P&L connection to core payments/telematics, requiring HO-cost allocation to be understood at all.
points.quote: We need to basically split this after allocating the HO cost into what is the core business EBITDA margin and what is the new business EBITDA margin because at the business line vertical level there is literally no connection in terms of both these businesses.

points.point: Superloads' losses and its independent investment decisions were explicitly described as driving the blended margin, with further 'depression' in EBITDA promised if they chose to out-invest.
points.quote: And this is essentially a independent business which has basically its losses.

points.point: Investors (Ankush Agarwal, Surge Capital) pressed for separate core vs growth profitability disclosure because the blended number made modelling impossible; management agreed but deferred it as too early — the closest thing on record to an outside party asking for separation, and it was about disclosure, not legal structure.
points.quote: Fully agree with you but we believe it's still too early we will evaluate this down the line when can we improve the visibility and I definitely understand your pain because modelling is tough for you.

points.point: Context for 'organizing businesses': management was already re-sorting verticals between 'core' and 'growth' buckets as they matured, saying vehicle finance would exit investment mode and migrate to core — a narrative reclassification that the Oct 2026 slump sale makes a legal one for loads.
points.quote: Vehicle finance business probably by the end of this financial year would no longer be in the investment mode and would start probably churning cash flows which will also enable us to move that into a core business kind of a trajectory from a narrative perspective.

points.point: The scale-up that preceded the carve-out: from four hubs to 14-15 within six months, with the Superloads team going from under 50 to about 250 people, and management admitting they could not yet model the resulting contribution or losses.
points.quote: we plan to open 10 new hubs and take this number in the range of 14-15 hubs over the course of next six months.

points.point: Why loads needed a different vehicle: the earlier enterprise freight model failed on working capital and was exited, and classifieds could not deliver trust or customer experience — hence the first-party Superloads brokerage with end-to-end payment flow through BlackBuck.
points.quote: But in classifieds, because it's a verticalized classifieds platform, delivering high trust and delivering strong customer experience is really not possible.
