verdict.rationale: What is being 'separated' is not a demerger or spin-off: it is a 40% minority dilution of Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited (NAIF), NAM India's wholly owned alternatives (AIF) subsidiary, to DWS Group GmbH & Co. KGaA via a fresh issue of 3,40,000 equity shares (face value INR 10) at INR 21,569 per share for INR 733,34,60,000 (~INR 733.35 crore), after which NAIF 'will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary' but 'continue to remain as a subsidiary' — so NAM India keeps control and consolidation, and the filing states 'No impact' on management or control of the listed entity. The stated purpose in the Scheme documents is 'to jointly develop and build a leading alternative investment funds franchise in India along with DWS'; management's own explanation on the calls is purely about distribution reach, not about fixing a problem inside the business. Sikka's logic, repeated across three calls, is that NAM India is strong domestically and has 'very strong Japanese access' through parent Nippon Life Insurance, but 'Europe access was lower', and DWS — described by him as 'the largest asset manager of Europe' (EUR 1,085 bn AUM at Dec 31, 2025, ~5,000 employees per the filing) — is the channel to bring European money into India, 'especially the alternate and the infrastructure side.' The collaboration is explicitly wider than the JV: the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation says NAM India and DWS 'will also work closely in other areas including passive investment products and global distribution,' and Sikka added it will help the mutual fund business on 'capability of international funds, ETFs, and also offshore money.' Scale context given: NAIF's cumulative AIF commitments were INR 95.8 bn (Q1 FY27, +18% YoY), up from INR 74.1 bn at Q4 FY25; NAIF contributed INR 101.96 crore of turnover (4.6%) and INR 102.18 crore of net worth (3.1%) in the last financial year; non-MF products are ~8% of gross revenue and MF was 91% of FY26 revenue; and Parag confirmed the AIF entity is already 'a profitable company. It's a profitable franchise.' The background pressure visible in the calls is the persistent failure of the offshore/international engine to scale — offshore AUM went from INR 172 bn (Sep-2024) to INR 161 bn (Sep-2025) to INR 139 bn (Mar-2026), and Sikka conceded 'we would have expected offshore contribution to be higher… it is a little binary' — so the DWS tie-up reads as the fix for foreign-inflow access rather than for anything in the domestic MF franchise. Nobody — no investor, lender or regulator — is said to have asked for it; the counterparty link is related-party-adjacent only in that promoter Nippon Life Insurance 'presently holds 5.00% stake in DWS,' and DWS had already been listed in Apr 2025 as one of the Nippon Life network entities through which offshore business was being sourced. The deal is conditional on SEBI and CCI approvals plus consent of NAIF's AIF investors, with a 12-month long-stop date, and the SHA gives DWS board and senior-management appointment rights, reserved matters requiring its consent, a put option, exit rights, non-compete, transfer restrictions and lock-in.
verdict.evolution: Through Jul 2024 and Oct 2024 AIF is only flagged as 'an important focus area' with senior hiring and seed capital, and in Apr 2025 DWS appears merely as one of several Nippon Life network entities (with GENKAI, BBLAM, Cathay) through which offshore money already trickles in, while Nov 2025 shows management conceding offshore is 'a small part of our overall business, but the ambition is to grow bigger.' The idea surfaces formally at the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, held Jan 29, 2026), which discloses the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation of a strategic collaboration with DWS taking 'up to 40%' of NAIF plus cooperation in passives and global distribution — still only a non-binding agreement, with Sikka declining detail beyond 'the idea will be to get more global flow into India.' By the Apr 2026 call it is called a JV and justified as access to overseas money 'especially the alternate and the infrastructure side' plus spillover to the MF business; the Mar 14, 2026 filings then harden it into signed SHA/SSA with a fixed 40%, INR 733.35 crore price and SEBI/CCI conditions. At the Jul 2026 call the stake is confirmed as 40%, approvals are still awaited, the Japan-plus-Europe positioning is sharpened ('one side it will be Europe and one side it will be Japan'), and unit economics are declined as 'too early.'

points.point: Pre-history: DWS is already named as one of the Nippon Life group entities through which NAM India's offshore business is sourced, alongside Japan, Thailand and Taiwan affiliates.
points.quote: Till now, if you see where most of our business that is coming, international business is coming – you can look at slide in the presentation, whether it is coming through DWS, whether it is from the GENKAI which is Japan, BBLAM which is Bangkok Life Asset Management and Cathay, which is Taiwan.

points.point: Context for the deal: the non-MF businesses (AIF subsidiary, offshore subsidiary) are tiny in the mix but are the stated growth ambition; yields on these products range 60–120 bps versus ~36 bps blended MF yield.
points.quote: Currently, it's a small part of our overall business, but the ambition is to grow bigger.

points.point: First disclosure of the separation: the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation of DWS acquiring up to 40% of the AIF subsidiary via fresh equity, plus a wider collaboration on passives and global distribution.
points.quote: Our Board of Directors at their meeting on November 13, 2025, authorised the Company to enter into a strategic collaboration with DWS Group (a leading European Asset Manager), wherein DWS intends to acquire a minority stake of up to 40% in Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited by subscribing to fresh issuance of equity shares.

points.point: Management's one-line rationale at first disclosure, delivered in the same breath as the admission that offshore inflows have disappointed and are 'binary'.
points.quote: As I mentioned in my speech earlier, our AIF is getting into a JV with DWS. Again, the idea will be to get more global flow into India.

points.point: The problem the tie-up is meant to address: offshore contribution has undershot management's own expectations for years, partly on USD-INR, and is lumpy institutional-mandate driven rather than predictable like SIPs.
points.quote: I have mentioned in past also - clearly we would have expected offshore contribution to be higher. It has taken a little more time; it is a little binary.

points.point: Purpose restated as sourcing overseas capital specifically for alternates and infrastructure, still under a non-binding agreement at that date.
points.quote: The idea is we clearly see an opportunity to get a lot of overseas money and especially the alternate and the infrastructure side.

points.point: The JV is explicitly not ring-fenced to AIF — management expects collateral capability transfer into the mutual fund business (international funds, ETFs, offshore money).
points.quote: Also, as far as the JV is concerned, it will also help in collaboration not only in the AIF where it will be a JV, but also with the mutual fund business, you know, to as in whether from a capability of international funds, ETFs, and also offshore money.

points.point: The strategic gap being closed is geographic: Japan access was already strong via the parent; Europe was the missing leg.
points.quote: The idea is to keep getting ready as India keeps, you know, getting stronger. More foreign money will come into India and I think building capabilities access, we were always very strong in Japan. So now this JV gives us an access to Europe.

points.point: Management also flags DWS's passive/ETF strength as a reason the partnership could extend to product launches in India if investor demand appears.
points.quote: And to your earlier question, having DWS with us, you know, and DWS is one of the largest international players both in not also in ETF space, but also passives, you know.

points.point: The signed deal (Mar 14, 2026): SHA with the Company, NAIF and DWS plus an SSA, with the stated object of jointly building an India alternatives franchise and DWS taking 40%.
points.quote: To jointly develop and build a leading alternative investment funds franchise in India along with DWS and in pursuance thereof DWS has agreed to acquire a minority stake of 40 percent in NAIF.

points.point: Price and mechanics: INR 733.35 crore of primary capital into NAIF for 3,40,000 fresh shares at INR 21,569 each — money goes into the subsidiary, not to the listed parent as sale proceeds.
points.quote: DWS has agreed to pay a sum of INR 733,34,60,000/- (Indian Rupees Seven Hundred Thirty-Three Crores Thirty-Four Lakhs Sixty Thousand only) as consideration for acquiring 40% equity stake in NAIF by subscribing to 3,40,000 equity shares [having a face value of INR 10/- (Indian Rupees Ten) per share], to be issued by NAIF by way of preferential allotment.

points.point: Scale of what is being diluted: NAIF is ~4.6% of turnover and ~3.1% of net worth — i.e. the separation touches a small slice of the group.
points.quote: During the last financial year, NAIF contributed INR 101.96 crore to the Turnover (4.6%) and INR 102.18 crore to the Net Worth (3.1%) of the Company.

points.point: It is a dilution, not a disposal — NAM India retains consolidation and, per the filing, control of the listed entity is unaffected.
points.quote: After the said issuance of equity shares, NAIF will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company and it would continue to remain as a subsidiary.

points.point: Governance price of the deal: DWS gets board and senior-management appointment rights, veto matters, a put option and exit rights, with non-compete, transfer and lock-in restrictions on NAM India.
points.quote: The SHA provides few customarily required covenants which includes inter alia, provisions w.r.t. board composition, senior management appointment, reserved matters requiring DWS's consent, put-option, exit rights granted to DWS, governance related matters, information-sharing obligations, provisions with respect to non-compete, transfer restrictions and lock-in provisions.

points.point: Conditionality and timeline: SEBI and CCI approvals plus consent of NAIF's AIF investors, within a 12-month long-stop date.
points.quote: The proposed transaction is expected to be completed within 12 months from the execution of the Agreement Date ("Long Stop Date") or such other date mutually agreed between the Parties, subject to receipt of regulatory approvals from SEBI and Competition Commission of India and requisite consent of investors of the AIFs managed by NAIF and upon fulfilment of other conditions precedent stipulated in the SSA.

points.point: The counterparty is not formally related, but promoter Nippon Life Insurance already owns 5% of DWS — the plausible origin of the relationship.
points.quote: DWS is not related to the Company in any manner, however, Nippon Life Insurance Company (i.e. the promoter of the Company) presently holds 5.00% stake in DWS.

points.point: Post-signing framing: DWS as Europe's largest asset manager is the whole point of the JV, with approvals still pending.
points.quote: But specifically, and I'd like to touch upon the JV with DWS, we believe from Europe a lot more money can come to India and DWS is the largest asset manager of Europe and the JV has been done with that in mind.

points.point: The competitive-positioning argument: a dual Europe-plus-Japan access channel is claimed as a unique edge for capturing foreign money into India.
points.quote: We have very strong Japanese access. But Europe access was lower -- and we will become one of the unique asset management companies in India where on one side it will be Europe and one side it will be Japan.

points.point: Management refuses to quantify the economics of the deal — no yields, no AUM or revenue contribution.
points.quote: I think it would be too early. We see a very big opportunity there.

points.point: The entity being part-sold is already profitable on its own, and the AIF book stands at INR 95.8 bn of cumulative commitments, up 18% YoY, with fundraising live across listed equity, private credit and direct VC.
points.quote: Yeah, so it's a profitable company. It's a profitable franchise.

verdict.what_management_expects: For NAIF: European capital into Indian alternates and infrastructure, INR 733.35 crore of fresh primary capital inside the subsidiary, DWS board/veto/put rights, and a jointly built 'leading' India AIF franchise that stays a consolidated, already-profitable subsidiary. For NAM India: Europe access added to its Japan access, spillover capability in international funds, ETFs, passives and global distribution. No margin, capital-release or valuation benefit was ever quantified.
verdict.gaps: No margin, valuation, capital-use or AUM targets; why 40%; how the INR 733 cr is deployed; NAIF standalone P&L; put/exit pricing; dilution impact on consolidated EPS; no investor or lender demand cited.

verdict.segment_name: Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited (Nippon India AIF) — not a reportable segment; the documents report a single primary segment, "asset management services"
verdict.measure_notes: No profit line exists for the AIF business. Segment Information notes in all three annual reports state the primary segment is asset management services and that there are no separate reportable segments under Ind AS 108 (FY2024 standalone/consolidated notes add that portfolio management services do not qualify as a reportable segment). Therefore no segment result / EBIT / EBITDA / PBT, and no external or inter-segment revenue, is disclosed for the AIF franchise on these pages.

years.source: Annual Report 2024 — page 231 (standalone Note 24) and page 285 (consolidated Note 24): single segment, no AIF breakout
Annual Report 2025 — page 246 (standalone Note 24) and page 296 (consolidated Note 24): single segment, no AIF breakout
Annual Report 2026 — page 267 (standalone Note 25) and page 317 (consolidated Note 25): single segment, no AIF breakout

verdict.not_found: Pages carry no AIF revenue, operating profit, PAT or AUM. Only NAM-India's own "Equity (AIF Schemes + Others)" investment-book holdings (e.g. INR 1,312 mn at Sep 30, 2026) appear — balance-sheet exposure, not AIF business P&L.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not the paints business but the Powder Coatings business division (Interpon) together with the Bangalore International Research Centre (IRC), which Akzo Nobel India sold back to its then parent AkzoNobel NV by slump sale, while simultaneously buying in the decorative IP including the Dulux brand. Management framed it as the outcome of AkzoNobel NV's October 2024 portfolio review, whose stated intent was to redeploy capital into the group's core paints and coatings business with initial focus on Deco South Asia, and whose stated premise was that although India was outperforming the industry there was 'a strategic mismatch between the group's priorities versus the India operation.' The request came from the parent, not from the Indian company: Rajgopal said the globe asked to carve out powder and R&D because AkzoNobel is the global No.1 in powder coatings with roughly twice the share of the No.2 player and wanted its distinctive technology and raw materials kept internal, while the IRC was a captive cost centre doing 99% of its work for the global automotive and specialty coatings unit (McLaren Mercedes F1 colour testing) and 'nothing for India', costing about ₹50 crore, with India's own decorative and coatings R&D labs separate and self-sufficient (Dulux Aquatech was created in India). Management stressed there were no dis-synergies: powder had no technology dependency, a completely different manufacturing process and largely separate facilities (Bangalore, Thane and the recently built Gwalior site). The economics were set by two SEBI-registered valuers, KPMG and Grant Thornton, at the Audit Chair's instruction: powder at ₹20.7 billion (range ₹20.6–20.7bn, about 24.5x trailing EBITDA on a business that is roughly 10% of the company), the IRC at ₹700 million (DCF range ₹579–700m), against the decorative IP bought for ₹11.5 billion (royalty-relief, range ₹11.5–11.8bn, relieving a 3% decorative royalty of about ₹68–69 crore plus five years of 11% growth), netting a pre-tax inflow of about ₹990 crore with roughly 14% tax — and management deliberately 'taken the highest of what we sell and the lowest of what we buy' for minority shareholders, with net proceeds paid out as dividend. The second, deeper rationale was strategic freedom: owning Dulux in perpetuity (covering India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan) ended a royalty of about ₹60–65 crore a year that was redeployed into growth, and removed the MNC constraint management repeatedly blamed for lost volume — global firms 'constrained by percentages, percent margin, percent EBITDA, right, not absolutes', global pricing modules that left Dulux 5–9% (in places 7–9%) overpriced versus competition, which the trade had been asking them to fix for years. AkzoNobel retained the industrial/performance coatings IP and stayed technology partner with royalty continuing, and gave a 36-month non-compete in Indian powder coatings. The residual cost of the carve-out was that certain coil-coating customers and the Dramatone/Acotone colorant export business stayed with the unlisted AkzoNobel Powder Coatings India entity, netting off roughly ₹200 crore of annual revenue, about ₹25 crore a quarter.
verdict.evolution: On the 7 Nov 2024 call management would only say AkzoNobel NV was running a strategic review 'across various businesses' with all options open and with Rajgopal and the CFO recused; by the 7 Feb 2025 call they disclosed that the parent had got in touch in early January asking to buy back powder coatings and the IRC while selling the decorative IP down to the listed entity, and that the Board had authorised KMPs to explore it. The 7 Mar 2025 shareholder meeting put numbers on it — KPMG and Grant Thornton valuations, ₹20.7bn powder, ₹700m IRC, ₹11.5bn Dulux IP, ~₹990 crore net pre-tax to be passed to shareholders, 36-month non-compete, IP in perpetuity — after the binding offer accepted in February 2025 and postal-ballot approval. By 15 May 2025 only Ind AS 105 balance-sheet reclassification had triggered, with a two-month extension taken pending AkzoNobel NV's completion, and the global CEO's timeline was end-June; the 5 Aug 2025 call confirmed the proceeds funded the dividend, and the 7 Nov 2025 call confirmed both slump sales closed via separate business transfer agreements on 1 July 2025 with restated comparatives and decorative royalty ceasing the same date. Thereafter the story shifted from separation to redeployment: on 3 Feb 2026 the ~₹200 crore of retained coil customers and ceased colorant exports was quantified and the ₹60–65 crore royalty saving was being spent on price corrections, and by 14 May 2026, under JSW ownership, the last real-estate sale (₹64.8 crore) completed and the proceeds-funded transformation was being run as a growth and market-share agenda.

points.point: First acknowledgement: the parent's portfolio review was live across businesses, nothing concluded, and Rajgopal and the CFO had recused themselves from the process.
points.quote: We are running a strategic review across various businesses.

points.point: Management positioned the review as aimed at putting the Indian business in a winning position given competitive intensity, not as a problem with the Indian business.
points.quote: They are looking at what exactly are the sort of things that they really want to do?

points.point: The carve-out was initiated by AkzoNobel NV, which asked to take back powder coatings and the R&D centre, leaving the listed entity as liquid coatings plus decorative.
points.quote: But again, to answer this question, this is a request which has come from the globe, and we've been upfront as in the spirit of true governance to immediately notify first to bring it to the Board, inform the Board and the Board has then asked to notify to the stock exchanges, which we've done.

points.point: Stated logic for keeping powder inside the global group: higher value-add and centrally performed R&D development, with powder and liquid kept as two distinct businesses.
points.quote: In the spirit of true disclosure, when the parent got in touch with us and said they wanted to carve out the powder coating business and the R&D business, the thought was to keep the 2 distinct businesses, liquid coatings and basically what the globe believes that they can continue -- if they continuously -- they own, they can see a higher value add, which is in the powder coating business, where there's a lot of R&D development, which is done centrally and the global -- what we call the International Research Center.

points.point: The IRC was explained as a global colour-development facility for automotive and specialty coatings, used as a test bed including for McLaren Mercedes F1, not an India asset.
points.quote: What the International Research Center in Bangalore does, it does the color development for the automotive and specialty coatings.

points.point: The explicit rationale disclosed with the October 2024 review: capital redeployment into core paints and coatings despite India outperforming, because group priorities and the India operation did not match.
points.quote: At the same time, there is a strategic mismatch between the group's priorities versus the India operation.

points.point: Precedent cited: the 2017-18 chemicals divestment, after which revenue CAGR ran 6%, EBIT rose from 8.8% (FY18) to 13.9% (FY24) and EPS from 44 to 94, with ~₹13.8bn (₹303/share) of dividends in five years.
points.quote: So coming to, previously last time we came to the investors, seeking their special approval in terms of mandate is that in 2017-18, and we intended to diverse the chemicals business with their objective to focus on the core of the paints and coatings businesses.

points.point: Why powder specifically: AkzoNobel is global market leader at roughly twice the No.2's share, with distinctive technology and raw materials it wanted to keep internal; powder is about 10% of the company.
points.quote: So look, I think powder coatings we are designed to keep it, because globally we are a market leader with a market share twice the number two player.

points.point: Why the IRC: a captive cost centre, ~₹50 crore spend, recharged to the Netherlands at a 12% markup, doing no India work since each India business has its own separate R&D lab.
points.quote: And along with that, we also told them to keep the R&D centre because it's a cost centre which only does 99% of the work for the global paint, automotive and specialty coatings business unit.

points.point: No operational entanglement claimed between powder and the retained businesses, which supported a clean slump sale.
points.quote: There's no dependency in technologies, with completely different manufacturing process.

points.point: Valuation governance: two SEBI-registered valuers (KPMG, Grant Thornton); powder ₹20.7bn (~24.5x trailing EBITDA, range ₹20.6–20.7bn), IRC ₹700m (range ₹579–700m), Dulux decorative IP bought at ₹11.5bn (royalty-relief, range ₹11.5–11.8bn) — deliberately skewed for minorities.
points.quote: So we've taken the highest of what we sell and the lowest of what we buy. Because we said that's the best for the minority shareholders, right?

points.point: The IP bought in is a perpetual full transfer of Dulux and related decorative brands plus knowledge, covering India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan, relieving a 3% decorative royalty (~₹68–69 crore) plus five years of 11% growth.
points.quote: It's a full transfer for perpetuity

points.point: Shareholder payout was the headline benefit: about ₹990 crore pre-tax inflow, taxed at roughly 14% of consideration, on top of the ₹70/share 70th-anniversary dividend.
points.quote: Shareholders are going to get quite a bounty.

points.point: Protection obtained in the business transfer agreement: a 36-month standstill by AkzoNobel NV in Indian powder coatings post execution.
points.quote: The Powder Coatings business is concerned. Business transfer agreement would be AkzoNobel India Limited as it's divesting the powder coatings though AkzoNobel NV would not be participating in the powder coatings business for the next 36 months post execution.

points.point: Timing slipped and disclosure was withheld: only Ind AS 105 balance-sheet reclassification had triggered, a two-month extension was taken pending AkzoNobel NV completing the separation, and no ex-powder operating numbers were given.
points.quote: Until the point of time that Akzo Nobel N.V. completes the elements of what the powder coating separation is, which is why we've taken two months extension, we would not be in a position to give you operations-wise numbers.

points.point: Confirmation that the powder (Interpon) sale to AkzoNobel Global was what funded the special dividend, with powder now housed in a separate unlisted AkzoNobel company.
points.quote: Interpon is a powder coating product which has now been a part of the transaction where we have sold it to AkzoNobel Global, which is the reason why we got the money and the dividend that we were able to give.

points.point: The dividend mechanics spelt out: sale proceeds, net of the cost of the Dulux IP rights and net of taxes, were distributed in toto to shareholders with no change in dividend policy.
points.quote: What we have done is as we wanted to always delight our shareholders as a part of our promise to the shareholders that look, once the AkzoNobel decided to buy out the powder coating and the IRC business, net of the IP rights and the brand Dulux rights that we have got, net of the taxes is the dividend that has got distributed amongst all the shareholders in toto.

points.point: The strategic problem the separation and IP purchase were meant to solve: an MNC owner judged on percentage margins rather than absolute profit, which capped investment behind Dulux.
points.quote: The global firms are constrained by percentages, percent margin, percent EBITDA, right, not absolutes which Indian firms look at.

points.point: The counterpart expectation: unlocking Dulux by putting investment behind it under new ownership, with AkzoNobel retaining International, Sikkens and Vehicle Refinish brands licensed to the new entity.
points.quote: I believe that, look, if the brand is unleashed to its true potential, the ability of the brand to unlock growth will be significantly higher.

points.point: Process confirmed: a binding offer from AkzoNobel NV accepted in February 2025, postal-ballot shareholder approval, two separate business transfer agreements, closed 1 July 2025 with restated comparatives.
points.quote: As you are aware, in February '25, we accepted the binding offer from AkzoNobel NV for the purchase of our Power Coatings business and International Research Center.

points.point: Powder and IRC were material enough that prior-year reported numbers became a misleading benchmark, forcing provisional restated like-for-like disclosure in the investor deck.
points.quote: Given that these are material contributors to the business as a comparison with our last year reported numbers will not be the right indicator of our performance.

points.point: First cash benefit of the IP purchase landed: decorative royalty ceased 1 July 2025, while industrial/performance coatings royalty continues to AkzoNobel as technology owner.
points.quote: I think, Aniruddha, we have fully factored in that the royalty, which we pay for the Decorative IP, ceased to exist effective 1st of July 2025.

points.point: The hidden cost of the carve-out quantified: the unlisted AkzoNobel Powder Coatings India entity also retained certain coil-coating customers, and Dramatone/Acotone colorant exports to Southeast Asia and the Middle East ceased — about ₹200 crore annually, ~₹25 crore a quarter.
points.quote: So hence, like to like, the total amount that got netted off was in the range of about approximately 200 crores.

points.point: Royalty saving sized and earmarked: roughly ₹60–65 crore a year from owning the decorative IP, redeployed into growth initiatives and market-share gain rather than dropped to the bottom line.
points.quote: In the month of June 2025, we acquired the decorative IP, and the Dulux brand is now owned by Akzo Nobel India Limited listed entity. So, the royalty ceased to exist which translates to roughly around 60 crores to 65 crores depending on the revenue trajectory.

points.point: The freedom gained from separation showed up as pricing: Dulux had been 5–9% overpriced under AkzoNobel's global pricing modules, which the trade had been asking them to fix for years.
points.quote: And we did see that we were usually overpriced between 5% and 9% which is what had led to volume erosion.

points.point: Asset monetisation continued after the carve-out: the last Board-approved real estate sale completed March 2026, contributing ₹64.8 crore of income, alongside a ₹50/share final dividend.
points.quote: And finally, the additional thing, which I would like to add on here is that the last of the real estate sale, for which we took the Board approval was completed in March 2026, which translated to INR64.8 crores of income from the real estate assets.

points.point: Accounting outcome of the separation booked in Q2 FY26: ₹18,925 million pre-tax gain, ₹79 million impairment of PPE rendered unusable, ₹71 million reimbursement, ₹2,704 million current tax and ₹544 million deferred tax on the capitalised IPRs.
points.quote: The Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025 are not comparable with the corresponding previous periods due to the slump sale of the Powder Coatings business division and the International Research Center division during the quarter ended 30 September 2025.

points.point: Lenders now constrain any repeat: JSW Paints' debenture trust deeds (₹3,300 crore, 30 Oct 2025; ₹2,950 crore, 4 Nov 2026) make demergers, slump sales, asset transfers and corporate reorganisations by JSW Dulux subject to Debenture Trustee consent.
points.quote: Further, with the view towards value preservation, the Issuer has also agreed that certain activities / actions may be carried out by JDL only if JDL meets certain parameters or conditions as set out in the DTD and / or with the consent of the Debenture Trustee and / or as may be permitted in accordance with the terms of the DTD

points.point: Any further disposal of fixed assets beyond permitted limits triggers a mandatory monetisation event, with proceeds applied to redeem debentures — a lender-imposed leakage of future separation proceeds away from JSW Dulux shareholders.
points.quote: Further, if JDL undertakes any Disposal of fixed assets other than as permitted under the terms of the DTD, it will result in occurrence of a monetisation event and the Issuer will be required to redeem such Debentures for an amount equivalent to the aggregate proceeds received as consideration from such Disposal.

verdict.what_management_expects: AkzoNobel NV keeps its global No.1 powder technology and captive colour-development centre and redeploys capital to core. The listed entity becomes a focused India decorative-plus-liquid-coatings play: ~₹990 crore pre-tax proceeds paid out as dividend, Dulux owned in perpetuity, ~₹60–65 crore annual royalty redeployed into pricing and growth, freedom from global EBIT%-driven pricing, 14.5–15% EBITDA while chasing volume and share.
verdict.gaps: No powder/IRC standalone revenue or margins (single reportable segment); why Akzo kept ~₹200 crore coil customers and colorant exports; stranded costs and dis-synergies unquantified.

verdict.segment_name: Powder Coatings business division and International Research Center (IRC) division (carved-out / AkzoNobel-retained business)
verdict.unit: ₹ million (annual report notes); ₹ crore in investor presentations
verdict.measure_notes: No profit line exists for this business on the tagged pages. Both the standalone and consolidated segment notes (Ind AS 108) state there is only ONE reportable segment, 'Paints' — so no segment result/EBIT/EBITDA is disclosed for Powder Coatings or IRC. Revenue shown in the segment notes is total entity external revenue (domestic + overseas), not segment or inter-segment split. Investor presentations give entity P&L EXCLUDING the carved-out business (LY restated, 'provisional, unaudited, based on Mgmt estimates'), plus reported entity P&L, but never the carved-out business's own revenue/EBITDA/PAT. Only transaction-level items for the divestment are disclosed: sale of Powder Coatings business division and International Research Center division to fellow subsidiaries of ₹21,922 million (Annual Report 2026 — page 81), and exceptional items of ₹1,874.2 crore (pre-tax proceeds from sale of Powder, IRC and related costs) in Q2 FY26 (Presentation Nov 2026 — page 13).

years.source: Annual Report 2024 — page 142 (standalone) and page 210 (consolidated): single 'Paints' segment, no Powder/IRC figures
Annual Report 2025 — page 156 (standalone) and page 230 (consolidated): single 'Paints' segment, no Powder/IRC figures
Annual Report 2026 — page 80 (standalone) and page 114 (consolidated): single 'Paints' segment; only sale consideration ₹21,922 mn on page 81

verdict.not_found: No standalone revenue, EBITDA/EBIT or PAT for Powder Coatings or IRC in any year or quarter. Pages carry only total-entity figures, entity P&L excluding the carved-out business, sale consideration ₹21,922 mn, and ₹1,874.2 Cr exceptional gain.

verdict.what_is_spun: No demerger: wholly owned PVPL's entire stake in associate BuildNext, home design and project management services, transferred to JSW One
demerged_business_names: JSW One Platforms Limited (acquirer, shares received)
verdict.reason: "We found strategic synergies in doing this transaction"; BuildNext "has a good home in JSW One" and "is best served with an owner like JSW who can provide its scale and profitability."
verdict.insiders: Promoter/promoter group/group companies have no interest in Buildnext; buyer JSW One is not promoter group. Consideration is JSW One shares to PVPL; "our shareholding will be insignificant in JSW One."
verdict.hidden_value: Buildnext is sub-scale: FY25 revenue Rs 18.38 cr (0.04% of consolidated), PAT Rs (9.11) cr, net worth Rs (1.87) cr. Pidilite instead takes unlisted JSW One stock; Finemake similarly exited. Parent cash ~Rs 3,000 crores.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No scheme of arrangement, no shares distributed to Pidilite shareholders, nothing listed; transferred business was 0.04% of consolidated revenue.
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — no listing of a demerged entity in the documents; expected completion of the Buildnext transfer was "10th August, 2026" (filing dated 29 April 2026), and on the 8 May 2026 call an analyst referred to "a plan for an IPO" at JSW One, which management did not confirm
verdict.read_next: The Share Swap Agreement's agreed valuation and PVPL's resulting percentage stake in JSW One — withheld "for confidentiality reasons."
verdict.quote: And we felt that the business is best served with an owner like JSW who can provide its scale and profitability.

verdict.rationale: On the record supplied, the "separation" is not a new divestiture announced by NMDC Steel Limited (NSL, scrip NSLNISP / BSE 543768 / CSE 74920) — it is the already-completed demerger of the NISP business (NMDC Iron & Steel Plant, Nagarnar, Dist. Bastar, Chhattisgarh, a 3 MTPA-class greenfield integrated plant) out of NMDC Ltd., the iron-ore mining parent, into NSL as the "Resulting Company" (CIN L27310CT2015GOI001618). The stated reason is entirely a Government of India privatisation mechanic, not an operating or synergy argument: the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs gave in-principle approval on 27 October 2016 for strategic disinvestment of several CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd., and then on 14 October 2020 approved the demerger of NISP from NMDC together with strategic disinvestment of the resulting entity by selling the entire GoI stake. In other words, the carve-out exists so that the steel plant could be made a separately listed, separately saleable entity, leaving NMDC Ltd. as a pure mining company; the asker is the sovereign owner through CCEA, not investors, lenders or a JV partner. The transaction terms set out in the Preliminary Information Memorandum and the Request for Expression of Interest are that GoI divests 50.79% of NSL along with management control to a strategic buyer, and will additionally offer 10% of NSL to NMDC Ltd. once the strategic buyer has been identified through the bidding process. The scheme also allocated legacy exposure to the parent: the Rs 111.19 Cr GST input-credit dispute for July 2017–March 2021 (Rs 8.45 Cr paid, Rs 45.90 Cr dropped, Rs 56.40 Cr in abeyance before the Bilaspur High Court, Rs 0.35 Cr under appeal) is pre-demerger, so NMDC Ltd. files the appeals "as per the demerger scheme." Nothing in the filings claims the separation improves margins, capital allocation or valuation; the only measurable consequence disclosed is that standing alone cost NSL its parent's credit umbrella — rating fell from AAA to A- on demerger (NCD coupon 7.30% to 8.80% from 16.02.2023), then to BBB+ (9.05% from 5 June 2024), with the Rs 523.80 Cr NCDs rated "ICRA BBB+ Rating Watch with Developing Implications" and Ind A-/Negative until redemption on 28.08.2025, and the SBI rupee term loan of Rs 4,476.20 Cr (drawn Rs 4,475.81 Cr) repricing off external rating from 7.1% to 12.45% w.e.f. 01.03.2025 before being repositioned at NSL's request to 8.70% (12.04.2025), 8.45% (12.10.2025) and 8.40% (12.01.2026). Financially the standalone entity moved from a FY25 loss before tax of Rs 3,321.72 Cr on revenue of Rs 8,503.05 Cr (PAT Rs -2,373.78 Cr, EPS -8.10) to FY26 revenue of Rs 13,641.81 Cr with PBT Rs 75.78 Cr and PAT Rs 58.72 Cr, and Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30.06.2026) revenue Rs 3,661.84 Cr with PBT Rs 73.95 Cr, PAT Rs 50.51 Cr, borrowings Rs 5,056.15 Cr and net worth Rs 13,228.35 Cr — i.e. the asset was handed to the market loss-making and has only just crossed into profit as the sale process remains open.
verdict.evolution: There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the only visible evolution is the repetition of the same two-step CCEA history — 27 October 2016 (in-principle strategic disinvestment of the NISP unit) and 14 October 2020 (demerger of NISP from NMDC plus sale of the entire GoI stake in the resulting entity) — carried verbatim as a note in each of the three filings dated 3 February 2026, 29 May 2026 and 14/15 August 2026, with the PIM/EoI terms (50.79% plus control to a strategic buyer, 10% offered to NMDC Ltd. afterwards) unchanged throughout. What changes across the three is the aftermath rather than the plan: by the 3 February 2026 filing the Rs 523.80 Cr NCDs had been redeemed on 28.08.2025 (principal plus Rs 42.98 Cr interest, net of Rs 4.42 Cr TDS), ending the "Rating Watch with Developing Implications" overhang, and the SBI term loan had been stepped down from the 12.45% post-DCCO reset to 8.45%. By the 14 August 2026 filing the rate is 8.40% (from 12.01.2026), term-loan outstanding is Rs 3,177.27 Cr after Rs 1,298.54 Cr repaid, and the entity is profitable (Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 50.51 Cr) — but no filing records any new stage of the sale, bidder shortlist or revised structure. No fresh separation is announced by NSL in this window; the company reports a single segment and no subsidiaries, JVs or associates.

points.point: Filings of 03.02.2026, 29.05.2026 and 14.08.2026 all trace the separation to CCEA's 27 October 2016 in-principle approval for strategic disinvestment of CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd. — i.e. the sale decision predates the carve-out.
points.quote: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs ("CCEA"), in its meeting dated October 27, 2016, gave in-principle approval for strategic disinvestment ("Strategic Disinvestment") of several CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd.

points.point: The demerger itself was approved on 14 October 2020 expressly as the vehicle for selling the Government's entire holding in the resulting entity — separation as a privatisation enabler, not an operating restructuring.
points.quote: Subsequently, on October 14, 2020, CCEA gave its 'in­principle' approval to the demerger of NISP from NMDC and strategic disinvestment of the resulting entity by selling entire stake of Government of India ("Gol").

points.quote: Accordingly, the interest rate was reset to 12.45% p.a. w.e.f. 01.03.2025. Based on the request of NSL towards repositioning of the interest rate, SBI has revised the interest rate to 8.70% p.a. linked to 3 months MCLR from 12.04.2025.

points.point: Post-separation NSL is a single-business, single-plant entity with nothing further to split — one reportable segment and no subsidiaries, JVs or associates as at 30.06.2026.
points.quote: The Company is engaged in the manufacturing of Iron and Steel Products and generates revenue primarily from Iron and Steel Products which is the only reportable segment of the Company.

verdict.rationale: No demerger or spin-off of a Pidilite operating segment appears anywhere in these texts; the only business separation disclosed is the exit of its venture-stage investments, chiefly BuildNext Construction Solutions Private Limited, a home design and project management services company held as an associate through wholly owned subsidiary Pidilite Ventures Pvt. Ltd. (PVPL). Per the 29 April 2026 Reg. 30 filing, PVPL signed a Share Swap Agreement dated 28 April 2026 with JSW One Platforms Limited and BuildNext to transfer its entire BuildNext shareholding to JSW One, consideration being JSW One shares at a 'mutually agreed valuation' withheld for confidentiality, expected to complete 10 August 2026; as part of the same transaction PVPL agreed to inject up to Rs. 22 crore into BuildNext via CCPS, which on full subscription would have given PVPL majority shareholding on a fully diluted basis. The economics management disclosed are small and loss-making: BuildNext FY25 revenue Rs. 18.38 crore (0.04% of consolidated revenue, versus Rs. 13.87 crore FY24 and Rs. 10.14 crore FY23), PAT of Rs. (9.11) crore and negative net worth of Rs. (1.87) crore. On the 8 May 2026 call Sudhanshu Vats said the reason was 'strategic synergies' and that BuildNext 'has a good home in JSW One', adding that after investing and watching it 'for some time' Pidilite concluded JSW One is 'the right home' to take BuildNext further; Sandeep Batra was blunter — BuildNext was strategic for both sides and 'the business is best served with an owner like JSW who can provide its scale and profitability', so Pidilite was 'very happy to swap' its shareholding, and its resulting JSW One stake will be 'quite insignificant'. Vats framed the residual JSW One shares as, at this moment, a financial investment, consistent with Pidilite's stated habit of taking small stakes in new platforms to look at them more closely, and separately said marketplaces like JSW One and Birla Pivot will go well beyond their own products, so Pidilite will keep evaluating when it is right to sell on one or many of them. The same pattern of pruning sub-scale, loss-making non-core holdings continued after the swap: on 29 September 2026 PVPL agreed to sell its entire stake in associate Finemake Technologies (FY26 revenue Rs. 24.36 crore, 0.06% of consolidated revenue; PAT Rs. (7.82) crore; net worth Rs. (6.18) crore) back to founders Nallu Rajashekar and Sambasiva Rao Chowdary Chana, completion expected 15 October 2026, and on 19 August 2026 step-down subsidiary Nina Percept (Bangladesh) was voluntarily liquidated because it had been 'inoperative since incorporation due to lack of business opportunities'. No investor, lender or partner is said to have asked for any of this — the only external parties named are the counterparties themselves (JSW One, the Finemake founders), and the filings state the deals are not related-party transactions and the buyers are not promoter group.
verdict.evolution: Through Aug 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 calls there is no mention of separating any business — only portfolio-level housekeeping: the FY24 Pulvitec Brazil divestment and Pidilite USA wind-down in the base (May 2025), a Rs. 20 crore standalone / Rs. 25 crore consolidated exceptional impairment of a loan and investment in an associate (May 2025), and Batra's Oct 31, 2025 remark that Pidilite Ventures 'continuously is evaluating' new investments or raising stakes, with roughly Rs. 3,000 crore of cash on hand. The plan surfaces only in the 29 April 2026 Reg. 30 filing of the Share Swap Agreement and is then explained for the first and only time on the 8 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call, in response to Abneesh Roy's opening question. It then widens into a broader clean-up without further call commentary: Nina Percept (Bangladesh) liquidated effective 19 August 2026 (filed 3 September 2026) and the Finemake stake sold back to its founders (filed 29 September 2026, completion 15 October 2026). The only shift in framing within the May 2026 call is from Vats's 'strategic synergies' to Batra's narrower position that Pidilite's JSW One stake will be insignificant and that scale and profitability belong with JSW.

points.point: The 29 Apr 2026 filing discloses PVPL's Share Swap Agreement (dated 28 Apr 2026) with JSW One Platforms and BuildNext: PVPL's entire BuildNext stake goes to JSW One for JSW One shares at an undisclosed valuation, completion expected 10 Aug 2026.
points.quote: The transfer of shares of PVPL in Buildnext to JSW One is proposed to be effected in consideration of issuance of shares of JSW One to PVPL at a mutually agreed valuation, the details of which have not been disclosed herein for confidentiality reasons.

points.point: Asked why Pidilite would transfer BuildNext, Vats gave the rationale as strategic synergies and a better owner, not a financial exit.
points.quote: So Abneesh, I think the reason is that we found strategic synergies in doing this transaction. I think BuildNext basically has a good home in JSW One.

points.point: Batra said the separation solves an ownership/scale problem: BuildNext was strategic to both sides, but JSW can supply the scale and profitability Pidilite could not, so Pidilite swapped out willingly.
points.quote: And we felt that the business is best served with an owner like JSW who can provide its scale and profitability.

points.point: Vats explained the decision followed a period of ownership and observation after Pidilite's own investment in BuildNext.
points.quote: Now having seen that for some time, we think JSW One is the right home for BuildNext to take BuildNext further as we go forward.

points.point: Batra pre-empted any read-through that this creates a meaningful JSW One holding or paints tie-up, capping the retained stake as immaterial.
points.quote: Our shareholding in JSW will be quite insignificant.

points.point: Vats characterised the retained JSW One shares as, for now, a financial investment arising from the swap rather than a strategic stake.
points.quote: So see, it is at this moment through the transfer of BuildNext financial investment.

points.point: Pressed on competing with JSW in paints (they bid against each other for Akzo), Vats would only say the marketplace relationship is a future option Pidilite will evaluate.
points.quote: So what our point of view is that we will keep evaluating it in a manner of speaking and see when it is right for us to be on one or many of these marketplaces.

points.point: The filing's only stated object for the holding being separated is 'Investment in adjacency business', with BuildNext's business described as home design and project management services, incorporated 16 Oct 2015.
points.quote: Investment in adjacency business.

points.point: BuildNext's disclosed numbers show why it was immaterial to Pidilite: FY25 revenue Rs. 18.38 crore, just 0.04% of consolidated revenue, with a Rs. 9.11 crore loss and negative net worth of Rs. 1.87 crore.
points.quote: The revenue of Buildnext for the financial year ended 31st March 2025 was Rs. 18.38 crores as per the financial statements of Buildnext, which contributed 0.04% to the consolidated revenue of the Company for the same period.

points.point: Unexplained in the calls: as part of the same exit transaction PVPL agreed to put up to Rs. 22 crore of fresh money into BuildNext via CCPS, which on full subscription would have made PVPL the majority shareholder on a fully diluted basis.
points.quote: As a part of the aforesaid transaction, PVPL has agreed to make additional investment in Buildnext of an amount not exceeding Rs. 22 crore, by subscribing to Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (CCPS) of Buildnext.

points.point: The same pruning extended to Finemake Technologies on 29 Sep 2026: PVPL's entire associate stake sold back to founders Nallu Rajashekar and Sambasiva Rao Chowdary Chana at an undisclosed valuation, completion expected 15 Oct 2026, with FY26 revenue of Rs. 24.36 crore (0.06% of consolidated revenue), PAT of Rs. (7.82) crore and net worth of Rs. (6.18) crore.
points.quote: Pidilite Ventures Pvt. Ltd. ("PVPL") has agreed to transfer its entire shareholding in Finemake Technologies Private Limited ("Finemake"), an associate company of PVPL, to the founders of Finemake at a mutually agreed valuation, the details of which have not been disclosed herein for confidentiality reasons.

points.point: A third, purely administrative separation: step-down subsidiary Nina Percept (Bangladesh) Pvt. Ltd. was voluntarily liquidated effective 19 Aug 2026, with nil turnover, a BDT 7,01,654 loss and BDT 30,13,824 net worth.
points.quote: NPBPL has been inoperative since incorporation due to lack of business opportunities.

points.point: Six months before the swap, Batra described Pidilite Ventures as a portfolio under continuous review for new investments or stake increases, with nothing then to report — the closest advance signal in any call.
points.quote: And Pidilite Ventures as part of its portfolio continuously is evaluating in either new investments, or investments in or companies in which they want to increase the stake.

points.point: Vats added that Pidilite raises or trims stakes in its start-up investments depending on how each performs, and noted roughly Rs. 3,000 crore of cash available for such choices.
points.quote: So we may increase our stake into a few of them, whichever work which we have done and all that.

points.point: Precedent for exiting non-core holdings: FY25 carried a Rs. 20 crore standalone exceptional loss on impairment of a loan to an associate, following the FY24 Pulvitec Brazil divestment (Rs. 72 crore loss) and the Pidilite USA wind-down.
points.quote: This year however, there is an exceptional loss of Rs. 20 crores largely on account of impairment of loan to an associate entity.

verdict.what_management_expects: For BuildNext: an owner able to give it scale and profitability, taking it further than Pidilite could. For Pidilite: an exit of a loss-making 0.04%-of-revenue adjacency, replaced by an admittedly insignificant JSW One shareholding treated as a financial investment, plus optional future access to JSW One's marketplace. No margin, capital-release, valuation or focus benefit was quantified on the call.
verdict.gaps: No valuation, swap ratio or stake percentage; no reason for the Rs. 22 crore CCPS top-up before exiting; no P&L impact; no Finemake rationale; no investor, lender or partner asked.

Where a profit line is given for those segments it is 'Segment Result' (and in quarterly presentations 'Segment Results (PBIT)' = profit before interest, tax and exceptional items), with revenue shown both as Segment Revenue (including inter-segment) and Net Revenue (external, after inter-segment at cost plus fixed margin). Buildnext appears only in Related Party Disclosures as an Associate (AR2024 p.100 item 'al'; AR2025 p.101 item 'am') and in the corporate-journey slide listing startup investments 'Buildnext, Kaarwan, Finemake, Onsite, Pace Robotics' (Presentation Feb 2026 p.5); the May 2026 version of that slide drops Buildnext from the list. Its share of associate results is not separately quantified — only an aggregate 'Share of Profit of Associates/Joint Ventures' is shown (₹(4.05) cr FY2024, ₹(3.28) cr FY2025, ₹(2.37) cr FY2026, consolidated).

verdict.rationale: On these texts alone, Pine Labs is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business — no scheme of arrangement for a separation, no record-date or share-entitlement ratio, no appointed date, and no board resolution to that effect appears in any of the three calls or eight filings. The only Scheme of Arrangement disclosed runs the opposite way: an amalgamation of Erstwhile Pine Labs Limited, Singapore (the erstwhile holding company, Transferor) into Pine Labs Limited, India (Transferee), approved by the two boards on 13 December 2023 (modified 7 February 2024) and 8 February 2024 under sections 230-232 read with 234 of the Companies Act, 2013 and sections 210/212 of Singapore's Companies Act 1967, effective 6 June 2025, under which the Transferor 'along with its investment in the subsidiaries have been transferred to and vested in' the Indian company, with retrospective common-control accounting from 1 April 2024 and cancellation of the Transferee's shares against Scheme shares. Every other structural action in the record is also consolidating, not separating: 100% acquisition of Shopflo Technologies for ₹88 crore (consolidated from 26 May 2026); rights-issue infusions into wholly owned subsidiaries — ₹128.99 crore (30 Jan 2026) and ₹25.00 crore each on 29 June 2026 and 21 October 2026 into Synergistic Financial Networks (FY26 turnover ₹189.75 crore), and ₹64.00 crore into BrokenTusk Technologies (FY25 turnover ₹66.62 crore) — each 'to meet certain working capital needs and pursuit of further growth opportunities' with the entity remaining wholly owned. The nearest thing to a separation is the voluntary strike-off of Mopay Services Private Limited (shareholders' approval 27 March 2026), a dormant WOS with nil FY25 turnover and negative net worth of ₹29,000, done 'to streamline the group structure and reduce administrative and compliance overheads,' with no material impact on financials. The company's two businesses — the Digital infrastructure and transaction platform (Q1 FY27 revenue ₹499.12 crore, contribution ₹408.02 crore) and the Issuing and acquiring platform (₹237.80 crore revenue, ₹124.60 crore contribution, ~30% of revenues) — are reported as separate Ind AS 108 segments but are run and argued for as one integrated platform. Management in fact argued explicitly against separating economics inside the issuing business, and declined to split out affordability/VAS disclosure; no investor, lender or partner on any call asked for a separation. What investors did push for, and management acted on, was working-capital and cash-flow discipline (early settlement/bill discounting of ₹202 crore, ₹676 crore Q4 OCF, ₹395 crore FY26 OCF) — not a structural split.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces. On the Dec 2025 (Q2 FY26, call 3 December 2025), Feb 2026 (Q3 FY26, call 28 January 2026) and Jun 2026 (Q4/FY26, call 26 May 2026) calls, management describes a deliberately multi-product, multi-segment, multi-geography single platform, and in Jun 2026 Sameer Kamath pushes back on treating issuance distribution and processing as two businesses. The only structural changes dated in the record move the other way: the Singapore-into-India amalgamation effective 6 June 2025, the Shopflo acquisition in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, repeated rights-issue funding of wholly owned subsidiaries (30 January 2026, 29 June 2026, 21 October 2026), and the 27 March 2026 strike-off of the dormant Mopay Services.

points.point: The only Scheme of Arrangement in the record is an amalgamation that pulled the Singapore holding company and its subsidiary investments into the listed Indian entity, effective 6 June 2025 — consolidation, not separation.
points.quote: The Scheme became effective on 6 June 2025, pursuant to the effectiveness of Scheme, the Transferor Company along with its investment in the subsidiaries have been transferred to and vested in the Transferee Company with effect from 06 June 2025

points.point: The scheme's stated legal purpose was an amalgamation between the Singapore transferor and the Indian transferee under Indian and Singapore company law, approved by the boards on 13 December 2023 (modified 7 February 2024) and 8 February 2024.
points.quote: to effect an amalgamation between Transferor Company and Transferee Company.

points.point: The only entity actually being removed from the group is Mopay Services Private Limited, a dormant wholly owned subsidiary with nil FY25 turnover and net worth of negative ₹29,000, struck off for housekeeping reasons rather than to separate a business.
points.quote: MSPL is not carrying on any business operations and does not have any activity, and therefore, in order to streamline the group structure and reduce administrative and compliance overheads, it has been decided to initiate the process for striking -off its name.

points.point: Capital is being injected into, not carved out of, the operating subsidiaries: ₹128.99 crore (Jan 2026) plus ₹25.00 crore each in June and October 2026 into Synergistic Financial Networks, and ₹64.00 crore into BrokenTusk, each leaving them wholly owned.
points.quote: The investment is intended to fund SFNPL’s  working capital requirements, support its growth opportunities , and enable  further  investments  in its step-down subsidiaries. Following the transaction, SFNPL will remain a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: Asked whether gift-card distribution and processing were economically distinct, Sameer Kamath explicitly refused to treat them as separable, calling distribution a moat that fuels processing — the opposite of a separation rationale.
points.quote: Look at this business as an integrated offering where at the CM level, you might see some changes, but at a flow through level, you will see it slightly differently and that is what my, my guidance to the street would be look at this as an integrated model and not like two separate businesses running within one.

points.point: Rau framed the company as two business lines inside one stack — digital infrastructure/transactions (offline, online, fintech infra) and issuing/acquiring at ~30% of revenue — presented as layers that monetise each other, not as units to be split.
points.quote: As we mentioned, we operate in two large business lines.

points.point: On lending, management deliberately chose NOT to create a separate credit/NBFC vehicle, because merchants want a multi-NBFC platform; this is the one adjacency they declined to build or hive off.
points.quote: So we have not launched our NBFC, but what we are continuing to deliver is we are continuing to deliver more choices to the merchants as well as their consumers.

points.point: Management ruled out any fundraising and pointed to ₹2,700 crore of cash plus organic free cash flow, removing the capital-raising motive that often drives a separation.
points.quote: No, we have no interest in raising funds. We are in a very comfortable position.

points.point: The investor pressure management did respond to was working capital and cash conversion — addressed through bill discounting/early settlement (₹202 crore inflow, ₹676 crore Q4 OCF, ₹395 crore FY26 OCF), not through any structural split.
points.quote: I think the street has told us very clearly, saying that they do not necessarily like the fact that our working capital is getting bloated and we have taken note of that and that is exactly what we have tried to solve for it because obviously, the messaging has been very clear to us.

points.point: Reporting is split into two segments for Ind AS 108 purposes only — digital payments (16% growth, ~82% gross margin) and issuance (42% growth) — with mix shifts between them explaining margin movement inside one company.
points.quote: We report our business broadly into two segments, the digital payments business, which includes in -store, the online business, the value -added services including affordability, and the fintech infrastructure business.

points.point: Management declined to disclose even a sub-segment revenue split for affordability versus VAS, which is inconsistent with preparing a business for separation.
points.quote: We have not been keen to show that in detail right now, Prakhar , but if you would have seen, we started to give out a little bit more information.

points.point: The stated vision through all three calls is a single diversified platform spanning online, offline, DPI and issuing across merchants, banks and brands — the strategic opposite of a separation narrative.

verdict.rationale: Across all four transcripts (Oct 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026) and both filings, Saatvik Green Energy announces NO separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement of any business, so no management rationale for one exists in these texts; the stated strategy is the opposite — consolidating a single integrated platform. Management repeatedly describes building "entire integrated forward, backward and sideways energy company" spanning ingot/wafer, cell (scaled from 4.8 GW to 6 GW), module (8.8 GW), encapsulant (2 GW commissioned in Ambala, roadmap raised to 5 GW), inverters (UDAY series), solar pumps, EPC, BESS, transformers and components — with backward integration justified as cost competitiveness, margin sustainability and supply-chain security, worth an additional 3-5% EBITDA on self-produced cell volume. The only 'separation' language is about creating standalone business units/entities INSIDE the group, not divesting: solar pumps (INR ~2 crore FY25 revenue, targeted INR 50-80 crore in FY26, 4,000-5,000 pumps, 15,000 next year) described as "a division which has a potential of becoming a separate business unit"; encapsulant built "not only for our supply chain resilience, but also as a separate business unit" because third-party module makers "are ready to pay a premium on encapsulant" (5-10% internal saving, 7-10% of module cost); plus Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited launched for BESS and an 80% stake bought in Melcon Transformers and Electricals. Capacity is also being housed in separate legal vehicles — subsidiary Saatvik Solar Industries Private Limited (FY25 turnover INR 11,852.52 million) holds the new-technology capacity and carries a 15% concessional tax rate versus 25% at the parent, pulling the blended rate to 18-20% — which is corporate structuring, not a separation. Management cites capital needs that argue against breaking anything off: INR 1,850 crore Odisha capex (INR 1,300-1,350 crore cell, INR 550 crore module), INR 1,700 crore FY27 capex, INR 1,800-2,500 crore for the 6 GW ingot project in FY28, funded 70:30 debt:equity at 8.9-9%, with debt-equity to be held between 1.0x and 1.5x (0.65x in FY26 versus 1.34x in FY25). No investor, lender or partner in any of these calls asks for a separation, and no analyst question on the topic appears.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces as a corporate separation in any call. Oct 10, 2025 (Q1FY26) is the first time 'separate business unit' appears, as an internal ambition for solar pumps; Nov 10, 2025 (Q2FY26) adds the subsidiary tax-rate point and Saatvik Solar Industries as the order-taking entity; Feb 5, 2026 (Q3FY26) hardens solar pumps into a targeted "standalone business unit" (then only 0.35% of revenue); May 21, 2026 (Q4FY26) extends the pattern to encapsulant as a merchant business unit, a new BESS company (Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited) and the Melcon transformer acquisition — all additions to the group, never a carve-out.

points.point: Solar pumps, scaling from under INR 2 crore to about INR 50 crore of revenue, is first flagged as a candidate to become its own business unit inside the group.
points.quote: So, the kind of growth which will be seen from less than INR2 crores revenue last year to about INR50 crores revenue this year and that is also a division which has a potential of becoming a separate business unit.

points.point: The strategic direction stated by the CEO is full integration across the value chain plus adjacencies, not separation of any business.
points.quote: So, all in all we are building -- we are also doing BESS projects and ultimately the target is to get into battery storage products also. So, all in all we are building entire integrated forward, backward and sideways energy company, renewable energy company especially.

points.point: Management explicitly says module capacity will be capped around 9-10 GW and growth will come from backward integration into cell and ingot-wafer, i.e. consolidation rather than divestment.
points.quote: So, our focus is not to grow our module capacities beyond 9, 10 gigawatts because that is a respectable where you can get economies of scale and we will focus on building our backward integration towards cell, towards ingot wafer and also bring in more products, you know, which are supportive to our solar module business in this industry.

points.point: The only entity-level rationale given is tax: new capacity sits in subsidiary Saatvik Solar at a 15% rate versus 25% at the parent, lowering the blended rate to 18-20%.
points.quote: So, in Saatvik Green Energy, we have normal tax rate, while in comparison , Saatvik Solar has a preferred rate at the rate of 15%. So, more revenue from Saatvik Solar Industries, the lower tax rate overall.

points.point: Solar pumps, at 0.35% of revenue, are being formalised as a standalone business unit within the company during FY26.
points.quote: This year we target to make it a business unit, a standalone business unit.

points.point: The 2 GW (now 5 GW roadmap) EPE encapsulant plant is being run as its own business unit selling to third-party module makers at a premium, on top of 5-10% internal cost savings on 7-10% of module cost.
points.quote: So initially we started this 2 gigawatt for our internal usage, but what we have found is that there are, you know, manufacturers who are not good at planning and they are not importing, they are not able to secure. So they are ready to pay a premium on encapsulant.

points.point: New activities are being placed in new legal vehicles and acquisitions rather than separated out of the company: a BESS company was launched and 80% of a transformer maker was bought.
points.quote: In parallel, we launched Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited, focused on battery energy storage systems.

points.point: Capital plans point to heavier consolidation, not separation: INR 1,700 crore FY27 capex and about INR 2,500 crore for the 6 GW ingot project, with gearing held at 1.0-1.5x.
points.quote: So, for FY27, our capex requirement for this expansion is about 1,700 crores.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger or spin-off is present in the filings; the only structural filing is a INR 251.60 crore rights-issue infusion into wholly owned subsidiary SSIPL for the Odisha 4 GW module plant, with no change in shareholding, alongside a postal ballot on an independent director and ESOP ratification.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not a shipping line but SCI's non-core land and property portfolio, carved out into a separate listed-to-be entity, Shipping Corporation of India Land and Assets Limited (SCILAL), with SCI as the 'Demerged Company' and SCILAL as the 'Resulting Company'. The filings state the mechanics precisely: MCA approved the demerger scheme by order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets were transferred from SCI to SCILAL with effect from 01 April 2021, and 185 of those assets are leased back to SCI so that the shipping operations can keep using the premises they occupy. The stated reason the separation exists is the Government of India's strategic disinvestment of SCI: note 7 says the process is being run by the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) with a Transaction Advisor, that the Preliminary Information Memorandum inviting expressions of interest was released on 22.12.2020, and that the Virtual Data Room is open and being managed by the Transaction Advisor for due diligence by Qualified Interested Parties — i.e. the buyer is being sold the shipping company, and the real estate is being kept out of the sale. So the asker is the owner-seller (the Government, via DIPAM and its Transaction Advisor) and the audience is prospective strategic bidders, not lenders or JV partners; no investor on either call asked for it. The problem it solves, as the documents frame it, is that the land and buildings are 'non-core' to a shipping business and would otherwise sit inside the entity being privatised; the leaseback keeps SCI operationally whole after they leave its balance sheet. The separation is still unfinished: the leaseback is accounted for as a short-term lease only because the final lease agreement has not been executed, pending the disinvestment process, and the joint statutory auditors (D. R. Mohnot & Co and PSD & Associates) flag both note 7 and note 8 as emphasis-of-matter items in the 31.12.2025 limited review. Management itself volunteered none of this on the calls — the only live discussion was a question about a possible reverse merger of SCILAL back into SCI, which the CMD declined to answer on the ground that SCILAL is a separate legal entity and the decision rests with the Government and the Ministry.
verdict.evolution: On the Q2 FY26 call of 10 November 2025 the demerger, SCILAL and the disinvestment were not raised at all — management's entire strategic narrative was additive (the 59-vessel oil-PSU JV, the 2047 business plan, VLGC inductions), not separative. It surfaced only on the Q4 FY26 call of 11 May 2026, and then from an investor: Amitabh Vatsya of Sadhan Ventures asked about 'rumours or some news about reverse merger of SILAL with SCI', citing a signed NBCC MOU, and Capt. Tyagi answered that the NBCC MOU concerns upgrading SCI's Powai training institute and that SCILAL is a separate legal entity on which only the Government/Ministry can decide, adding 'We have no information regarding this at this stage.' Across the three filings of 06.02.2026 the language is unchanged and boilerplate — same note 7, same note 8, same auditor emphasis — so the only movement in the period is directional ambiguity (an investor floating reversal of the demerger) rather than any new company disclosure.

points.point: Note 8 of the 31.12.2025 standalone and consolidated results sets out the carve-out: MCA order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets moved from SCI to SCILAL effective 01 April 2021, and 185 of them leased back to SCI, with the leaseback treated as a short-term lease only because the final agreement is unexecuted pending disinvestment.
points.quote: Pursuant to approval of demerger scheme by MCA vide its order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets were transferred from the Company (Demerged Company) to Shipping Corporation of India Land and Assets Limited (Resulting Company) (hereinafter referred to as SCILAL) w.e.f. 01 April 2021 and 185 non-core assets are leased back to the demerged company, has been treated as short term lease, pending execution of final agreement and disinvestment process as detailed in note no. 7.

points.point: Note 7 names who is driving the separation and why it is still open — DIPAM with a Transaction Advisor, a PIM issued 22.12.2020, and a Virtual Data Room currently open for due diligence by Qualified Interested Parties, i.e. prospective strategic buyers of the shipping business.
points.quote: The proposed strategic disinvestment of SCI is being handled by Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) with the engagement of Transaction Advisor. In this regard, Preliminary Information Memorandum (PIM) for inviting expression of interest was released on 22.12.2020. The Virtual Data Room is open and is being managed by the Transaction Advisor for the process of due diligence by the Qualified Interested Parties.

points.point: The joint statutory auditors draw attention to the demerger and leaseback as an emphasis-of-matter in their limited review report dated 06.02.2026, expressly tying management's short-term-lease judgement to the unexecuted formal lease agreement and the disinvestment process.
points.quote: Note no. 8 regarding MCA’a approval in FY 22-23 for demerger between The Shipping Corporation of India Limited (“Demerged Company”) and The Shipping corporation of India Limited Land and Assets Limited (“Resulting Company”) and consequently, transfer of non-core assets to SCI LAL and leaseback of the same to SCI and management’s assessment of treating the same as short term lease pending execution of formal lease agreement and disinvestment process.

points.point: An investor (Amitabh Vatsya, Sadhan Ventures) raised press reports of a reverse merger of SCILAL back into SCI, linking it to a newly signed NBCC MOU — the only time the separation was discussed live on either call.
points.quote: So, is there are some rumours or some news about reverse merger of SILAL with SCI?

points.point: Capt. B.K. Tyagi declined to give any rationale or status, treating SCILAL as outside SCI's control and the decision as the Government's/Ministry's alone, and disclaiming any information.
points.quote: As far as this SCILAL and SCI reversal is concerned, SCILAL is a separate legal entity, and this is a matter where Government, our Ministry will take decision if at all anything is there.

points.point: He redirected the question to the NBCC MOU's actual purpose — upgrading and better utilising SCI's large maritime training institute at Powai, alongside an MOU with international ship manager Synergy — not to any land-entity restructuring.
points.quote: See, number one, this NBCC MOU was signed few days back. And idea is we have got a one big training institute in Powai.

points.point: The November 2025 call contains no reference to the demerger, SCILAL, non-core assets or disinvestment; management's strategic framing was entirely about adding entities (a 50%-owned oil-PSU JV for 59 vessels, later Bharat Container Shipping Line) rather than separating existing ones.
points.quote: It will be a separate entity and where SCI will hold a shareholding up to 50%.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing was stated on either call — no margin, capital, valuation or focus claim for SCI or SCILAL. Only the filings imply the intent: 192 non-core land assets sit in SCILAL while SCI operates on 185 leased back, keeping property out of the shipping entity DIPAM is selling. The sole forward statement was upgrading the Powai training institute via the NBCC/Synergy MOUs.
verdict.gaps: No rationale, valuation, rent quantum, lease term, timetable, SCILAL listing/shareholding plan, or buyer status; management would not address the reverse-merger reports or confirm anything about SCILAL.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not contain a separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or hive-off of any Tata Consumer business, so no management rationale for one can be reconstructed from them. Across all seven transcripts (Feb 2025 through Jul 2026) management never mentions separating, demerging, listing or divesting a business; the strategic direction stated is the opposite — consolidation and acquisition. Sunil D'Souza says of M&A, "I wouldn't change my thought process on the M&A side at all" (Jul 2025) and "we remain open" to acquisitions (May 2026), and the Nov 2025 call describes having "consolidated or merged our wholly owned subsidiaries into the mother company," which produced a one-time tax credit of Rs 74 crores in the base quarter. The only corporate-structure event in the filings is the voluntary strike-off and dissolution of Tata Tea Holdings Private Limited (TTHPL), effective June 29, 2026 — a dormant shell with Nil turnover, revenue, income and net worth contribution in the last financial year, which the company states "will have no material impact on the operations or financial position of the Company"; the Reg. 30 annexure marks every sale/consideration/buyer field "Not Applicable, since this is the case of voluntary strike-off and consequent dissolution." The 2025 filings also carry Rs 11 crores of legal and professional costs "relating to the Scheme of arrangement" in the Q2 FY25 exceptional line, but that Scheme is nowhere described in these documents and, per the Nov 2025 call, relates to merging wholly owned subsidiaries inward, not separating anything out. The nearest thing to a "separation" discussed is operational, not legal: a pan-India split of the go-to-market into separate "core" (Tata Salt / Tata Tea) and "growth" (Sampann, Capital Foods, Organic India, Soulfull) distributors, salespeople, TSEs and ASMs — justified because in Calcutta 91% of business came from tea and salt and only 9% from growth categories, so growth brands got no focus. No investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for any entity separation. Anything beyond this would be invention.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea surfaces at any point: Feb 2025 (Q3 FY25) and Apr 2025 (Q4 FY25) discuss integrating the Capital Foods and Organic India acquisitions and split sales routes; Jul 2025 reaffirms the buy-side M&A thesis unchanged; Nov 2025 reports subsidiaries being merged inward (Rs 74 crore tax credit in base). The only structural step is in the Jan 2026, May 2026 and Jul 2026 calls, and it is distribution, not entity: pilots of split core-vs-growth distributors (Jan 2026, 82% rolled out, 270 distributors transitioned, 160 added), full national rollout completed (May 2026), and early revenue benefit claimed (Jul 2026). The single filing-level change is the June 30, 2026 intimation that dormant subsidiary TTHPL was struck off effective June 29, 2026.

points.point: The only entity-level change in the filings is the voluntary strike-off and dissolution of dormant wholly owned subsidiary Tata Tea Holdings Private Limited, effective June 29, 2026 — not a separation of any operating business.
points.quote: Accordingly, TTHPL has ceased to be the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, effective June 29, 2026.
