verdict.rationale: The business being separated is GAIL's own directly-authorised city gas distribution (CGD) retail business — the six geographical areas Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum (Jamshedpur), Cuttack and Khordha (Bhubaneswar) — which the Board resolved to hive down into its 100% subsidiary GAIL Gas Limited as a slump sale on a going-concern basis, effective 01.01.2027, with the subsidiary then to be listed via IPO diluting up to 25% of GAIL's equity. Management's stated reason was structural, not financial distress: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta said it was 'in order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach' — i.e. GAIL group CGD was split across GAIL's own balance sheet (six GAs, 0.36–0.55 MMSCMD, 195→215 CNG stations and 3.53→4.64 lakh DPNG connections over FY25–Q3FY26, volumes up ~25% in FY25 but 'currently in their early stages of development'), GAIL Gas (16 GAs plus 9 JVs, 7.0→7.8 MMSCMD, 12.46 lakh DPNG connections, 674 CNG stations, FY25 turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore up 42%, PAT Rs 451 crore up 40%) and 72 group GAs in all. A pipeline-and-marketing parent was also an awkward owner of a retail business: management said 'we are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies', and segment reporting of the CGD/marketing split was itself confusing analysts (the Rs 400 crore standalone-to-consolidated regrouping queried in Jul 2025). The upside case cited was CGD demand: a PNGRB projection of consumption rising '2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY 24' (~15% CAGR), PNGRB capping CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion lowering CGD input costs. For the IPO, the argument was scale and timing — 'GAIL Gas is one of the biggest company in the country in terms of city gas distribution... now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas' — with a consultant already selected and a roughly one-year timeline. The impetus came largely from sell-side investors (Citi's Saurabh Handa on restructuring CGD investments in Nov 2024; Alliance Services' Balaji Das on the IPO consultant in Oct 2025); the only external consent management named was CCEA, 'since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA' — no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. Running in the opposite direction, GAIL simultaneously pulled Konkan LNG Limited in: it bought out MSEB Holding's 7,40,55,220 shares via a NCLT-approved capital reduction (paid 06.07.2026, GAIL to 100%) and then merged KLL (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into GAIL to 'create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure'.
verdict.evolution: The idea first surfaced only as an unprompted analyst question on the Nov 06, 2024 Q2 FY25 call, where R.K. Jain said no call had been taken on restructuring GAIL Gas — 'this is in our mind, but nothing concrete' — while adding that GAIL was 'looking for listing one or two JVs'; the Jan 30, 2025 call did not touch it. It became concrete at the May 14, 2025 annual analyst meet, where the CMD disclosed the Board's recommendation (passed 13.05.2025) to transfer the six GAs to GAIL Gas for a 'single entity... retail focused business approach', subject to CCEA. On Oct 31, 2025 the second leg appeared: GAIL confirmed it had started the GAIL Gas listing process, had selected a consultant, and expected 'a one year time line or so'; the Feb 02, 2026 Q3 FY26 call was silent on both. The filings then executed it: 31.07.2026 KLL merger into GAIL, and 30.10.2026 Board approval of the six-GA slump sale effective 01.01.2027 plus in-principle approval of a GAIL Gas IPO diluting up to 25%.

points.point: Citi's Saurabh Handa raised the split of CGD investments between GAIL standalone and GAIL Gas and asked whether GAIL would restructure them — the first time the idea appears in the record.
points.quote: On your City Gas investments, whether they are at the standalone entity or in GAIL Gas? Is there any thought process to look at restructuring these streamline these investments?

points.point: Director (Finance) R.K. Jain confirmed restructuring was under internal consideration but that no decision existed, while separately flagging that GAIL was working on listing one or two JVs with an update promised in Q3.
points.quote: As a company about GAIL Gas has not yet taken any call for restructuring of GAIL Gas. This is in our mind, but nothing concrete I can share with you right now.

points.point: Alongside CGD restructuring, Jain said listing of group entities was already in progress and at 'a good stage', promising an update in Q3 FY25.
points.quote: So also, we are looking for listing one or two JVs, which we are in the process and once we move forward and we take a call, we'll come back to you, but that we are certainly working and we are in a good stage.

points.point: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta disclosed the Board's 13.05.2025 recommendation to transfer GAIL's six directly-held CGD geographical areas to wholly-owned GAIL Gas Limited — the core rationale being one single, synergistic, retail-focused CGD entity.
points.quote: In order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach, the Board has recommended to transfer six geographical areas of GAIL to its wholly owned subsidiary, GAIL Gas Limited.

points.point: The only approval condition management named was CCEA, because the six GAs (Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack) had been awarded to GAIL by CCEA rather than won by GAIL Gas.
points.quote: This is subject to approval of CCEA since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA.

points.point: The six GAs were described as early-stage but fast-growing (volumes up ~25% in FY25, then ~0.4–0.45 MMSCMD) and under continuous cost review — the sub-scale retail assets being pushed into the dedicated CGD vehicle.
points.quote: In the Financial Year 24-25, these six GAs have shown impressive growth with volumes increasing by approximately 25%. We are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies.

points.point: The growth case for a standalone CGD entity rested on PNGRB's demand projection, supplemented by PNGRB's proposal to cap CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion to cut CGD input costs.
points.quote: the CGD sector is anticipated to be the key driver of growth, with consumption expected to increase 2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY '24

points.point: GAIL Gas's own FY25 numbers framed the receiving entity as a scaled, improving business: turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore (+42%), PAT Rs 451 crore (+40%), 16 GAs owned plus 9 JVs.
points.quote: During the current financial year, that is FY '25, GAIL Gas Limited's turnover stood at Rs. 12,231 crores as against Rs. 10,944 crores in FY '24. PBT increased by 42% and stood at Rs. 615 crores as against Rs. 434 crores in FY '24.

points.point: On the other entity later consolidated in, management said Konkan LNG (Dabhol) would swing to profit once the all-weather breakwater let it run 34–36 cargoes versus 21, worth roughly Rs 300 crore.
points.quote: So this year certainly we were not in positive because of the breakwater issue. But going forward, we will have positive bottom line from KLL.

points.point: An investor (Balaji Das) pressed on the GAIL Gas IPO and the consultant being hired for listing analysis, confirming the second leg of the plan was investor-driven.
points.quote: And the second question is on, we had like on the listing of the GAIL Gas IPO actually. So, any further progress on consultant and when are the future plans actually for GAIL Gas actually, because we heard that we are hiring consultants for analysis of listing.

points.point: Jain confirmed the listing process had begun — consultant selected, order imminent — and justified it on GAIL Gas's scale: 7.72 MMSCMD of volume and more GAs than any peer, with Bangalore alone at 1 MMSCMD.
points.quote: And we in GAIL believe that now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas, in that regard we have already started the process of hiring of consultant.

points.point: He put a roughly one-year timeline on the listing, contingent on the consultant's study — the only timing guidance given on the IPO.
points.quote: So, we are on a path to study about listing of GAIL Gas and after conclusion of that study, certainly that study is very important for us, we expect a one year time line or so should be good enough.

points.point: The last call in the record discussed the six GAs and GAIL Gas purely operationally (0.55 MMSCMD, 215 CNG stations, 4.64 lakh DPNG; GAIL Gas 7.8 MMSCMD, PBT Rs 143 crore) with no mention of the transfer or the IPO.
points.quote: GAIL has direct authorization of 6 GAs and has an infrastructure of 215 CNG stations and 4.64 lakh DPNG connections.

points.point: Filing 30.10.2026: Board approved the carve-out of the six named CGD GAs to GAIL Gas as a slump sale, via Business Transfer Agreement on a going-concern basis, effective 01.01.2027.
points.quote: GAIL Board in its meeting held today i.e. 30.10.2026 accorded approval for Transfer of Six CGD Geographical Areas of GAIL India Ltd. viz. Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum, Cuttack and Khordha to GAIL Gas Ltd. (wholly owned Subsidiary of GAIL) through slump sale by Execution of Business Transfer Agreement on going concern basis, with effective date of transfer as 01.01.2027.

points.point: Same-day filing: in-principle Board approval to list GAIL Gas on Indian exchanges via IPO, diluting GAIL's stake by up to 25%, with valuation, price band and final dilution left to BRLM recommendations and a later Board approval.
points.quote: accorded in-principle approval for Listing of shares of GAIL Gas Limited, (a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL) (GGL) on the Indian stock exchanges through Initial Public Offering (IPO) route by diluting GAIL's equity in GGL upto 25%.

points.point: Filing 31.07.2026: in the opposite direction, GAIL approved absorbing wholly-owned Konkan LNG (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into itself under Section 233, with KLL's shares cancelled and no change in GAIL's shareholding.
points.quote: To create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure which will enhance operational efficiencies.

points.point: Filing 10.07.2026: the KLL merger was preceded by an NCLT-approved capital reduction (order 03.06.2026) buying out partner MSEB Holding, taking GAIL from 50% to 100% of Konkan LNG before the absorption.
points.quote: an aggregate of 14,81,10,440 equity shares of ₹10 each, including 7,40,55,220 equity shares held by GAIL and 7,40,55,220 equity shares held by MSEB in KLL stand cancelled and extinguished i.e. MSEB holding in KLL reduced to Nil and GAIL shareholding increased to 100% of the equity share capital of KLL.

verdict.what_management_expects: One consolidated, retail-focused CGD entity with business synergy and efficiency; the six early-stage GAs (0.55 MMSCMD) folded into GAIL Gas's 7.8 MMSCMD platform (674 CNG stations, 12.46 lakh DPNG) to capture CGD demand rising 2.5–3.5x by 2030, aided by Zone-1 tariff capping and expected GST; price discovery and capital via an IPO of up to 25%. Parent keeps transmission/marketing; Konkan LNG's merger simplifies the group and adds its cargo-driven profit.
verdict.gaps: No valuation, slump-sale consideration, IPO size or use of proceeds, standalone margin/ROCE or capex targets, CCEA timing, or why 25%; calls after Oct 2025 went silent.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not contain any separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement by HCL Technologies — the word 'carve-out' appears only on the buy side, where HCLTech is the acquirer of businesses other companies are separating. The two filings provided (both dated 12 January 2026) are the Q3 FY26 un-audited results and the dividend record-date intimation; their only structural notes are Note 4, a definitive agreement signed 18 December 2025 to 'carve-out and acquire' HPE's Telco Solutions Business for ₹1,438 crores ($160 million), including a ₹135 crore ($15 million) performance incentive, to gain IP, product engineering and R&D talent and CSP relationships; and Note 5, a definitive agreement signed 22 December 2025 to carve-out and acquire Jaspersoft from Cloud Software Group for ₹2,157 crores ($240 million) for an embedded analytics/pixel-perfect reporting platform and its developer community. Management framed both as additive — Telco Solutions building on the 2024 HPE CTG acquisition ('which is now growing nicely') to deepen telecom IP, and Jaspersoft/Wobby/Zeenea completing the Actian data-intelligence stack with the missing 'visualize layer' (Jaspersoft closed in early July 2026, guided at $10–15 million revenue per quarter). The only separations discussed as HCLTech's own doing are internal restructuring (a people-and-non-people program costing ~40–50 bps of FY26 margin, 62 bps in Q1 FY27, intended to give 'structural agility' in the AI era), the creation of new subsidiaries rather than divestments (HCLTech Public Sector Solutions in the US, April 2025), discontinuation of some HCL Software products, and walking away from deals worth '$1 billion more' of TCV. Separation appears as a demand theme, not a corporate action: in Oct 2025 CVK cited 'carveout related separation work' at Retail/CPG clients as a revenue pocket. HCLSoftware is described as structurally distinct — 'a dedicated products and platform organization that operates largely independent of the Services business with its own GTM and R&D investments', reported as its own segment with its own ROIC (21.6% in Q1 FY27) and ARR ($1.063 billion) — but no call or filing proposes separating it, and no lender, partner or investor is recorded asking for any separation. The nearest new-entity decision is the July 2026 AI datacenter business: up to ₹3,500 crores, scaling toward 50 MW, possibly funded with partners, equity and debt — but it is described as a new growth vector inside HCLTech, not a carve-out.
verdict.evolution: Jan 2025 (Q3 FY25) is the first structural note: HPE's CTG assets closed 2 December 2024 and HCLSoftware is described as operating 'largely independent' of Services, with no separation proposed. Apr 2025 adds a new subsidiary (HCLTech Public Sector Solutions) and Jul 2025 announces a restructuring program, while Oct 2025 cites clients' own 'carveout related separation work' as a demand pocket. Jan 2026 and the 12 January 2026 filing record HCLTech as the buyer of two carve-outs (HPE Telco Solutions, $160M; Jaspersoft, $240M), Apr 2026 flags both as delayed by US government approvals, and Jul 2026 confirms Jaspersoft closed and CTG-follow-on still pending — never once a separation of HCLTech's own business.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger or separation document is present; both supplied filings dated 12 January 2026 are the Q3 FY26 results and the dividend record-date intimation, whose only structural notes are inbound acquisitions.
points.quote: On 18 December 2025, the Group has signed a definitive agreement to carve-out and acquire Telco Solutions Business from HPE for ₹ 1,438 crores ($160 million), including ₹ 135 crores ($15 million) incentive payable based on performance.

points.point: The second carve-out in the filing is also an acquisition — Jaspersoft from Cloud Software Group for ₹2,157 crores ($240 million) — bought for a BI/reporting platform and its global developer community.
points.quote: On 22 December 2025, the Group has signed a definitive agreement to carve-out and acquire Jaspersoft, a business unit of CSG providing a leading embedded analytics and pixel-perfect reporting platform, for ₹ 2,157 crores ($240 million).

points.point: Management explicitly labels both carve-outs as acquisitions excluded from guidance, delayed by the US government shutdown of the approving departments — confirming HCLTech is the buyer, not the seller.
points.quote: This guidance does not include the two acquisitions, the Telecom Solutions Group from HPE that we announced to carve -out and Jaspersoft.

points.point: CVK positions the HPE Telco Solutions purchase as doubling down on telecom IP, building on the 2024 CTG acquisition, to gain nonlinear growth and new CSP relationships.
points.quote: This strategic move builds on the momentum from our successful integration of HPE's Communications Technology Group (CTG) , acquired in 2024, which is now growing nicely.

points.point: The only 'separation' HCLTech discusses is its clients' — carve-out separation work is named as a pocket of Retail/CPG demand, i.e. a revenue opportunity rather than a corporate action by HCLTech.
points.quote: A couple of areas where we see this include integration work in M&A , a carveout related separation work , and in large scale SDLC transformation work supported by Generative AI, especially our AI Force platform.

points.point: HCLSoftware is described as already structurally distinct from Services with its own GTM and R&D, yet no separation of it is proposed on any call; it stays a reported segment with its own ROIC and ARR.
points.quote: We a s the only Indian service provider are uniquely positioned for the medium to long term with a dedicated products and platform organization that operates largely independent of the Services business with its own GTM and R&D investments.

points.point: The structural action HCLTech did announce is an internal restructuring program across people and facilities for AI-era agility — not a business separation; it cost ~40–50 bps of FY26 margin and 62 bps in Q1 FY27.
points.quote: We plan to execute a restructuring program , both on people and non -people side during the rest of this fiscal year.

points.point: Corporate structuring in the period created new entities rather than separating existing ones — a dedicated US public-sector subsidiary was established to address government spend.
points.quote: Further to capitalize on the large spend of public sector , and in line with the strategy to expand our market participation, we recently established HCLTech Public Sector Solutions, a subsidiary dedicated to serving state and local government , and education organizations , as well as federal, civilian and defense agencies in the United States.

points.point: The newest structural decision is entering the AI datacenter business with up to ₹3,500 crores toward a long-term 50 MW plan, possibly part-funded by partners, equity and debt — a new vector inside HCLTech, explicitly not at the expense of the payout policy.
points.quote: In this regard, we will make a strategic investment of up to INR3,500 crores and with the potential to scale to 50 megawatts of capacity.

verdict.what_management_expects: Not applicable — no separation is proposed. For the inbound carve-outs management expects telecom IP, R&D talent and CSP access (HPE Telco Solutions) and a completed data-intelligence stack (Jaspersoft, ~$10–15m revenue/quarter). Restructuring is expected to restore margins toward 17.5–18.5% and give structural agility; software stays a separate segment at ~21.6% ROIC.
verdict.gaps: Everything: the texts contain no HCLTech separation — no scheme, rationale, perimeter, ratio, listing plan, timeline, requesting party or entity-level financials exists to reconstruct.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these calls or filings describes a demerger or spin-off of a business line out of IRB — the 'separation' management actually explains is an asset-level one, executed continuously under what it calls the B.E.S.T. strategy (first articulated as 'Bid, Execute, Stabilize & Transfer' in Feb 2025 and restated as 'Build–Execute–Stabilise–Transfer' in May 2026): mature, de-risked toll SPVs are separated out of IRB's own balance sheet and out of the Private InvIT (IRB Infrastructure Trust, where IRB holds 51% alongside GIC 25% and Cintra 24%) and sold into the listed Public InvIT (IRB InvIT Fund, where IRB is Sponsor/Project Manager with ~16–17%). The stated reason is capital, not strategic incompatibility: management said in Feb 2025 that 'this transfer of assets from the Private InvIT to the Public InvIT will ensure that there is no need to dilute equity or alternatively raise debt at IRB level,' and sized it — the first tranche of 5 matured assets at ~₹15,000 crore EV less ~₹6,500–7,000 crore debt releases ~₹8,000 crore of equity, which at 51% IRB ownership funds ~₹25,000 crore of new projects in the Private InvIT. The second stated reason is a risk-allocation split: construction and executional risk plus construction/O&M margin stays at IRB, development risk sits in the Private InvIT, and stabilised long-life cash flows sit in the Public InvIT, which management called 'a perfect fit' and a 'win-win' because the Public InvIT's portfolio expands and 'the residual life of the assets under management will get enhanced.' A third, accounting-driven reason was given in Feb 2025: because of 'the joint control mechanism in the Private InvIT, the cash flows generated aren't reflected in IRB's balance sheet, despite our 51% ownership… This creates an incomplete picture for investors' — leading to the new 'InvIT and related assets' segment and fair-value-through-P&L treatment, since >85% of IRB's EV sits in the asset business. Execution has been delivered with hard numbers: three SPVs (Kishangarh Gulabpura, Kaithal Tollway, Hapur Moradabad) at ~₹8,450 crore EV approved by Public InvIT unitholders (Aug 2025), releasing ₹4,905 crore cash and ~₹15,000 crore of bid capacity at 70:30 gearing while adding ~₹3,100 crore to the Sponsor's O&M order book (total ~₹33,600 crore); the VM7/Gandeva-Ena HAM SPV sold from IRB itself for ₹513 crore equity with IRB retained as Project Manager for ~15 years for up to ₹244.6 crore; and Solapur Yedeshi plus CG Tollway signed in Sept 2026 at ₹2,744 crore equity / ₹4,605 crore EV, part-funded by the Public InvIT's ₹2,351 crore raise (₹2,000 crore QIP + ₹351 crore preferential to IRB to hold ~16%). No lender or activist demand is cited; the pull named is the Government of India's asset-monetisation push, NHAI's pipeline (100,000→200,000 km, >₹50 trillion, ~40% PPP), Public InvIT unitholder approval 'with overwhelming majority support,' and persistent analyst pressure (Deepak Krishnan, Parikshit Kandpal) that book-value accounting was hiding the portfolio's value. Separately, the only formal Scheme of Arrangement in the filings runs the other way: a Scheme of Amalgamation (26 Aug 2026) folding nine wholly-owned subsidiaries into IRB to simplify structure and cut compliance cost — a consolidation, not a separation.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced obliquely on the Oct 30, 2024 call, where management conceded the Private InvIT stakes 'reflect at book value' and the real value 'is not getting duly captured,' and said 'even at the risk of jumping the gun' that it was seriously working on the BEST policy with 'more color… in near future.' It became concrete on Feb 1, 2025, when the Private InvIT issued a preliminary non-binding offer of 5 matured assets (~₹15,000 crore EV) to the Public InvIT, with the ~₹8,000 crore equity-unlock-to-₹25,000 crore-of-projects arithmetic and the new 'InvIT and related assets' segment introduced the same quarter. By Aug 14, 2025 the first tranche had shrunk to three SPVs at ₹8,450 crore EV but was unitholder-approved and quantified (₹4,905 crore cash, ~₹15,000 crore bid capacity), and by May 21, 2026 it had become a repeatable annual programme — ₹8,400 crore monetised, ₹4,900 crore unlocked, ₹14,000 crore added, asset base ₹80,000→₹94,000 crore — plus a HAM asset sold out of IRB itself (₹500 crore), two more (Solapur-Yedeshi, Chittorgarh-Gulabpura, ~₹4,500 crore EV) in motion and five remaining Private InvIT assets worth ₹30,000–35,000 crore queued over 2–3 years.

points.point: First hint: management said it was working on the BEST (bid, execute, stabilize, transfer) policy to keep resources available for upcoming TOT bids, but would not yet give detail — framed as supporting the Government of India's asset-monetisation drive.
points.quote: yes, we have been working on BEST policy, as we have always articulated, which is bid, execute, stabilize and transfer.

points.point: The trigger problem admitted to Deepak Krishnan: the Private InvIT stakes sat at book value, so robust portfolio cash flows were not visible in IRB's reported results, and the company was 'working on this'.
points.quote: What is happening is these investments today reflect at book value, and the real value that this portfolio is generating is not getting duly captured in the essence of the results to my mind.

points.point: The capital rationale was sized against the opportunity: NHAI doubling the highway grid from 100,000 to 200,000 km at over ₹50 trillion, ~40% (₹20 trillion) on PPP, with cash flow to come from asset monetisation, two InvITs and asset churn — enough to triple the portfolio in six to eight years.
points.quote: Supported by our extensive asset portfolio and prudent long-term leverage management, it will enable us to triple our portfolio over the next six to eight years, building on our established asset base of for FY 25.

points.point: The separation became formal: the Private InvIT issued a preliminary non-binding offer of five matured assets, ~₹15,000 crore EV per its independent valuer as of Sep-24, to the Public InvIT, with proceeds earmarked for new sector opportunities.
points.quote: Pvt InvIT - IRB Infrastructure Trust, has issued a preliminary and non-binding offer ("NBO") to offer 5 of its matured assets to Pub InvIT - IRB InvIT Fund.

points.point: The core stated purpose: fund growth from monetisation so that IRB itself never has to issue equity or borrow.
points.quote: This transfer of assets from the Private InvIT to the Public InvIT will ensure that there is no need to dilute equity or alternatively raise debt at IRB level.

points.point: What the receiving entity gets: a bigger portfolio and a longer weighted residual concession life, which management argued should lift the Public InvIT's yield as long-dated assets are added.
points.quote: For the Public InvIT, this is a win -win situation as not only their portfolio expands but also the residual life of the assets under management will get enhanced.

points.point: The structural logic is a deliberate risk split — development platform (Private InvIT), mature-asset platform (Public InvIT), and IRB keeping executional risk plus construction and O&M margin and stakes in both.
points.quote: I think this combination is a perfect fit, where value unlocking occurs based on the project's risk allocation. At the IRB end, we capture executional risk and reap benefits from construction and O&M margins.

points.point: The arithmetic given to Parikshit Kandpal: ₹15,000 crore EV less ~₹6,500–7,000 crore debt leaves ~₹8,000 crore of equity unlocked at the Private InvIT, enough to build another ₹25,000 crore of projects — and this was only the first tranche of a >₹60,000 crore Private InvIT.
points.quote: Let's do a simple calculation: if Rs. 8,000 crores -plus of equity unlocking occurs at the Private InvIT end, where IRB owns 51%, this equity capital can then be deployed for another Rs. 25,000 crores worth of projects that Private InvIT can develop.

points.point: An accounting/valuation motive: joint control of the Private InvIT kept its cash flows off IRB's balance sheet despite 51% ownership, which drove the new 'InvIT and related assets' segment and fair-valuation through P&L (management noted >85% of IRB's EV is the asset business and that ROE would improve).
points.quote: However, due to the joint control mechanism in the Private InvIT, the cash flows generated aren't reflected in IRB's balance sheet, despite our 51% ownership. This creates an incomplete picture for investors.

points.point: First tranche executed and approved by Public InvIT unitholders — three SPVs (Kishangarh Gulabpura, Kaithal Tollway, Hapur Moradabad) at ~₹8,450 crore EV, releasing ₹4,905 crore cash, which at 70:30 debt-equity supports ~₹15,000 crore of new bids and lifts the Sponsor's O&M order book by ~₹3,100 crore to ~₹33,600 crore.
points.quote: This transaction is expected to release ■4,905 crore in cash. Applying the standard 70:30 debt -to-equity funding model, this equity release enhances our financial capacity to bid for new projects valued at approximately ■15,000 crore.

points.point: The programme restated as delivered FY26 output: ~₹8,400 crore of assets monetised, ~₹4,900 crore of equity unlocked, ₹14,000 crore of projects added, asset base up from ₹80,000 crore to ₹94,000 crore, on track to ~₹1,40,000 crore in three years; plus one HAM asset (VM7) moved from IRB itself for ~₹500 crore equity value.
points.quote: We have successfully executed our B.E.S.T. (Build–Execute –Stabilise –Transfer) strategy, monetising mature road assets through our Public InvIT.

points.point: The separation replaces equity raising entirely: growth now comes from churning assets between the two InvITs, with IRB targeting net-debt-zero in five years, interest cost already down ~₹50 crore in the quarter and ₹150–200 crore more expected, dividend policy of 20%+ and guided 25% profit CAGR.
points.quote: We do not see any capital raising requirement at the IRB simply because if you look at our strategy of asset rotation, the growth is primarily going to come by unlocking capital by moving assets from Private InvIT to the Public InvIT .

points.point: Forward pipeline of separations quantified for Parikshit Kandpal: of the first 9–10 Private InvIT assets, three are transferred, two more (Solapur-Yedeshi and Chittorgarh-Gulabpura, ~₹4,500 crore EV) are in process, and five remain at ~₹30,000–35,000 crore EV to migrate over 2–3 years, against a Public InvIT that grew from ₹8,000 crore to ₹18,000 crore EV and targets ~₹40,000 crore AUM.
points.quote: So another 5 assets continue at the private end which have an EV of roughly INR 30,000 crores – INR 35,000 crores which will be migrated to the Public InvIT platform over next 2- 3 years.

points.point: Why monetisation rather than new BOT building is the growth engine: management conceded to Alok Deora that the much-touted BOT pipeline has not materialised and that portfolio growth will come primarily from TOT/monetisation and asset rotation.
points.quote: I tend to agree with you that our focus will definitely remain more on the asset monetization side and we will be unleashing the asset rotation strategy to grow our portfolio and that will remain our forte.

points.point: The only formal Scheme of Arrangement in the filings is the opposite of a separation: the Board on 26 Aug 2026 approved amalgamating nine wholly-owned subsidiaries (ATR Infrastructure, Aryan Toll Road, Aryan Hospitality, IRB Goa Tollway, IRB Infra Industries, GE1 Expressway, IRB PS Highway, Mhaiskar Infrastructure, Thane Ghodbunder Toll Road) into IRB, with no consideration, no new shares and no change in shareholding, subject to NCLT Mumbai.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation is intended to simplify the group structure, improve operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization and reduce administrative and compliance costs.

verdict.what_management_expects: IRB: equity unlocked (~₹4,900cr in FY26) redeployed without equity dilution or IRB-level debt; rising operating leverage, recurring construction/O&M and project-manager fees, 18–20% construction margins, net-debt-zero by 2030, interest cost down ₹150–200cr, 25% profit CAGR, 20%+ dividend payout, better ROE. Private InvIT: fresh capital for new TOT/BOT development. Public InvIT: larger portfolio, longer residual asset life, higher yield and distributions.
verdict.gaps: No spin-off of EPC from assets is proposed or explained; no rationale, timing, tax or accounting detail for the nine-subsidiary amalgamation; GIC/Cintra consent economics and three scanned calls absent.

verdict.segment_name: No reported segment for the demerged group — figures are entity-level "Share in Profit / (Loss)" for Mhaiskar Infrastructure Private Limited, ATR Infrastructure Private Limited, Aryan Toll Road Private Limited, Aryan Hospitality Private Limited, IRB Goa Tollway Private Limited, IRB Infra Industries Private Limited (formerly IRB Kolhapur Integrated Road Development Company Private Limited), GE1 Expressway Private Limited and IRB PS Highway Private Limited
verdict.measure_notes: PAT = post-tax 'Share in Profit / (Loss)' per Schedule III note (Note 37 FY24 / Note 40 FY25 & FY26), net of intra-group elimination; the figure shown is the arithmetic sum of the eight named entities' individually disclosed amounts (each entity's own number is in the source page). These entities are not a reportable segment: the segment note reports only BOT/TOT, InvITs & Related Assets, Construction and Unallocated corporate, so no revenue, EBITDA, EBIT or segment result exists for this group. Entity-wise revenue and operating profit are not disclosed on any supplied page.

verdict.rationale: On the documents supplied, Lloyds Engineering Works Ltd. (LEWL) is NOT separating a business — it is doing the opposite: a Scheme of Merger by Absorption approved by all four boards on 29 December 2025 that folds three group entities INTO the listed company, with Appointed Date 1 April 2025. The transferors are Lloyds Infrastructure & Construction Ltd. (LICL, an unlisted associate in which LEWL holds ~24.20%, EPC/roads, bridges, railways, industrial civil, slurry pipelines, BOOT/BOO/BOLT/PPP), Metalfab Hightech Pvt. Ltd. (MHPL, 76% subsidiary, heavy fabrication for steel, railways and infrastructure) and Techno Industries Pvt. Ltd. (TIPL, wholly owned, elevators, escalators, motors and pumps); LEWL itself makes process plant equipment for hydrocarbon, steel, captive power, marine, ports and nuclear heat exchangers. The headline number management cites repeatedly is LICL's 'robust order book of over ₹4,500 crores', which combined with LEWL's manufacturing and execution capability is said to create one 'unified engineering and infrastructure company' able to bid for larger, multidisciplinary contracts; the merging businesses are described as having 'complementary capabilities, overlapping customer base and shared execution requirements'. The stated problems it solves are structural and financial: duplicated/redundant functions, fragmented management, scattered technical and financial resources, a complex multi-entity shareholding that burdens the 'ever-evolving regulatory compliance framework' and governance/transparency, and a smaller balance sheet with costlier borrowing — hence 'improved borrowing capabilities and reduced borrowing costs' and 'unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined businesses'. Scale being consolidated: LICL FY26 revenue ₹1,902.25 cr / PAT ₹173.81 cr / EBITDA ₹280.01 cr (vs ₹1,060.98 cr / ₹66.66 cr in FY25 and ₹395.14 cr / ₹22.10 cr in FY24), MHPL ₹173.36 cr / ₹33.47 cr, TIPL ₹185.74 cr / ₹5.20 cr, against LEWL's own ₹1,052.22 cr / ₹118.27 cr / ₹188.12 cr; assets/liabilities transferred are LICL ₹1,315.93 cr/₹1,012.61 cr, MHPL ₹321.60 cr/₹269.67 cr, TIPL ₹240.83 cr/₹158.55 cr. Consideration is 1,798 LEWL shares per 1,500 LICL shares (Streamland Estate LLP gets 36,19,97,330 shares, Pravriddhi Trust 59,93,333, all classified Public) and 94 LEWL shares per 5 MHPL shares (Manan Agrawal 1,29,72,000); nothing is paid for TIPL as a wholly owned subsidiary. Who asked: no investor, lender or partner demand is recorded anywhere — it is board-driven, with lenders merely consenting (NOC from lending scheduled commercial banks/financial institutions obtained, 'no conditions imposed by the lenders'), CCI clearing it on 12 May 2026, NSE/BSE observation letters on 18/19 May 2026, NCLT ordering meetings on 19 August 2026, and on 16 October 2026 equity shareholders and unsecured creditors (758,413,241 votes, 72.54% of outstanding, 100% in favour) approving it.
verdict.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts were provided ('no transcripts on file'), so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the only record is filings. It surfaces fully formed on 29 December 2025 (simultaneous board approvals, valuation by Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP and fairness opinion from Mark Corporate Advisors, both dated that day), is prepared through 2026 by moving MHPL's registered office to Mumbai (20 December 2025) and TIPL's from Ahmedabad to Mumbai (Regional Director order, 27 February 2026), clears CCI (12 May 2026), the exchanges (18–19 May 2026) and NCLT (19 August 2026), and is approved by shareholders and unsecured creditors on 16 October 2026 with results filed 17 October 2026. In parallel the group consolidates further rather than separating: a 17 August 2026 preferential allotment of 7,00,42,458 shares at ₹71.25 swaps in 1,66,35,087 shares of Steel Infra Solutions Company Ltd. (SISCOL), plus 7,00,000 shares for cash; and on 6 August 2026 the board re-cut the April 2025 rights-issue objects (₹987.25 cr gross, ₹660.52 cr spent, ₹326.73 cr unutilised at 30 June 2026), cutting the Bhilai Engineering Corporation asset purchase from ₹130.25 cr to ₹71.25 cr and adding ₹86.59 cr to working capital — passed by postal ballot on 25 September 2026 (99.9948% in favour).

points.point: The scheme is a merger by absorption of LICL, MHPL and TIPL into listed LEWL, with the transferors dissolved without winding up — a consolidation, not a separation or demerger.
points.quote: Merger of LICL, MHPL and TIPL with LEWL and dissolution of LICL, MHPL and TIPL without winding up.

points.point: The core stated purpose is to end the split between the listed equipment-manufacturing business and the group's EPC/construction business by putting them in one company.
points.quote: The amalgamation will create a unified engineering and infrastructure company.

points.point: The one hard number management leans on is LICL's order book, repeated in the synopsis, the explanatory statement and the revenue-capacity section.
points.quote: The amalgamation of LICL with LEWL will enable the combined entity to leverage LICL’s robust order book of over Rs. 4500 crores and proven project execution capabilities, thereby expanding operational scale in India, and enhancing competitiveness in bidding for and executing larger, multidisciplinary contracts.

points.point: The businesses are presented as overlapping rather than distinct, which is the stated reason to combine instead of keep apart.
points.quote: Considering the complementary capabilities, overlapping customer base and shared execution requirements of the manufacturing/engineering business and the infrastructure/construction business, the proposed restructuring would enable the combined entity to leverage LICL's robust order book of over ₹4,500 crores together with LEWL's proven manufacturing and project execution capabilities, thereby expanding operational scale, achieving focused management, consolidating technical and financial resources, and enhancing competitiveness in bidding for and executing larger, multidisciplinary contracts across the sector.

points.point: Problem named: a complicated multi-entity group structure creating compliance burden and weaker governance/transparency.
points.quote: The amalgamation will result in a simplified shareholding and group structure, thereby streamlining the ever-evolving regulatory compliance framework.

points.point: Problem named: cash and capital trapped in separate entities, a smaller balance sheet and higher cost of borrowing.
points.quote: The combined entity will have enhanced financial strengths with large net worth, strong asset base and balance sheet, greater efficiency in cash management, unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined businesses, efficient capital allocation and better capital utilization.

points.point: Problem named: duplicated functions and dispersed management across the four companies; cost synergies and compliance-cost reduction are the claimed fix.
points.quote: The combined entity will have greater operational efficiency through elimination of duplication/redundant functions, centralized and focused management, consolidating and optimizing resources under a unified leadership;

verdict.rationale: Two distinct things are going on, and only one of them is explained in detail. The hard, documented action is a composite scheme of arrangement approved by SAMIL's board on 07.02.2025 and sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26.10.2026, with an Appointed Date of 01.04.2024: the 'Automotive Manufacturing and Services Business' (the Demerged Undertaking) is carved out of wholly owned subsidiary Samvardhana Motherson Innovative Solutions Limited (SMISL) and vested in listed parent Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL), while SMISL's 'Remaining Business' stays behind; alongside it, Samvardhana Motherson Auto System Private Limited (SMAS) amalgamates into SAMIL and Motherson Machinery and Automations Limited (MMAL) amalgamates into SMISL, both amalgamating companies dissolving without winding up and their share capital simply cancelled. Management's stated reasons for the demerger are focused management attention and leadership, independence and flexibility over each business's cash flows so projects can be run 'more consistently and advantageously', a leaner and more focused organisation, a reduction in layers of investments producing a simpler structure, more transparent shareholding with better visibility and accountability, and enhanced shareholder value. The merger legs are justified separately as eliminating multiple group entities, pooling financial, human, technological and managerial resources, cutting duplicated administrative expenses and overheads and compliances, better day-to-day coordination, and unlocking synergies across products, customers, technology and manufacturing. No valuation, ratio or cash changes hands: because SMISL is a 100% subsidiary, 'no shares will be issued by the Resulting Company', and SMAS/MMAL shareholders likewise get nothing — the scheme is pure structural plumbing within wholly owned entities. Separately and far more loudly, the Sep 2025 investor meet framed a different kind of separation as a Vision 2030 deliverable: having 'successfully took out MSWIL', management said many businesses are 'ripe to now leave the SAMIL fold and be independently listed on their own', explicitly flagging aerospace (grown 550x in five years, ~USD 250mn revenue, >USD 1bn order book then, USD 1.6bn by May 2026) as 'probably ripe for the independence'. Nobody outside management — no investor, lender, customer or JV partner — is cited as asking for either; the RD, ROC and Official Liquidator raised only process points (SMAS's negative net worth, protection of creditors, BEN-2 filings, Income Tax scrutiny), and the Petitioners answered that nothing in the Companies Act bars merging a negative-net-worth company and that both demerged and resulting net worth are positive.
verdict.evolution: The idea first appears as corporate action on 07.02.2025 (board approval, intimated to exchanges 28.02.2025), then NCLT first motion on 30.05.2025 and further service affidavits through 18.09.2025; the earnings calls never mention it. The only management articulation comes at the Sep 2025 investor meet, where Vaaman Sehgal makes 'independent companies from SAMIL' a Vision 2030 target, citing the MSWIL precedent and naming aerospace as the likeliest candidate. The Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 calls say nothing about any separation — they stay on European restructuring, consumer electronics GF1/GF2/GF3, aerospace order book and acquisitions (Atsumitec, Yutaka Giken, Nexans Autoelectric). Final NCLT sanction landed 26.10.2026, binding from the 01.04.2024 Appointed Date, with SMAS and MMAL dissolved.

verdict.rationale: These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off, divestment or carve-out of any Newgen business — the premise cannot be supported from them, and I will not invent one. The only corporate restructuring disclosed is the exact opposite: on 23 October 2026 the Board approved a Scheme of Arrangement for the amalgamation of Newgen Computers Technologies Limited (NCTL), a wholly owned subsidiary, INTO the listed parent Newgen Software Technologies Limited (NSTL), under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013, with an Appointed Date of 1 April 2026. NCTL is a dormant shell: paid-up capital of INR 0.21 crore, turnover of NIL and net worth of INR 0.85 crore for FY ended 31 March 2026, against NSTL's paid-up capital of INR 141.16 crore (since risen to INR 142.51 crore), turnover of INR 1,419.93 crore and net worth of INR 1,631.72 crore; it was originally incorporated to deal in computer hardware, peripherals and software. The stated reasons are purely structural and administrative: both companies are under common management, so folding NCTL into NSTL simplifies the existing group structure into a single legal entity and rationalises administrative, operational, legal and regulatory compliances and their associated costs, giving a more streamlined corporate structure and efficient utilisation of resources that creates and preserves long-term value for all stakeholders. Because NCTL is wholly owned, no shares are issued and no cash or other consideration is paid, no share exchange ratio or valuation report is required, the shareholding pattern of the listed entity is unchanged, and under Regulation 37(6) no 'No Objection Letter' is needed from BSE or NSE; the Scheme still needs shareholder/creditor approval (to the extent not dispensed with) and NCLT sanction. No lender, partner, customer or investor is identified anywhere as having asked for this, and no margin, capital-release or valuation benefit is quantified. The only shareholder-driven capital-structure asks in the transcripts are repeated requests for a buyback (Rahul Jain, April 2026; Sanjay, July 2026) and questions on acquisitions and the cash pile — not a separation.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces in any of the eleven earnings calls from Jan 2025 through the Jul 2026 (Q1 FY27) call: not one question or management remark mentions a demerger, spin-off, separation or subsidiary merger across Jan 2025, May 2025, Jul 2025, Nov 2025, Jan 2026, May 2026 or Jul 2026. The adjacent corporate-action discussion runs the other way — inorganic growth and acquisitions (May 2026: Jeet says options are being explored to accelerate mature-market go-to-market and add complementary product technologies; Jul 2026: management says an acquisition has been deliberated 'for last couple of years' without finding the right fit) plus buyback requests from Rahul Jain (May 2026 call) and Sanjay (Jul 2026 call), with management saying inputs had been given to the Board. The amalgamation therefore appears for the first time, fully formed, in the 23 October 2026 Board outcome and its Annexure-II, alongside the Q2 FY27 results; it is dated after the last transcript provided, so no call explains or precedes it.

verdict.rationale: There is no business separation in these texts: across all four calls (Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026) and all four filings, Oswal Pumps never announces a demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement, or listing of any division — the only entity being separated from the group is a dormant shell, wholly owned subsidiary Oswal Green Private/Industries Private Limited, which the board resolved to strike off because 'it has no significant business operations', with a written-off investment of just INR 0.10 million. Every other structural move runs the opposite way — toward consolidation and deeper backward integration of the same solar-pumping value chain. On 08 June 2026 the company bought an additional 13,07,000 shares of associate Walso Solar Solution Pvt Ltd (mounting structures, BOS, turnkey solar pumping components) at Rs 28/share for Rs 3.66 crore via rights issue, taking it from 38.5% (plus 4.5% on 08 April 2026 and 8% in June) to 51% and converting it from associate into subsidiary, on the stated logic that vertical integration lets the group 'design and develop new products, optimize our operational costs and improve our margins'; Walso's FY26 turnover was INR 1,702.65 million versus INR 720.54 million in FY25. On 10 October 2026 the board approved a greenfield 1.2 GW solar cell plant at Karnal under WOS Oswal Solar Energy Pvt Ltd (formerly Oswal Solar Structure), total project cost INR 4,558.50 million, funded partly by re-directing INR 1,598.50 million of unutilised IPO proceeds away from the Aluminium Frame Facility, the remaining 300 MW EVA encapsulant line and the remaining 500 MW of module capacity, because DCR cells — not frames — are 'the binding constraint', with domestic cell makers offering long-term contracts 'only at elevated prices' and demanding 'very large deposits'; the captive plant is to cover ~75% of cell requirement. Earlier, the December 2025 postal-ballot 'First Variation' merely relocated the module plant to a larger adjacent Karnal parcel (28,000 sq m vs 13,983 sq m, 15-year lease from 25 June 2024) to share workforce, R&D, admin infrastructure and an existing electricity feeder. The one genuinely new legal vehicle is additive, not a carve-out: Oswal Solar Energy incorporated SPV Oswal Doon Baran Bundi Solar Projects Limited with Doon Infrapower Projects Pvt Ltd, holding 60%, to execute HAM rooftop PV on Rajasthan state government buildings. Management's answer to its real problem — single-scheme dependency on PM-KUSUM, whose 2.0 rollout slipped from 'before the end of this fiscal' to June 2026+ — is diversification inside the existing group (rooftop/PM Surya Ghar, utility, C&I, ~300 MW pipeline, exports, private network, in-house inverters), explicitly kept as backward integration and never 'a revenue model', not separation.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea ever surfaces. Aug 2025 describes a fully integrated group (pumps/motors/controllers in-house, modules via Oswal Solar, structures/BOS via 38.5% associate Walso) and a backup plan of exports and private-market pumps if KUSUM 2.0 slips; Nov 2025 adds the module-plant land shift and the Oswal Green strike-off. Feb 2026, after receivable days hit 157 and Maharashtra's Magel Tyala payments stalled, management says the KUSUM 2.0 delay 'brought a point of diversification to our mind' — new verticals, EPC for large rooftops, invoice discounting — all housed internally. May 2026 formalises that with the first PM Surya Ghar order and the 60% Rajasthan HAM SPV, and the October 2026 cell-plant variation pulls capital further into the group rather than out of it.

points.point: The only entity exiting the group is a dormant wholly owned subsidiary being struck off — not a business separation but the wind-up of a shell with no operations (investment of INR 0.10 million written off).

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these three years of earnings calls or in the filings provided describes Premier Energies separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving off any business, and there is no scheme of arrangement in the record — so the premise of the question cannot be supported from these texts. The direction management describes is the opposite: consolidation and diversification into one group. Across the Nov 2025, Jan 2026 and May 2026 calls the company adds businesses rather than sheds them — a 51% stake in transformer maker Transcon Ind Limited for up to ₹5,003.00 million (₹2,500.02 million for 34.21% in Dec 2025, the balance ₹2,502.98 million in April 2026, taking Transcon and its subsidiary Neotrafo to subsidiary/step-down status), a 51% inverter JV with Syrma SGS around KSolare (FY25 revenue cited at ₹143 crores), a 6 GWh-per-phase cell-to-pack BESS line at ₹280 crores, aluminium frames at ₹260 crores, a 10 GW ingot-wafer project at about ₹5,900 crores, and a 51% stake in HeliosAnthos Energies for ₹10.45 lakh. Management's stated rationale for keeping these together is synergy, not separation: Vinay Rustagi argued 10 GVA of transformer demand per GW of renewable capacity added, with roughly 80% of installs now renewable, so transformers, inverters and BESS go to 'the same clients who we are selling our modules', 'reducing the cost of customer acquisition', and the new businesses together with BESS are expected to contribute 'approximately 30% of our revenue over time'. The only two events in the record that even resemble a separation are (a) the voluntary winding-up by strike-off of IBD Solar Powertech (Pvt.) Ltd, a Bangladesh step-down wholly owned subsidiary with nil revenue, nil turnover contribution and negative net worth of ₹2.09 lakh, where the Reg. 30 annexure marks every sale/disposal/scheme field 'Not Applicable'; and (b) the abandonment of the KSolare acquisition in Q1 FY27 — a reversal of an inbound deal, not a carve-out, with 'no financial implications arising from the same'. There is also an accounting-only split — Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment became a separate reportable segment under Ind AS 108 from the Transcon acquisition date — but that is segment disclosure, not a legal or structural separation. On these texts alone, there is no separation to explain, and no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for one.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces: in Feb 2025 and May 2025 management frames 'Mission 2028' as a single integrated 10 GW ingot-wafer-cell-module platform plus BESS and inverters, with ₹125,000 million of capex inside one group. Jul 2025 and Nov 2025 add, not subtract — the 4.8 GW cell line is scaled to 7 GW, and the KSolare (inverter) and Transcon (transformer) acquisitions are announced as 'highly complementary and value accretive'. Jan 2026 reports the Transcon acquisition completed in Dec 2025 and KSolare closing 'in the next one month'; by May 2026 the KSolare deal is dropped for lack of agreement on final documentation while Transcon's 51% is completed, and the Aug 2026 and Sep 2026 filings record only a new reportable segment and the strike-off of the dormant Bangladesh shell. At no point in May 2025, Jul 2025, Nov 2025, Jan 2026 or May 2026 does any analyst or executive mention a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme.

points.point: The only disposal-type disclosure in the filings is the strike-off of a dormant, non-operating Bangladesh step-down subsidiary — not a business separation; the Reg. 30 annexure marks turnover contribution nil, net worth negative ₹2.09 lakh, and every sale/disposal/scheme-of-arrangement field 'Not Applicable'.
points.quote: IBD, had no revenue or commercial operations and had filed an application for voluntary winding-up by way of strike off of name on 10th October, 2023 with the Office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms, Bangladesh.

points.point: Transcon is described as a future growth engine being scaled sevenfold inside the group (2.5 GVA to 16.75 GVA by July 2026) and moved up into MV/HV/EHV, with a ₹1,000 crore-plus top line targeted by FY28 — the opposite of a carve-out.

points.quote: I think that is the reason why the transaction could not be completed.

points.point: The only 'split' in the record is an accounting one: a new reportable segment created by the Transcon acquisition under Ind AS 108, effective from the April 3, 2026 acquisition date.

points.point: Forward capital plans are framed as one diversified platform funded centrally (FY27 capex ₹5,100 crores across cells, ingot-wafers, batteries and inverters; ₹5,000 crores enabling fundraise resolution), with no mention of releasing capital by separating an entity.

verdict.what_management_expects: Not applicable — no separation is described. Management's stated expectations are for the combined group: ~30% of revenue from inverters, BESS and transformers over time; Transcon margins rising toward 20-25% EBITDA as mix shifts to MV/HV/EHV with 7x-10x fixed-asset turns; cross-sell synergies lowering customer-acquisition cost; and debt/equity held near 1.0 and debt/EBITDA near 1.5 through the capex cycle.
verdict.gaps: The calls and filings never mention any demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement, so no rationale, no requesting party, and no expected benefits are explained anywhere.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe Power Mech Projects separating, demerging or spinning off any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no NCLT filing, no record date, no share-entitlement ratio, and no management discussion of hiving off a division on any of the six calls (May 2025 through May 2026) or in either filing (postal ballot of 10 November 2025 and AGM notice of 8 August 2026). The only occurrences of the words 'merger/demerger, sale of division/undertaking' are inside the standard corporate-action adjustment clause of the proposed 'Power Mech Projects Limited -Employee Stock Option Plan -2026' (10,00,000 options, of which up to 2,00,000 for subsidiary employees, 3.16%–3.19% of capital on a fully diluted basis), which merely says options would be re-priced fairly if such an action ever occurred; it is boilerplate, not a plan. What the texts actually show is the opposite of separation — consolidation and the use of subsidiaries/SPVs inside one listed entity: the Transmission/Electrical division was wound down and its portfolio 'shifted' into the Civil business while a new BOP EPC vertical was added (May 2026); a 100% subsidiary, PM Green, was incorporated for the 250 MW / 1,000 MWh West Bengal BESS BOO project (INR 800 crore capex, INR 103 crore/year over 15 years, INR 1,563 crore, 51% Power Mech-led consortium, 16–18% equity IRR) which was later cancelled by the West Bengal State Electricity department; MDO assets sit in SPVs (Tasra SPV carrying INR 400 crore of coal-handling-plant and railway-siding capex, KBP raising a INR 256 crore term loan, the INR 690–700 crore washery built in Power Mech's own books) and riverbed-mineral/sand mines sit in LLPs taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated effective tax rate to 28–29%. Portfolio pruning that did happen was order-book, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders (Kawai, Tiroda, Mundra) were removed by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi job, and management said it is 'not showing interest' in new water projects, with the UP Jal Jeevan Mission book run down to about INR 900 crore pending central funding. Management's stated strategic direction is to concentrate the same listed company on power, O&M, BOP EPC and MDO (visibility to FY30, 12.3% FY26 EBITDA rising toward 14% by FY30) — not to separate anything. If a separation exists, it is documented somewhere outside the material supplied here.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces: across CALL Feb 2025, CALL May 2025, CALL Aug 2025, CALL Nov 2025, CALL Feb 2026 and CALL May 2026 no analyst asks about a demerger and no manager raises one; the only corporate-structure questions concern succession (Rohit Sajja's induction to the Board, May 2025) and fund-raising (QIP of INR 240 crore, borrowing limit raised from INR 5,000 crore to INR 7,500 crore in the November 2025 postal ballot). The two filings in the window are an ESOP-2026 postal ballot (10 November 2025, voting 21 November–20 December 2025, with a 1%-of-capital grant resolution) and the 27th AGM notice (8 August 2026, meeting 17 September 2026) re-tabling the same ESOP plus a INR 1.50 dividend, independent-director appointment and director remuneration — none of which mention a separation. The nearest thing to a structural change evolves as consolidation: PM Green is created for BESS (disclosed CALL Feb 2026), the BESS order is then cancelled (CALL May 2026), and the Electrical/Transmission division is declared 'over' and merged into Civil while BOP EPC is created as the new vertical (CALL Nov 2025 signalling, confirmed CALL May 2026).

points.point: The closest actual restructuring is internal consolidation, not separation: the Transmission/Electrical segment was discontinued and absorbed into the Civil division, with BOP EPC created as the replacement reporting vertical.
points.quote: No, it is a different business because, actually, earlier the Transmission division used to do the transmission erection of the lines and other things. That business is over now.

points.point: Management explicitly folded the electrical/T&D portfolio into civil rather than separating it, and added BOP EPC as a new line of activity.
points.quote: So, now we shifted that entire portfolio to the civil business, and we added a new line of activity of BOP EPC business.

points.point: New energy-transition activity was housed in a wholly owned subsidiary (PM Green) kept inside the group, described as a cautious experiment, not a business being carved out.
points.quote: So , we have incorporated a 100% subsidiary as a PM Green for this, and this is a small attempt we to see where the renewable segment fits into the Power Mech's vision of sustained growth and margins.

points.point: MDO assets are held in SPVs within the consolidated group, with capex split between the Tasra SPV and Power Mech standalone - a financing structure, not a separation.
points.quote: And in TASRA SPV, INR 400 crores of Capex Tasra Coal Handling Plant and railway siding is added.

points.point: Riverbed-mineral/sand-mine operations run through LLP entities taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated tax rate to 28-29% - the only structure-driven economic friction management quantified.
points.quote: The exceptional revenue generat ed from the Riverbed Minerals business was booked through L LP. Where applicable tax rate is 35%, compared to 25% at the company level .

points.point: Portfolio pruning that did occur was contractual, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders were removed from the order book by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi package.
points.quote: So, we have taken a djustment of non moving FGD orders – after discussion and negotiations with the client.
