verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not the Visa & Consular or Digital segment discussed on the calls, but the Joint Liability Group (JLG) financial-lending business housed inside Atyati Technologies Private Limited (ATPL), a step-down subsidiary of BLS that became part of the group only on July 2, 2026 — after the last transcript on record (May 20, 2026). On September 28, 2026 ATPL's board approved a Business Transfer Agreement to sell and transfer the JLG Business Undertaking on a going-concern basis, as a slump sale, to TVAM Technologies Private Limited for Rs. 59,49,000, subject to post-closing adjustments based on closing accounts, and subject to lender, regulatory and other consents, expected to close in about 90 days. The only reason management has given anywhere in these texts is in the filing itself: the transaction 'forms part of the Company's broader business re-organisation and operational restructuring initiatives' and is 'intended to streamline business operations, optimise deployment of resources and enable greater strategic and operational focus through an appropriate business structure.' The numbers cited are that JLG turnover was Rs. 100.56 crores, i.e. 26.8% of ATPL's total FY2025-26 turnover, while its net worth, computed as at July 1, 2026 (no separate March 31, 2026 net worth exists), was only Rs. 59.49 lakhs, or 0.9% of ATPL's total net worth — so a quarter of ATPL's revenue sits on under 1% of its net worth, and the consideration is set exactly at that book net worth. ATPL keeps its Business Correspondent services for banks for last-mile connectivity and its technology solutions; only the micro-lending book goes. The buyer is a related party — 'TVAM is a Private Company in which a director of ATPL is a Director and Member' — and the company states the deal is on arm's length terms; TVAM is not a promoter/promoter-group entity. It is not a Scheme of Arrangement, Regulation 37A does not apply since the transferor is a step-down subsidiary, and there is no change in BLS's shareholding pattern. No lender, investor or partner is named as having asked for it; the filing frames it purely as internal reorganisation.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces on the earnings calls: across all ten transcripts (Feb 2024 through May 20, 2026) neither Atyati, the JLG lending book, nor any divestment is mentioned, and the only structural logic management ever articulates is the opposite direction — the Aug 6, 2024 call explains the BLS E-Services IPO as wanting to run the two businesses separately and keep visa cash out of digital, and on Feb 12, 2025 management flatly rejected a suggestion to spin off the Digital business, calling it not a drag. The restructuring instead appears only in filings, and in escalating steps: Nov 11, 2025 (board approves strike-off of dormant WOS Reired BLS International), Aug 17-18, 2026 (Turkish step-down subsidiary BLS International Vize Hizmetleri merged into iDATA 'to align the business synergies of step down subsidiaries'), then Sept 28-29, 2026, when ATPL's board approves the JLG slump sale to TVAM — within three months of ATPL joining the group on July 2, 2026. The plan therefore did not evolve in public commentary at all; the first and only explanation is the September 2026 Regulation 30 disclosure.

points.point: The stated rationale is internal reorganisation, not a problem with the business: the JLG transfer is positioned as part of BLS's broader re-organisation and operational restructuring, aimed at streamlining operations, optimising resource deployment and sharpening strategic and operational focus.
points.quote: The proposed transaction forms part of the Company’s broader business re-organisation and operational restructuring initiatives.

points.point: The purpose clause names the three intended outcomes — streamlining, resource optimisation and focus — delivered via an 'appropriate business structure', with no quantified benefit attached.
points.quote: The transfer of the JLG Business Undertaking of Atyati Technologies Private Limited (“ATPL”) to TVAM Technologies Private Limited (“TVAM”) is intended to streamline business operations, optimise deployment of resources and enable greater strategic and operational focus through an appropriate business structure .

points.point: Scale of what leaves: JLG contributed Rs. 100.56 crores of revenue, 26.8% of ATPL's FY26 turnover — a material revenue line for the subsidiary, though immaterial to consolidated BLS revenue of Rs. 2,998 crores.
points.quote: Turnover of JLG Business Undertaking was                   Rs. 100.56 Crores (Indian Rupees One Hundred Crore and Fifty-Six Lakh Only) which represents 26.8% of the Total Turnover of ATPL for Financial Year 2025-26.

points.point: The undertaking carries almost no net worth — Rs. 59.49 lakhs, 0.9% of ATPL's net worth, computed as at July 1, 2026 because no divisional net worth existed at March 31, 2026 — and the consideration was set at exactly that figure, Rs. 59,49,000, subject to closing-account adjustments.
points.quote: However, the Net worth as computed as on July 1, 2026 for the unit or division or undertaking is Rs. 59.49 lacs (Indian Rupees Fifty-Nine Lakhs and Forty-Nine Thousand Only) which represents 0.9% of the total Net Worth of ATPL.

points.point: The buyer is an ATPL-related party — a private company in which an ATPL director is both director and member — and the company asserts arm's-length pricing; TVAM is not in BLS's promoter or group.
points.quote: TVAM is a Private Company in which a director of ATPL is a Director and Member. Therefore, TVAM is a related party of ATPL.

points.point: Mechanics and ring-fencing: a going-concern slump sale rather than a Scheme of Arrangement, needing lender/regulatory consents, targeted to close in roughly 90 days, with no impact on BLS shareholders' holdings.
points.quote: There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the listed entity pursuant to the Transaction.

points.point: An earlier step in the same restructuring: the Turkish step-down subsidiary BLS International Vize Hizmetleri (FY26 standalone revenue INR 167,858,678) was merged into iDATA (INR 1,877,772,130) on August 17, 2026, with no cash or new shares and its capital cancelled.
points.quote: To align the business synergies of step down subsidiaries.

points.point: Asked directly whether the Digital business would be spun off into a separate entity as E-Services was, management refused and defended it as a volume, INR-denominated business whose profit had doubled year-on-year to INR 18 crores.
points.quote: See, first of all, we do not believe it's a drag.

points.point: The only separation logic management ever volunteered on a call was for the BLS E-Services IPO — keeping the visa and digital businesses insulated so that neither funds the other's growth.
points.quote: Jaiprakash, we basically wanted to deal in both the businesses separately.

points.point: That insulation rationale was explicitly about cash ring-fencing between segments — the same 'appropriate structure' language later used for JLG, but applied to keeping capital pools apart rather than exiting a business.
points.quote: We do not want to use the cash generated by Visa business into the digital business requirement as well the digital business cash generation into Visa.

points.point: Context for what remains: digital was described as three verticals — business correspondent, loan distribution and e-governance — with loan distribution (Aadifidelis, ~3-5% EBITDA margin) the acknowledged drag on digital's margin, which fell from 14.2% to ~7%.
points.quote: So in digital offering, we have currently 3 verticals. One is the business correspondent which is a banking business wherein we provide the last mile banking. Then we have our loan distribution company, which we acquired last year, and the third is the E -governance where we provide, (we call it G2C ) government to citizens.

points.point: The last call before the sale gave no hint of any divestment — capital priorities were framed entirely as more acquisitions and contract deployment, in both Visa and Digital, with Rs. 1,434 crores net cash.
points.quote: So major utilization of the cash will be for the expansion of the existing business as well as for inorganic growth, which we plan to do.

verdict.what_management_expects: Only the filing speaks: streamlined operations, optimised resource deployment, and greater strategic and operational focus for the retained business through an appropriate structure. ATPL keeps Business Correspondent last-mile banking and technology solutions, shedding 26.8% of its turnover carrying 0.9% of its net worth. BLS shareholding is unchanged. No margin, capital-release, valuation or re-rating benefit is claimed anywhere.
verdict.gaps: Calls never mention Atyati, JLG or the sale. Unexplained: valuation basis for Rs. 59.49 lakh, margin/loss profile of JLG, use of proceeds, lender consents needed, related-party safeguards, and who initiated it.

verdict.segment_name: Joint Liability Group / JLG Business Undertaking (Atyati Technologies Private Limited / Tvam Technologies Private Limited) — not a reported segment in these pages; the only reportable segments are Visa and Consular Services and Digital Services
verdict.unit: ₹ lakh (consolidated segment notes) / ₹ crore (presentations) — no JLG-specific figures stated in either unit
verdict.measure_notes: The documents disclose only two Ind AS 108 reportable segments: (a) Visa and Consular Services and (b) Digital Services (E-Governance, Business Correspondent and allied services). Segment result is labelled 'Segment results (profit/(loss) after taxes)' in the annual reports — in FY24/FY25 it sums to Profit Before Tax, and in FY26 it is labelled 'Total profit before interest and tax' before finance cost, i.e. effectively a pre-tax/EBIT-type measure, not PAT. verdict.rationale: On the texts supplied, Capillary is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business, and no scheme of arrangement, slump sale or business-transfer document is present — so no management rationale for one exists to reconstruct. The only corporate separation of any kind disclosed is the November 2, 2026 intimation that Capillary Technologies (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., a non-operative step-down wholly-owned subsidiary, has completed voluntary deregistration in China; the company's stated reasons are simply that it 'was not carrying on any business operations', that its proposed closure had already been flagged in the RHP dated November 18, 2025, and that it is not a material subsidiary. The quantified impact given is nil: FY26 revenue 'Nil' and net worth of INR 0.50 million, with the Annexure A disclosure marking consideration, buyer, agreement date and 'outside Scheme of Arrangement' all as 'NA' — i.e. no sale, no consideration, no counterparty. Both earnings calls (February 6, 2026 for Q3 FY26 and May 6, 2026 for Q4/FY26) run in the opposite direction: management describes consolidating businesses in, not out — four completed acquisitions (Persuade, Brierley, Rewards, Kognitiv in May 2025) plus the $35 million SessionM merchant-loyalty business bought from Mastercard at ~0.5x revenue, announced February 24 and closed May 1, 2026, taking the group toward $115 million ARR, and 'a couple of other letters of intent' outstanding. The only 'separations' management discusses are platform sunsets inside the group — one of Brierley's two platforms 'fully sunset' in Q3 FY26 — done to lift gross margin from ~30% on acquired stacks to 65–70% on Capillary, not to separate a business from the listed entity. Management does segment the P&L for investors (loyalty stack ~90% of revenue, Engage and Rewards each ~5–7%, aiRA a few million dollars, ~INR 80–100 crores of the INR 735 crores being low-margin acquisition revenue, organic NRR 114–115% vs inorganic 94–96%), and Aneesh Reddy said 'We'll probably change the slides hopefully next time' to show core and inorganic margins separately — but that is disclosure presentation, not a legal or structural separation. No investor, lender or partner on either call asked for a separation; the questions were on margins, ACV-to-ARR bridge, AI disruption, US healthcare payer exposure and cost leverage. Treating the China deregistration as a 'business separation' would misread it: it is housekeeping on a dormant shell already disclosed pre-IPO.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaced as a separation: on the February 6, 2026 Q3 FY26 call management framed the group as a roll-up ('let's go buy some of these competitors at 0.5x to 1.5x revenue'), with two LOIs live and Brierley's second platform sunset. On the May 6, 2026 Q4/FY26 call the direction was reinforced — SessionM acquired from Mastercard and closed May 1, 2026, FY27 revenue guided to INR 1,000–1,050 crores — with only a promise to split core versus acquired margins in future slides. The November 2, 2026 filing then completed the one separation in the record: deregistration of the dormant Capillary Shanghai, a step already disclosed in the RHP dated November 18, 2025, so the plan did not evolve, it simply closed out.

points.point: The only separation disclosed is the completed voluntary deregistration of Capillary Technologies (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., justified solely on the basis that the entity had no operations and the closure was pre-flagged in the RHP dated November 18, 2025.
points.quote: Capillary Shanghai was not carrying on any business operations, and its proposed closure was disclosed in the RHP.

points.point: Materiality is expressly denied — no revenue, earnings or balance-sheet consequence for the company or group, and Annexure A shows FY26 revenue 'Nil' and net worth of INR 0.50 million, with sale agreement, consideration, buyer and scheme-of-arrangement fields all 'NA'.
points.quote: Capillary Shanghai is not a material subsidiary of the Company, and its cessation does not have any impact on the business operations, revenue, or financial position of the Company or its group.

points.point: Strategy on the latest call is acquisition and consolidation, not separation: the SessionM merchant-loyalty business was bought from Mastercard (announced Feb 24, closed May 1, 2026) at about 0.5x revenue, $35 million of revenue, 40+ logos, five Fortune 500 customers, pushing the group toward $115 million ARR.
points.quote: We closed that transaction on May 1st. So it's a sizeable $35 million business, 40 plus logos, including five Fortune 500 companies.

points.point: Management's framing of the two 'parts' of the business is a margin-reporting distinction, not a structural one — core Capillary revenue carries essentially all EBITDA while roughly INR 80–100 crores of FY26's INR 735 crores is acquisition-linked low-margin revenue, and the only action promised is a change to the slides.
points.quote: For the organic platform side, you will continue to see this 2%, 3% more margin growth and probably that's a better way to show it.

points.point: The stated purpose of the M&A machine is to absorb competitors and migrate their customers onto one platform, moving gross margin from ~30% on acquired stacks to 69–70% on Capillary and paying back purchase price in four to five years — the economics of combining, not separating.
points.quote: So what we've done is we say let's go buy some of these competitors at 0.5x to 1.5x revenue and migrate those customers over ourselves.

points.point: The only businesses being 'separated out' are acquired legacy platforms being shut down inside the group, with Brierley (bought 2023) having one of its two platforms fully sunset in Q3 FY26 to release gross margin and below-the-line technology cost.
points.quote: Like for example, the last quarter we got done with the Brierley, which was one of the companies that we bought in 2023 had two platforms, so one of those platfo rms is fully sunset now.

points.point: No investor, analyst, lender or partner on either call asked about a demerger, spin-off or carve-out; questions covered AI disruption risk, US healthcare payer exposure, cost leverage, the ACV-to-ARR bridge and aiRA monetisation, and management added that it intends to stay confined to loyalty rather than hive anything off.

For the China deregistration the company states zero effect: no impact on operations, revenue or financial position, nil FY26 revenue, INR 0.50 million net worth, no consideration. Margin, capital and valuation benefits management does cite come from acquiring and migrating customers onto one platform — 30% to 65–70% gross margin, 45% contribution margin, four-to-five-year cash payback.

verdict.rationale: These texts contain no announcement, scheme or rationale for Borosil Renewables separating one of its own businesses into a new entity — the only forward-looking corporate-action question, on reported 'strategic investment' talks (Jul 2026 call), was met with 'I cannot offer any comment on this.' The separation management does explain at length is the severing of the European solar-glass business from the Indian one, executed through insolvency rather than a demerger: the hot end (melting furnace) of step-down subsidiary GMB Glasmanufaktur Brandenburg was cooled on 31 December 2024, GMB filed for insolvency on 4 July 2025, its holding company Geosphere Glassworks filed on 22 December 2025, and the marketing arm Interfloat Corporation was progressively impaired. The cause given was that from June 2023, roughly 6–7 months after the takeover, about 80 GW of Chinese modules were dumped into Europe in a couple of months, destroying local module manufacturing so that GMB's tailor-made customers disappeared and it could not sell beyond 50% of production, while promised EU/German policy support never turned into action. The cost of staying was quantified repeatedly: EBITDA losses of about INR 8 crore per month before shutdown, targeted down to INR 4 crore (employee cost ~INR 2 crore plus ~INR 2 crore other fixed cost), an inventory write-off of ~INR 16 crore, and standing charges of about EUR 900,000 (~INR 9 crore) a month that Geosphere would have had to keep funding. Management's stated purpose was that 'this filing of insolvency of the subsidiary would arrest recurring losses and permit reallocation of capital and managerial focus towards the India operations,' and that the one-time INR 325.91 crore provision against Geosphere/GMB (Rs 32,590.81 lakhs; written off in the FY26 accounts, with a INR 75 crore tax provision written back in Q4 FY26) would remove the continued drag on consolidated results so that 'the ROCE and EPS will substantially improve'; Laxman AG separately impaired INR 33.87 crore of its INR 57.59 crore exposure to Interfloat. The push came from several directions: GMB's own managing director was obliged under the German Insolvency Code to file once no further shareholder funding was available; German state bank ILB demanded repayment of the EUR 4.81 million capital subsidy, which Geosphere could not honour and which triggered its own filing; Borosil had already paid INR 185 crore from the February 2025 preferential issue to settle the SBLC given to GMB's lenders, while roughly INR 120–125 crore of GMB's remaining external liabilities (severance plus the government grant) were said not to travel to Borosil; and investors on the November 2025 call explicitly pressed management to shut Interfloat down as well. The group's only genuine demergers appear incidentally in a share re-lodgement filing — the NCLT-approved composite scheme of 15 January 2020 that amalgamated Gujarat Borosil (solar glass) into Borosil Renewables while demerging the consumer and scientific & industrial businesses to Borosil Limited, and the 2 November 2023 scheme demerging scientific & industrial out of Borosil Limited into Borosil Scientific — producing the 'three listed companies with different products, different businesses' and separate CEOs/teams described on the Jul 2026 call. Notably, the newest business, Borosil-branded rooftop solar kits (module, inverter, battery; ~INR 36–75 crore first-year revenue target, single-digit margins, no capex), is being built as a division inside Borosil Renewables, not separated out.
verdict.evolution: On the Nov 2024 call management was still 'reviewing all our options' for Germany, trying to fill the furnace with orders from the USA and EU; by Feb 2025 it had cooled the GMB furnace on 31 December 2024 pending the German election, and in May 2025 it sounded hopeful about the new Christian Democrat/Social Democrat government and was evaluating a cold-end-only restart using imported annealed glass. The Jul 2025 call reversed that: insolvency had been filed on 4 July 2025, the full INR 325.91 crore exposure was provisioned, and the stated purpose became arresting losses and reallocating capital and managerial focus to India. The Nov 2025 call extended the exit to Interfloat (INR 33.87 crore impaired; a shutdown decision promised 'by next quarter'), Feb 2026 confirmed GMB and Geosphere were fully deconsolidated so that consolidated and standalone results were now nearly identical, and May 2026 recorded the formal write-off after the Cottbus administrator's 1 December 2025 report said creditors would receive nothing; Jul 2026 only cleaned up the associated INR 75 crore tax shield.

points.point: Germany's problem was framed as collapsed demand, not cost: with local module makers unprotected and Chinese modules cheap, GMB's local demand fell to about 40% of production, and management said it was still weighing alternatives.
points.quote: So we are reviewing all our options. We are trying to first get the orders from other geographies so that we can still run at higher capacity, bring down the per unit cost of production and manage to bring both ends together in terms of revenue and cost, failing which we will have to look at more alternatives.

points.point: First physical step in the separation: the GMB melting furnace was cooled on 31 December 2024 while the German government was in crisis, with EBITDA losses of ~INR 8 crore/month to be halved to ~INR 4 crore and most workers put on state-funded short-time work.
points.quote: Since no decision could be expected until the formation of a new government, we decided to cool down the furnace on 31st December 2024, thus temporarily pausing the hot-end operations.

points.point: Still trying to save it — a cold-end-only restart processing imported annealed glass was being evaluated, an INR 16 crore inventory write-off was taken, and INR 185 crore of fresh Indian equity money was pushed out to settle GMB's lender liability.
points.quote: INR185 crores from this amount has been utilized to repay the loan liability of our step-down subsidiary, GMB.

points.point: The decisive explanation of the separation: insolvency filed 4 July 2025, INR 325.91 crore provisioned in full, and the stated gain was stopping ~INR 9 crore/month of standing charges and redirecting capital and management attention to India.
points.quote: For our Company, this filing of insolvency of the subsidiary would arrest recurring losses and permit reallocation of capital and managerial focus towards the India operations where we see a long-term potential and policy support.

points.point: The root cause given for the European exit was the June 2023 dumping of roughly 80 GW of Chinese modules into the EU, which wiped out GMB's customers for tailor-made glass and left it unable to sell beyond 50% of output.
points.quote: In June '23, just immediately after 6 to 7 months of our takeover of the Company, the imported Chinese modules started to be dumped in European markets, almost 80 gigawatts of modules were dumped in couple of months' time over there, which destroyed the local manufacturing.

points.point: The accounting purpose of taking the hit in one quarter was explicitly to clean up the entity left behind — no further consolidated drag, with better ROCE and EPS.
points.quote: However, this one-time provision will ensure that there is no continued drag on the consolidated results and performance, and that the ROCE and EPS will substantially improve.

points.point: The separation was extended to the European marketing arm: Interfloat lost its customers after GMB stopped annealed glass on 31 December 2024, and Laxman AG impaired INR 33.87 crore of its INR 57.59 crore exposure, with an investor pressing management to shut it entirely (answer: a decision 'by next quarter').
points.quote: Following an independent review by the management of Interfloat, it is assessed that there are no clear indicators of demand recovery in the near term that would support a return to profitable operations.

points.point: Separation complete in accounting terms — both GMB and its holding company Geosphere were deconsolidated, control lost to the court-appointed administrator, so consolidated results now essentially equal standalone India.
points.quote: So from the perspective of accounting and losses, we already deconsolidated the balance sheet by deconsolidating GMB, which is an operating step-down subsidiary and now we also deconsolidated Geosphere, which was a holding company of GMB.

points.point: Final step: after the Cottbus administrator's 1 December 2025 report said GMB's assets were insufficient and creditors would get nothing, the INR 325.91 crore exposure was written off, with no additional loss because it was already provided.
points.quote: In view of this, the company in its books of accounts for the financial year ended 31 March, 2026 has written off the above exposure in Geosphere and GMB.

points.point: The only governance rationale offered for keeping businesses in separate listed vehicles was management bandwidth: three listed companies, each with its own chairman/MD, CEO and functional teams, with Borosil Renewables' policy-heavy solar business needing P.K. Kheruka's full attention.
points.quote: So we have three listed companies with different products, different businesses.

points.point: Asked directly about press reports of a strategic investment, management declined to say anything — no further corporate restructuring was disclosed on any call.
points.quote: I cannot offer any comment on this.

points.point: The group's actual demergers appear only in a 4 March 2026 share re-lodgement filing: the 2020 NCLT composite scheme amalgamated solar-glass maker Gujarat Borosil into Borosil Renewables and demerged the consumer and scientific/industrial businesses out to Borosil Limited (50 shares of each per 100 Gujarat Borosil shares).
points.quote: In terms of the Composite Sheme of Amagalmation and Arrangement approved by Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal ( NCLT ), Mumbai, on January 15, 2020, inter-alia, Gujarat Borosil Limited (producer of solar glass) had been amalgamated with the Company, and the consumer and scientific & industrial product business of the Company had been transferred by way of demerger to Borosil Limited ("Scheme 1").

points.point: A second, later demerger split scientific & industrial products out of Borosil Limited into Borosil Scientific (37 shares for every 50 Borosil Limited shares), completing the three-company group structure.
points.quote: Further, as per the Composite Scheme of Arrangement of Borosil Limited ("Scheme 2"), approved by NCLT Mumbai on November 02 , 2023, its scientific and industrial product business had been transferred by way of demerger to Borosil Scientific Limited.

points.point: A lender forced the last leg: German state bank ILB demanded back the EUR 4.81 million capital subsidy because GMB's five-year operating condition was unmet, and Geosphere — a non-operating SPV holding GMB — filed for voluntary insolvency on 22 December 2025, its INR 13,003.09 lakh exposure already provided for.
points.quote: Geosphere in its response to the German Bank has clarified that GMB's shutting down of production was a result of inaction by the European Union and Federal Government of Germany to protect the solar PV manufacturing in Europe and conveyed that it has filed for insolvency due to lack of sufficient resources for honouring the aforesaid demand of German Bank.

verdict.what_management_expects: India: end of the consolidated loss drag, substantially improved ROCE and EPS, capital and managerial focus redeployed to the Bharuch 600 TPD expansion, and sustained 30–33% EBITDA margins. Europe (GMB/Geosphere/Interfloat): handed to court-appointed administrators, with roughly INR 120–125 crore of liabilities staying there rather than travelling to Borosil, and nothing expected back for shareholders.
verdict.gaps: No demerger scheme, swap ratio, record date, valuation, listing plan or shareholder vote is discussed; nor why rooftop solar stays an in-house division.

verdict.rationale: A caveat on the premise: across these three years of calls and filings, Bosch Ltd.'s dominant structural move is consolidation, not separation — on April 8, 2026 the Board approved buying 100% of Bosch Chassis Systems India Pvt. Ltd. (RBIC, the Vehicle Motion / safety-and-braking business: ABS, ESP, occupant safety, new braking systems, conventional actuation) for not more than INR 9,068.68 crore (10.6x FY25 EV/EBITDA), ~INR 9,060 crore in cash plus a token 2,460 shares at INR 35,200 so former holders Robert Bosch Investment Nederland B.V. and Robert Bosch LLC keep 'skin in the game', closed July 1, 2026; management's reasons were complementarity with Power Solutions 'without any overlap', powertrain-agnostic demand, day-one margin accretion (FY25 pro forma revenue INR 18,087cr → 22,022cr, EBITDA margin 12.8% → 13.9%, ~5% EPS accretion), and RBIC's own record (FY23–25 revenue CAGR 17% to INR 4,000cr, EBITDA margin 12.8% → 19.3%, net margin 8.1% → 13.9%, one-third two-wheeler). What Bosch Ltd. actually *separated* was the Building Technologies product lines — Video Solutions, Access & Intrusion and Communication Systems — sold under a Business Transfer Agreement approved January 28, 2025 to Keenfinity India Private Limited for Mio INR 5,950 (ex purchase-price adjustment), completed May 1, 2025, booking an exceptional gain of Mio INR 5,560 that drove FY26 PAT to INR 27,702mn (+37.6%). Management framed that exit three ways: it was a sub-scale 'product business' of roughly INR 400–450 crore revenue at about 6% EBIT margin ('not a major impact on our business operations in any way'); it needed 'significant additional investment, a lot of IP and a lot of change dynamics' to reach Bosch's rule of being top-3 in every segment, which 'was not in our focus'; and it was the India leg of a Bosch Group global carve-out of Building Technologies to private-equity owner Triton — routed to a subsidiary of the parent who 'will then take it back to Triton'. The same decluttering logic explains earlier exits (OE/OES Diagnostics, gain INR 485mn in Q2 FY25; Project House Mobility Solutions, gain INR 7,850mn in FY24, 'taken out of the listco... because of the very heavy investments required... heavily negative') and the deliberate decision to leave Bosch Automotive Electronics (RBAI) outside the listed company as a low-margin, capex-heavy captive contract manufacturer with 'no real logic' to buy in. So the driver is portfolio curation by the parent and board, not deleveraging — the company is nearly debt-free with ~INR 10,000 crore of investments at cost — and minority investors were the ones pushing the other way, repeatedly asking for group entities to be folded *into* the listco; management said the discussions were 'going on in the RBIN and Board with the promoter' and that the parent 'has always supported when it makes logical sense... when they want a fair value for whatever has been invested'. Separation also took a third form: new product lines were put into 50:50 JVs rather than built inside the listco — eAxles with Tata AutoComp (volumes too small, 'One Bosch e-axle line produces 150,000 e-axles. The volumes are not there') and, announced May 2026, electronically controlled air compression/processing/suspension/parking-brake modules with Brakes India and Wheels India, an area where 'Bosch is not a player at all'.
verdict.evolution: On the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 (Nov 12) calls management would only say portfolio moves were 'sensitive' and under discussion 'in the RBIN and Board with the promoter'; the Jan 28, 2025 board meeting then approved the Business Transfer Agreement, and the Feb 2025 call (Jan 28, 2025) explained the Video/Access/Communications exit as the India leg of the global Building Technologies carve-out to Triton, alongside a INR 471mn Mobility restructuring provision. The Jun 2025 (May 29) and Aug 2025 (Aug 5) calls generalised it into doctrine — 'top 3 in every segment', hive off what needs IP and investment we won't fund — with the sale completed May 1, 2025 and the gain flowing through the Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 results. From the two Apr 13, 2026 calls the direction inverted: RBIC was bought in as 'the next logical step', RBAI and the loss-making mobility-solutions business were explicitly left with the parent, and by May 2026 management described a permanent two-way process of 'portfolio expansion, portfolio decluttering and enhancement', plus a second JV with Brakes India and Wheels India.

points.point: Asked about restructuring the many unlisted Bosch auto entities in India, management confirmed talks were live with the promoter but refused detail, framing portfolio moves as a standing board-level discussion.
points.quote: These are discussions that are going on in the RBIN and Board with the promoter.

points.point: Karin Gilges gave the core separation test for the Building Technologies video/access/communications exit: it is a product business judged against what is core to Bosch Ltd.'s strategy.
points.quote: This is a product business, and therefore we all the time also have to look at our portfolio and we have to manage our portfolio. And we have to see what is our core and what is our strategy.

points.point: Guruprasad Mudlapur said the India divestment was not a local decision but the India leg of the Bosch Group's global sale of Building Technologies to private-equity firm Triton, routed first to a parent subsidiary.
points.quote: And you may have seen that the building technologies division globally has been sold to venture capitalist Triton, and this is an ongoing part of that sequence and in India, we are doing it to subsidiary of our parent who will then take it back to Triton.

points.point: Management sized the business being separated at roughly INR 450 crore of revenue and about 6% EBIT margin, i.e. immaterial to the listed company's operations.
points.quote: It's a very small business. About the revenue that goes out is about Rs. 450 crores.

points.point: Alongside the divestment, the quarter carried a INR 471 million exceptional provision for restructuring Mobility operations to stay cost-competitive as the product mix shifts to common rail and NOx sensors.
points.quote: During the quarter, the Company has made a provision of 471 million INR towards restructuring its operations to be competitive in the Mobility business .

points.point: Asked for the criteria that decide what to retain, grow, divest or merge, Mudlapur gave the group's top-3 rule and said Video Solutions/Access/Communications failed it because the IP and investment needed were not a Bosch Ltd. focus.
points.quote: We want to be in the top 3 in every segment we operate.

points.point: He made the hive-off reasoning explicit: becoming a top performer in that portfolio would have required investment, IP and change dynamics the listed company did not want to commit.
points.quote: So based on this, certain portfolio actions are taken and one of them was the building technologies area of Video Solutions, Access and Communication systems, where we realized that significant additional investment, a lot of IP and a lot of change dynamics are required to make this into a top performer, which we believed at that point of time was not in our focus.

points.point: At the group meeting management cited the earlier separation precedent — the mobility solutions business removed from the listco for heavy investment needs, a market outside India and sustained losses now funded by the parent.
points.quote: Yeah , see, we had one mobility solutions business which we actually took out of the listco a couple of years ago because of the very heavy investments required.

points.point: The same logic kept Bosch Automotive Electronics (RBAI) outside the listed entity: a captive, low-margin, capex-intensive contract manufacturer whose consolidation would add no turnover and little profit.
points.quote: So, at this point of time, we did not find a good commercial logic to bring this business in when it does not add turnover, doesn't contribute much to the margins, and there is very heavy intensity on investments.

points.point: The counter-move was consolidation: RBIC was bought because its safety and braking portfolio is powertrain-agnostic, complementary with no overlap, and margin-accretive from day one — structured as a fast all-cash close rather than a Maharashtra-Karnataka scheme.
points.quote: And therefore, all cash deal, even after the close of the ballot and the approval, we would really try to make a fast close, and the target would be a 100% subsidiary under the Bosch Limited.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these texts describes Castrol India Ltd. separating one of its own businesses — there is no scheme of demerger, no segment carve-out of lubricants, Auto Care, industrial or the Castrol Auto Service network; the separation being reconstructed is at the parent, where BP p.l.c. is detaching the entire Castrol lubricants business (including its 51% promoter stake in the listed Indian entity, held via Castrol Limited and Castrol Group Holdings Limited) from BP's oil and gas group. Management said BP announced a global strategic review of Castrol around February 2025 'with the intention of accelerating Castrol's next phase of value delivery,' and Kedar Lele twice framed the driver as BP's own balance sheet: 'BP's decision to carve out Castrol is driven by the global compulsion that a large oil and gas major faces... the global CEO of BP has said this that they would want to retire the debt and they see in Castrol a good asset that can be monetized' (Aug 2025), repeated in Nov 2025 as 'BP retires some of its debt by giving the value of the assets called Castrol.' The second stated reason is strategic mismatch: Castrol's growth agenda — core mobility, industrial lubricants (12–14% of volume, growing double digit versus high single digit automotive), mobility services (750+ Castrol Auto Service centres, the ~INR 400–500 crore ki Mobility stake, the VinFast aftersales MoU), Auto Care and data-centre immersion/direct-to-chip coolant fluids at roughly $1/litre gross margin — are 'different from the oil and gas business,' so separate ownership brings 'a focus on value creation for Castrol' and lets it be 'a more effective and innovative business partner to our customers.' India was positioned as a reason the asset is attractive rather than a problem being solved: 'a little over 10% of the volume of global Castrol and a little better than that in terms of profitability,' because its mix skews to 2-wheelers and cars. The buyer side was run by BP, not by Castrol India: data was supplied 'into a data room for potential investors... run from our central team bound by the NDA and administered by BP's global M&A team directly,' with the local MD saying 'I do not participate in any of that transaction.' The outcome, announced December 2025, is a joint venture — Motion JVCo Limited (Stonepeak-controlled, with CPP Investment Board taking a non-controlling interest) buying 100% of Castrol Group Holdings Limited under an SPA dated 23 December 2025, with BP Motion Holdings retaining 35% of the acquirer and Stonepeak 65% in sole control; that indirect change of control over the 51% promoter block (50,44,52,416 shares) triggered a mandatory 26% open offer for 25,71,71,820 shares at INR 194.04 per share, up to INR 4,990.16 crore, conditional on roughly two dozen antitrust clearances (including CCI) and a dozen foreign-investment/national-security approvals plus an EU FSR review. For the listed Indian company management insisted the consequence is deliberately nil: no change in structure, strategy or operating model, and specifically that the year-end global base-oil volume rebates that lift Q4 margins to ~26% 'will not get affected by any strategic sales.'
verdict.evolution: It surfaced only as a parent-level item: the Oct 2024 and Feb 2025 calls carry no mention, and the first discussion is the 29 Apr 2025 call (May 2025), where Kedar Lele answers Abinash S. that BP has announced a global strategic review of Castrol to 'unlock value' and accelerate growth in industrial, mobility services and data-centre fluids. By the 6 Aug 2025 call it is named a 'carve out' with an explicit motive — BP retiring debt by monetising Castrol — plus the first sizing of India at ~10% of global Castrol volume and better-than-average profitability; the 6 Nov 2025 call adds process detail (data room, NDA, BP global M&A running it, MD excluded) and reassurance that global base-oil rebates survive any sale. The 4 Feb 2026 call reports the December 2025 outcome — a JV with an investor at 65% and BP retaining 35%, subject to worldwide regulatory approval, expected to close 'toward the end of the year' — consistent with the 24 Dec 2025 open-offer announcement, and by the 29 Apr 2026 call (May 2026) the new interim CEO reduces it to 'no change in our structure, strategy or operating model' pending approvals.

points.point: First mention: BP's global strategic review of Castrol, framed as unlocking value and accelerating Castrol's growth in core mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services and data-centre fluids.
points.quote: So BP announced the strategic review of its Castrol business globally with the intention of accelerating Castrol's next phase of value delivery.

points.point: The stated driver is BP's own debt, not any problem inside Castrol: a large oil and gas major monetising a good asset.
points.quote: Now BP's decision to carve out Castrol is driven by the global compulsion that a large oil and gas major faces. And it is, the global CEO of BP has said this that they would want to retire the debt and they see in Castrol a good asset that can be monetized.

points.point: Strategic-fit argument for separation: Castrol's growth lines (mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services, data-centre fluids) sit outside oil and gas.
points.quote: All of these businesses are different from the oil and gas business. And with this, there will be a focus on value creation for Castrol.

points.point: Sizing of the Indian piece inside the asset being sold — above-average profitability because of the 2-wheeler and car mix.
points.quote: at an overall level, we do about a little over 10% of the volume of global Castrol and a little better than that in terms of profitability because our business is structured around 2-wheelers and cars, which is really more profitable part of the business versus the average trucks and the average profitability that you see in the segment.

points.point: Process disclosure in answer to Kirtan Mehta (Baroda BNP Paribas): bidders were being served data by BP's M&A team, with the Indian MD walled off.
points.quote: We have been supplying data into a data room for potential investors, and that gets run from our central team bound by the NDA and administered by BP's global M&A team directly. And I do not participate in any of that transaction.

points.point: Restates the dual purpose — accelerate Castrol's value delivery while BP pays down debt — and dates the review to roughly February 2025.
points.quote: And the intention was very simple that they accelerate Castrol's next phase of value delivery while BP retires some of its debt by giving the value of the assets called Castrol.

points.point: Answering Harsh on the Q4 margin uplift, management ring-fenced the global base-oil volume rebates (which take Q4 EBITDA to ~26% versus ~24% full year) from the sale.
points.quote: So none of these discounts that we see in the Q4 will get affected by any strategic sales.

points.point: Outcome disclosed to Lokesh (Aionion Capital): a JV where BP keeps 35% and the incoming investor takes 65%, pending approvals, with closure expected toward end of the year.
points.quote: So at the parent level, BP has signaled that they will form a joint venture with an investor, where BP will remain a 35% shareholder and the investor will take 65%.

points.point: No India-level consequence asserted; any disclosures to follow will come from the new shareholders.
points.quote: To your question on what may or may not impact, very early, it's business as usual for us over here.

points.point: Interim CEO Saugata Basuray reduces 'shareholder development at parent level' to a non-event for the listed company while global approvals are pending.
points.quote: From Castrol India standpoint, there's no change in our structure, strategy or operating model.

points.point: The 24 Dec 2025 public announcement shows the mechanism: an SPA dated 23 Dec 2025 under which Motion JVCo Limited buys 100% of Castrol Group Holdings Limited from BP p.l.c., indirectly acquiring the 51% (50,44,52,416-share) promoter block in Castrol India held by Castrol Limited.
points.quote: The Acquirer has entered into an agreement for sale and purchase with BP p.l.c. ("Seller") dated December 23, 2025 ("SPA"), pursuant to which the Seller has agreed to sell and transfer to the Acquirer, and the Acquirer has agreed to acquire from the Seller, 100% (one hundred percent) of the equity share capital of Castrol Group Holdings Limited ("CGHL").

points.point: Consideration structure confirms the 65/35 split: BP Motion Holdings is allotted 35% of the acquirer, Stonepeak Motion Holdco retains 65% and sole control, with CPP Investment Board Private Holdings (6) Inc. a non-controlling co-investor.
points.quote: Following this, PAC 1 (which presently holds the entire equity share capital of the Acquirer) will hold 65% (sixty five percent) of the equity share capital of the Acquirer and remain in sole control of the Acquirer. BPMH will hold a non-controlling interest in the Acquirer.

points.point: Minority consequence: a mandatory 26% open offer for 25,71,71,820 shares at INR 194.04 (up to INR 4,990.16 crore), with the price to be escalated 10% p.a. from 23 Dec 2025 to the DPS date, and contingent on completion of the parent deal.
points.quote: The Acquirer and the PACs hereby make this Open Offer to the Public Shareholders to acquire up to 25,71,71,820 (twenty five crore seventy one lakh seventy one thousand eight hundred and twenty) Equity Shares ("Offer Shares"), constituting 26.00% (twenty six percent) of the Equity Share Capital ("Offer Size"), at a price of INR 194.04/- (Indian Rupees one hundred and ninety four and four paise only) per Offer Share

points.point: The separation is gated on a very long regulatory runway — roughly two dozen antitrust regimes including CCI, a dozen foreign-investment/national-security screens, and an EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation appraisal.

verdict.what_management_expects: For BP: cash to retire debt and monetise a good asset. For Castrol: dedicated owners focused on value creation, accelerating core mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services and data-centre fluids, and making it a more effective, innovative partner. For Castrol India: explicitly nothing changes — same structure, strategy, operating model, 21–24% EBITDA band, retained global base-oil rebates and R&D access. Minorities get a 26% exit at INR 194.04.
verdict.gaps: No stated post-close terms for brand licensing, BP R&D/technology access, or global base-oil contract scale; no India P&L, dividend-policy or delisting implications; no closing date.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these eight transcripts or ten filings describes CGCL separating, demerging, spinning off or listing any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no swap ratio and no record date anywhere in the material, and as late as the Jan 2026 filing the company still states that it 'operates mainly in the business segment of fund based financing activity' with 'no separate reportable segments' under Ind AS 108. The only corporate separations management actually explains are internal: the car-loan distribution (DSA) business was moved out of the listed parent into a newly formed wholly-owned subsidiary, Capri Loans Car Platforms Private Limited, and three further subsidiaries were incorporated in FY26 — Capri Global Capital Markets Private Limited (debt-capital-market investment banking, subsidiary w.e.f. 8 Jul 2025), Capri Global Securities Private Limited (institutional debt placement, online bond platform, exchange trading, w.e.f. 15 Jul 2025) and Capri Global Insurance Brokers Private Limited (w.e.f. 2 Dec 2025), funded with ₹100 mn, ₹600 mn and ₹7.5 mn respectively in Q3 FY26. The logic given for housing these in separate entities is that they are capital-light, pure fee/distribution businesses — 'no capital involved, there's no risk involved' in car loans — that ride on the same supervisory team and 1,800-person field force, so they are 'accretive to the profit' from year one rather than denting the cost-to-income ratio. The only cost management attributed to the car-loan carve-out was transitional: FY25 car-loan profit was guided 'slightly lower than the last year because of various transition from old CGCL to the new company,' with volumes of ₹10,700 cr and ₹96 cr net fee in FY25 rising to ₹11,910 cr origination (up 13%) across 14 partner banks in FY26. No investor, lender or bank partner is cited anywhere as having asked for a separation; the mortgage business already sits in a separate licensed subsidiary (CGHFL) for regulatory reasons, into which the parent injected ₹200 cr via a rights issue allotted 23 Mar 2026 at ₹274/share. On the evidence given, the premise of a business separation is not supported, and I have not inferred one.
verdict.evolution: Aug 2024 (Q1 FY25) is the first mention, reported as already done: the car-loan vertical had been shifted out of CGCL into a newly formed subsidiary, with the softer Q1 fee (₹246 mn vs ₹271 mn) explained by seasonality. Nov 2024 (Q2 FY25) added the only stated cost — transition to the new entity plus the used-car launch would hold FY25 car-loan profit below FY24, with 'all-time high' profit promised the next year. Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) extended the pattern to two newly incorporated companies for debt-capital-market investment banking and securities/bond distribution, described as capital-light and profit-accretive from year one; the Jan 2026 filing adds Capri Global Insurance Brokers and the funding amounts. By May 2026 the framing had become monetisation of the car-loan entity alone — ₹20 cr profit next year scaling to ₹60–70 cr of fee income over 4–5 years, with used cars, credit cards, personal loans and mortgages added over 3–4 years.

points.point: First disclosure, after the fact, that the car-loan distribution business had been moved out of the listed parent into a new wholly-owned subsidiary; the Q1 fee dip (₹246 mn vs ₹271 mn) was attributed to seasonality, not the move.
points.quote: Car loan, we have shifted the business from the Capri Global Capital Limited to the newly formed subsidiary.

points.point: The only cost management ever attached to the carve-out: FY25 car-loan profitability would fall below FY24 because of the transition out of CGCL into the new company, alongside the used-car product launch.
points.quote: This year, we will have profitability slightly lower than the last year because of various transition from old CGCL to the new company.

points.point: Management framed the drag as purely transitional stabilisation cost in the new entity, with volume and profit expected at an all-time high the following year.
points.quote: This year, it will take some stabilization in the new entity along with the launch of the new product, where we'll see some operational cost offsetting the profit of this vertical.

points.point: The rationale for keeping car loans as a separate, non-lending vehicle: it is pure origination for 12 partner banks (₹10,700 cr disbursed, ₹96 cr net fee in FY25, 813 locations across 31 states) with no balance-sheet exposure.
points.quote: So, this is a pure fee vertical where we just originate the lead and share. There's no capital involved, there's no risk involved.

points.point: Two further subsidiaries incorporated — one for debt-capital-market investment banking, one securities company for institutional debt placement, an online bond platform and exchange trading, staffed by a team of about 10 people.
points.quote: There are two companies we have incorporated. One is going to carry out the investment banking activities only for the debt capital market.

points.point: The stated test for putting these businesses in separate entities is that they are capital-light and self-funding, so they add fee income without hurting the cost-to-income guidance for FY26.
points.quote: Both of these will not consume much capital, and they will be from the year 1 that will be accretive to the profit rather than taking any dent on the cost income side.

points.point: The car-loan entity is described as a distribution-only platform across 12–14 partner banks, targeted to earn ₹20 cr of profit in FY27 and ₹60–70 cr of pure fee income in 4–5 years, adding used cars, credit cards, personal loans and mortgages on the same 1,800-person team.
points.quote: And next year, we will be able to see that about INR20 crores of profit is able to deliver by the car loan entity alone.

points.point: The capital-markets subsidiary's purpose is given as reducing a 2–3% negative carry on an earmarked ₹600–800 cr treasury book plus ₹40–50 cr gross (₹20–25 cr net) fee income once the licence is received, expected by end-June.
points.quote: So, it will contribute to the fee income as well as also to reducing our negative carry in our treasury income.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger, spin-off or separation of any business appears in any of the ten filings; as of the Q3 FY26 results the company still reports itself as a single-segment lender, and the only equity actions disclosed are fund-raising (₹4,000 cr enabling resolution, USD 30 mn bonds, GMTN programme) and a ₹200 cr rights-issue injection into housing subsidiary CGHFL.
points.quote: The Company operates mainly in the business segment of fund based financing activity. All other activities revolve around the main business.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation economics are claimed, because no separation is announced. For the subsidiarised fee businesses management expects capital-light, profit-accretive-from-year-one income: car loans ₹20 cr PAT in FY27 scaling to ₹60–70 cr fee income in 4–5 years on 12–15% origination growth; capital markets ₹20–25 cr net fee plus removal of 2–3% treasury negative carry; no change to lender capital or parent valuation is asserted.
verdict.gaps: No separation, demerger or listing is explained anywhere — no scheme, rationale, valuation, swap ratio, record date, subsidiary-level financials, or any investor, lender or partner request.

verdict.rationale: The premise needs correcting before the reasoning: in these texts CIE Automotive India is not separating a business — it is doing the opposite, absorbing one. The only live corporate action is a Scheme of Merger by Absorption, approved by the Board on 23 April 2026 (Appointed Date 1 April 2026), under which CIE Aluminium Casting India Limited (CIEALCAST/CACIL), a 100%-owned subsidiary acquired in April 2019 — turnover INR 11,728 million and PAT INR 948 million for CY2025, versus the parent's standalone INR 48,964.02 million and INR 6,169.27 million — is folded into the listed parent, with no shares issued and CACIL's 29,40,000 shares (Rs 2.94 crore capital) simply cancelled. Management's stated reasons are five: production and marketing synergies from a larger combined aluminium die-casting plus forgings/castings/stampings/gears portfolio with coordinated capacity planning and load balancing; cross-selling across OEM relationships, since CACIL brings deeply embedded two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle arrangements including 'near sole-supplier positions' for several aluminium die-cast parts, letting the merged entity offer multi-technology sourcing bundles; organisational and operating efficiencies by removing managerial overlap and duplicated IT, HR, finance, secretarial, legal and compliance functions and simplifying the group structure; a stronger financial position, because OEMs 'are more likely to rely on a supplier whose presence can be assured across the lifecycle of the vehicle model' and award bigger projects to financially sound suppliers — pro-forma net worth of Rs 4,469.50 crore versus Rs 4,375.28 crore standalone — plus better cash deployment and dividend-paying ability; and elimination of inter-company payables/loans (CACIL carried one unsecured borrowing of Rs 169 crore), freeing capital. No investor, lender or OEM is said to have demanded the merger: creditors face no compromise, no new shares are issued, there is no change in shareholding pattern, and SEBI/stock-exchange NOC and related-party approvals were not required, so the push is internal and OEM-sourcing-driven rather than externally forced. The business context in the calls is an aluminium vertical that has chronically underperformed — bought at about 10% EBITDA in 2019, roughly 15% now and still 'below our expectations' — undergoing portfolio restructuring, a sales-recognition change to value-add only, a CNG-programme collapse, Bajaj dependence cut from 75–80% to 60–65%, and now heavy capex into higher-tonnage machined castings and new factories. The only genuine separations in these texts are historical or trivial: the 2023 sale of the four German forgings subsidiaries (JECO, GSA, FUG, SCG) to Mutares, still reported as discontinued operations, and the June 2026 sale of a 27.89% associate stake in Ojaha Renewables for Rs 1.62 crore.
verdict.evolution: Through the Oct 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Jul 2025 and Oct 2025 calls the aluminium business is discussed only as a separately-held subsidiary needing fixing — Oct 2025 notes 'it remains a step down subsidiary' with margins up from ~10% to ~15% but still short, and an investor asks why the fast-growing sunroof business sits unlisted at CIE Spain rather than in the listed arm. The Feb 2026 (Q4 CY25) call attributes part of the Indian growth shortfall to 'the restructuring of our business portfolio that we are carrying out at our aluminum and magnetics verticals' and a Q4 sales-recognition change, while promising further aluminium factories and a bigger CY26 capex. The Board approved the merger scheme on 23 April 2026 and the very next day, on the Apr 2026 call, the CFO confirmed it in answer to a direct question and the resulting structure was described as standalone plus CIE Hosur plus Europe. Execution then ran through the filings: NCLT Mumbai allowed CA(CAA)-115/MB/2026 on 24 September 2026 and dispensed with shareholder and creditor meetings, notices were dispatched to 1,00,114 shareholders and creditors on 8 October 2026, and the 22 October 2026 Q3 CY26 results still carry it as pending NCLT approval.

points.point: One day after the Board approved the scheme, an analyst asked whether the aluminium business would now be merged into the standalone entity, and the CFO confirmed the intent to absorb CACIL into the parent.
points.quote: Yes, that is the intent to merge CACIL into the parent company, yes.

points.point: Management described the post-merger India structure: only the standalone entity plus CIE Hosur, which stays a subsidiary, with Europe (including Bill Forge Mexico) separate.
points.quote: So in India, we will have CIE Hosur and the stand-alone entity, that's how it would be.

points.point: The scheme's first stated rationale is production and marketing synergies — a larger, more diversified product portfolio with coordinated capacity planning and load balancing, and direct use of assets instead of inter-company transfer mechanisms.
points.quote: Creation of production and marketing synergies by enabling the combined entity to offer a larger and more diversified product portfolio to a broad base of customers.

points.point: Cross-selling is the second rationale: CACIL brings near sole-supplier positions in two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle aluminium die-cast parts, enabling multi-technology sourcing bundles to OEMs.
points.quote: CIEALCAST contributes strong and deeply embedded set of arrangements with its customers that creates enforceable contractual right and obligation in the two-wheeler and passenger vehicle segments, including near sole-supplier positions for several aluminium die-cast components.

points.point: Third rationale: removing the overhead of running two legal entities — managerial overlap, duplicated systems and processes, and separate IT, HR, finance, secretarial, legal and compliance functions.
points.quote: Delivery of substantial organisational synergies through the elimination of managerial overlaps inherent in operating multiple legal entities, resulting in improved decision-making speed and clearer governance structures.

points.point: Fourth rationale is a customer-facing balance-sheet argument — OEMs award larger, lifecycle-long projects to financially sound suppliers; pro-forma net worth rises to Rs 4,469.50 crore from Rs 4,375.28 crore standalone, and dividend capacity strengthens.
points.quote: Moreover, as the business dynamics mainly depend on the market demand and its likeability, the OEMs are more likely to rely on a supplier whose presence can be assured across the lifecycle of the vehicle model.

points.point: Fifth rationale: wiping out inter-company payables and loans — CACIL carried 688 sundry creditors of Rs 112.05 crore, 31 capex creditors of Rs 3.32 crore and one unsecured borrowing of Rs 169 crore — to free up capital.
points.quote: Elimination inter-company payables/loans/other transactions leads to a stronger, more resilient financial position and enhanced business's creditworthiness.

points.point: Because CACIL is wholly owned, there is no consideration, no new shares and no change in the parent's capital structure or shareholding pattern; CACIL's Rs 2.94 crore paid-up capital is cancelled.
points.quote: Accordingly, upon the Scheme becoming effective, no shares of the Transferee Company shall be allotted in lieu or exchange of the holding of the Transferee Company in the Transferor Company and the issued and paid-up capital of the Transferor Company shall stand cancelled on the Effective Date without any further act, instrument or deed.

points.point: The scheme traces the logic back to the April 2019 acquisition, framed around OEMs raising aluminium content per vehicle for lightweighting and favouring full-system suppliers.
points.quote: OEMs globally were increasing aluminium usage per vehicle to reduce weight and improve efficiency. By acquiring CIEALCAST, CIEINDIA positioned itself structurally closer to OEM sourcing strategies that increasingly favour full-system and lightweight component suppliers.

points.point: The parent attributed part of its India growth shortfall to ongoing restructuring of the aluminium (and magnetics) verticals and to a Q4 change recognising only value-add on some aluminium categories.
points.quote: First, the restructuring of our business portfolio that we are carrying out at our aluminum and magnetics verticals.

points.point: Management said the aluminium unit is adding customers, moving to higher-tonnage, higher value-add parts, and will likely launch a new factory, with production starting Q3–Q4 CY26 — the growth case the merger is meant to support.
points.quote: So yes, we expect that the aluminum business will go up. You know that till now, our performance was not very good because in terms of sales because we were -- we are mainly dependent on Bajaj 2-wheelers.

points.point: The aluminium business was still described as a separately-reported subsidiary whose margins rose from about 10% at acquisition in 2019 to around 15%, yet remained below management's own expectations.
points.quote: I just wanted to reinforce that our margins in aluminum are improving in the last years. However, we are still below our expectations and we are improving and working in the technology transfer from Europe to India.

points.point: The only shareholder-driven structural demand in the calls runs the same direction — an investor asked for the fast-growing sunroof business to be brought into the listed Indian arm; management declined to move it.
points.quote: So is that business, like any chances of that business being included in the Indian arm? Because it's an unlisted company, which is under direct control of CIE Spain and we have CIE Automotive India as a listed entity and the benefits of growth in that vertical is something which the minority shareholders are not enjoying?

points.point: NCLT Mumbai allowed the application on 24 September 2026 and dispensed with shareholder and creditor meetings of the parent, since no capital is reorganised and no creditor's liability is diminished; notices went out on 8 October 2026 to 1,00,114 shareholders and the creditors.
points.quote: Based on the above, the meeting of the Equity Shareholders of the Transferee Company is dispensed with since the Transferor Company is a wholly owned subsidiary and there is no re-organisation of share capital of the Transferee Company as no new shares are being issued.

points.point: Context for the 'stronger financial position' argument: consolidated net financial debt was negative INR 18.8 billion and management was hunting ways to deploy the cash, alongside a Rs 7 per share dividend.
points.quote: Net financial debt has further improved and is negative INR18.8 -- negative INR18.8 billion versus negative INR12 billion last year.

verdict.what_management_expects: Not a separation — a single merged entity. Expected: production/marketing synergies, cross-selling multi-technology bundles to OEMs, fewer managerial and functional duplications, stronger net worth (Rs 4,469.50 crore pro-forma) to win bigger lifecycle projects, better dividend capacity, unfettered cash-flow deployment, and elimination of inter-company loans including CACIL's Rs 169 crore unsecured borrowing. No margin, valuation or cost-saving number was given.
verdict.gaps: No separation, demerger or spin-off is proposed anywhere. Synergies, cost savings, margin and valuation impact are never quantified; no lender, investor or OEM demand cited; sunroof exclusion unexplained.

Note also that CACIL is being merged INTO CIE Automotive India Limited (Board approval 23 April 2026, scheme filed with NCLT), i.e. absorbed rather than separated out.

verdict.rationale: These documents do not describe any separation, demerger, spin-off, hive-off or scheme of arrangement at Aditya Infotech Ltd. (CPPLUS), so no rationale for one can be reconstructed from them; the only occurrences of the words 'demerger' and 'spin-off' are inside boilerplate corporate-action adjustment clauses of the Aditya Infotech Employee Stock Option Plan 2024 resolutions in the February 26, 2026 postal ballot notice, which list them generically alongside rights issue, bonus, merger, amalgamation, sale of division and split as events that would trigger fair adjustment of option counts and exercise prices. Every structural move management actually discusses runs the other way — toward consolidation and vertical integration, not separation. The company bought Dixon Technologies' 50% stake in the manufacturing JV in September 2024 (a share swap valuing the deal at about Rs. 4,000 crores, leaving Dixon with roughly 6.6% of the parent and a board seat), made AIL Dixon a wholly owned subsidiary, and management repeatedly cites 'consolidation of the subsidiary AIL Dixon' as an FY26 margin driver; the Feb 26, 2026 postal ballot even adds Article 102A preserving Dixon's right to nominate one director while it holds at least 4%. New entities being created are additive, not carve-outs: Aditya Infotech Taiwan Company Limited (wholly owned R&D subsidiary) and a 50:50 JV with Orient Cables for coaxial/network/CCTV cable manufacturing in a ~1 lakh sq ft Rajasthan plant (commercial ops Q2–Q3 FY27), both framed as backward integration for 'quality consistency, supply consistency, contribution to the EBITDA basis points.' The one business genuinely shrinking is the legacy Dahua third-party distribution line, but management describes it as a natural STQC-driven runoff (down 25–30% in FY26, under Rs. 100–150 crores in FY27, 'INR10-15 crores a month', at roughly one-third the margin of own-brand CP PLUS, which is 86–87% of revenue), not as an entity being separated; no board approval, no scheme, no record date and no appointed date appear anywhere. The capital actions on record are the opposite of a separation: Rs. 375 crores of IPO proceeds used to cut gross debt 89% to Rs. 48 crores, and an August 19, 2026 board approval to raise up to Rs. 1,500 crores via public issue and/or QIP, with shareholder approval by postal ballot. No investor, lender or partner on any of these four calls asks for a separation; questions concern margins, memory/SoC shortages, price hikes, market share (20.8% FY25 to ~45.4% in Q3 FY26), capex and exports. Any answer naming a separated business, its numbers or its rationale would have to be invented, which these texts do not support.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces. Across Aug 20, 2025 (Q1 FY26, maiden call), Nov 13, 2025 (Q2 FY26), Feb 13, 2026 (Q3 FY26) and May 28, 2026 (Q4/FY26) the structural narrative moves only toward integration — AIL Dixon fully consolidated, a Taiwan R&D subsidiary, an Orient Cables 50:50 JV, Qualcomm and L&T Semiconductor collaborations, and multi-brand launches (Nexivue, Eyra) inside the same listed entity. The filings follow the same direction: the Feb 26, 2026 postal ballot entrenches Dixon's nominee-director right and ratifies the ESOP, and the Aug 19, 2026 board meeting approves a Rs. 1,500 crore equity raise. The only textual trace of 'demerger'/'spin-off' is undated boilerplate in the ESOP adjustment clauses, which signals nothing about intent.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these texts alone, Cohance Lifesciences is NOT separating a business: across the nine supplied transcripts (Dec 2024 through May 2026) and the one supplied filing (Board outcome, 27 April 2026) there is no demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement, carve-out or divestiture of any segment — the corporate action running through this period is the opposite, consolidation. The company merged Cohance into Suven Pharmaceuticals (shareholder approval 99.99%, NCLT hearing 18 Feb 2025, 38.11 crore shares outstanding post-merger, rebranded Cohance in May 2025) and bought capability rather than shedding it: Sapala Organics (oligonucleotides, consolidated from 11 July 2024) and NJ Bio of Princeton NJ (ADCs — 56% stake, ~US$100m pre-money equity value, US$64.4m outlay of which US$49.4m secondary and US$15m primary, on US$32m revenue growing at ~70% CAGR, with call/put on the balance after 5 years), with Himanshu Agarwal stating 'inorganic growth is a core part of our thesis' and Vivek Sharma saying 'our hope is that we don't end at six. We keep adding more.' The only 'separation' management actually describes is organisational, not legal: three distinct business verticals — Pharma CDMO (Yann D'Herve), API+ (Gunjan Singh) and Specialty Chemicals (Amrit Singh) — each given full operational ownership and P&L accountability reporting directly to the Executive Chairman, approved by the Board alongside MD Dr Prasada Raju's resignation and disclosed on the 28 October 2025 update call. The problems that restructuring was said to solve were internal, not structural: a 'multi-business portfolio and expanding global footprint', six formerly family-owned businesses welded into one needing 'greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability', and getting to the US$1bn/2030 vision faster; Vivek Sharma explicitly denied there had been any overlap problem at the top ('There was no such thought process that there was an overlap of responsibility'). It was board- and management-driven — no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for it; the only investor pressure on record is Varun Bang of Bandhan Life attacking Advent's stewardship ('execution discipline seems to have collapsed') and Chirag Shah of White Pine asking for governance and selective-information-flow fixes, neither of which asked for a separation. The numbers an investor might build a separation case from are disclosed but never framed that way by management: consolidated FY26 EBITDA margin of 21% versus 24.6% standalone (9M FY26: 21% vs 24%; Q3 FY26: 15.5% vs ~19%), i.e. a 4–5% drag Himanshu attributes to first-year NJ Bio consolidation and subsidiary losses in the biotech funding winter, plus INR260 crore of destocking in two large commercial molecules and INR55 crore (INR610 million FY26) lost at the Nacharam formulation site after its OAI and warning letter — and management's answer to all of it is remediation and recovery, with Yann saying NJ Bio needs 'a little bit more than two years to get back to this level', not a sale or demerger.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces: no call in the supplied window raises separating, demerging or selling a segment. The structural idea that does evolve is the opposite — segmentation into three reporting engines (Pharma CDMO, Specialty Chemicals, API+) described as 'engines of growth' from the Feb 2025 and Jun 2025 calls, hardened on 28 October 2025 (filed 1 Nov 2025) into three business-unit CEOs with full P&L authority reporting to Executive Chairman Vivek Sharma plus a platform COO, restated on the 12 November 2025 and 12 February 2026 calls, and then carried into a leadership handover rather than a split: the 27 April 2026 filing records Sharma's resignation effective 30 April 2026 (staying nine months as Special Advisor) and Umang Vohra's appointment as Chairman and Group CEO, who on his first call (12 May 2026) promised only 'a strategic blueprint for growth and sustainable value creation' by fiscal year end — explicitly declining to say whether tough decisions were coming ('I do not know if we are at a point where we will make tough decisions at this stage'). If a separation exists, it is in the six older calls omitted for length or in filings not supplied here.

points.point: On the 28 October 2025 update call (filed 1 Nov 2025), announcing MD Dr Prasada Raju's resignation, Sharma said the Board approved a revised organisational structure — not a corporate separation — citing the multi-business portfolio and the US$1bn vision.
points.quote: In light of this development, the board has approved a revised organizational structure, one that better reflects our multi-business portfolio and expanding global footprint and positions Cohance strongly on its path towards a $1 billion U.S. vision.

points.point: The stated purpose of that restructuring was speed and accountability inside one company, with the three business-unit leaders given full P&L ownership reporting to the Executive Chairman.
points.quote: This new structure is designed to bring greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability across our businesses.

points.point: Operational ownership was pushed down to the three vertical CEOs — Yann D'Herve (Pharma CDMO), Gunjan Singh (API+), Amrit Singh (Specialty Chemicals) — with CFO Himanshu Agarwal joining the Board; no entity was carved out.
points.quote: These business unit leaders have full operational ownership and accountability will henceforth report directly to me.

points.point: On the 12 November 2025 Q2 FY26 call Sharma restated the same three-vertical structure as a capability-amplification phase of integration, again with no mention of separating any of them.
points.quote: Over the past year, we had established three distinct business verticals, each led by highly experienced and accomplished industry leaders who bring deep expertise and proven track record in their respective domains and each has full operational ownership and accountability.

points.point: The underlying complexity management was managing is the merger of six separate businesses into one platform — an integration problem, which Sharma answered with cultural and leadership change rather than any split.
points.quote: Somebody started saying we are a combination of six family-owned businesses that have now become part of who we are today, right?

points.point: The one fact pattern that could support a separation thesis is the subsidiary drag Himanshu quantifies — consolidated versus standalone margin — but he frames it as timing and first-year NJ Bio consolidation, not a reason to separate.
points.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for nine-month FY '26 has declined by 43% to INR348 crore , with adjusted EBITDA margins at 21%. For context, stand-alone adjusted EBITDA margins stood at 24%, highlighting the impact of subsidiary consolidation and muted operating leverage.

points.point: FY26 repeats the same standalone-versus-consolidated gap (24.6% vs 21%), and when Ashish of UTI asked directly about Sapala and NJ Bio dragging margins, the answer was a turnaround plan and a $10m Princeton expansion — not a disposal.
points.quote: The adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 4.77 billion. EBITDA margin stood at 21%, while our standalone adjusted EBITDA margin were at 24.6%.

points.point: Management's declared capital-allocation philosophy over the window is acquisitive consolidation, treating organic and inorganic as one capital-allocation decision — the opposite of a separation rationale.
points.quote: So, for us, inorganic growth is a core part of our thesis.

points.point: Asked about M&A direction on the 28 October 2025 call, Sharma described buying differentiated niche-tech capability (ADC, oligo) across East and West — adding businesses, including unwanted assets inside bundles, rather than divesting.
points.quote: So, idea is to look for capabilities, not capacities.

points.point: The only supplied filing is a Board outcome covering Vivek Sharma's resignation as Executive Chairman effective 30 April 2026 (continuing nine months as Special Advisor), Umang Vohra's appointment as Chairman and Group CEO, and a new ESOP 2026 of 25,918,613 options (6.25% fully diluted, floor price INR 325). It contains no scheme of arrangement, demerger or separation.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing — no separation benefits are claimed anywhere in these texts. For the three-vertical reorganisation they claimed only agility, faster execution, deeper accountability, full P&L ownership per CEO, and faster progress toward US$1bn revenue by 2030 with mid-30s EBITDA margins. Margin recovery is pledged via volume, mix and operating leverage within the single consolidated platform, not via separation.
