verdict.rationale: On the evidence in these documents, Grasim is not demerging one of its own reported segments — the only separation described is the carve-out of renewable energy from Essel Mining & Industries Ltd. (EMIL) and its consolidation into Grasim's subsidiary Aditya Birla Renewables Ltd. (ABReN), approved by Grasim's Board on 29th December 2025 as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement. The Scheme does three things: (a) transfers the 'EMIL Renewable Energy Undertaking' (141 MW of operating wind and solar) out of EMIL and vests it in ABReN 'as a going concern, on a slump sale basis' under Section 2(42C) of the Income Tax Act; (b) amalgamates Electrotherm Renewables Pvt. Ltd. (ERPL, an EMIL WOS holding Palace Solar, a 15 MW Gujarat PV project) into ABReN; and (c) amalgamates ABReN's own three EPC subsidiaries — ABREL EPCCO Services, ABREL Renewables EPC and ABREL EPC — into ABReN, cancelling their shares. The stated problem is structural mismatch and fragmentation: EMIL's mining/mining services/Noble Ferro Alloys/iron ore pellets business and its renewables projects are described as 'two business verticals… distinct and separate', and the renewables assets plus ancillary EPC capability sat in five separate legal entities; the fix is 'a consolidated renewable energy platform under the Transferee Company along with ancillary services', to 'simplify the management and operational structures' and 'increase efficiencies by reaping benefits of economies of scale and synergies', with 'distinct value creation opportunities for the Transferee Company and EMIL'. Who asked for it is visible from the capital, not the text: the clean-up is bracketed by two outside/related cheques approved the same day (9th December 2025) — ₹500 crore from EMIL by preferential issue 'for meeting urgent business needs of ABRen' (49,26,10,837 shares) and up to ₹3,000 crore from Global Infrastructure Partners via GIP EM Star Pte Ltd (₹2,000 crore committed in CCPS plus equity, with a ₹1,000 crore pro-rata greenshoe), at an enterprise value of ~₹14,600 crore, which Grasim called one of the largest primary private-equity commitments into an Indian renewable company. Consideration inside the Scheme is all paper at ₹10.15 per ABReN share (₹10 face + ₹0.15 premium) — 39,90,75,667 shares for the EMIL slump sale and 9,35,35,000 shares for ERPL (1,87,070 ABReN shares per 100 ERPL shares) — on a Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP report and a Fedex Securities fairness opinion, taking ABReN's share count from 118,10,43,563 to 167,36,54,230 (216,62,65,067 after the EMIL preferential), still 100% promoter-group. The consequence Grasim disclosed is dilution: 'Upon the Scheme becoming effective, the shareholding of the Company in the Transferee Company shall stand diluted' and ABReN 'will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company but will continue to be a Subsidiary'; by 28th July 2026 Grasim was at 70.15%, and it topped up with 23,15,27,093 shares for ₹234.99 crore at the same ₹10.15 on 23rd September 2026, going to 73.76%. The growth case management attached to it is ABReN's ~4.3 GW operational-plus-contracted pan-India portfolio across 10 states (from ~2 GW peak installed at Q3 FY26, up from 1.2 GW), a largely captive Aditya Birla Group anchor book (37% of offtake in Q3 FY25, ~43% in Q1 FY26), and a stated target 'beyond 10 GW of peak capacity in coming years' — scale that Grasim, which said it is reinvesting its own EBITDA into paints and B2B e-commerce, chose to fund with third-party capital and GIP's operating experience rather than its own balance sheet.
verdict.evolution: Through FY25–H1FY26 renewables appears only as a scaling line item in 'other businesses' with no structural intent: 1.2 GW and 37% group offtake (Feb 2025 call), 1.9 GW vs 946 MW and ~43% group offtake (Aug 2025 call), ~2 GW peak and revenue nearly doubling to ₹259 crore (Nov 2025 call). The structure then changes entirely in filings, not on a call: on 9th December 2025 Grasim's Board approves EMIL's ₹500 crore preferential issue and GIP's up-to-₹3,000 crore investment, both of which end ABReN's wholly-owned status, and on 29th December 2025 it approves the Composite Scheme pulling EMIL's renewables undertaking, ERPL and the three EPC subsidiaries into ABReN. Only in the Feb 2026 (11th February) call does management discuss any of it, and then only the GIP cheque — ₹2,000 crore plus ₹1,000 crore greenshoe, ₹14,600 crore EV, 4.3 GW, 10 GW+ ambition — never the Scheme itself; the May 2026 call reports renewables revenue +60% and EBITDA +55% with no structural mention at all, and the follow-through is again a filing: Grasim's ₹235 crore subscription (28th July 2026 board approval, 23rd September 2026 allotment) lifting it from 70.15% to 73.76%.

points.point: The 29th December 2025 Composite Scheme's stated rationale is consolidation and simplification: one renewables platform with EPC folded in, under ABReN, to capture scale and synergy efficiencies.
points.quote: The Scheme is being proposed to create a consolidated renewable energy platform under the Transferee Company along with ancillary services, to simplify the management and operational structures of the Companies and to increase efficiencies by reaping benefits of economies of scale and synergies.

points.point: The reason renewables leaves EMIL is that it does not belong there: EMIL is a commercial mining, mining-services, Noble Ferro Alloys and iron ore pellets business that also happens to own 141 MW of wind and solar.
points.quote: These two business verticals of EMIL are distinct and separate.

points.point: The Scheme is framed as unlocking value separately on both sides of the carve-out — a focused renewables platform for ABReN and a focused mining/alloys business for EMIL.
points.quote: Further, the Scheme would result in distinct value creation opportunities for the Transferee Company and EMIL.

points.point: Mechanically the renewables undertaking moves as an undivided going concern on a slump-sale basis under Section 2(42C), with no values assigned to individual assets and liabilities — a tax-efficient business transfer rather than an asset sale.
points.quote: transfer and vesting of the EMIL Renewable Energy Undertaking from EMIL to the Transferee Company, as a going concern, on a slump sale basis, without values being assigned to individual assets and liabilities, in accordance with Section 2(42C) and other applicable provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961

points.point: Grasim disclosed the cost to itself: paying for EMIL's assets in ABReN paper (39,90,75,667 shares for the slump sale and 9,35,35,000 for ERPL at ₹10.15 each) dilutes Grasim out of 100% ownership.
points.quote: Upon the Scheme becoming effective, the shareholding of the Company in the Transferee Company shall stand diluted.

points.point: The same 9th December 2025 board meeting approved GIP (BlackRock) putting in up to ₹3,000 crore — ₹2,000 crore committed plus a ₹1,000 crore greenshoe — for a minority stake at ~₹14,600 crore EV, explicitly to fund a 10 GW+ build-out from the ~4.3 GW portfolio across 10 states.
points.quote: GIP's investment marks a pivotal moment in our growth journey, laying a strong foundation for an accelerated buildout of our renewables platform, as we target a capacity of 10  GW+ in the coming years.

points.point: Both external cheques (GIP ₹2,000–3,000 crore and EMIL ₹500 crore, the latter for ABReN's 'urgent business needs') were disclosed with the same consequence for ownership status.
points.quote: Pursuant to this, ABRen will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company but will continue to be a Subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The only management commentary on the restructuring in three years of calls: Kadel presented the GIP deal as capital plus operating capability for a business growing 82% YoY at ~2 GW peak, valuing it at ₹14,600 crore EV with a 4.3 GW pipeline and 10 GW+ target.
points.quote: This transaction brings not only capital, but also the GIP's global infrastructure operating experience to support disciplined expansion and contribute meaningfully to India's energy transition growth.

points.point: Weeks before the Scheme, renewables was still presented purely as a fast-scaling 'other business' (revenue nearly doubled to ₹259 crore including a one-time ₹50 crore rate differential), with no hint of a structural change.
points.quote: The business current peak capacity stood at nearly 2 gigawatt and is laying the foundation for a greener, more resilient India.

points.point: The platform being consolidated is heavily captive to the group, which explains why group entities (EMIL) are both asset contributors and funders alongside the financial investor.
points.quote: The business has strong anchor clientele with Aditya Birla Group companies representing ~43% of the existing portfolio.

points.point: A year earlier the same captive-offtake framing applied at 1.2 GW installed, up 37% from 894 MW, with ~2 GW targeted by FY25-end — the growth runway that later needed outside capital.
points.quote: The business has strong anchor clientele with Aditya Birla Group company representing 37% of the power offtake against the existing portfolio.

points.point: Post-Scheme, renewables performance is reported with no reference to the restructuring, while Grasim reiterated that its own cash goes into Grasim's businesses — consistent with funding renewables from EMIL/GIP instead.
points.quote: For the quarter, revenue for the renewable business grew by 60% year -on-year and textile business was higher by 14% year -on-year.

points.point: Capital-allocation Q&A (Siddharth Mehrotra, Kotak) shows Grasim's own surplus earmarked for new businesses and holding its ABCL stake, not renewables build-out — yet Grasim still topped up ABReN with ₹234.99 crore at ₹10.15 in September 2026, taking it from 70.15% to 73.76%.
points.quote: The entire revenues and EBITDA generated from Grasim will be reinvested in growth of Grasim businesses.

verdict.what_management_expects: ABReN: one consolidated pan-India renewables platform with EPC in-house, simpler structure, scale/synergy efficiencies, ₹14,600 crore EV, ₹3,000 crore of GIP capital plus its operating experience, and a path from ~4.3 GW to 10 GW+. EMIL: a focused mining/ferro-alloys business after shedding 141 MW. Grasim: 'distinct value creation opportunities', majority retained (73.76%) despite dilution, with build-out funded outside its own balance sheet.
verdict.gaps: No call ever mentions the Scheme, EMIL carve-out, EPC mergers, dilution, ₹10.15 valuation basis or NCLT path; no standalone ABReN P&L, no listing/IPO intent, no lender or approval detail.

verdict.segment_name: EMIL Renewable Energy Undertaking / Renewable Power business (not a reportable segment; disclosed only inside the 'Others' segment together with Textiles and Insulators)
verdict.measure_notes: No profit or revenue line exists for this business on the supplied pages. Grasim's segment note (AR2024 p.518) states 'Others' mainly represents Textiles, Insulators and Renewable Power, and the Others-segment profit line is Segment Result = EBITDA, with revenue shown both as external 'Sales (As reported)' and inter-segment; no renewables-only split is given, so no figure can be attributed to the separating undertaking.

verdict.not_found: All revenue, operating profit and PAT for the renewables/EMIL undertaking. Pages carry only group and 'Others' segment aggregates plus standalone 'Renewables Subsidiaries' investment carrying value (₹1,253 cr).

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is Greaves Electric Mobility Limited (GEML) — the Ampere/ELE/Greaves 3-Wheelers electric 2W and L5 3W business, with step-downs MLR Auto and Bestway Agencies — which management reclassified under its GREAVES.NEXT strategy (Nov 2025) as an 'investee business' alongside Greaves Finance (ev.fin), as distinct from the 'core' B2B engineering company of Energy, Mobility and Industrial Solutions. Management's stated reasons were: (1) GEML needs growth capital the core cannot and should not fund — the DRHP (filed 23 Dec 2024) sought a ₹1,000 crore primary issue plus a smaller OFS, for technology development, the technology centre, in-house battery assembly, expanding subsidiaries' manufacturing capacity, raising stake in one subsidiary, digitisation/IT, inorganic growth and general corporate purposes, while the core's own ₹500–700 crore capex is funded internally; (2) GEML's losses dilute consolidated profitability — Q2 FY26 EV loss of ~₹50 crore against >₹100 crore EBIT in the other segments, FY26 EV segment result of −₹182.01 crore, GEML consolidated FY26 net loss of ₹204.51 crore, EBITDA improving only from −30% to −20%; (3) capital locked in the investees wrecks returns — of ₹1,619 crore net worth a large part sits in GEML/GFL plus ₹500+ crore cash, roughly ₹900 crore that Manish Poddar took out of the ROCE calculation to leave ~₹700 crore of core capital employed earning 'healthy returns'; (4) the two have different maturity curves, different paths to profitability and different orientation (B2B engineering vs consumer), so they must be managed, measured and valued separately, with GEML's employee cost and investment ahead of revenue not comparable to GCL's; (5) partner Abdul Latif Jameel (then ~36%) did not want to be a promoter after a public listing and so was forced to dilute toward 20%, as set out in the DRHP; and (6) investors repeatedly pressed that the two are worth more apart — Zaki Nasser said Greaves and Greaves EV 'will be worth much more separately' and that against Ola/Bajaj/Ather valuations and a re-rating Kirloskar Oil the combined entity is 'caught somewhere in between', while Krisha Kansara wanted the market 'valuing both our businesses separately'. Post-IPO GCL intended to drop below 51% while remaining the largest shareholder, after which consolidation of EV losses and the parent's financial support would cease — which Parag Satpute confirmed as 'a fair understanding'.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced from investors first: on the Nov 2024 call shareholders asked about an IPO or demerger of EV and 'unlocking' value via a separate listing, and Akhila Balachandar would only say the board was 'cognizant'; by the Jan 2025 call the DRHP had been filed (23 Dec 2024) with its use of proceeds, and on the May 2025 call the chairman disclosed SEBI's observations and ALJ's forced dilution from 36% toward 20% because it would not be a promoter post-listing. Through Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 the IPO stayed in 'active conversations' and the separation was formalised conceptually as 'core' versus 'investee' businesses under GREAVES.NEXT, with management saying GCL would fall below 51% but stay the largest shareholder; by Feb 2026 the ₹1,000 crore primary was spelled out, Akhila said there was no plan B, and Saket Kapoor got agreement that the EV drag on parent profits would end. On the May 2026 call the plan had slipped — SEBI extended the observation letter's validity to 30 Sep 2026 and the IPO committee would act only when it could get 'a proper valuation' — and the DRHP gag left management unable to answer breakeven questions at all. The plan then changed materially in the filings: on 9 Jul 2026 the board approved subscribing ₹331.12 crore to a GEML rights issue, on 31 Jul 2026 GEML told SEBI it would not avail the extension so the Offer lapsed, the ₹530 crore rights issue was fully subscribed on 2 Aug 2026 (GCL ₹331.12 crore, ALJ ₹198.87 crore) leaving GCL at an unchanged 62.48%, and the Oct 2026 results wrote off ₹12.66 crore of IPO costs as exceptional — separation deferred to 'an appropriate time'.

points.point: Investors, not management, raised separation first — asking directly whether an IPO or demerger of the EV business would improve focus and growth parameters; management gave no commitment.
points.quote: Second, are we considering an IPO or a demerger of the EV mobility business?

points.point: Asked about value unlocking and listing the segments separately within two-three years, the CFO said only that the board was aware of the option.
points.quote: Any decisions on unlocking of value, capital raise, this is something that the board is cognizant of, and we will come back to you as and when the board gives a different decision.

points.point: GEML's DRHP was filed with SEBI on 23 December 2024, and the use of proceeds was laid out — technology, battery assembly, subsidiary capacity, stake increase, digitisation and inorganic growth, i.e. capital the core would otherwise have to supply.
points.quote: We propose to utilize the proceeds for investments in technology development, enhancing capabilities at our technology center, development of in-house battery assembly, funding expansion of manufacturing capacities of our subsidiaries, increasing the stake in one of the subsidiaries, increasing digitization and deployment of information technology infrastructure, funding inorganic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes.

points.point: A partner requirement drove part of the structure: ALJ, then holding 36%, refused promoter status after listing and therefore had to dilute toward 20%, as reflected in the DRHP.
points.quote: And I think I said in my speech that ALJ did not want to be a promoter post a public listing.

points.point: Shareholders framed the separation as a valuation problem — the engineering business had begun a strong growth trajectory and they wanted the market to price the two businesses independently.
points.quote: I wanted to understand if there is a demand in the market for us to successfully launch this IPO because as investors of Greaves Cotton, it is also very crucial for us that the market starts seeing and valuing both our businesses separately.

points.point: Management made the timing conditional from the outset — SEBI's final observations were in hand but the launch depended on markets, readiness and 'strategic considerations'.
points.quote: The actual IPO launch, however, will be subject to prevailing market conditions, internal preparedness, and other strategic considerations.

points.point: GREAVES.NEXT formalised the split: GCL core is a B2B engineering company (Energy, Mobility, Industrial Solutions) while Greaves Electric and Greaves Finance are consumer-facing 'investee' businesses to be managed differently, with core growth of 16–20% CAGR and ₹500–700 crore capex ring-fenced to the core.
points.quote: While our investee companies of Greaves Electric and Greaves Finance will continue to pursue their growth ambitions, the core of Greaves Cotton Limited will remain centered on building a trusted future-ready engineering company.

points.point: An investor quantified the drag the separation is meant to remove — a ₹50 crore quarterly EV loss against more than ₹100 crore of EBIT in the rest of the group, with consolidated EBIT margin of 17% ex-EV.
points.quote: This quarter also, EV reported Rs. 50 crore loss, while the other segments reported more than Rs. 100 crore of EBIT?

points.point: Management stated the intended end-state ownership: GCL would go below 51% after the IPO (deconsolidating control) but stay a large shareholder.
points.quote: But yes, that is the strategic thinking that post the IPO, we will be below 51% but we will continue to remain significant large shareholders in the company.

points.point: The funding purpose was restated with numbers — a ₹1,000 crore primary issue flowing directly into GEML (plus a smaller OFS to GCL and ALJ), which the CFO identified as the very point of the IPO when asked how long the loss-making business could be sustained.
points.quote: And if you have read through the documents, we will be raising approximately a primary of 1,000 crores, which will be utilized for funding the growth aspirations of Greaves Electric Mobility.

points.point: Management confirmed an investor's reading that after the raise the parent's financial support to, and consolidation drag from, the mobility business would cease, leaving a clean view of core operations — Parag Satpute replied 'That's a fair understanding.'
points.quote: So that is the only fair understanding investors can keep in mind that by May, we should expect that this depleting of the profitability for the parent company because of consolidation and its financial support to the mobility franchise will cease and we will have fair understanding of the core operations of the company.

points.point: Pressed on the nine-month delay since SEBI's May 2025 observations and on alternatives if the IPO did not happen, the CFO said there was no plan B.
points.quote: The plan A is to go for the IPO and we are working on that.

points.point: Timing slipped again: SEBI's April 2026 circular extended observation-letter validity to 30 September 2026, and the IPO committee would wait for a favourable market and 'a proper valuation'.
points.quote: This allows us more time therefore to get into a favorable market scenario and then the investment committee and the IPO committee to take an appropriate call on timing for the IPO.

points.point: An investor pressed that the combined structure was being penalised in the market relative to loss-making EV peers whose capitalisation was rising and to core peer Kirloskar Oil at highs.
points.quote: But the path is there to separate the two, right, sir?

points.point: The return-on-capital case: of ₹1,619 crore net worth, the investee stakes plus ₹500+ crore cash — roughly ₹900 crore — must be stripped out, leaving ~₹700 crore of core capital employed earning healthy returns, with normalisation expected in 2–3 years.
points.quote: I think overall, if you see the net worth at INR 1,619 crores, a big portion of that is into the invest ee businesses, the Greaves Electric Mobility and Greaves Finance Limited.

points.point: The 13–15% EBITDA and 16–18% growth guidance applies only to the core (standalone plus Excel and Greaves Technologies); GEML and GFL are explicitly excluded as being on a different path to profitability.
points.quote: Grea ves Electric Mobility and Greaves Finance Limited are part of our invest ee businesses.

points.point: A cost of the unfinished separation: the live DRHP barred management from giving GEML breakeven, loss-reduction or topline guidance to its own shareholders, repeatedly, through FY26.
points.quote: Sorry to interrupt, but we are held back by the statutory compliances and therefore kindly appreciate our limitations to answer this question.

points.point: On 9 July 2026 the GCL board approved subscribing its full entitlement — about ₹331.12 crore — in a GEML rights issue, and authorised the Risk, Strategy and Investment Committee to take up any unsubscribed shares: funding GEML from the parent instead of from the public market.
points.quote: (a) Subscription to the equity shares proposed to be issued by Greaves Electric Mobility Limited, a material subsidiary of the Company, pursuant to its rights issue, to the full extent of the Company's rights entitlement, aggregating up to approximately ₹331.12 crore; and

points.point: On 31 July 2026 the BRLMs told SEBI that because of the rights issue and SEBI ICDR restrictions on further issuances, GEML would not use the extension, so the final observations lapsed and the IPO was abandoned.
points.quote: Consequently, the Company will not be proceeding with the Offer.

points.point: The ₹530 crore rights issue was fully subscribed on 2 August 2026 by GCL (~₹331 crore) and ALJ (₹198.87 crore) pro rata, so GCL's holding stayed at 62.48% and GEML remained a consolidated material subsidiary — no separation occurred.
points.quote: The Company's shareholding in GEML remains unchanged at 62.48%, and GEML continues to be a material subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The listing was deferred rather than cancelled, with the stated purpose of the capital being next-generation products, battery management systems, powertrains and new-age technology.
points.quote: While GEML has presently decided not to avail itself of the SEBI extension for the proposed Offer , it remains committed to pursuing a public listing at an appropriate time, subject to market conditions, regulatory approvals and other relevant considerations.

points.point: The abandoned separation was written off in H1 FY27 — ₹12.66 crore consolidated (₹1.72 crore standalone) of IPO costs as an exceptional item, alongside ₹20.09 crore of Bestway goodwill/brand impairment and accelerated depreciation of ₹7.75 crore on discontinued 2W tooling and ₹19.55 crore on a 3W brand.
points.quote: Consequentl y, IPO­ refated expenses of Rs. 12.66 crore have been recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss and disclosed as an exceptional item.

points.point: Separation also showed up in reporting structure: from H1 FY27 Cables & Control Levers was merged into Engines and Engineering Products and vehicle finance was carved out as its own reported segment.
points.quote: During the period ended September 30, 2026, the Group has reorganised its segments by (a) merging Cables & Control levers segment as part of Engines and Engineering Products and (b) Separately reporting the vehicle finance business.

verdict.what_management_expects: GEML: ₹1,000 crore primary for technology, in-house battery assembly, subsidiary capacity, digitisation, inorganic growth, and its own market valuation. GCL core: 16–18% organic growth, 13–15% EBITDA, ₹500–700 crore internally funded capex, no further consolidation drag on profits, improved ROCE once the ~₹900 crore tied up in investees and cash is deployed; GCL below 51% yet largest shareholder.
verdict.gaps: No GEML breakeven date or volume, no valuation, no post-listing accounting treatment, no reason rights replaced the IPO beyond market conditions, no cap on further GCL funding.

verdict.rationale: Management presents this as an exit from fertility to concentrate capital and management bandwidth on oncology. The business separated is Milann, HCG's fertility/IVF chain held through BACC Health Care Private Limited — a majority stake taken in 2013 and a fully-owned subsidiary from 2020 — sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund I at an enterprise valuation of INR 63 crore, with equity consideration of INR 37.6 crore for 100% including certain transition services support, 75% received upfront at closing and 25% over 18 months (filings specify INR 28.23 crore at closing and INR 9.41 crore deferred, not contingent). The problems cited: Milann's operating footprint had steadily declined, centres falling from 9 to 6; the business ran at a low EBITDA margin and was only marginally above break-even on a post-rent basis; and reviving and scaling it would need significant management bandwidth plus primary capital infusion, both outside HCG's focus on building the core oncology network. Filings add that BACC is not a material subsidiary and that fertility is not a core business activity — FY26 revenue of INR 60.45 crore (4.45% of HCG standalone revenue) and net worth of INR 17.53 crore (1.09%). The root cause of the decline was named earlier: Milann's original founder/partner exited, her non-compete lapsed, and she opened her own centres very close to HCG's, denting revenue at Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar. The buyer was described as better positioned to infuse growth capital, scale the business independently and carry forward the Milann legacy, and was chosen through a comprehensive, competitive sale process focused on maximizing valuation, transaction certainty and a smooth transition for Milann's employees, with Audit Committee and Board approval and an independent third-party valuation. Crucially, the buyer is a related party: Inviga Healthcare Fund I is sponsored and controlled by Dr. B.S. Ajaikumar, HCG's promoter and Non-Executive Chairman. The push came repeatedly from analysts (Avener Capital, ChrysCapital, Sameeksha, Ambit, Pratap Securities) rather than lenders or partners, and the exit was explicitly held back until the incoming majority shareholder arrived — Ajaikumar said HCG was waiting for the new investor and had discussed it with them.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 2023 call, where Ajaikumar said post-COVID Milann had been through a tough time, a Delhi centre had been closed, and HCG was looking at divesting with no firm timeline; on the Mar 2025 call (Feb 27, 2025) he named the cause — the founder's non-compete expiring and her new centres next to HCG's — and said the timing of a divestment was still being decided. By May 2025 it hardened into intent: HCG was definitely putting a proposal to divest, hopefully within that fiscal year, having waited for and consulted the new investor (KKR/Hector). At the Dec 4, 2025 investor meet the new CEO Manish Mattoo said operations had been stabilised but the focus would be cancer care, with several strategic options under evaluation and divestment of the vertical named as one; Feb 2026 carried no update though revenue was already reported excluding fertility. It completed on May 19-20, 2026 — SPA signed May 19, board approval and pricing disclosed, closing guided to Q1 FY27 — and filings confirm BACC ceased to be a subsidiary from June 30, 2026.

points.point: First flagged: Milann had suffered post-COVID, a Delhi centre was closed for efficiency, and divestment was on the table with no timeline given.
points.quote: It has come, it is coming up the ladder, and we are looking at it in the future for divesting, but we cannot give any firm timeline for it.

points.point: Ajaikumar named the competitive cause of Milann's revenue dip — the founder's exit, expiry of her non-compete, and her new centres opening next to HCG's Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar units — while saying divestment timing was still being weighed.
points.quote: In view of that, she has started her own few centers very close to our center. So because of that, particularly in Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar, we have seen a dip in the revenue.

points.point: Divestment was framed as a decision of timing, not of principle, with Milann's turnaround (including a new andrology focus) pursued in parallel.
points.quote: But at the same time, there is a decision where we want to see what time to divest it, we will be looking at that also as we move forward.

points.point: Asked by Umang Gada (Avener Capital) whether HCG would spin off Milann, Ajaikumar said a divestment proposal was being put forward, and that HCG had deliberately waited for the incoming investor (KKR) and discussed it with them.
points.quote: We have addressed this issue internally. We were just waiting for the new investor also to come. We have also discussed with them. So, we are definitely putting a proposal to divest. And hopefully, this will happen definitely this fiscal year, and we will keep you updated.

points.point: At the investor and analyst meet the new CEO reset the rationale around single-specialty focus: Milann operations had been stabilised, but future focus would be cancer care, with strategic options under evaluation. Milann was also lumped into the new international cluster rather than given its own segment.
points.quote: But going forward, our focus will be on cancer care. And hence, we are evaluating several strategic options on the way ahead for Milann.

points.point: Pressed by Rajas Joshi (ChrysCapital) on what options existed, Mattoo named divestment explicitly but stopped short of commitment.
points.quote: I think one of the options, while we are still evaluating, could be divestment of this vertical.

points.point: No divestment update was given, but management had already begun reporting the core business excluding fertility (Q3 FY26 revenue INR 633 crore total versus INR 618 crore ex-fertility), effectively pre-separating Milann in disclosure while the review ran.
points.quote: Excluding the fertility business, HCG delivered revenues of INR 618 crore, supported by healthy patient volume growth of 8% year-on-year, underscoring resilient demand for oncology care across the network.

points.point: Announced: board approved the sale of Milann to Inviga Healthcare Fund, signed the previous day, closing expected within Q1 FY27 — presented as a strategic decision to sharpen oncology focus.
points.quote: Finally, we have taken a strategic decision to sharpen our focus on oncology. In line with this, the board has approved the sale of Milann, our fertility business, to Inviga Healthcare Fund.

points.point: Terms: enterprise valuation INR 63 crore; equity consideration INR 37.6 crore for 100% including certain transition services support, 75% upfront at closing and 25% over 18 months.
points.quote: The equity consideration for 100% of the business, including certain transition services support is INR37.6 crore, of which 75% will be received upfront at closing and the balance 25% over 18 months.

points.point: The operational problem quantified for Pranav Chawla (Ambit): 13 years inside HCG, centres down from 9 to 6, low EBITDA margin and barely above break-even after rent.
points.quote: The number of centers has come down from 9 to 6 and today the business operates at a low EBITDA margin and remains only marginally above break-even on a post-rent basis.

points.point: The core why: fixing Milann would consume management bandwidth and require primary equity capital, both of which HCG wants aimed at the oncology network instead.
points.quote: So, reviving and scaling the platform would require significant management bandwidth and primary capital infusion, both of which are outside HCGs current strategic focus because we are focused on developing the primary oncology network, core oncology network.

points.point: The buyer rationale: an owner better able to fund and scale fertility independently and preserve the Milann brand legacy.
points.quote: So, HCG then decided to exit this non-core business and transfer it to a buyer who was better positioned to infuse growth capital, scale the business independently, and carry for/ward the Milann legacy.

points.point: Process described as a competitive sale with Inviga shortlisted as preferred buyer, optimising for valuation, deal certainty and employee transition, cleared by Board and Audit Committee.
points.quote: See, we initiated a comprehensive sale process, a competitive sale process where HCG shortlisted Inviga as the preferred buyer and the focus was on maximizing valuation and ensuring that the transaction, you know, was done with certainty and it facilitated a smooth transition for Milann's employees as well.

points.point: Abdulkader Puranwala (ICICI Securities) linked the divestment and the INR 425 crore rights issue to leverage; management said net debt/EBITDA had fallen from 2.2-2.3x to 1.4x against an internal ceiling of 2.5x, giving headroom for brownfield capacity (200+ beds, INR 90-100 crore) and the 1,000-bed FY30 plan.
points.quote: So the net debt to EBITDA ratio has, come down favourably. Earlier it was 2.2 x, 2.3x. It is come down to 1.4 x as of today and this gives us enough headroom to invest in capacity addition, expansion, brownfield, technology additions and all.

points.point: Filing (May 19, 2026) confirms it is a share sale of BACC Health Care Private Limited, not a scheme of arrangement or demerger (the LODR question on disposal outside a Scheme of Arrangement is answered Not Applicable), and states fertility is non-core.
points.quote: BACC is not a material subsidiary of the Company and is engaged in the business of fertility and reproductive healthcare services, which is not a core business activity of the Company.

points.point: Filing states the capital-allocation purpose: greater operational focus and redeployment of capital into high-growth areas and cancer services.
points.quote: The Proposed Transaction is aligned with the Company's broader strategic and capital allocation objectives and is expected to facilitate greater operational focus and business alignment, allowing the Company to reinvest capital in high growth areas and cancer services.

points.point: Materiality quantified: BACC FY26 revenue INR 60.45 crore (4.45% of HCG standalone revenue) and net worth INR 17.53 crore (1.09%); consideration split INR 28.23 crore at closing and INR 9.41 crore deferred within 18 months, with the deferred piece explicitly not contingent.
points.quote: The deferred consideration referenced above is not a conditional or contingent payment.

points.point: The buyer is promoter-controlled: the transaction is a related party transaction done on an arm's length basis, based on an independent third-party valuation and a competitive process.
points.quote: Dr. B.S. Ajaikumar, Promoter and Non-Executive Chairman of the Board of the Company is the Sponsor of the Inviga Healthcare Fund I (Fund) and also the Promoter of Inviga Investment Advisors Private Limited, the Investment Manager of the Fund. Accordingly, the Fund is controlled by Dr. B S Ajaikumar.

points.point: The exit was value-destructive on the books: on reclassification as held for sale, HCG recognised a standalone impairment of INR 37.52 crore and a consolidated goodwill impairment of INR 31.91 crore as FY26 exceptional items, against the fair value of the consideration receivable.
points.quote: Accordingly, the investment was measured at the lower of its carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Accordingly, an impairment loss of Rs. 3,752 lakhs was recognised as an exceptional item during the previous year ended 31 March 2026 based on the fair value of the consideration receivable, net of related expenses.

points.point: Completion confirmed in the Q1 FY27 results: sale closed June 29, 2026 for INR 37.64 crore (INR 28.23 crore received upfront, INR 9.41 crore receivable within 18 months), BACC deconsolidated from June 30, 2026, with a INR 2.96 crore gain booked in consolidated other income.
points.quote: Consequent to completion of the transaction, BACC ceased to be a subsidiary of the Company with effect from 30 June 2026.

points.point: A separate, earlier internal separation: the Triesta lab and Cyclotron (FDG production) businesses were slump-sold into a wholly-owned subsidiary so oncology sat in one company and the scalable diagnostics business could grow outside the HCG network with greater freedom; management said the restructuring under the Triesta brand was completed by the Mar 2025 call.
points.quote: So this is more on account of business realignment where onco comes under one company and the expandable business, which we can look at expanding beyond our own network, which is the lab and the Cyclotron business can move to a separate entity. It also allows greater freedom with a separate entity structure.

verdict.what_management_expects: For HCG: management bandwidth and capital freed for the core oncology network (brownfield/greenfield, 1,000 beds by FY30), sharper single-specialty focus, modest cash (INR 37.6 crore, 75% upfront) on an already de-levered balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 1.4x after the INR 425 crore rights issue). For Milann: a new owner able to infuse growth capital, scale it independently and carry its legacy forward. No margin or valuation uplift was quantified.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these texts there is no separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement at Hindalco to explain: across the five earnings calls (May 2025 through May 2026) management never proposes separating Novelis, the India aluminium, downstream, specialty alumina or copper businesses, and the single filing supplied is not a scheme but a voluntary strike-off of a dormant shell. That filing records that East Coast Bauxite Mining Company Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, was struck off by the Registrar of Companies, Cuttack under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013 on its own application, effective June 22, 2026, with turnover/income and net worth contribution stated as 'Nil' and the sale-consideration, buyer, related-party and Regulation 37A/scheme fields all marked 'Not Applicable' precisely because it is a dissolution rather than a disposal; the company states it has no material impact on operations or financial position. The only other separations discussed are operational, not corporate: Novelis idling one of two cast lines in China (management citing smaller low-aluminium-content Chinese vehicles softening long-term auto demand growth to 3%-5%), exiting two North America specialty facilities 'to consolidate capacity and drive higher asset utilisation', a non-binding letter of intent received in early April 2025 to sell the Fairmont property after Novelis had announced closure in late March, and the return/surrender of coal blocks (Kathautia, with a Rs 160 crore impairment of mining rights; Radhikapur East already surrendered; three of four original blocks gone, only IV/4 still run). The nearest thing to an inter-company separation is the opposite direction — an acquisition: Hindalco buying the Essel Mining subsidiary holding Bandha at cost (Rs 48 lakh share capital plus Rs 1,000 crore of debt, c. Rs 2,000 crore paid in FY26, a further c. Rs 4,000 crore capex over a 45-year mine life, 18.5-20 km from Mahan), where Satish Pai said Essel is 'quite happy that we take over the CAPEX' and will stay on only as MDO operator, i.e. ownership of capital separated from mining services. Far from separating Novelis, management repeatedly asserts the group is managed as one pool of capital: AV Minerals raised $800 million at SOFR+105 bps (upsized by $200 million on 10 February 2026) with $750 million injected as equity into Novelis in December 2025, justified by Hindalco's cheaper cost of debt, not wanting Novelis's net debt/EBITDA 'to go too high', worry about 'bond owners' and Novelis's ratings, and the value of 'showing parental support'; on fungibility Pai said 'we look at it as one consolidated. That's how the shareholder will look at it,' and the governing commitment is consolidated net debt/EBITDA at or below 2x (1.02x June 2025, 1.23x September 2025, 1.73x December 2025, 1.83x March 2026) against a $10 billion FY26-FY29 capex plan. The only 'separation' management promises is in disclosure, not legal structure: Pai said specialty alumina would be carved out as a separately reported segment 'sometime next year, just like we have done downstream alumina.' Stated strategy through the May 2026 call is integration and scale — doubling upstream aluminium and copper, a fourfold rise in India downstream EBITDA by FY30, Novelis's '3 by 30' and the $5 billion, 600 KT Bay Minette plant — not disaggregation.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea surfaces at any point: the May 2025 call introduces footprint exits (two North America specialty plants, a China auto finishing line) and the Fairmont letter of intent, plus the inbound Bandha/Essel transfer; the August 2025 call adds the Kathautia coal-block return and its Rs 160 crore write-off. The November 2025 Novelis call reframes the China line idling as strategic (3%-5% auto growth) and introduces the $750 million parent equity infusion, which the November 2025 Hindalco call and the February 2026 call then execute via AV Minerals ($800 million, upsized $200 million on 10 February 2026) while explicitly defending a single consolidated balance sheet. The February 2026 call's only 'separation' is reporting — specialty alumina to be split out, as downstream already was. By the May 2026 call the direction is purely expansionary, and the June 22, 2026 filing is a dormant-subsidiary strike-off, not a scheme of arrangement.

points.point: The only corporate separation on the record is the voluntary strike-off and dissolution of a dormant wholly owned subsidiary, East Coast Bauxite Mining Company Private Limited, by the RoC Cuttack under Section 248, effective June 22, 2026 — not a demerger of any operating business.
points.quote: East Coast has ceased to be the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, effective June 22, 2026.

points.point: The filing itself rules out a scheme of arrangement, sale, buyer, consideration or related-party angle, answering each field as not applicable because the entity was merely dissolved, and reports its revenue and net worth contribution as Nil.
points.quote: Not Applicable, since this is the case of voluntary strike-off and consequent dissolution, effective June 22, 2026.

points.point: Hindalco states the strike-off changes nothing financially, which is the company's entire stated rationale — there is no value-unlock, focus or valuation argument offered.
points.quote: These aforesaid action will have no material impact on the operations or financial position of the Company.

points.point: The closest thing to a business separation at Novelis is footprint rationalisation: exiting two North America specialty facilities and idling a China auto finishing line, framed as consolidating capacity and lifting asset utilisation, not as separating a business unit.
points.quote: And exiting two North America specialty facilities to consolidate capacity and drive higher asset utilisation.

points.point: Steve Fisher explained Fairmont as a closure that turned into a possible property sale after an unsolicited approach in early April 2025, with closure to proceed over the following months if no agreement was reached.
points.quote: So, on Fairmont, after announcing that we were moving towards closing the facility in late March, we were approached in early April, we have entered into a non -binding letter of intent to see if we can sell the property.

points.point: The Bandha transaction runs the other way — Hindalco takes the Essel Mining subsidiary (Rs 48 lakh share capital plus Rs 1,000 crore debt, c. Rs 4,000 crore further capex, 45-year life, 18.5 km from Mahan) at cost, with Essel separating out of ownership and staying only as mine operator because of the capex burden.
points.quote: I think for Essel Mining, because of the CAPEX spend and all required, I think that they are quite happy that we take over the CAPEX. And they will continue to be the MDO operator of mine.

points.point: Asset exits in India are coal-block surrenders rather than business separations: Kathautia is being returned, forcing a Rs 160 crore impairment of mining rights, leaving only IV/4 operating out of the original four blocks.
points.quote: Kathautia. We are in the process of returning Kathautia. So for that, we had to write off some of the mining rights, et cetera.

points.point: Steve Fisher gave a demand rationale for idling one of two China cast lines — smaller, lower-priced Chinese vehicles with less aluminium content cutting long-term auto demand growth to 3%-5% — a capacity decision, not a separation.
points.quote: We estimate this will soften the longer -term aluminum demand growth rate to a range of 3% to 5% and is the strategic rationale behind our decision earlier this year to idle one of two cash lines in China.

points.point: Pai argued for keeping the group financially integrated — raising debt at AV Minerals and injecting it as equity into Novelis to protect Novelis's leverage, bondholders and ratings and to show parental support — the opposite of separating Novelis.
points.quote: We have bond owners that we are worried about. We don't want the ratings of Novelis to get negatively impacted.

points.point: Asked directly whether Hindalco and Novelis are two standalone businesses, Pai confirmed cash is treated as fungible and the group is run and judged on one consolidated net debt/EBITDA (below 2x).
points.quote: we look at it as one consolidated. That's how the shareholder will look at it.

points.point: The only 'separation' management commits to is in segment disclosure — specialty alumina (c. 500 KT from Muri and Belgaum, part index-linked, part value-added) to be reported separately from metal-grade Utkal alumina, as downstream already is.
points.quote: We will start to separate that out sometime next year, just like we have done downstream alumina.

points.point: The financing step that an investor might mistake for a separation is an intra-group equity injection: AV Minerals, a wholly owned Hindalco subsidiary, raised $800 million at SOFR+105 bps, $750 million of it infused as Novelis equity in December 2025, upsized by $200 million on 10 February 2026 and five years in tenor.
points.quote: During the quarter, Hindalco's wholly-owned subsidiary, AV Minerals, raised $800 million at SOFR plus 105 basis points.

points.point: The final call in the record restates an integration-and-expansion strategy — doubling upstream aluminium and copper, fourfold India downstream EBITDA by FY30, Novelis '3 by 30', $200 million cost run-rate toward $350-400 million by FY28 exit — with no separation mentioned.
points.quote: Our strategic priorities are clearly defined in our accelerating upstream expansion in aluminium and copper, while driving a fourfold increase in downstream EBITD A in India by FY 30.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is claimed for a separation, because none is proposed. For the struck-off subsidiary: no material impact, Nil revenue and net worth. For footprint exits: consolidated capacity and higher asset utilisation at Novelis, supporting the $350-400 million cost programme and $600/t goal. For the group: one consolidated balance sheet at or below 2x net debt/EBITDA funding $10 billion of capex.
verdict.gaps: Everything a separation thesis needs: no demerger, no scheme, no entity split, no listed-entity rationale, no valuation, capital-structure, lender, partner or investor demand for one.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe Indus Towers separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving down any business, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them — the premise is not supported by the supplied material. Across all seven transcripts (Nov 2023 through May 2026) and the one filing (Q1 FY27 results, July 27, 2026), management discusses the opposite direction: consolidation and bolt-on expansion of a single tower business. The only structural actions named are (a) the acquisition of about 12,600 towers (including lean) from Bharti Airtel, completed in the last week of March 2025 for roughly INR 18-20 billion of consideration (Rs. 1,800 crore line item in cash flow; Rs. 18 billion booked to common control reserves; Rs. 1.7 billion of restated opex/depreciation from 19 Nov 2024), and (b) the creation of a new Africa holding structure — wholly owned subsidiaries in UAE plus Zambia, Uganda and Nigeria entities, and Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited (incorporated 28 April 2026) — which management repeatedly frames as greenfield organic growth of the same core tower business, not a carve-out of an existing one. The only 'separation' language anywhere is operational, not corporate: the EV-charging pilot was to be run by a 'separate business unit, separate team' (Jan 2025), and by May 2025 that pilot was still being evaluated and might be held back so 'focus will remain on the towers.' The filing's single reference to a 'scheme of arrangement' is a legacy depreciation-to-general-reserve adjustment (Rs. 185 million in Q1 FY27, Rs. 795 million in FY26), not a new separation, and both standalone and consolidated results state the company 'has a single reportable segment.' Capital-structure debate in these calls is about dividends versus leverage (INR 14 per share final dividend for FY26, about INR 37-38 billion, roughly 100% of FY26 free cash flow of INR 37.6 billion) — not about separating anything. No investor, lender or partner on any of these calls asks for a separation.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces. Nov 2023 through May 2025 the structural theme is consolidation (Airtel's 12,600 towers, 'aggressively pursuing market share through both organic and inorganic routes'); Jan 2025 adds an EV-charging pilot as a 'separate business unit,' which by May 2025 is merely 'evaluating that pilot' and may be dropped in favour of towers. Oct 2025 announces Africa (Nigeria, Uganda, Zambia) explicitly as the same tower business, not diversification; Feb 2026 adds the UAE/local-country holding structure and possible GIFT City debt funding, and the July 2026 filing lists ten subsidiaries plus Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited (28 April 2026). May 2026 closes on Zambia licence in hand, Uganda/Nigeria approvals pending, and a resumed dividend — with no separation mentioned on any call.

points.point: Africa is framed as an extension of the existing tower business rather than a separate or separable venture — management explicitly rejects the diversification framing.
points.quote: So I think the overall Africa strategy is not diversification business. It's our tower business. That's our core strength.

points.point: The only new corporate structure described is an Africa holding chain of wholly owned subsidiaries (UAE plus each local market) created for execution and funding, not to separate an existing business out of Indus.
points.quote: We have set up a holding structure through the incorporation of wholly owned subsidiaries in UAE and at the local country level in each of our markets, establishing a clear country-level execution framework.

points.point: Funding for the Africa entities was still undecided between UAE-level and GIFT City-level debt, with 'nothing major' required — the scale discussed is a start-up, not a carve-out.
points.quote: It could be -- one of the possibilities, it could be at the UAE level. It could also be at the GIFT City level and so on. So we are yet to work on those details.

points.point: Strategy articulated to the Board was consolidation and market-share capture — the opposite of separating a business — evidenced by acquiring about 12,600 Airtel towers.
points.quote: The strategy includes aggressively pursuing market share through both organic and inorganic routes as demonstrated by our acquisition of Bharti Airtel's towers.

points.point: The acquired Airtel portfolio was booked as a common control transaction with Rs. 18 billion to common control reserves and Rs. 1.7 billion of restated opex/depreciation — an in-bound consolidation, with no counterpart separation.
points.quote: Accordingly, the difference of Rs. 18 billion between purchase consideration and carrying value is recognized as common control reserves.

points.point: The only 'separate' entity language in three years is operational ring-fencing of an EV-charging pilot inside the company, deliberately kept apart so the tower business does not suffer.
points.quote: I think it is something that will be new to the industry as well so we will be very cautious on that one but it is a separate business, yes.

points.point: By the next call that EV pilot was still unproven and might be abandoned rather than scaled or separated, with focus returning to towers.
points.quote: And if not, I think our focus will remain on the towers.

points.point: Management explicitly denied even considering a data-centre business, attributing the idea to media speculation — no adjacent business exists that could be separated.
points.quote: So I don't think we have discussed that as an option currently because our focus remains on the tower growth primarily.

points.point: The Q1 FY27 filing (July 27, 2026) uses 'scheme of arrangement' only for a legacy depreciation-to-general-reserve adjustment (Rs. 185 million in the quarter, Rs. 795 million in FY26) and reports Indus as one business with one segment — no demerger, hive-off or separation is disclosed.
points.quote: Accordingly, the Company has a single reportable segment.

points.point: The same filing lists ten consolidated entities — the UAE companies, Zambia/Uganda/Nigeria operating companies, Smartx Services, the ESOP trust and Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited incorporated 28 April 2026 — all additions to the group, none a separation.
points.quote: Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited (incorporated on April 28, 2026)

points.point: The latest call's capital-allocation discussion is about distributing FY26 free cash flow (INR 37.6 billion; INR 14 per share final dividend) and preserving leverage headroom for growth — not about separating or releasing a business.
points.quote: See, the Board evaluated the FCF situation and the debt levels that we want to maintain and decided accordingly to distribute the FCF of FY26.

points.point: The earliest call in the set also describes only organic expansion of one passive-infrastructure business (record 5,928 macro towers, 5,583 co-locations in Q2 FY24), with no structural review of any kind.
points.quote: Driven by continued strong demand from one of our customers, we added 5,928 macro towers and 5,583 corresponding co-locations.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation is announced, so no per-entity expectation is stated. For the Africa subsidiaries management expects differentiation on cost per tower, SLA, uptime and energy efficiency, debt-funded, 'value accretive over the long term,' with return profile, MSA structure and hurdle rate explicitly still undecided. India expectations stay 55%-plus EBITDA margin, growth capex and progressive FCF distribution.

verdict.rationale: On the documents supplied, ixigo (Le Travenues Technology Ltd.) is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business of its own — there is no scheme of arrangement in the filings, and the one filing tagged 'Diversification/Disinvestment' (August 13, 2026) is expressly marked 'Not applicable' against the question of whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement or needs Regulation 37A compliance. The only actual separation disclosed is the unwinding of ixigo's minority holding in Freshbus Private Limited, the electric intercity bus operator it first backed under an Investment and Shareholders' Agreement dated October 28, 2022 (68,258 CCPS plus 1 equity share at ₹2,344 per share). Under a Share Purchase Agreement dated August 13, 2026 with Twelve Stone LLP and Freshbus, ixigo sells 46,264 CCPS at ₹7,911 per share for cash of ₹365,994,504 (~₹36.6 crore), being 17.39% of Freshbus' paid-up capital, cutting its stake from 25.66% to 8.27% and ending Freshbus' status as an associate company; completion is set for on or before August 30, 2026. The buyer is Twelve Stone LLP, whose designated partners are Sudhakar Reddy Chirra, Freshbus' Founder and Managing Director, and Sasya Chirra — i.e. a founder-side vehicle buying ixigo out — and the filing states it is not a related-party transaction and that ixigo has no identifiable promoter group with an interest in it. The economics ixigo discloses are the only 'problem' the documents attach to the holding: Freshbus was a persistent drag on consolidated profit, with share of associate losses of ₹11.22 crore in FY26, ₹9.1 crore in FY25 versus ₹5.9 crore in FY24, and quarterly call-outs of ₹2.0 crore (Q1 FY25), ₹1.93 crore (Q2 FY25), ₹1.9 crore (Q3 FY25), ₹3.29 crore (Q4 FY25), ₹2.34 crore (Q1 FY26), ₹1.47 crore (Q2 FY26), ₹2.9 crore (Q3 FY26) and ₹45.59 million (Q4 FY26), against a carrying value of just ₹18.87 crore, or 0.96% of consolidated net worth. The exit price of ₹7,911 versus a ₹2,344 entry is roughly 3.4x, so the disclosed facts support a profitable exit from a loss-making, immaterial, non-core associate rather than a structural separation. Management never discusses the sale on any call — the latest call (May 21, 2026) predates the SPA — and in the same period the group is moving the other way, consolidating rather than separating: a ₹1,296 crore Prosus preferential issue (46,270,092 shares at ₹280, allotted November 12, 2025), a new wholly owned Singapore subsidiary IXIGO PTE. LTD., and a 60% upfront acquisition of Spain's Online Travel Solutions S.L. ('Trenes') for €11.70 million through that subsidiary. The only 'separation' management itself describes is organisational, not legal: the 'NewCo inside the old co' AI team built inside ixigo, which has no separate entity, capital or shareholding attached to it.
verdict.evolution: Freshbus enters the story as a deconsolidation, not a separation: on the Aug 2024 call (Q1 FY25, August 1, 2024) management explains it was a subsidiary until September 13, 2023 and became an associate after a primary round diluted ixigo, so its losses moved below EBITDA. Through May 2025 (May 14, 2025), Jul 2025 (July 16, 2025), Nov 2025 (October 29, 2025), Jan 2026 (January 22, 2026) and May 2026 (May 21, 2026) it appears only as a recurring one-off call-out of rising associate losses, never as a candidate for exit, and no analyst asks about it. Separately, on Nov 2025 Rajnish Kumar introduces the 'new co inside the old co' idea for AI self-disruption, which by May 2026 has become 'NewCo inside ixigo' and ixigo NEXT — an internal team, explicitly not a carve-out. The actual disposal surfaces only in the August 13, 2026 filing, after the last transcript, with no management narrative attached.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these texts, Jubilant FoodWorks is not separating a business in any demerger, spin-off or scheme sense — none of the seven earnings calls contains a single word about separating, demerging, hiving off or listing any business, and no scheme of arrangement is filed. The only separation document present is the Regulation 30 intimation dated December 29, 2025, under which the Company executed a Share Purchase Agreement with Mr. Karan Chechani, one of the founders of Hashtag Loyalty Private Limited, to sell its entire 31.66% stake, after which Hashtag ceases to be an associate; the filing itself answers 'Not Applicable' to whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement. The stated reason is prior discontinuance of Hashtag's business operations, and the numbers management disclosed make the exit economically trivial: Hashtag's FY2024-25 total income was Rs. 27.47 million and its net worth as on March 31, 2025 was Rs. 1.22 million, each contributing 'Nil' to JFL's consolidated financials, the investment was already fully impaired during FY2024-25, and total consideration is Rs. 6,415.94 — a token sum returning the stake to a founder who is explicitly not part of the promoter or promoter group, in a transaction that is not a related-party transaction, with completion expected on or before February 12, 2026. The nearest thing to a portfolio-separation narrative on the calls is pruning, not separation: management repeatedly described curtailing or stopping expansion of Dunkin' and Hong's to concentrate on Domino's and Popeyes, quantifying the emerging-brands EBITDA drag at roughly 200 bps (FY24 base, Nov 2025) and 230-250 bps (Feb 2026), and targeting at least halving it within 12-18 months as part of the 200 bps margin-improvement commitment to FY28. Separately, the Turkey (DP Eurasia) acquisition debt of about EUR 110 million sitting in the Netherlands entity was de-linked from India cash flows — serviced entirely from Turkish internal cash flows and dividends for three quarters by Feb 2026 — but management framed this as refinancing and self-funding, never as a separation of the entity. No investor, lender, brand partner (Domino's International, RBI, Inspire Brands) or aggregator is recorded anywhere in these texts as asking for a business to be separated. The only shareholder-driven structural question was Vivek M.'s May 2025 query about the group's HCCB transaction, which Hari Bhartia answered by reaffirming that focus stays at Jubilant FoodWorks and that funding was already arranged.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces as a separation on any call: Nov 2024 through May 2026 contain only portfolio pruning — Nov 13, 2024 (no expansion for Hong's and Dunkin' until store economics work), May 14, 2025 (expansion in both formally curtailed mid-year to focus on Popeyes; drag to halve), Aug 13, 2025 (expansion 'down to a trickle or stopped', drag halving in 12-18 months), Nov 13, 2025 and Feb 10, 2026 (drag quantified at ~200 bps on FY24 and 230-250 bps, to halve), and May 20, 2026 (drag reduction 'ahead of the plan'). Hashtag Loyalty is never mentioned on any of the seven calls; it appears only in the December 29, 2025 filing, which itself refers back to 'various disclosures made' earlier about discontinuance of Hashtag's operations — disclosures not included in this pack. The plan therefore did not visibly evolve in these texts; a dormant, fully impaired 31.66% associate stake was simply sold back to a founder for Rs. 6,415.94, with completion due on or before February 12, 2026.

points.point: The only separation/disposal document in the pack: a Share Purchase Agreement dated December 29, 2025 selling JFL's entire 31.66% stake in Hashtag Loyalty Private Limited to founder Karan Chechani, who is not part of the promoter group.

points.point: The closest the calls come to separating businesses is pruning the emerging brands: Khetarpal said JFL had decided mid-year to stop expanding Dunkin' and Hong's and concentrate on Popeyes, expecting the drag between Domino's 14.5% margin and the 11.8% standalone quarterly margin to halve.
points.quote: And as you would see, we have already taken the stance of curtailing any or not doing any expansion in Dunkin' and Hong's.

points.point: Hegde confirmed expansion of Dunkin' and Hong's had effectively ceased and that the ~200 bps FY25 drag from emerging formats would be at least halved in 12 to 18 months by fixing unit economics rather than by any corporate separation.

points.point: Hegde quantified the emerging-brands drag at roughly 230-250 bps as disclosed, to be halved on the path to the 200 bps EBITDA improvement over FY24 by FY28 — framed as margin repair inside the listed entity, not as carving anything out.
points.quote: And the reduction of the drag on the EBUs, at the point in time that we had disclosed our numbers, the drag was of Popeyes, Dunkin and Hong's was approximately about 230 bps, 250 bps.

points.quote: We are pleased to share that Turkey is now servicing its acquisition-related debt entirely through internal cash flows.

verdict.rationale: The texts do not support the premise: in the three years of calls and the one filing provided, KSB Ltd. announces no demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any operating business, and management never gives a separation rationale. The only separation of any entity is administrative — the 28 Sep 2026 filing says Pofran Sales and Agency Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on 7 January 2005, has applied for voluntary strike-off with the Registrar of Companies, Pune, and will cease to be a subsidiary on completion. The stated reason is simply dormancy: Pofran 'was not operating for past seven years' and 'has been inoperative since last 7 years.' The Annexure A disclosure confirms there is no economics to it — turnover/revenue/income and net worth contributed are 'Not applicable,' as are the sale agreement date, consideration, buyer details, related-party and arm's-length questions, and the regulation 37A / scheme-of-arrangement item; the only timeline given is 'according to the prescribed guidelines of voluntary strike off under Companies Act 2013.' No investor, lender or JV partner is said to have asked for it, and no cost, capital, focus or valuation benefit is claimed. The nearest portfolio decisions management does discuss run the other way or are exits, not separations: in Mar 2026 Rajeev Jain says of the BP&CL reciprocating-pump business that 'initially, we thought to sell it off, luckily we did not and we decided to build it ourselves,' and in Mar 2025 he describes having exited cast-iron foundry work (about 1,100 patterns and 3,000 metric tonnes) by handing it to third-party foundries, while FGD business 'suddenly overnight has vanished' because of a change in government regulation. Throughout, the strategy presented is consolidation and range-completion within one listed entity — nuclear (₹1,300 crore order book), solar (₹245 crore CY25 to 300+ crore CY26), valves, SupremeServ at ~15-17% of sales, firefighting, mining, exports at 17% — not separation of any of it.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces in the calls: Mar 2024, Mar 2025, Sep 2025, Nov 2025 and Mar 2026 all discuss capacity additions (Shirwal and Sinnar sheds to be commissioned by March 2026), new segments and the group's willingness to localise more products, with no question or answer about demerging, hiving off or listing any division separately. Over this period the only direction of travel discussed is inward: BP&CL technology (acquired 2023) being built up rather than sold, and openness to further acquisitions ('if such opportunities occur in future, we are definitely exploring it', Sep 2025). The single separation event appears only in the 28 Sep 2026 filing, as the voluntary strike-off of the dormant shell Pofran Sales and Agency Limited. The plan therefore has no evolution to trace — one administrative cessation announced once, with no prior or subsequent discussion in the transcripts supplied.

points.point: The only separation disclosed is a voluntary strike-off application for the wholly owned subsidiary Pofran Sales and Agency Limited, filed with the Registrar of Companies, Pune; on completion Pofran ceases to be a subsidiary.
points.quote: With reference to the captioned subject, we would like to inform you that Pofran Sales and Agency Limited ("Pofran"), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, has made an application for strike-off with the Registrar of Companies, Pune.

points.point: The entire stated reason is dormancy — the entity, incorporated 7 January 2005, has not traded for seven years. No strategic, capital or valuation rationale is offered.
points.quote: Pofran was incorporated on January 7, 2005 and was not operating for past seven years.

points.point: Annexure A confirms the separated entity contributed nothing: turnover/revenue/income and net worth contribution are 'Not applicable' because it has been inoperative for seven years.

points.quote: whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations Not applicable.

points.point: The only timeline given is the statutory strike-off process under the Companies Act 2013, not a board-approved scheme with record dates or share entitlement ratios.
points.quote: Time line according to the prescribed guidelines of voluntary strike off under Companies Act 2013.

points.point: Management explicitly rejected divesting a business: the BP&CL reciprocating-pump line was considered for sale after the 2023 acquisition and deliberately retained and developed in-house, with an NPCIL-approved prototype.
points.quote: Reciprocating pump business we acquired from BP&CL and it was good acquisition. Initially, we thought to sell it off, luckily we did not and we decided to build it ourselves.

points.point: The closest real exit discussed is the step-by-step closure of the captive cast-iron foundry business, roughly 1,100 patterns and 3,000 metric tonnes, outsourced to third-party foundries — framed as supply-chain simplification, not as a separation of a business unit.
points.quote: You know that our foundry also for cast iron, we have closed it step by step. We have come out of the cast iron business and almost 1,100 patents and the 3,000 metric tons of business. We have given it to other foundries here, and we did not have any issues.

points.point: Asked directly what worries him and what the parent provides, Jain names no portfolio restructuring — only the pace of nuclear project implementation — and describes royalty, IT and service charges to the parent, with no entity reorganisation.
points.quote: It's only I would say if I would have a wish, I would say the implementation of nuclear projects, if it could be faster.

points.point: Management frames the multi-segment structure as the deliberate hedge that makes separation unnecessary — mixed margins across nuclear, valves, SupremeServ, solar and firefighting are pooled to hold a 13-14% EBITDA band.
points.quote: So, that's why overall, I would say, the return which we always target is that EBITDA level what we have.

points.point: On the same logic, segment volatility is presented as internally absorbed — FGD vanishing overnight was offset by the L&T supercritical win — rather than as a reason to carve any segment out.
points.quote: But something else, this is KSB's strength that we have all segments and today we got this L&T supercritical and we are expecting much, much more with the next five years what is being invested.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is claimed. The filing states only that Pofran ceases to be a subsidiary on completion; it attributes no revenue, income or net worth to it, names no consideration, and asserts no benefit to margins, capital, focus or valuation for KSB or for the struck-off entity. Management's stated goals stay unchanged: double-digit topline growth, 13-14% EBITDA, rising dividend.
verdict.gaps: Everything: no demerger exists in these texts. Unexplained why Pofran was dormant seven years before strike-off, and why no earlier call mentioned it.
