verdict.rationale: These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale out, hive-off or scheme of arrangement by KRN — there is no Scheme document among the ten filings, no shareholder resolution for one (the 15 April 2026 EGM covers only promoter re-appointments, an ESOP plan of 6,00,000 options and a ₹500 crore QIP), and no call question or management answer about separating any business. The only going-concern business transfer in the record runs inward, not outward: on 6 October 2025 wholly-owned subsidiary KRN HVAC Products Pvt Ltd signed a Business Transfer Agreement with Sphere Refrigeration Systems Pvt Ltd to acquire its bus air-conditioning division, which management framed as buying technology, know-how, the three ex-Subros/'Sparrows Motherson' professionals, their 12–13 years of experience, employees, assets and store, with the price 'not much' and never disclosed — Sphere Refrigeration's own top line was only ₹2–3 crore, while the related Sphere Thermal did ₹40–50 crore and had been sold six months earlier to a third party wanting railway HVAC entry. The separation visible in that deal is the counterparty's: Sphere's founders sold Sphere Thermal and 'bought back' the bus AC business into Sphere Refrigeration, which KRN then acquired. KRN's own structure is deliberately multi-entity rather than separating: the new 600,000 sq ft Neemrana plant sits in KRN HVAC because it carries the 15% concessional tax rate, the ₹141.72 crore white-goods PLI sanctioned by IFCI (5%, then 4%, over three years) and Rajasthan RIPS at ~1.56% of top line for 10 years, while the listed parent runs at the old tax rate and full capacity; Thermotech Research Laboratory Pvt Ltd was incorporated as a 100% subsidiary with a separate plot, separate building, separate investment and a name 'not linked to KRN' precisely so it can act as an independent AHRI-accredited third-party lab. Two filings point the other way from separation: on 12 January 2026 the parent amended its 15 April 2023 loan agreement (₹100 crore limit, ₹99.94 crore outstanding) to make the loan convertible into KRN HVAC equity at the lender's discretion, and granted Thermotech a ₹10 crore unsecured loan at 12% — deeper consolidation of ownership, not a split. Nobody asked for a separation: no investor on any of the seven calls raised it, lenders appear only via the CRISIL A-/Stable rating and the ₹350 crore QIP allotted 1 June 2026 at ₹1,060 (to ValueQuest, Ashoka WhiteOak, ADIA, Bank of India funds, Subhkam and others), and partners/customers appear only as OEM approvals. The 9 June 2026 promoter sale of 10,00,000 shares (1.52%, Santosh Kumar Yadav and Anju Devi 5,00,000 each, taking the group from 67.22% to 65.69%) is an open-market OFS of shares, not a separation of any business.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea surfaces in any call. The nearest structural events are: 15 May 2025 and 1 August 2025, when Thermotech Research Laboratory is described as deliberately kept 'separate' in identity, plot, building and name so it can serve as an AHRI third-party lab; 6 November 2025, when the inbound Sphere bus-AC Business Transfer Agreement is announced alongside the CRISIL A-/Stable rating and management says both 'have not contributed to the H1 FY26 performance' but 'set the stage for the next leg of growth'; 9 February 2026, when the acquisition cost is refused ('cost of course we cannot disclose… it's not much'), gross margin is said to beat existing products and the ₹1,000 crore-plus Indian bus AC market growing 20–25% is targeted at 15% share; and 15 May 2026, when bus AC has delivered ~₹10 crore in FY26 against a ₹150 crore presentation figure, with 12 January 2026 and 1 June 2026 filings adding loan-to-equity convertibility in KRN HVAC and the ₹350 crore QIP.

points.point: The only going-concern business transfer disclosed is an acquisition into the subsidiary, not a separation out of KRN: KRN HVAC signing a BTA for Sphere Refrigeration's bus AC division, presented as expanding into automotive HVAC.
points.quote: Our subsidiary, KRN HVAC Products Private Limited has signed a business transfer agreement to acquire the best air-conditioning division of spare refrigeration systems Private Limited.

points.point: There is no scheme of arrangement in the filings; the 6 February 2026 results note records the same transaction as an inbound going-concern transfer dated 6 October 2025.
points.quote: During the quarter, the Company's wholly owned subsidiary (KRN HVAC) entered Into a Business Transfer Agreement on 6th October, 2025 with a private company (Sphere Refrigeration Systems Private Limited) for transfer of certain identified business/assets on a going-concern basis.

points.point: The separation described is the seller's, not KRN's: Sphere's three founders sold Sphere Thermal to a buyer seeking railway HVAC credentials, then moved the bus AC business back into Sphere Refrigeration, which KRN bought.
points.quote: And then they promoted three, they buy back bus air conditioning from their old company to this spare refrigeration.

points.point: Management sized the two Sphere entities — the bigger one (₹40–50 crore) already sold away six months earlier, the acquired one only ₹2–3 crore of top line — in a ₹1,000 crore-plus market growing 20–25%.
points.quote: So main business they do in Sphere Thermal but they already like had some agreement with some other guy and they already sold that company before six months with like aligned with us.

points.point: The acquisition rationale was technology, know-how, people and Pan-India service capability without large investment — backward integration already in-house — not divestment or focus-sharpening.
points.quote: So, we have new facility, but we don't have technology that time and know-how. So, that's why we acquired this company.

points.point: The one business KRN deliberately held apart is the testing lab, kept as a separate entity, plot, building and brand so its certificates carry third-party (AHRI) credibility with OEM customers.
points.quote: So, there is a separate plot number, separate building and we invest in separately and even name is also not linked to KRN.

points.point: The parent/subsidiary split exists to park new capacity where the fiscal benefits sit — 15% tax in KRN HVAC, the ₹141.72 crore PLI and RIPS — while the listed entity stays at the old rate and full utilisation.
points.quote: So, HVAC have new tax rate and Heat has old tax rate. So, now whatever growth will come is from new facility only.

points.point: The 12 January 2026 filing moves toward tighter consolidation, not separation: the ₹100 crore parent loan to KRN HVAC (₹99.94 crore outstanding) became convertible into the subsidiary's equity at the parent's discretion.
points.quote: The Lender shall have the right, but not the obligation, at its sole discretion, to convert the whole or any part of the outstanding unsecured loan(s), together with accrued interest thereon, into fully paid- up equity shares of the Borrower.

points.point: The only ownership 'separation' in the record is a promoter share sale on 9 June 2026, cutting the promoter group from 67.22% to 65.69% — shares, not a business.
points.quote: in respect of transfer of 10,00,000 equity shares, representing 1.52% of the paid-up equity share capital of the Company, pursuant to an sale transaction undertaken on June 9, 2026.

points.point: By FY26 close the acquired bus AC business was being scaled inside the group — ~₹10 crore achieved, 15% market share targeted, full in-house backward integration — with no mention of separating it or anything else.
points.quote: Last year, we achieved around Rs.10 crores from bus AC only. And this year, whatever is the market size, so we are expecting at least 15% market share.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation is discussed, so no expectations are stated for one. For the acquired bus AC business they expect gross margin above 20% and better than existing products, 15% of a ₹1,000 crore-plus market, and ₹150–160 crore revenue. For KRN HVAC they expect 15% tax, ₹141.72 crore PLI, RIPS 1.56% for 10 years, solar savings and 1–2% PAT improvement. Thermotech's separateness is expected to deliver credible AHRI third-party certification.
verdict.gaps: Everything: no separation, demerger or scheme is mentioned, so no rationale, structure, record date, entity split, valuation or requester exists in these texts. Sphere acquisition price also undisclosed.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is KOEL's entire B2C arm — the Water Management Solutions (pumps/pumpsets) domestic and export business carved out of the standalone company and transferred by slump sale, as a going concern, to its wholly owned subsidiary La-Gajjar Machineries Private Limited (LGM), which was then renamed KOEL Fluid Dynamics Private Limited; net assets of ₹188.88 crore moved at carrying value against issue of 10,65,150 LGM equity shares of ₹10 each on private placement, board-approved 10 October 2025 and effective 11 October 2025, with B2C thereafter shown as discontinued operations in the standalone accounts (H1 FY26 discontinued revenue ₹318.07 crore, PBT ₹27.49 crore; FY26 ₹318.07 crore and PBT ₹26.09 crore) and no impact at all on consolidated results. Management's stated reason was structural focus and efficiency, not value unlocking: KOEL standalone (₹5,604 crore FY26 net sales, 25% growth) was running two fundamentally different customer models under one roof, and B2C sat as a near-duplicate of LGM, so Gauri Kirloskar said the objective was 'dedicated focus on each segment' through 'structures best suited to their respective customer needs,' and that two 'essentially very similar businesses' were consolidated so they could be driven 'more effectively.' The problems it was said to solve were duplicated pump operations across KOEL and LGM, sub-scale B2C profitability (LGM did ₹350 crore sales at just 1.4% EBITDA for 9M FY25; the segment had posted a ₹4 crore PBIT loss in Q3 FY25 before turning to ₹18 crore PBIT in Q3 FY26), dilution of the standalone B2B margin (Rahul Sahai: 'a slight improvement in the EBITDA margin with this move'), and the need for a clean pumping-solutions entity ('focused growth in the segment while unlocking synergies across LGM operations'). It followed a sequence of portfolio cleaning rather than a one-off: the Sanand mega-plant consolidation of five Ahmedabad units (~₹140 crore capex), the June 2025 slump-sale exit of LGM's cables/wires/pipes business 'Optiqua' to Vira Logistics for ₹10.70 crore (gain ₹4.25 crore) to 'free up capital for redeployment into higher growth areas,' and the April 2025 regrouping of Farm Mechanisation out of B2C into B2B industrial for 'operational synergy.' Gauri also tied the restructuring to entering non-internal-combustion technologies, calling it 'one such step' with 'further developments in the coming quarters.' No investor, lender or partner was said to have demanded the B2C carve-out — the live external pressure was on the other, still-unseparated business, Arka Fincap (FY26 AUM ₹7,947 crore, PAT ₹69 crore), where Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers said the ~₹1,100 crore of injected capital earned 'barely 3%-4%' ROE and 'clouds the picture on a consolidated business basis,' and Jeetu Panjabi asked outright whether the two entities could be separated; management answered only that Arka should 'stand on its own two feet' and that a spin-off was 'not off the table.' A further carve-out followed on the B2B side: Kirloskar Advanced Systems Private Limited (incorporated 30 March 2026) for defence/railway systems-integration and defence contracting work that is 'slightly different from our core engines business,' plus a Netherlands entity to 'structure ourselves efficiently' for the international build-out.
verdict.evolution: The separation theme surfaced first on Arka, not pumps: on 8 Aug 2024 Jeetu Panjabi asked about a 'spinoff' of the ₹5,768 crore-AUM NBFC and Gauri called it a timing issue that was 'not off the table,' and at the 16 May 2025 investor meet the Arka 1.0/2.0 pivot, the '333' targets and a January capital raise were laid out with the intent that it 'stand on its own.' By 7 Aug 2025 the portfolio clean-up had become concrete — Optiqua divested, Farm Mechanisation moved from B2C to B2B — while Bharat Shah pressed on Arka's strategic fit and returns. The B2C carve-out itself appeared on 12 Nov 2025 as a board decision of 10 October 2025 (slump sale to LGM, renamed Fluid Dynamics), was reported as completed and reflected in restructured standalone numbers on 12 Feb 2026 alongside the new Kirloskar Advanced Systems entity, and by 14 May 2026 Fluid Dynamics was being discussed as a consolidated entity in its first full quarter (6% domestic, 36% international FY26 growth) with Netherlands and defence entities added.

points.point: The earliest separation question in the window was about Arka Fincap's ₹5,768 crore AUM balance sheet, with an investor explicitly using the word spin-off; Gauri Kirloskar neither confirmed nor ruled it out, framing it as a question of timing and external circumstances.
points.quote: And would there be some kind of -- I don't know how to say, spinoff or whatever activity over there that we had talked about earlier?

points.point: Management's answer set the template it would repeat for two years: the financial services business should eventually be self-standing, but no structure or date would be given until plans were firm.
points.quote: So what I say is, it's not off the table, but when there is the adequate update, it's only then that I can give it to you.

points.point: At the year-end investor meet an analyst asked directly whether KOEL and Arka could be separated; Gauri answered with intent rather than mechanism, after Arka's MD Samrat Gupta said a private-equity capital raise would be approached 'somewhere around January' once the retail book reached ~₹1,000 crore against 20% Tier 1 capital.
points.quote: So over the long term, of course, the intent is that the business should stand on its own.

points.point: The same meeting established the capital-allocation logic later used to justify the B2C restructuring: ₹520 crore invested in FY25 of which ₹140 crore went into consolidating five Ahmedabad pump plants into one Sanand mega-site, plus ₹200 crore earmarked for acquisitions along the technology tracks.
points.quote: As I mentioned that we have done the plant consolidation work there, wherein the 5 plants in Ahmedabad location got converted into 1 mega site consolidation.

points.point: The first completed separation was a sale, not an internal transfer: LGM's cables and pipes business Optiqua was divested, which management framed as a core-versus-non-core decision and a source of redeployable capital.
points.quote: This moves free up capital for redeployment into higher growth areas aligned with our core strategy.

points.point: In the same quarter Farm Mechanisation was regrouped out of B2C into the B2B industrial segment, on the stated ground of operational synergy with the existing agri product line — the same focus-and-synergy argument later used for the whole B2C carve-out.
points.quote: Now in the B2B, basically the industrial business, we already had an agri segment and we saw a lot of operational synergy with the industrial business within B2B.

points.point: Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers pressed repeatedly on Arka's strategic fit, citing ~₹1,100 crore of group capital for ~₹10 crore quarterly profit on a ₹7,200 crore book, i.e. 3%-4% ROE, and argued the NBFC obscures the operating business in consolidated numbers.
points.quote: And it actually clouds the picture on a consolidated business basis of the real business performance.

points.point: Gauri declined to explain Arka's strategic fit further but restated the end-state — self-sufficiency and core-business-level returns on invested capital — with group support until then; Umakant Sharma's question on a timeline for 'strategic action' was answered as premature.
points.quote: But when we look at it, we would want the business to stand on its own two feet in a certain period of time, but we will support the business as it does that.

points.point: The B2C separation was announced: the board approved transferring KOEL standalone's entire B2C (pumps/Water Management Solutions) business by slump sale as a going concern into wholly owned subsidiary LGM, effective in reporting from Q3 FY26, with B2C renamed Fluid Dynamics.
points.quote: The Board approved the transfer of B2C business within KOEL stand-alone by way of slump sale as a growing concern to its wholly owned subsidiary, LGM.

points.point: The stated rationale was segment focus and structural efficiency — matching each business to the structure its customer type needs — rather than any valuation, funding or partner requirement.
points.quote: The key objective is to maintain dedicated focus on each segment and drive greater efficiency through structures best suited to their respective customer needs.

points.point: Asked by Sourabh Arya whether this was substance or nomenclature, Gauri gave the operational reason: KOEL's in-house B2C and LGM were near-duplicate pump businesses that needed to be run as one.
points.quote: So, the reason we have done this restructuring is for efficiencies in the business, because it was essentially very similar businesses.

points.point: Rahul Sahai added that the efficiency sought was both growth and margin, not just tidier reporting — the only forward-looking benefit quantified anywhere was later described as a 'slight' standalone margin gain.
points.quote: So, efficiency, see the idea is to improve our performance, both in terms of business growth as well as our margin.

points.point: Gauri linked the carve-out to the strategic shift beyond internal combustion engines and signalled more restructuring steps to come, which the later Kirloskar Advanced Systems and Netherlands entities delivered.
points.quote: The recent restructuring of our B2C business is one such step, and we expect to share further developments in the coming quarters.

points.point: On completion, management described the benefit as two-sided: sharper focus for the pumps business itself plus synergies realised inside LGM's existing operations.
points.quote: Strategically, this integration of Fluid Dynamics business marks a milestone, enabling focused growth in the segment while unlocking synergies across LGM operations.

points.point: The transfer materially reshaped the reported standalone entity — Q3 FY26 standalone sales of ₹1,371 crore (35% growth) versus ₹1,503 crore on a like-for-like pre-restructuring basis (30% growth) — leaving KOEL standalone as a pure B2B company.
points.quote: For ease of comparison, top line without the restructuring effect on like-for-like basis would be at INR1,503 crores for Q3 FY '26 versus INR1,154 crores for Q3 FY '25.

points.point: Asked by Harsh Shah of Axis Capital whether removing B2C lifts standalone margins, Rahul Sahai confirmed a modest improvement — the only margin effect management put on record for the separation.
points.quote: So we will see a slight improvement in the EBITDA margin with this move from B2C business to LGM.

points.point: The resulting entity was defined by product focus — KOEL Fluid Dynamics as a pumping-solutions subsidiary covering water, domestic and agri pumps — with Water Management Systems and LGM now reported as one business.
points.quote: It is going to be a subsidiary of Kirloskar Oil Engines focused on pumping solutions.

points.point: A second, B2B-side carve-out was explained in the same call: defence and railway systems-integration and defence contracting work was judged different enough from the core engines business to warrant its own entity, Kirloskar Advanced Systems.
points.quote: We felt it best to carve that work into a separate business entity, and that entity is called Kirloskar Advanced Systems Limited.

points.point: The Advanced Systems rationale was restated as a focus argument layered on existing engineering capability, aimed at key defence accounts and systems integration beyond engines.
points.quote: This requires focussed effort which is the rationale behind this new entity.

points.point: Fluid Dynamics' first full quarter as a consolidated entity delivered 10% domestic and 13% international growth in Q4 and 6% domestic and 36% international for FY26 — growth Gauri called only 'reasonable,' with significant headroom still open.
points.quote: As this is the first full quarter for the consolidated entity, we saw reasonable growth with exports outperforming.

points.point: The new Netherlands subsidiary was justified on the same structural-efficiency logic as the B2C transfer, tied to international being a major component of the $2 billion FY30 goal (international group sales up 37%, gross international crossing ₹1,000 crore).
points.quote: So, given international is a very big component of our five-year goal, it's just important for us to structure ourselves efficiently as we're growing to create value for our stakeholders.

points.point: The mechanics: B2C (Water Management Solutions, domestic and exports) moved to KOEL Fluid Dynamics Private Limited (formerly La-Gajjar Machineries) effective 11 October 2025, paid for in shares of the subsidiary rather than cash.
points.quote: The consideration was in the form of issuance and allotment of 10,65,150 equity shares of KFD having face value of ₹ 10/-each to the Company, on a Private placement basis, on terms as set out in the Business Transfer Agreement.

points.point: The transfer was at book value — net assets of ₹188.88 crore added to the carrying value of the subsidiary investment — so no gain, revaluation or cash consideration arose.
points.quote: Accordingly, the net assets of ₹ 188.88 Crores was transferred on a slump sale basis at their carrying values, and the consideration was accounted for at such carrying values of net assets as an addition to the Company's investment in the subsidiary, consistent with the Company's accounting policy.

points.point: Because the transferee is wholly owned, the carve-out is a reporting and management-structure change only: B2C becomes discontinued operations in the standalone accounts (H1 FY26 revenue ₹318.07 crore, PBT ₹27.49 crore, PAT ₹20.57 crore) while group numbers are untouched.
points.quote: Since the transaction was with the wholly owned subsidiary company , there is no impact on the consolidated financial results.

points.point: The non-core exit inside the same subsidiary was a genuine third-party sale: LGM's cables, wires and pipes business (Optiqua) went to Vira Logistics on 30 June 2025, producing a ₹4.25 crore gain and ₹7.92 crore of investing cash inflow.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these three transcripts or the single filing describes MOIL separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving off any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no record date, no resulting-company structure, no swap ratio, and no mention of investors, lenders or partners asking for a separation. Across all three Investors' and Analysts' Meets (Nov 2023, Aug 2024, Mar 2026) management consistently frames MOIL as one integrated manganese miner that it intends to grow, not divide: 10 mines (7 underground, 3 opencast) in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, ~50-52% of Indian manganese ore production, plus two small downstream units — the 12,000 tpa ferromanganese plant at Balaghat and the 1,500 tpa EMD plant at Dongri Buzurg — which are described as segments to be grown, not detached. In Mar 2026, Director Finance Rakesh Tumane explicitly minimises the ferroalloy unit rather than proposing to separate it: capacity 12,000 tons per year, "it's not going to have any impact" and "not something impactful thing here." The only corporate-structure actions discussed are additive and outward: proposed joint ventures (GMDC in Gujarat at 51% MOIL / 49% GMDC on a 9.5 million-ton resource, MP State Mining Corporation for Bhudkum and Selva blocks, CMDC for 218 sq km in Nilkanthpur/Balrampur, Chhattisgarh), DIPAM and NITI Aayog approvals for JV formation, INR275 crore earmarked for overseas acquisition within a INR600 crore FY26 capex target, and a possible third-party beneficiation plant near the mines if MOIL can commit ~3 lakh tons per annum of low-grade ore. The lone filing provided (28.05.2026) is unrelated to any restructuring: it is a request to waive an NSE fine of Rs 5,31,000 for non-compliance with Regulation 17(1) of SEBI LODR because the Ministry of Steel / President of India has not appointed enough Independent Directors. On these texts alone, the premise of a separation cannot be supported, so no rationale, no cited numbers justifying a split, and no requesting stakeholder can be reconstructed.
verdict.evolution: Nov 2023 (17.11.2023): only JV/MoU expansion is raised — GMDC (9.5 mt resource, proposed 51:49), MPSMC, CMDC — alongside buybacks, dividends and capex of INR245-295 crore; no separation. Aug 2024 (23.08.2024): the same JV path advances ("nearing the signing of joint venture with GMDC"), plus EC expansion from 24.88 lakh to 50 lakh tons and the 3.5 million-ton-by-2030 goal; still no separation. Mar 2026 (17.03.2026): DIPAM/NITI Aayog approvals for the GMDC and MP JVCs, a possible third-party beneficiation tie-up and INR275 crore for overseas assets — all additions to MOIL, never a carve-out of an existing business. The 28.05.2026 filing concerns only board-composition non-compliance and an NSE penalty waiver.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is not a diagnostics or genomics unit at all — it is the company's External Quality Assessment Services (EQAS) Division, the proficiency-testing/quality-assessment arm, which Metropolis Healthcare Ltd. transferred to Metropolis Quality Solutions Private Limited (MQSPL), a subsidiary incorporated on September 15, 2025 and described as being in the 'Healthcare Technology' business, versus the parent's 'Diagnostic services'. The only rationale management ever put on the record is in the Feb 4, 2026 board filing: the slump sale 'enables the EQAS Division to operate as a separate and independent unit, focusing on its core services, with dedicated management and resources to drive efficiency, excellence, and growth potential' — i.e. a focus-and-dedicated-management argument, not a capital, debt or valuation argument. The scale explains why it never reached the earnings calls: EQAS contributed INR 84.4 lakh of revenue in FY2024-25, just 0.07% of standalone revenue (company turnover INR 1,216.54 crore), and had a net worth of about INR 2 lakh, 0.002% of the Company's net worth. It was structured deliberately as a slump sale outside any Scheme of Arrangement (Regulation 37A held not applicable), as a related-party transaction with a wholly owned subsidiary at arm's length, with consideration of up to INR 1.25 crore subject to closing adjustments, dischargeable in cash and/or MQSPL equity; on completion, effective August 27, 2026, it was settled entirely by issuance of MQSPL equity shares to the Company, so no cash left the group and 'there will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company'. The second, and arguably real, purpose surfaced on August 20, 2026, when MQSPL's board approved issuing 10,000 OCRPS of INR 10 each (INR 1,00,000 in total, at par) to Dr. Puneet Kumar Nigam, the Company's former Chief Quality Officer, who is not a promoter — conversion 1:1, in tranches, over a timeline 'expected to be up to 6 years' — after which MQSPL 'will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company but will continue to remain a subsidiary'. So the sequence reads as carving out a sub-crore quality-services unit into a technology vehicle in which the ex-quality head can earn an equity stake and run it with dedicated management, while Metropolis retains control and consolidation. No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere as having asked for it; the ask, as disclosed, is management's own, and the mechanism (OCRPS at par to a named former KMP) points to an incentive/founder-style structure rather than a divestment. Nothing in the three years of transcripts frames this as solving a problem with the core business — on the contrary, the calls describe Metropolis consolidating businesses in (four acquisitions, lab and vendor consolidation), not out.
verdict.evolution: Across all six transcripts in the window (Feb 5, 2025; May 14, 2025; Aug 8, 2025; Nov 6, 2025; Feb 5, 2026; May 14, 2026) EQAS, MQSPL and the separation are never mentioned once — management's narrative is entirely inorganic growth (Core Diagnostics, Scientific Pathology Agra, DAPIC Dehradun, Ambika Kolhapur), genomics, margin expansion and network productivity. The idea surfaces only in filings: the Board approved the Business Transfer Agreement on February 4, 2026 — one day before the Q3 FY26 call of February 5, 2026, where Ameera Shah announced the 3:1 bonus issue from the same board meeting but said nothing about selling the EQAS Division. It then widened from an internal reorganisation to a partial deconsolidation: the August 20, 2026 filing disclosed OCRPS to former Chief Quality Officer Dr. Puneet Kumar Nigam that will end MQSPL's wholly-owned status over up to six years, and the August 27, 2026 filing confirmed completion with consideration of INR 1.25 crore discharged in MQSPL equity shares, referring also to an intimation dated August 04, 2026 that is not among the documents provided. By the May 14, 2026 call — a full strategy reset with a three-year 14–15% growth and 27–28% EBITDA vision — the transfer had been board-approved for three months and still went unmentioned.

points.point: The Feb 4, 2026 board filing gives the only stated rationale for the separation: letting EQAS run as an independent unit with its own management and resources.
points.quote: The slump sale enables the EQAS Division to operate as a separate and independent unit, focusing on its core services, with dedicated management and resources to drive efficiency, excellence, and growth potential.

points.quote: The Company is engaged in the business of providing Diagnostic services and MQSPL is engaged in the business of Healthcare Technology.

points.point: It was deliberately done as a slump sale to a wholly owned subsidiary outside a Scheme of Arrangement, as an arm's-length related-party transaction, with no effect on the listed entity's shareholding.
points.quote: There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the slump sale of the EQAS Division.

points.point: Completion on August 27, 2026 was paid for in MQSPL's own equity, so no cash moved out of the group.

points.point: The August 20, 2026 filing reveals the downstream step: 10,000 OCRPS at INR 10 par (INR 1,00,000 total) to the Company's former Chief Quality Officer, a non-promoter, converting 1:1 in tranches over up to six years.
points.quote: Dr. Puneet Kumar Nigam, former Chief Quality Officer of the Company, is the proposed allottee. He does not belong to the Promoter or Promoter Group of the Company.

points.point: That issuance ends wholly-owned status while preserving control and consolidation — the structural end-state of the separation.
points.quote: Upon successful subscription to and subsequent conversion of these OCRPS into equity shares, MQSPL will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company but will continue to remain a subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: On the call held one day after the board approved the EQAS transfer, management disclosed the bonus issue from that same meeting but made no mention of the business separation.
points.quote: Lastly, the company is pleased to inform its shareholders that the Board of Directors has approved the issue of bonus shares in the ratio of 3:1, that is 3 fully paid-up equity shares of face value of INR 2 each for every 1 existing equity share, subject to the necessary statutory and shareholder approvals.

points.point: The FY26 wrap-up and three-year strategic plan is framed entirely around consolidating acquisitions in and raising group margins, with no reference to carving anything out.
points.quote: We are going to reimagine our processes through automation and technology enablement to drive center productivity and margin expansion with the goal of achieving a sustainable group EBITDA margin of 27% to 28% over the next 3 years, supported by profitability across every regional market and bringing core to a 20% plus margin profile.

points.point: While MQSPL was already incorporated (Sept 15, 2025), management's stated direction was organic scaling and integration, explicitly ruling out further portfolio action for 6–9 months.
points.quote: Importantly, we are not planning any new acquisitions over the next 6, 9 months as we believe the immediate opportunity lies in organically scaling the business and strengthening key strategic drivers already in motion.

verdict.what_management_expects: Only one expectation is stated, and only in filings: EQAS, as a separate independent unit under MQSPL with dedicated management and resources, should gain efficiency, excellence and growth potential. For Metropolis itself, nothing is claimed — no margin, capital, valuation or focus benefit is quantified; consideration (INR 1.25 crore) is paid in MQSPL shares, shareholding is unchanged, and MQSPL stays a consolidated subsidiary even after the OCRPS convert.
verdict.gaps: Never discussed on any earnings call. No valuation basis for INR 1.25 crore vs ~INR 2 lakh net worth, no EQAS growth/margin targets, no stated reason for granting the ex-CQO equity, and no OCRPS tranche conditions.

verdict.rationale: These documents do not describe NIACL separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving down any business, and no scheme of arrangement is included — the only separation event in the texts is a financial stake sale. In the 09-Sep-2026 Regulation 30 filing, NIACL disclosed that it 'proposes to divest 1,05,00,000 equity shares of the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSEIL)', representing 29.83% of the total shares it then held in NSEIL, to be executed as an Offer for Sale through NSE's IPO, subject to regulatory approvals. The filing's own annexure forecloses the 'business separation' reading: it answers 'No' to whether the disposal is outside a Scheme of Arrangement (Reg 37A), 'No' to related-party status, and marks slump-sale disclosures 'Not Applicable'; the only financial magnitude disclosed is the FY2025-26 dividend from NSEIL of Rs 123,20,00,000, i.e. an investment-income metric, not a divisional P&L. Mechanically, the shares were already moved to an Escrow Account on 08 September 2026, completion was expected 'End of September 2026 (As indicated by NSE)', and consideration was to be received only after the OFS concluded — the pattern of a selling shareholder in an IPO, not of a demerger with share entitlement ratios, record dates or a resulting entity. The only call-level trace is the Feb-2026 Q&A, where an analyst noted 'one of your portfolio companies wherein you have a significant holding has just gotten SEBI approval for IPO' and asked about participation; management gave no rationale, replying 'That is in the future, so we will look into it when it comes up.' The nearest thing management did explain at length is not a separation but portfolio exits — walking away from loss-making group mediclaim accounts ('more than nine hundred such accounts we have left in the last year'), roughly Rs 800 crore of business foregone in FY23 and Rs 500 crore in FY24 on price correction, and exits from loss-making motor dealer/CV accounts — all framed as 'growth with profitability' and risk-weighted underwriting, with capital staying inside the same legal entity. Separately, the texts give a plausible monetisation motive for selling holdings generally: of Rs 4,236 crore of profit on sale booked up to Q3FY26, 'Rs. 2,000 crore is pertaining specifically to the wage revision provision', with management stating they 'monetized our investments to help in the provision that we made for the wage revision' (total wage revision ~Rs 2,500 crore, plus Rs 700-800 crore of family pension still to be provided) — but management never linked that motive to the NSEIL sale. No investor, lender or partner is recorded in these texts as having asked for any separation.
verdict.evolution: Nothing resembling a separation appears in the Feb-2024, May-2024, Aug-2024, Nov-2024, Jan-2025, May-2025 or Aug-2025 calls; in Jan-2025 management in fact ruled out structural expansion, saying under a composite licence they have no plans to enter life insurance, and in Nov-2024 said any government-stake dilution awaits Finance Ministry/DFS instructions. The idea first surfaces only obliquely on the Feb-2026 call (02-Feb-2026), as an analyst's question about a portfolio company that had just received SEBI IPO approval, which management declined to address. It crystallises only in the 09-Sep-2026 filing, which converts it into a concrete 1,05,00,000-share (29.83% of holding) Offer for Sale in NSEIL's IPO, with shares already in escrow as of 08-Sep-2026 and completion expected end-September 2026. So the plan did not evolve as a separation thesis at all — it went from an unanswered analyst question to an executed investment divestment, with no stated rationale in between.

points.point: The only 'separation' in the record is a minority stake sale: 1,05,00,000 NSEIL shares, equal to 29.83% of NIACL's holding, tendered into NSE's IPO as an Offer for Sale, subject to regulatory approvals.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these texts describes NCC separating, demerging or spinning off any business — the only corporate action on record is the opposite: an amalgamation that absorbs a wholly owned subsidiary into the listed parent. Under the Scheme of Arrangement approved by NCLT Hyderabad on 30 January 2026 (board approval 6 August 2024, appointed date 1 April 2024, effective date fixed by the board as 28 February 2026), NCC Infrastructure Holdings Limited (NCCIHL) merges into NCC Limited and 'shall stand dissolved without being wound up'. The stated reasons are structural, not operational: consolidation of businesses under one roof, a simplified corporate structure with direct control of NCCIHL's assets, fewer legal entities and less managerial overlap, optimum use of resources, reduced duplication of systems and processes, and 'enhanced shareholder value'. The economics are small: NCCIHL — originally set up to hold infrastructure SPVs and once RBI-registered as an NBFC (CoR N-09.00419, cancelled 4 March 2022) — earned income from operations of only ₹48 lakh with a net loss of ₹33.54 crore in FY24 and ₹1.65 crore in FY25, carried forward ₹58.63 crore of tax losses, had already impaired ₹62.05 crore of investments (₹33.51 crore equity in Pondicherry Tindivanam Tollway plus ₹28.49 crore of Ind AS fair-valued loan, and ₹0.05 crore in Samashti Gas Energy), and had one unsecured creditor owed ₹45 crore. Because NCCIHL is wholly owned, no shares are issued and its ₹709.49 crore paid-up capital held by NCC is cancelled; NCC's authorised capital is clubbed up by ₹750 crore to ₹911.50 crore. Nobody external demanded it: the sole unsecured creditor and the seven NCCIHL shareholders gave individual consents, the RBI gave a 'no objection' on 11 September 2024 because it still monitored the entity, and no stock-exchange NOC was needed under Regulation 37(6) of SEBI LODR since it is a wholly owned subsidiary merging into its holding company.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaces only at the margins of the calls. On the 16 May 2025 call an analyst (Ankita Shah) referred in passing to 'emerging [merging] NCC Infra with the parent' while asking about rising subsidiary exposure, and management answered about the Oman impairment and smart-meter equity instead, never addressing the merger. By the 6 February 2026 call the scheme was through: the CFO volunteered that 'NCCIHL merger has been approved' to explain why investments in subsidiaries fell to ₹896 crore and loans to group companies to ₹233 crore, and quantified a ₹270–330 crore balance-sheet reduction against the ₹558 crore carrying value, with no debt or P&L impact. By the 16 May 2026 Q4 call and results the merger appears only as restated comparatives under Appendix C to Ind AS 103 (pooling of interests, effective 1 April 2024), and management discussed no separation of any kind.

points.point: The transaction is an amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary NCC Infrastructure Holdings Limited into NCC Limited, not a separation; the stated aim is consolidation and a simpler structure with direct control of the subsidiary's assets.
points.quote: enable consolidation of businesses under one roof and will result in a simplified corporate structure and direct control of assets of the Transferor Company in the hands of the Transferee Company.

points.point: A second stated reason is cutting entity count and managerial duplication across the group.
points.quote: reduce the number of legal entities in the group thereby reducing managerial overlaps, which are necessarily involved in running multiple entities would channelize synergies.

points.point: No consideration is paid and no shares are issued, because NCCIHL is 100% owned; its entire paid-up capital of ₹709.48 crore held by NCC is cancelled, and NCC's authorised capital is clubbed up by ₹750 crore to ₹911.50 crore.
points.quote: Since the Transferor Company, being a wholly owned subsidiary of the Transferee Company, is being amalgamated with the Transferee Company, there would be no issue of shares pursuant to the amalgamation.

points.point: The subsidiary ceases to exist on the effective date (fixed by the board as 28 February 2026, after the NCLT order of 30 January 2026).
points.quote: With effect from the Effective Date, the Transferor Company shall stand dissolved without being wound up.

points.point: NCCIHL was a near-dormant holding vehicle: ₹48 lakh of operating income with a ₹33.54 crore net loss in FY24 and a ₹1.65 crore loss in FY25, against NCC's ₹19,205 crore standalone revenue and ₹761 crore profit in FY25.
points.quote: It is submitted that the Transferor Company was originally incorporated for setting up infrastructure projects through special purpose entities and investing in the said entities by way of equity/debt participation and providing project management consultancy services to such infrastructure projects and has recorded an income from operations of Rs.48 lakhs with a net loss after tax of Rs.33.54 crore for the year ended 31st March, 2024

points.point: The only external party that had to be asked was the RBI, which still monitored NCCIHL after cancelling its NBFC registration in March 2022; it gave a no-objection on 11 September 2024. No exchange NOC was needed under Regulation 37(6) of SEBI LODR.
points.quote: Since RBI continues to monitor the Transferor Company, it had sought the approval of the RBI for the proposed Scheme vide an application dated 9th August, 2024 pursuant to which the RBI accorded its 'no objection to the proposed merger of the Transferor Company with the Transferee Company vide its letter dated 11th September, 2024.

points.point: The first and only pre-approval mention on a call came from an analyst asking why subsidiary exposure had risen; management replied about the Oman impairment and smart-meter equity and never explained the merger.
points.quote: We're looking at emerging NCC Infra with the parent. What are we trying to do in the subsidiaries?

points.point: Management first disclosed the approval only as the explanation for investments in subsidiaries dropping to ₹896 crore and loans to group companies to ₹233 crore at 31 December 2025 (from ₹1,191 crore and ₹179 crore at September).
points.quote: Yes. It has come down. I think you are aware that NCCIHL merger has been approved, and we have consolidated those numbers into our accounts now.

points.point: Asked for the material impact, the CFO quantified it as a ₹270–330 crore write-down in the consolidated balance sheet against a ₹558 crore carrying value of the investment, with no effect on debt or P&L.
points.quote: When we started merging those NCCIHL into my console, there is a reduction of INR 270 crores or INR 330 crores in the overall balance sheet, that is what we have written after merger.

points.point: Management explicitly ruled out any leverage effect from the merger, and said the profit and loss account was untouched.
points.quote: There is no impact on the debt levels of the stand-alone because of the merger.

points.point: By the Q4 FY26 results the merger shows up only as a restatement of comparatives from 1 April 2024 under pooling-of-interests accounting; it was not discussed on the call at all, where management instead withheld FY27 guidance.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme of Amalgamation approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Hyderabad, vide order dated January 30, 2026, NCC Infrastructure Holdings Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary) has merged with the Company, with effect from April 1, 2024 as required by Appendix C to Ind AS 103 on Business Combinations.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation is expected, since none is planned. For the merged NCC: a simpler group with fewer entities, direct ownership of NCCIHL's assets, focused leadership, less duplication of systems and overheads, better resource use, higher long-term returns and financial flexibility, and enhanced shareholder value. Quantified effects: ₹270–330 crore consolidated balance-sheet reduction, no debt or P&L impact.
verdict.gaps: The calls never explain the merger's rationale, timing, NCCIHL's residual assets (OB Infrastructure, PTTPL), its ₹58.63 crore tax losses, or any separation — none was announced.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe Orkla India separating, demerging or spinning off any business — on the evidence here the company is moving the other way, having merged Eastern with MTR Foods into a single listed entity (Feb 2026: 'Post-the merger of Eastern with MTR Foods and the creation of Orkla India'), merged the two export books into one international business of ~21% of sales across 45 countries, and named M&A a 'major priority' for acquiring, not divesting. The only 'separation' management discusses is operational and internal: a re-architecting of brand Eastern's legacy direct-to-retail distribution system in Kerala, which Orkla left untouched from the 2021 acquisition until FY26. Management says Eastern runs on 'one system for all' with a 200-SKU range, and that this legacy route-to-market has 'sub-optimal market coverage, lack of customer focus in tune with the trade evolution', and 'ineffective focus on convenience food'. The fix is to split the channel into separate units — one dedicated to spices, one to convenience foods — plus a dedicated standalone modern-trade structure, further digitisation of the retailing framework and better trade-marketing effectiveness. The stated problems it solves: Eastern is 'very heavily indexed on spices and more so pure spices' and carries lower EBITDA margin than MTR, so convenience food needs its own feet-on-street; and numeric reach in Kerala is only 70% despite being 2x the nearest competitor, so coverage can still be extended. The cited cost is real: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6.2% versus 7.8% excluding Kerala, domestic growth 6.5% versus 8.9% ex-Kerala, spices 6.1% versus 11.1% ex-Kerala (6.5% volume), and Kerala category share fell 50bps MAT March '26 (Kerala also hit by a HoReCa LPG crisis). No investor, lender or partner is said to have asked for it; the nearest external push is Ravi Purohit (May 2026) pressing on why Orkla earns ~16% EBITDA versus MDH/Everest at 20-25%, to which management tied Eastern's margin catch-up to this restructuring and the convenience-food shift.
verdict.evolution: Nov 13, 2025 (first post-listing call): disclosed as a modest efficiency project — Eastern's direct-to-retail Kerala model untouched since acquisition, now to be improved via three changes, the first being splitting the 200-SKU channel into separate spices and convenience-food units. Feb 11, 2026: the project is not mentioned at all; the call instead covers deflation, GST 2.0, MTR Prakriti and M&A ambitions. May 19, 2026: it reappears much larger and renamed an 'internal sales restructuring project'/'re-architecting' of the distribution model, kicked off early in Q4 FY26, now with three phases (one done, second by end-May, third over two more quarters), a dedicated modern-trade structure added, and quantified Kerala damage plus completion by Jan 1, 2027. The July 25, 2026 filing is only the AGM notice (ESOP/MSOP ratification) and contains no scheme of arrangement.

points.point: First disclosure: Eastern's Kerala distribution is a non-standard direct-to-retail system that Orkla deliberately left unchanged since the 2021 acquisition, and is only now being made more efficient.
points.quote: Post acquisition of Eastern, we have not made any changes to this distribution model.

points.point: The only literal 'separation' in these texts — the Eastern sales channel is split into two dedicated units because one force cannot carry a 200-product range across both spices and convenience foods.
points.quote: We have a very large range of 200 products. So, we have split the channel into two separate units. One that will focus only on spices and one that will focus on the convenience foods range.

points.point: Direction of travel is consolidation, not separation: the two companies and two cultures have been merged into one entity, Orkla India, with a single integrated international business.
points.quote: Post-the merger of Eastern with MTR Foods and the creation of Orkla India, this was the first engagement survey that we conducted.

points.point: Asked about portfolio moves, management flags buying businesses in new states, not separating any — and the Kerala restructuring is never mentioned on this call.
points.quote: Yes, so as far as M&A is concerned, I think it's an important strategy for our growth to go beyond our local agenda.

points.point: Re-framed as a structural re-architecting; the diagnosis is that a single undifferentiated distribution system caps what the company can capture by category and channel.
points.quote: Today, our distributions for Eastern operates on a "one system for all" approach, which limits our ability to fully capture the potential across categories and channels.

points.point: A third dedicated structure is added for standalone modern trade, alongside deeper spices coverage and a sharper convenience-food engine.
points.quote: Third, we are creating a dedicated structure for standalone modern trade, enabling us to capture growth more effectively and strengthen our market shares.

points.point: The quantified cost: Kerala dragged Q4 growth to 6.2% (7.8% ex-Kerala), spices to 6.1% (11.1% ex-Kerala, 6.5% volume), domestic to 6.5% (8.9% ex-Kerala), with Kerala share down 50bps; execution is district-by-district in three phases, complete by Jan 1, 2027, with impact for about two more quarters.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is One 97 Communications' (OCL) Offline Merchant Payments business — the device-led acquiring franchise (soundbox, card soundbox/EDC card machines, QR) — which has been carved out of the listed parent and transferred as a going concern, on a slump-sale basis, to Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), OCL's wholly owned subsidiary that holds the online payment-aggregator licence. The stated reason in the Business Transfer Agreement filing is regulatory: "The transfer is being undertaken to take steps to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's Master Directions on Regulation of Payment Aggregators dated September 15, 2025"; the filing additionally characterises it as "an internal restructuring intended to consolidate the related business within a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, in alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and to achieve operational efficiency." Mechanics and numbers: shareholder approval on November 23, 2025, BTA executed November 28, 2025, effective from midnight of November 30, 2025, for a lump-sum cash consideration equal to the book value of the transferred undertaking at the effective date, with approximately INR 960 crore cited as the March 31, 2025 reference book value; Mr. Ripunjai Gaur (COO – Offline Payments) and Mr. Deependra Singh Rathore (CTO – Payments) transferred to PPSL and ceased as OCL Senior Management Personnel. Because it is a parent-to-wholly-owned-subsidiary transfer at book value, the filing stresses "there is no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control, and the entire economic interest in the Transferred Undertaking will continue to vest with the holding company." On the calls, the problem management says this solves is legal-entity fragmentation: online and offline acquiring sat in separate legal entities, so omnichannel merchants "could have not onboarded" — and online merchant onboarding had been paused/under embargo since 2021-22. With licences and entities combined, Vijay Shekhar Sharma says Paytm can "formally" do omni-channel, give a merchant a single dashboard, and layer value-added services — spend analytics, settlement, payout — so "per payment, we make more bps"; he also took over as CEO of PPSL (disclosed on the Jan 30, 2026 call) and called online "literally a new line of business" that will be "materially sizable," carrying platform fees plus EMI and card initiatives and feeding payment processing margin (guided above 4 bps, with net payment margin ~9 bps in Q4 FY26). Who asked for it: the RBI, via the September 15, 2025 Payment Aggregator Master Directions, with OCL shareholders approving the slump sale on November 23, 2025 — no investor, lender or commercial partner demand is cited anywhere in these texts. Critically for a special-situation investor, this is not a demerger to shareholders: there is no scheme of arrangement (the filing marks the Regulation 37A/scheme questions "Not Applicable"), no separate listing and no value-unlock event — the separation is purely intra-group consolidation into the licensed entity.
verdict.evolution: On the July 22, 2025 call there is no mention of any carve-out at all — payments is discussed as one full-stack business ("We own the machine, we own the customer") operating at breakeven. The plan surfaces in the Oct 15 and Nov 24, 2025 disclosures referenced by the BTA filing, and on the November 5, 2025 call Vijay Shekhar Sharma confirms the rationale for the first time — the regulator "made both licenses and one license together," so "now formally, we can do omni-channel," plus new VAS revenue per payment; the BTA is then executed November 28, 2025, effective November 30, 2025. By the January 30, 2026 call the framing has shifted from compliance to offence: VSS discloses he has become CEO of PPSL, says "now we can acquire both in the same entity," and calls online a new, materially sizable line of business paused since 2021. On May 7, 2026 Madhur Deora describes online as a tailwind that "obviously has a full license now" and "a very meaningful double digits" of GMV, and by July 21, 2026 the subject disappears into broad-based growth commentary (GMV +31%, embargo described as past).

points.point: The BTA filing of November 28, 2025 states the sole purpose of transferring the Offline Merchant Payments business to wholly owned subsidiary PPSL is compliance with the RBI's September 15, 2025 Payment Aggregator Master Directions.
points.quote: The transfer is being undertaken to take steps to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's Master Directions on Regulation of Payment Aggregators dated September 15, 2025.

points.point: The company frames it as intra-group consolidation at book value — not a value-unlock demerger — with the related-party/arm's-length answer spelling out the consolidation and efficiency logic.
points.quote: Yes, the transfer is proposed to be carried out at book value, given that it forms part of an internal restructuring intended to consolidate the related business within a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, in alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and to achieve operational efficiency.

points.point: Consideration is lump-sum cash based on book value at the November 30, 2025 effective date; the only number given is the prior-year reference book value of the transferred undertaking.
points.quote: For reference, the book value of the Transferred Undertaking as on March 31, 2025 is approximately INR 960 Crores (Indian Rupees Nine Hundred Sixty Crores).

points.point: Because it is a parent-to-WOS slump sale, OCL argues there is no economic change for shareholders — no scheme of arrangement, no listing, no dilution.
points.quote: As the transaction is between the holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary, there is no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control, and the entire economic interest in the Transferred Undertaking will continue to vest with the holding company.

points.point: Two Senior Management Personnel — Ripunjai Gaur, COO Offline Payments, and Deependra Singh Rathore, CTO Payments — moved with the undertaking and ceased to be OCL SMPs from midnight of November 30, 2025, after shareholder approval on November 23, 2025.
points.quote: Further Mr. Ripunjai Gaur, COO - Offline Payments and Mr. Deependra Singh Rathore, CTO - Payments, both designated as Senior Management Personnel (SMPs) of the Company, will also be transferred to PPSL w.e.f. midnight of November 30, 2025 and upon such transfer they will cease as SMPs of the Company.

points.point: Baseline before the carve-out: payments is presented as a single full-stack, breakeven business with no mention of any entity transfer, and VSS insists Paytm owns both the device and the merchant relationship (the assets that later move to PPSL).
points.quote: We own the machine, we own the customer. We are in that business.

points.point: First call-level rationale, three weeks before the BTA: VSS says the regulator collapsed the two licences into one, which finally lets Paytm serve a merchant omnichannel from one entity with a single dashboard.
points.quote: And now formally, we can do omni-channel. I mean, you can imagine that a single company will be able to see their single dashboard, et cetera, et cetera. So we are very happy about it. The regulator has also made both licenses and one license together.

points.point: Asked directly by Vijit Jain (Citi) whether combining online and offline payment aggregation is what enables omnichannel, VSS names the constraint explicitly — the offline business sitting in a different legal entity blocked onboarding of omnichannel merchants.
points.quote: So all these businesses, we couldn't have onboarded and just because there's an offline entity was a different company, a legal entity could have not onboarded.

points.point: The commercial payoff claimed is incremental bps per payment from value-added services that only a combined entity can sell.
points.quote: Yes, not just this element, but there are other VAS elements like spend analytics, like settlement, like payout. All those things start to show up as new value-add items. So per payment, we make more bps or more money than we will make standalone and offline or standalone and online.

points.point: Management links the restructuring to margin mix: newly onboardable online merchants carry higher MDR and net margin, supporting the payment processing margin improvement reported that quarter.
points.quote: Sachin, another thing that we now have is the privilege of onboarding online merchants. Online merchants eventually are high MDR plus high net margin.

points.point: Post-transfer, VSS discloses he has personally taken over as CEO of PPSL, the entity now holding both online and offline merchant payments.
points.quote: You may have noticed that I've become the CEO of the PPSL company. So online business will start generating more upside in payments and financial services.

points.point: He reframes the carve-out as creating a new revenue line — online acquiring, effectively paused since 2021 — boosted by both the licence permission and the new entity structure, with enterprise sales hiring behind it.
points.quote: I mean, it's an important thing to note that the payment business will get boosted because of permission and the structure that we are doing.

points.point: The single-entity point is stated as the operational unlock: offline and online merchants can now be acquired by the same company.
points.quote: And because we are championing offline, we were championing online. Now we can acquire both in the same entity.

points.point: Management quantifies the attraction of the online leg as platform-fee, EMI and card-led monetisation on top of processing — a materially sizable business after being paused since 2021.
points.quote: In fact, I want to put it on the table that online business has a margin because of platform fees and many other EMI and card initiatives that we do with merchants, leading to more monetization on payments.

points.point: Madhur Deora attributes FY27 revenue acceleration partly to online merchants now operating under a full licence, after a year in which they could not onboard new customers for about half the year.
points.quote: We are seeing strong tailwinds in payments, both in offline merchants as well as online merchants, which obviously has a full license now.

points.point: Sizing the combined franchise: online is a meaningful double-digit share of GMV despite three years of no new onboarding, and the three merchant books (online, large-enterprise offline, SMB) are run with independent growth drivers.
points.quote: We are a very significant player in online merchants, despite the fact that until last year, we were not really adding new customers for more than three years, right?

points.point: A year after the transfer the separation itself is no longer discussed; online is simply one of several accelerating payment businesses, with the prior constraint described in the past tense.
points.quote: As you know, online business was also under embargo. So that is obviously a headwind. Now, the increase in growth has come in all of those businesses, including the consumer side, as you mentioned.

verdict.what_management_expects: One licensed entity for all merchant acquiring: formal omnichannel, a single merchant dashboard, VAS (spend analytics, settlement, payout) and more bps per payment; online — higher-MDR, platform-fee, EMI/card-led — becomes a materially sizable new revenue line lifting payment processing margin past 4 bps. OCL receives book-value cash; no change in beneficial ownership or economic interest.
verdict.gaps: No final consideration, no PPSL standalone financials or online/offline revenue split, no tax, capex or capital-structure impact, no reason for slump sale over demerger, no shareholder value event.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these transcripts and filings, Persistent is NOT separating, demerging, spinning off or carving out any business — the premise cannot be reconstructed from these texts, because every disclosed corporate action runs the opposite way, toward consolidation. The headline event is an acquisition announced on the Aug 2026 call (held Sunday June 28, 2026, transaction announced June 26, 2026): a voluntary public takeover of Nagarro SE (Munich; ~€1bn revenue, ~$1.14bn TTM, 18,500 professionals, 13.9% EBITDA, 10.9% CY25 EBIT, 12.1% Q1 CY26 EBIT) at €81/share cash, €1.27bn enterprise value, 1.27x EV/revenue and 9.12x EV/EBITDA, a 140% premium to the undisturbed close and 94% to the 3-month VWAP, with 21% already secured by SPA from Lantano Beteiligungen GmbH and a 50%+1 share minimum acceptance — creating a $2.9bn+, 46,000-person, 40+-country group in which Europe rises to 22% and North America falls from 81% to 62%; funded by a €1.4bn Barclays bridge (Euribor +175–250bps, ~4.1–4.8%) at 1.9–2.5x net debt/EBITDA, later refinanced via a ₹70bn 8.95% NCD programme (Nov 4, 2026) and a ₹42,646mn QIP at ₹5,550/share (Oct 26, 2026). The only 'separation-shaped' facts in the record are four, and none is a business separation: (1) a deliberate decision NOT to integrate — no domination/profit-and-loss transfer agreement for two years, with squeeze-out deferred ('we are in no hurry'), so Nagarro runs as a controlled but distinct entity; (2) intra-group entity rationalisation in the other direction — mergers of Arrka Infosec (NCLT order Apr 21, 2026), MediaAgility India, Starfish Associates LLC and Persistent Telecom Solutions Inc. into their parents; (3) an intra-group transfer of 100% of Persistent Systems UK Ltd from the Indian parent to Aepona Group Limited, Ireland, plus similar re-parenting of French, German, Romanian, Polish, Swiss and Costa Rican subsidiaries under PSIOL/PSI; (4) an undecided option, raised by Abhishek Bhandari's question, to sell a minority stake 'at the asset level, not at the Persistent level' to private equity purely to deleverage. The separations that are actually discussed belong to other parties: Nagarro's own historical carve-out from Allgeier (source of the BaFin accounting queries Persistent diligenced), customer-side carve-outs Persistent services for PE sponsors, a Japanese industrial client's 'engineering carve-out', and a single passing reference to Persistent's 'erstwhile Accelerite business'. Nobody — no investor, lender or partner — asked for a separation on any of these calls; investors asked instead about integration risk, Nagarro's flat revenue, the 85%-off-peak share price, EPS-accretion math, interest cost, cash-plus-share-swap alternatives and tail-account rationalisation.
verdict.evolution: The Apr 2025, Jul 2025, Oct 2025, Jan 2026 and Apr 2026 calls contain no separation idea whatsoever — only an M&A framework of capability-led tuck-ins plus 'one scaled acquisition' reserved for Europe (Jul 2025, Apr 2025), alongside organic aspirations of $2bn run-rate by FY27 and $5bn by FY31 (Jan 2026), and margin aspiration of 16–17% (Apr 2026). The nearest precursor is Apr 2026's 60bps margin hit from 'consulting and advisory expenses related to corporate development initiatives', i.e. undisclosed deal work. On the Aug 2026 call (June 28, 2026) that work resolves into the Nagarro takeover plus a $125m-a-year / $650m-over-6.5-years net-new deal — and the only separation-adjacent commitments appear there: a two-year non-integration/squeeze-out deferral and an explicitly undecided asset-level PE stake. Filings from Jun–Nov 2026 then move purely toward consolidation (subsidiary mergers, re-parenting) and funding (USD 1,250m debt plus USD 450m equity authorisation on Sep 2, 2026; QIP Oct 26, 2026; NCDs Nov 4, 2026).

points.point: Management framed the Nagarro transaction as the opposite of separation or consolidation-for-cost: an expansion that adds complementary geographies, verticals and service lines (ERP, CX, consulting, public sector, Middle East, Japan).
points.quote: This is not a consolidation play. This is an expansion play for us bringing together, as Anand rightly pointed out, people, capabilities, markets which are all complimentary to us and very much aligned to the direction in which we want to take our company and make a company to last for many, many decades to come.

points.point: Vinit Teredesai gave the acquisition economics: €81 per share in cash, €1.27bn EV (€1bn equity value on ~12.4m non-treasury shares plus €267m net debt), 1.27x EV/revenue, 9.12x EV/EBITDA falling to ~7.73x on upper-end CY26 guidance.
points.quote: Persistent has agreed to acquire 100% of the Nagarro shares at an enterprise value of €1.27 billion based on an €81 per share in cash; a premium of 140% to the undisturbed closing price on June 25-26 and 94% to the 3-month volume weighted average price.

points.point: The closest thing to a separation is a deliberate NON-integration: Nagarro stays a distinct controlled entity, with no domination/profit-and-loss transfer agreement for two years and the minority squeeze-out deliberately deferred, while contracts are used to drive synergies.
points.quote: We'll, over a period of the next two years, look at where we can do the squeeze out. And we are in no hurry to do the squeeze out.

points.point: Asked by Abhishek Bhandari whether a cash-plus-share-swap would have de-risked the all-debt deal, Sandeep Kalra floated the only partial-separation option in the record — selling PE or other participation in the Nagarro asset itself, not in Persistent — while ruling out a QIP at that time and stating no decision had been taken.
points.quote: We may look at if there is a merit in deleveraging by having a private equity or some other participation at the asset level.

points.point: The only portfolio pruning discussed is customer-level, not business-level: possible rationalisation of Nagarro's long tail (the two companies together have 350+ accounts above $1m; ~180 Nagarro logos above $1m, largest under $50m) to release SG&A for reinvestment.
points.quote: Now, is there a possibility of, you know, tail accounts being rationalized? There's always a possibility and we'll look into that as well.

points.point: The June 8, 2026 board filing approves an intra-group share transfer — 100% of Persistent Systems UK Limited moving from the Indian parent to Aepona Group Limited, Ireland — explicitly as housekeeping, with no benefit to promoters and no change in listed-entity shareholding.
points.quote: To achieve entity rationalisation and operational efficiency within the group, the Board of Directors approved the transfer of 100% shareholding of Persistent Systems UK Limited from Persistent Systems Limited, India to Aepona Group Limited, Ireland upon execution of the Share Purchase Agreement ('SPA') in due course.

points.point: Legal-entity activity is absorption, not separation: MediaAgility India Private Limited merging into Persistent Systems Limited (June 8, 2026), Arrka Infosec into the parent (NCLT Mumbai order April 21, 2026, effective April 1, 2025), and Starfish Associates LLC (March 2, 2026) and Persistent Telecom Solutions Inc. (February 28, 2026) into Persistent Systems Inc. — each with the same stated reason.
points.quote: To achieve entity rationalisation and operational efficiency within the group

points.point: The ₹70bn NCD allotment of November 4, 2026 ring-fences the acquisition structure rather than separating any Persistent business: Series 1, 2, 5 and 6 are secured on the Bidco (Galaxy Germany Holding SE) and Nagarro SE share pledges and intercompany receivables, with Series 3 and 4 unsecured, all at 8.95% for 2–5 years.
points.quote: prior to the merger of Galaxy Germany Holding SE (Bidco) and Nagarro SE (Target), a pledge over the 100% shares of Bidco by the Issuer and the present and future intercompany receivables owed to the Issuer (as lender) by the Bidco

points.point: The single reference to a previously separated Persistent business is incidental — the legacy Accelerite products business, cited only to explain why India revenue looked artificially strong (an INR-denominated GCC renewal) and North America artificially weak that quarter.
points.quote: The thing that happened there is one of our IT customers in our erstwhile Accelerite business, the renewal happened in rupee (INR) terms through their GCC.

points.point: A year earlier the stated inorganic plan was additive only — capability-led tuck-ins plus a single scaled European asset to lift Europe toward 15% of revenue — with no mention of divesting, demerging or separating anything.
points.quote: The only place where we would do a scaled acquisition would be if we get some good asset in Europe.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing — no separation was announced, so no separation benefits were claimed. For the Nagarro combination they expect: margins maintained or bettered, cost synergies reinvested in growth, Cash and Reported EPS accretion in Year 1 excluding transaction costs, leverage of 1.9–2.5x falling to 1x by FY2030, Europe at 22% of revenue, $2.9bn+ scale, and Nagarro margins lifted under a new CFO.
verdict.gaps: No separation is discussed at all — no perimeter, rationale, listing, or capital split. Also unquantified: Nagarro revenue/cost synergies, the value-creation plan, and any asset-level PE stake terms.

verdict.rationale: There is no demerger or spin-off scheme in these texts: the 'separation' PNC Infratech describes is a staged, 100% equity divestment of a ring-fenced road-concession portfolio — 12 SPVs comprising 11 National Highway HAM projects plus 1 State Highway BOT-Toll project, spanning about 3,800 lane-km — to KKR-backed Highways Infrastructure Trust (later renamed Vertis Infrastructure Trust), under definitive agreements/SPA dated 15 January 2024, approved by shareholders by special resolution on 28 September 2024 and executed explicitly 'outside Scheme of Arrangement' (Reg 37A), completing on 27 March 2026 with PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways. Management's stated purpose was capital recycling and de-leveraging: the 12 SPVs carried Rs 6,480 crore of project debt, and after tranche 1 consolidated debt fell from Rs 9,345 crore to about Rs 4,300 crore, taking net debt/equity from 1.56x to 0.72x (0.76x by FY26). The realization was pitched at roughly 1.67x equity invested at SPA signing — tranche 1 (10 HAM SPVs, closed 22 May 2025) fetched Rs 1,827.6 crore equity consideration against Rs 1,371 crore invested, plus about Rs 200 crore of back-to-back receivables and Rs 624 crore of change-of-scope works (Rs 584 crore received); Bareilly-Nainital BOT-Toll closed 31 July 2025 at Rs 716.2 crore enterprise value (Rs 153.48 crore equity, Rs 239.35 crore unsecured loan, Rs 80 crore further receivables); Challakere closed at Rs 683.84 crore EV (Rs 80.48 crore equity, Rs 134.94 crore unsecured loans) against Rs 114 crore equity invested, having contributed only 1.30% of FY25 consolidated revenue (Rs 164.03 crore) and 2.42% of consolidated net worth. Gains were booked in the holding subsidiary PNC Infra Holdings (about Rs 460 crore pre-tax, Rs 400 crore post-tax), with no gain in standalone, and roughly Rs 2,200 crore net of debt was collected across 11 assets, leaving Rs 1,100–1,300 crore of cash in PNC Infra Holdings. That cash was explicitly 'earmarked' for fund-based project equity — Rs 1,744 crore of HAM equity commitments (Rs 663 crore, later Rs 542 crore, still to be infused) and about Rs 400 crore for the NHPC solar-plus-BESS SPV — and a buyback was explicitly ruled out. Management also tied the lighter balance sheet to bidding power: with cash and investing capacity it could bid large HAM and BOT-Toll projects directly, where competition is 'moderate' versus 'cutthroat' EPC. The counterparty, not investors or lenders, drove the deal; lenders and the authority were only consent-givers (NOCs from 34 lenders across 11 projects, NHAI in-principle change-of-control approvals obtained asset by asset).
verdict.evolution: The programme was announced with the 15 January 2024 definitive agreements and was tracked purely as execution thereafter: by Nov 2024 management split it into 10 assets (equity value Rs 1,490 crore, enterprise value ~Rs 7,690 crore) for FY25 and 2 assets for FY26, and said the MoRTH debarment did not disturb it. Feb 2025 was about consents — 34 lender NOCs for 11 projects and NHAI in-principle approvals for 8 of 11 — with the target raised to 11 assets by March 2025; Jun 2025 reported tranche 1 of 10 HAM SPVs closed 22 May 2025 at Rs 1,827.6 crore (after a negative Rs 378 crore descoping adjustment that explained the slip from the Rs 2,900 crore headline) and consolidated debt down to ~Rs 4,300 crore. Aug 2025 added Bareilly-Nainital (11 of 12 done), Nov 2025 confirmed the last change-of-control approval and Rs 2,200 crore received net of debt, and Feb 2026 showed the proceeds landing in cash (standalone cash jumping to Rs 1,299 crore 'includes the proceeds received from the KKR') while a second-round divestment of the newer HAM assets was only 'evaluating all the options' with investors approaching. The 27 March 2026 filing and the May 2026 call closed the loop: all twelve SPVs transferred, described as the final tranche of the strategic divestment announced in January 2024, with the next monetisation framework still undecided.

points.point: The 27 March 2026 filing records the transfer of PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways to Vertis Infrastructure Trust at Rs 683.84 crore enterprise value (Rs 80.48 crore equity, Rs 134.94 crore unsecured loans), completing all twelve SPVs under the 15 January 2024 SPA; it is a sale outside any scheme of arrangement, shareholder-approved by special resolution on 28 September 2024, and the asset was only 1.30% of FY25 consolidated revenue and 2.42% of consolidated net worth.

points.point: Management closed out the programme: the March 2026 Challakere sale to Vertis Infrastructure Trust was the final tranche of the 12-asset strategic divestment announced in January 2024, with the entire consideration received.

points.point: The strategic payoff cited was bidding capacity: a clean balance sheet (standalone net surplus Rs 327 crore, consolidated net debt/equity 0.76x) lets PNC bid large HAM and BOT-Toll projects directly, where competition is lighter than in cutthroat EPC — it won two UP HAM projects of Rs 3,483 crore combined bid cost.
points.quote: So, since we are in a position to invest into these projects, either it Is a HAM or BOT Toll with our healthy balance sheet and our investing capacity, so we look forward to have a lesser competition in the HAM projects, That too, particularly the larger size HAM projects.

points.point: No framework had yet been set for monetising the next generation of assets; only 5 of the 14 HAM projects had reached PCOD/COD and management called a second deal premature.
points.quote: So, we certainly will let you know once we reach out to any kind of framework mechanism on how to monetize these projects.

verdict.what_management_expects: For PNC: consolidated debt down (Rs 9,345 crore to ~Rs 4,300 crore, 1.56x to 0.72x), ~Rs 2,200 crore cash net of debt realised at ~1.67x equity invested, held in PNC Infra Holdings and earmarked for Rs 1,744 crore HAM equity plus ~Rs 400 crore solar/BESS equity, no debt-funded equity, no buyback; a balance sheet that supports direct bidding for large HAM/BOT-Toll with less competition. For the buyer-trust: operating concessions transferred with their debt.
verdict.gaps: No stated hurdle IRR or valuation method, no transaction costs/tax detail, no InvIT-unit or sponsor-stake option, no framework or timing for monetising the remaining 14 assets.
