verdict.rationale: On the evidence supplied, Poly Medicure is not separating a business — nothing in the seven earnings/acquisition call transcripts or the one filing announces or discusses a demerger, spin-off, slump sale, hive-off or carve-out of any division, and no scheme of arrangement is on record. The structural direction management describes is the exact opposite: inbound acquisition and consolidation into one entity. In FY26 the company bought PendraCare (Netherlands, interventional cardiology guiding/diagnostic catheters; CY24 revenue €9.9m, EBITDA €1.4m, 74% gross margin; 90% stake for €11m equity plus €3.2m intra-group loans, ~1.8x EV/revenue and 13x EV/EBITDA, remaining 10% to be bought in 2030 off CY29 EBITDA), Citieffe (Bologna, Italy, trauma and extremities orthopaedics; CY24 revenue €17.3m, EBITDA €3.1m, ~90% gross margin; €18.8m equity plus €4.2m shareholder loan plus €8m debt = ~€31m EV, ~10x EBITDA) and Medyneo in Brazil (a shell with ANVISA and import licences, ~$40,000, bought to save 18–24 months of registration time). Himanshu Baid's framing on 25 May 2026 was explicitly integrative — 'in 1 or 2 years, we'll make these 3 businesses into a single global platform' — with cross-selling both ways, Indian R&D supporting Europe, some manufacturing eventually shifted to India, and subsidiary EBITDA guided from 12–14% to 18–20% over 2–3 years. The core Infusion Therapy business is being de-weighted in mix (65% historically, 57% of Q4 FY25, 50% of Q4 FY26, with Renal ~11%) but is expressly retained and used to fund the new verticals: 'this doesn't mean that we are not focusing on our core infusion business, which is generating significant profits, enabling us to invest into these new high-growth areas.' The only deliberate exit described is channel-level, not structural — shrinking government/tender business from ~10–12% of domestic revenue to a target 6–7% because of L1 pricing and state payment delays — and the only facility decision reversed was dropping the planned Jaipur plant in favour of land at YEIDA. The single filing (5 Nov 2026) is a routine board-approved refresh of five governance policies; 'demerger' appears in it only as a generic Schedule III disclosure category, not as a transaction. Financial context given: FY26 standalone revenue ₹1,662 crore (+4%), consolidated ₹1,875 crore (+12.3%), standalone EBITDA ₹446 crore at 26.8%, consolidated cash ₹842 crore, FY26 capex ₹296 crore, FY27 guidance ₹1,900–1,950 crore standalone and ₹2,300–2,400 crore consolidated; no part of that guidance is attributed to any separation.
verdict.evolution: Across the window the corporate-structure thread runs only one way — toward acquiring and absorbing. On 7 May 2025 management said only that it was on a 'constant lookout' for technology M&A and refused to name a vertical; on 8 Aug 2025 it added a wholly owned Brazil subsidiary and two CDMO contracts; the dedicated calls of 4 Sep 2025 (PendraCare) and 25 Sep 2025 (Citieffe) set out the two acquisitions, closed 23 Sep and 6 Nov 2025 respectively and reported in the 10 Nov 2025 call as adding ~₹280 crore of annualised revenue. By 6 Feb 2026 the language was integration and 'a fundamental upgrade of our business model' (not a split), and by 25 May 2026 it was explicit consolidation of three businesses into one platform plus the Medyneo bolt-on. At no point — including the 5 Nov 2026 filing — does any separation, demerger or divestment of a Polymed business appear.

points.point: Management's stated structural intent is to merge, not separate: Polymed standalone plus PendraCare plus Citieffe are to be run as one global platform, with cross-selling, shared R&D and procurement synergies.
points.quote: I think in 1 or 2 years, we'll make these 3 businesses into a single global platform for growth.

points.point: Despite Infusion Therapy falling from 57% of Q4 FY25 revenue to 50% in Q4 FY26, Baid insists it stays in-house at ~50% of mix, citing ~11% global IV-catheter share — i.e. no carve-out of the legacy business.
points.quote: Again, that is our core, core, core business.

points.point: The acquired entities are to be margin-upgraded inside the group (12–14% EBITDA now, 18–20% in 2–3 years) through Indian engineering, global supply chain and partial manufacturing transfer — the opposite of separating them out.
points.quote: All that will help us in the long run will help us to -- see, currently, these companies will operate, let's say, around 12% to 14% margin.

points.point: The 'transition' repeatedly described is a product/technology mix shift from low-tech to cardiology, critical care and orthopaedics — explicitly funded by the retained infusion business, not a legal separation of either part.
points.quote: Having said that, this doesn't mean that we are not focusing on our core infusion business, which is generating significant profits, enabling us to invest into these new high-growth areas.

points.point: The only business management says it is deliberately exiting is the government/tender channel (~10–12% of domestic revenue, degrowth of 18% in Q3 FY26, target 6–7%) on price and receivables grounds — a channel de-emphasis, not a separation.
points.quote: And deliberately, we are reducing our government business exposure as the prices are lower in government business.

points.point: The two European deals were presented as additive to the existing business, adding roughly ₹280 crore of annualised revenue, with integration already begun — no mention of any offsetting disposal.
points.quote: With these two acquisitions, we will add around close to Rs. 280 crores of revenue to our existing business on an annual basis.

points.point: On the Citieffe call, the stated M&A doctrine is to stay inside medical devices and its adjacencies and to pause and absorb — Citieffe adds orthopaedics on top of cardiology, critical care and renal, with no suggestion of separating any vertical.
points.quote: I think on the M&A strategy, which we have said in the past that we want to obviously stick to the medical devices and we'll stick to the adjacencies of the medical devices.

points.point: Even manufacturing is kept where it is: Rahul Gautam rejects moving Citieffe's Bologna production to India because customers value Made-in-Europe, limiting change to outsourcing parts of processes.
points.quote: We have currently no such plans.

points.point: PendraCare was framed as a bolt-on platform to globalise Polymed's own cardiology products (DES clinical registry of 2,000 patients, EU/FDA approvals), targeting €3–4m of incremental group EBITDA synergies and ~€25m revenue by 2030.
points.quote: This is very much part of our core strategy to grow into cardiology, something which we have been doing over the last 12 to 18 months.

points.point: At the start of the window the only structural plan disclosed was inorganic expansion funded by the Aug-2024 QIP cash (~₹1,100 crore liquidity, ~₹500 crore earmarked for organic capex); no divestment or demerger was contemplated.
points.quote: Of course, we are looking at some new opportunities in M&A side and as soon as we finalize something, we will definitely get back to you with proper details.

points.point: There is no scheme of arrangement in the record. The sole filing (5 Nov 2026) is a board-approved refresh of five governance policies; 'demerger' appears in it only inside the boilerplate Schedule III list of disclosable event categories.
points.quote: Acquisition(s) (including agreement to acquire), Scheme of Arrangement (amalgamation/ merger/ demerger/restructuring), sale or disposal of any unit(s), division(s), whole or substantially the whole of the undertaking(s) or subsidiary of the listed entity, sale of stake in the associate company of the listed entity or any other restructuring.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing — no separation was proposed. The only structural expectations stated are for acquisitions: PendraCare and Citieffe moving from 12–14% to 18–20% EBITDA over 2–3 years, €3–4 million of group synergy EBITDA, Citieffe revenue doubling in five years, standalone EBITDA 25–27% versus consolidated 23–25%, and three businesses run as one global platform.
verdict.gaps: No call or filing mentions a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or carve-out, so no rationale, perimeter, swap ratio, or investor/lender/partner demand for one is explained.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these texts, RKFORGE is not demerging or spinning off a business: no scheme of arrangement for a demerger appears anywhere, and the group's actual structural work runs the other way — toward consolidation. Two genuine 'separations' do exist. First, a disposal: the Board approved disinvestment of 100% of Globe All India Services Limited (GAISL) — the non-forging services business (tour and travel, sanitization and cargo) that formed the entire 'Others' reporting segment — to Yatra Online Limited for an aggregate Rs 12,800 lakhs (Rs 128 crore), with the full consideration received in the quarter ended September 30, 2024 and GAISL ceasing to be a subsidiary w.e.f. August 31, 2024; RKFL booked a standalone exceptional gain of Rs 10,287.33 lakhs and a consolidated gain of Rs 9,510.39 lakhs after related expenses of Rs 602.85 lakhs, cost of the investment of Rs 1,809.82 lakhs, goodwill of Rs 503.19 lakhs and Rs 273.75 lakhs of profit earned till disposal, and net investing proceeds of Rs 12,197.15 lakhs; the prior year was restated as 'discontinued operations' under Ind AS 105, leaving RKFL a single 'Forging components' segment. Management never gave a reason for this sale on any of the seven calls and no analyst asked — the only linkage offered is Naresh Jalan's list of FY26 deleveraging sources (warrant money, the ACIL-merger tax refund, free cash flow, end of the capex cycle). Second, a deliberate ring-fence rather than a separation of something existing: the forged rail wheel business was placed in a JV SPV with Titagarh (Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheel Limited), to which 'the railway wheel contract has been assigned', structured 70:30 debt:equity on a Rs 2,000 crore project (Rs 1,600 crore phase 1 for 100,000+ machined wheels sufficient to FY28, Rs 400 crore phase 2 only on reaching that utilisation), with roughly Rs 900 crore of debt and Rs 370 crore of equity already in and about Rs 115-120 crore more of RKFL equity to come. Management stressed the JV is not consolidated and 'does not carry risk in terms of RKFL consolidated', excluded wheel sales from RKFL's revenue guidance entirely, and repeatedly fenced its scope — wheels only, with all other railway work (frames, bolsters, assembled bogie frames, undercarriages) staying in standalone RKFL. Meanwhile the opposite motion was executed twice: ACIL Limited merged into RKFL (NCLT order March 27, 2025; Rs 18,737.28 lakhs of deferred tax asset recognised on ACIL's carried-forward losses, Rs 3,160.64 lakhs set against current tax), and Multitech Auto plus step-down MAL Metalliks merged into Ramkrishna Casting Solutions Limited (NCLT Kolkata order February 27, 2026, effective March 25, 2026, appointed date January 1, 2024) — explicitly 'a key milestone in our plan to simplify our business structure'. The only margin logic given for keeping castings in a separate subsidiary is structural: castings run 15-17% versus 20-22% for forgings, costing 100-150bps at the consolidated level.
verdict.evolution: The SPV idea surfaced on the Jan 17, 2025 call, where Chirag Shah asked whether a newly announced railway-wheel SPV was new or the existing JV, and Naresh Jalan confirmed it was a continuation with the wheel contract assigned into it; GAISL had already been sold by then (August 31, 2024) but was never raised on that call or any later one. On Jun 2, 2025 Lalit Khetan framed the structural agenda as simplification — ACIL's merger into the parent was done and Multitech/MAL Metalliks into Ramkrishna Casting Solutions was 'the final step' — while Jalan listed the ACIL tax refund among FY26 deleveraging levers. By Aug 1, 2025 the ring-fence was explicit in numbers (Rs 2,000 crore in two phases, 70:30 debt:equity, Rs 900 crore of JV debt that 'does not carry risk' to RKFL), and on Nov 12, 2025 Khetan said the NCLT order was expected in Q3 FY26; the Feb 2026, May 2026 and Jul 24, 2026 calls then narrowed the JV's remit progressively — wheel sales excluded from RKFL's consolidated revenue, JV 'only for manufacturing of wheels', all other railway business 'isolated standalone RKFL'.

points.point: The only outright business separation in the record: 100% of Globe All India Services Limited — the non-forging tour and travel, sanitization and cargo business that was the whole 'Others' segment — was sold to Yatra Online Limited for Rs 12,800 lakhs, and the prior year was restated as discontinued operations under Ind AS 105.
points.quote: GAISL ceased to be a subsidiary of the Holding Company w.e.f. August 31, 2024 and accordingly the results for the previous year ended March 31, 2025 pertaining to GAISL have been classified as "discontinued operations" in the consolidated financial results in line with the requirements of Ind AS 105 (Non-current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations).

points.point: The disposal produced a large one-off gain: Rs 10,287.33 lakhs standalone exceptional income in FY25, and Rs 9,510.39 lakhs consolidated after related expenses of Rs 602.85 lakhs, investment cost of Rs 1,809.82 lakhs, goodwill of Rs 503.19 lakhs and Rs 273.75 lakhs of subsidiary profit to the disinvestment date.
points.quote: ₹ 10,287.33 lakhs for the year ended March 31, 2025 represents net gain on sale of investments in a subsidiary.

points.point: Asked whether the newly announced railway-wheel SPV was separate from the existing Titagarh JV, Jalan confirmed it was the same vehicle and that the Indian Railways wheel contract itself had been transferred into it — the legal act that separated wheels from RKFL.
points.quote: Basically, the railway wheel contract has been assigned to the SPV and now the SPV has taken up the manufacturing of the wheels.

points.point: Mitul Shah pressed on the roughly Rs 900 crore of debt sitting in the JV on top of RKFL's Rs 1,800 crore net debt; Jalan's answer is the clearest statement of the separation's purpose — the wheel project's leverage is ring-fenced on the JV's own plant, machinery and land and stays off RKFL's consolidated balance sheet.
points.quote: But I think the JV does not carry risk in terms of RKFL consolidated is concerned. And neither this balance sheet is getting consoled in RKFL right now.

points.point: The Rs 2,000 crore project is staged inside the separate entity so the second tranche is contingent on volume: Rs 1,600 crore in phase 1 covers 100,000+ machined wheels, enough for Indian Railways to FY28, before any further Rs 400 crore is committed.
points.quote: So, second phase of investment of Rs. 400 Crores, which is going to happen, is going to happen once we have a utilization level of 100,000 plus wheels sent to Indian Railways, then only we will invest the second phase to augment full capacity of 200,000 plus wheels.

points.point: Asked about railway targets, Jalan excluded wheels from RKFL's own revenue build entirely because they sit in the JV, keeping the listed entity's railway growth story (bogie assemblies, frames, bolsters) distinct from the wheel venture.
points.quote: Wheel production sales is going to come in the JV and we are right now not building any sales from the wheels right now.

points.point: When Harsh Shah of Marcellus assumed all railway opportunity was routed through the JV, Jalan corrected him firmly: the JV's remit is wheels and nothing else, with RKFL's own railway order book — including a stated Rs 2,000 crore annual Indian Railways undercarriage/bogie opportunity — retained in the listed company.
points.quote: Wheels JV is only going to be part and parcel of manufacturing wheels, nothing else.

points.point: Management quantified what the separate wheel entity is expected to earn in its own right at scale, on a 230,000-wheel installed capacity with an 80,000-wheel Indian Railways offtake guarantee plus about 25,000 wheels of JV-partner obligation.
points.quote: 80%, 85% utilization, which we expect to have in FY '28. We are looking at almost Rs. 1,600 crore to Rs. 1,700 crore revenue from that operation and that will be a 17% to 18% opportunity for us in terms of EBITDA margins.

points.point: The stated structural rationale on the calls is simplification by combining entities, not separating them: ACIL was merged into the parent (NCLT order March 27, 2025) and the castings entities were being folded into Ramkrishna Casting Solutions as the closing step.
points.quote: This is a key milestone in our plan to simplify our business structure. The final step, merging Multitech Auto and Mal Metalliks into Ramkrishna Casting Solution is underway and will be completed during this year.

points.point: Progress on that consolidation was tracked as a formal NCLT process, with the order expected in Q3 FY26 — reinforcing that the live corporate action in this period was amalgamation, not a demerger.
points.quote: Further, amalgamation proceeding of Multitech Auto and the step-down subsidiary MAL Metalliks with Ramkrishna Casting Solutions Limited is progressing well, and we expect the order from NCLT in Q3 FY 26.

points.point: The castings amalgamation completed on March 25, 2026 with an appointed date of January 1, 2024; both transferor companies were dissolved, current tax and deferred tax were recomputed for their carried-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation, and the group's subsidiary count shrank.
points.quote: Consequent to the Scheme becoming effective, both Transferor Company No.1 and Transferor Company No. 2 stands dissolved without winding up and ceased to the subsidiaries of the Company, with effect from March 25, 2026.

points.point: The one economic reason given for castings living in a separate 100% subsidiary rather than the parent is a permanently lower margin structure — 16-17% versus 20-22% for forgings — which Khetan said costs 100-150bps at the consolidated level.
points.quote: Castings will always remain to be a 16%, 17% margin.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation benefits were claimed. For the JV: Rs 1,600-1,700 crore revenue at 17-18% EBITDA on 80-85% utilisation in FY28, with its ~Rs 900 crore debt unconsolidated and not a risk to RKFL. Castings in subsidiary stay 15-17% margin, diluting consol 100-150bps. GAISL exit booked Rs 95-103 crore gain.
verdict.gaps: No demerger or spin-off scheme exists here; no call explains the GAISL sale's rationale, buyer, valuation or use of proceeds; no investor, lender or partner is said to have asked.

verdict.rationale: These documents do not disclose any separation, demerger, spin-off or business transfer by Ashapura Minechem Ltd.; on the evidence here there is no separation rationale to reconstruct, and the premise of the question is not supported by the texts. Across all four calls (Sep 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026) management consistently describes a single consolidated company run as two halves — the Guinea resource business (bauxite from the HUDA, BOFFA and FAKO concessions, >700 million tons of bauxite reserves, >300 million tons of iron ore, three in-house ports of 16 million tons capacity going to 27 million tons, 370 km of road) and the India value-added minerals business organised into four/three verticals: Bentonite & Allied Minerals and White Performance Minerals, Specialty Adsorbent Solutions through the 50% JV Ashapura Perfoclay, and Advanced Ceramic Materials through the stake in Orient Ceratech. Far from separating them, management argues for keeping them together: Manan Shah says on 11 Feb 2026 that 'Ashapura Group has seen lot of volatility in the bauxite business' but 'our Indian business has always been a source of strength and consolidation for us,' i.e. India is presented as the stabiliser for a cyclical Guinea. The only time separation is raised at all is by an investor, not management: on 4 Sep 2025 Nalin Shah of NVS Brokerage asks whether any value-unlocking strategy, acquisition or 'de-merger' is 'on the card,' and management replies that the company is 'open to all opportunities of acquisitions or any other kind of strategic activities' but that 'our management focus is on the growth of both Guinea and India business as they stand for the time being' — an explicit deferral, with no plan, structure, timeline, swap ratio, record date or appointed-date disclosed then or in any later call. The only filing supplied (postal ballot dispatched 27 March 2026) contains no scheme of arrangement: its items are the Ashapura Minechem Limited – Employee Stock Option Plan 2026 for up to 20,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 2 face value, extension of that ESOP to holding/subsidiary/group/associate company employees, re-appointment of Shri Hemul Shah as Executive Director & CEO for two years from 16 February 2026 at up to Rs. 1,00,90,000 p.a., and regularisation of Shri Jagdish Shetty and Shri Wilson Mathais as Independent Directors from 5 February 2026. Words such as 'merger, demerger, sale of division' appear in that notice only as standard anti-dilution boilerplate for adjusting option entitlements on corporate actions, not as any announced transaction. The nearest things to structural change actually disclosed are capital and partnership moves inside the existing entity: the China Railway tie-up for mining, logistics and port operations in Guinea (a partner, explicitly 'not the end customer'), a possible build-operate-transfer model so beneficiation capex sits with vendors/partners rather than Ashapura's balance sheet (4 Jun 2026), roughly INR 150 crores of India capex across divisions, and a holding chain India → UAE → Guinea that management defended on 11 Feb 2026 when asked about related-party loans and investments.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaced from management: it was raised once by an investor, Nalin Shah of NVS Brokerage, on the maiden call of 4 Sep 2025, bundled with questions on acquisitions and inorganic growth, and management set it aside in favour of growing Guinea and India 'as they stand for the time being.' It was not mentioned again on 21 Nov 2025, 11 Feb 2026 or 4 Jun 2026 by any analyst or by management; instead the integrated story hardened, with Guinea framed as the growth engine (8 million tons exported in FY26, INR 4,200 crores revenue, INR 561 crores EBITDA) and India as the stabilising, value-added pillar (INR 998 crores revenue, INR 112 crores EBITDA). The 27 March 2026 postal ballot, the only filing provided, moved in the opposite direction by proposing a single group-wide ESOP extended across holding, subsidiary, group and associate companies, which presumes the group stays together. As of the last call on 4 Jun 2026 the forward agenda was port expansion to 20-27 million tons, a 20,000 tpd bauxite washing plant, iron ore beneficiation and a 100% dividend — no separation.

points.point: The only mention of a demerger in all four transcripts comes from an analyst, Nalin Shah of NVS Brokerage, asking whether any value-unlocking move — acquisition, inorganic growth or demerger — is planned.
points.quote: So I just only would like to know if there are any strategies or for unlocking of value what we are considering, is there any strategy or any thing on the card in terms of acquisitions and inorganic growth as well as any like de - merger or something which can create further value for the company if you can throw some light on that?

points.point: Management declines to commit to any such structural action, saying it is open in principle but focused on operating both businesses as they currently stand — no scheme, rationale, structure or timeline is offered.
points.quote: We are open to all opportunities of acquisitions or any other kind of strategic activities. However, our management focus is on the growth of both G uinea and I ndia business as they stand for the time being.

points.point: Rather than arguing for separation, management argues the two businesses belong together: India is explicitly positioned as the counterweight to Guinea's bauxite-price volatility, which is the opposite of a demerger case.
points.quote: But our Indian business has always been a source of strength and consolidation for us.

points.point: Asked directly about related-party loans and advances (over 70% of loans/advances and about 71% of investments) and loss-making subsidiaries, management defends the existing India-UAE-Guinea holding chain as a business necessity, not something to be unwound.
points.quote: So there -- this is a more like the nature of the structure rather than anything else.

points.point: The forward plan presented is integrated investment inside one company — INR 150 crores of India capex plus Guinea port expansion from 15 to 20 million tons, a 20,000 tpd bauxite washing plant and iron ore beneficiation — with no reference to carving anything out.
points.quote: We are, therefore, looking at a significant capex over the next year, roughly around INR150 crores across all business divisions, to upgrade our plant facilities and add new products to our portfolio.

points.point: Asked about the three-to-five-year future, both promoters describe growing Guinea and India side by side within the same company, including exploring other African countries, with no structural separation contemplated.
points.quote: Coming to the India business, we are very optimistic about our India business in the next three to five years.

points.point: Where capital-structure creativity is discussed, it is about keeping capex off Ashapura's own balance sheet via partners under a build-operate-transfer model — not about separating a business.
points.quote: Regarding to the capex on these projects, we are currently evaluating models wherein the capex can be handled by our potential vendors or partners, and we are looking at perhaps a build-operate-transfer kind of a model.

points.point: No scheme of arrangement, demerger, slump sale or business transfer is present in the filings supplied. The single filing (postal ballot dispatched 27 March 2026) covers only ESOP 2026 for up to 20,00,000 shares, its extension to group-company employees, Hemul Shah's re-appointment as Executive Director & CEO, and two Independent Director regularisations.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these texts announces or explains POWERINDIA separating, demerging, spinning off or divesting a business — the premise is not supported by the seven supplied transcripts or the one AGM filing, and I am not importing anything from memory. The only 'separation' management actually describes is internal and organisational: the carve-out of Service into a standalone fifth business unit effective 1 April 2025, sitting alongside the four existing BUs (Transformers, High Voltage Products, Grid Integration, Grid Automation), mirroring a 'separate global BU Service' at Hitachi Energy — no new legal entity, no share issuance, no record date, no NCLT scheme, no listed-entity restructuring. The reasons given for that carve-out were an aging installed base (Venu cited 'Rs.60,000 crores worth of installed base in India since last 75 years' in the May 2025 call; the Feb 2025 slide said 'approximately Rs. (+80,000) crores'), the urgency of the energy transition, an 'ever evolving workforce' and the organisational shift to digitalization. The prize was sized at roughly Rs. 2,000 crores of service orders per year against a then run-rate of Rs. 500–600 crores, described as a 3-to-5-year journey; service was 7.4% of FY25 orders, 11–12% in individual quarters, and 'high single digit' thereafter, with service orders up ~60% YoY in FY25 and ~90% YoY in Q1 FY26. The problems it was said to solve were fragmented lifecycle engagement and an inconsistent customer experience ('develop service and digital proficiency and unify the customer service experience'), plus new-age customers such as data centres wanting a 'life cycle partner' rather than only equipment supply. It was also explicitly a margin lever, named by Venu alongside volume/fixed-cost leverage, exports and pricing excellence in the road map to and beyond double-digit EBITDA. Nobody asked for a separation: no investor, lender, analyst or partner in any call requests one — analysts instead pressed on margins versus peers, the ~4% royalty, admin and other expenses (Dhavan Shah even suggested cutting royalty and raising dividend instead), and management defended the royalty and promised operating leverage rather than any structural split. The single occurrence of the word 'demerger' anywhere in the record is a backward-looking administrative reference in the 31 July 2026 AGM notice to the Scheme of Arrangement that created the company, cited only to explain 1,07,421 shares allotted to the IEPF account, with no rationale attached.
verdict.evolution: The idea first surfaced on the Jan 30, 2025 call (tagged Feb 2025), where Venu said the company 'will work towards a new service business unit' as a fifth BU from 1 April 2025 and framed it against the aging installed base and digitalization. It was confirmed as launched on the May 15, 2025 call (installed base Rs. 60,000 crores, potential Rs. 2,000 crores of orders per year versus Rs. 500–600 crores today), described as 'carved out' on the Jul 30, 2025 call, and reframed on the Nov 7, 2025 call as a top-line and bottom-line margin lever. By Feb 5, 2026 it was a 'separate global BU Service including in India' with the stated aim of 'shifting center of gravity' toward export, service and digital; by May 26, 2026 service was merely a 'key pillar' and the only structural news ran the other way — Rs. 2,000 crores of additional capex (Rs. 4,000 crores cumulative) and a greenfield Karjan transformer plant, i.e. consolidation and expansion inside one entity, not separation.

verdict.rationale: On these texts alone, Physicswallah is not demerging or spinning off a business under any scheme of arrangement — the 06-Mar-2026 filing expressly answers "Not applicable" to whether the disposal is outside a Scheme of Arrangement, and neither earnings call mentions a demerger, listing of a subsidiary, or value unlock. What the documents do show are three narrow, separate acts of legal carve-out, each explained in operational rather than capital-markets terms. First, PWL sold 10% of Bharat Innovations Global Private Limited (BIGPL), so it ceased to be a wholly-owned subsidiary while PWL retained 90% and consolidation continues; the buyer is NSDC International Limited (not promoter/promoter group, not a related-party transaction), the agreement for sale is dated 04-Dec-2024, completion 19-Feb-2026, with "an inadvertent delay in intimating", and crucially the consideration was received other than in cash, "in exchange for the brand name and goodwill of the acquirer" — i.e. a brand/partnership swap, not a cash divestment; BIGPL is immaterial (FY25 turnover INR 30,018 and net worth of negative INR 20,591, each 0% of the group, incorporated about a year earlier and having "recently commenced its core business operations"). Second, on the Feb-2026 call management said a newly incorporated hostel-services entity exists to pull the fragmented hostel operations of subsidiary Xylem in Trivandrum, plus scattered student-housing pockets (Patna, Trivandrum), out of the operating businesses into "an independent entity" — a business that is "less than a percent" of revenue and which they explicitly do not intend to grow aggressively, framed purely as facilitating student/parent needs. Third, the K-12/schools push is being ring-fenced in a separate legal and reporting vehicle: INR 400 crores has been invested "in our wholly owned company" (the school-management company running Indore, Gurgaon and Varanasi, plus management control of Tender Heart, Ranchi, with 8 more schools — 4 brownfield, 4 greenfield on nine-year build-to-suit leases), and schools will sit in "others", not in the offline segment, once online/offline segmental EBITDA reporting starts on 1 April 2026. The stated problems these solve are fragmentation (hostels run piecemeal inside Xylem), reporting cleanliness (schools and housing, each under 1% of revenue, not muddying offline economics the market is being asked to judge), and acquiring a partner's brand and goodwill without cash (BIGPL/NSDC International). No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere as having asked for any of it; the only external-party driver disclosed is the NSDC International counterparty itself, and the only shareholder action in the filings is ESOP ratification/extension to group, subsidiary and associate companies plus deletion of Part B of the AoA after the shareholders' agreements lapsed on listing.
verdict.evolution: Dec-2025 (Q2 FY26, the maiden post-listing call) contains no separation at all — only the promise to report online and offline EBITDA separately from 1 April 2026, and an M&A template of taking 25–50% first-stage equity with three-to-four-year earnouts rather than one-shot majority. By Feb-2026 (Q3 FY26) two carve-outs surface in the same call: the newly incorporated hostel-services entity consolidating Xylem's Trivandrum hostels and scattered student housing, and the INR 400 crore wholly-owned school-management company, with the clarification that schools go into "others" and not offline. The 06-Mar-2026 filing then discloses the third and only actual stake disposal — 10% of Bharat Innovations Global to NSDC International — on an agreement dated 04-Dec-2024 that completed on 19-Feb-2026 and was intimated late, i.e. a transaction agreed almost a year before listing and surfacing publicly only after it had closed.

verdict.rationale: On the evidence of these nine transcripts and the single filing, RITES is not separating a business, and no rationale for one was ever articulated by management. The only divestment on record is corporate, not operational: the Board at its 303rd meeting on June 25, 2026 approved sale of RITES' entire holding in associate company Elicius Energy Private Limited — 1,573 equity shares, 13% of Elicius' equity — and on August 19, 2026 the Competent Authority decided to transfer them to Dr. Raghunathan Rengasamy, Elicius' own promoter and director, at a fair value of Rs. 38.49 per share from a valuation certificate by SPGM & Associates (FRN 332387E), for a total of Rs. 60,544.77, with completion expected before September 30, 2026 and Elicius then ceasing to be an associate. The filing itself states the holding contributed 'Nil' turnover, revenue, income and net worth in the last financial year, that the buyer is not a promoter/promoter-group/group-company of RITES, that it is not a related-party transaction, and that the 'outside Scheme of Arrangement' / Regulation 37A question is 'Not applicable' — i.e. there is no scheme, no demerger, no undertaking being carved out. No problem to be solved is named, and no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for it; the only comparable wind-down mentioned anywhere is the legacy IRSDC equity of about Rs. 48 crore (Nov 2023), which management said was safe and 'in the process of being wound up' with no impairment expected. Across all nine calls management instead argued for structural continuity of the existing four revenue streams — consultancy, turnkey (Rs. 4,580 crore of the Rs. 9,416 crore order book at FY26 end), exports (Rs. 1,700+ crore) and leasing/REMCL — explicitly refusing to split out or re-badge anything, insisting RITES is 'a project management consultancy company', not an EPC/construction company, and that turnkey is only a method of accounting (Rs. 105 crore booked where the fee is Rs. 5 crore). Related entities that an investor might expect to be separated were discussed as being retained and grown: REMC Ltd (FY26 revenue Rs. 163 crore, PAT Rs. 90 crore, ~50%+ PAT margin, Rs. 42 crore dividend to RITES, now adding non-IR renewables consultancy and a first international order) and the SAIL wagon JV SRBWIPL (Rs. 480 crore order book at June 30, 2025). So any separation thesis cannot be sourced to these documents.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces in the calls: from Nov 2023 through May 2026 the only structural items raised are the IRSDC/RLDA investment being wound up (Nov 2023 call), partnerships and non-binding MOUs (Etihad Rail, Abu Dhabi Ports, DNV, BEML, NHAI, DMRC), and repeated denials of any change of shape — most pointedly in the Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) call, where the CMD promised no surprise of 'suddenly changing our colour from a consultancy company to some other company', and again in the May 2026 (Q4 FY26) call, which closed on continuity of the high-dividend, four-stream model. The only separation event appears afterwards and only in the filing: Board approval on June 25, 2026, Competent Authority decision and disclosure on August 19, 2026, completion expected by September 30, 2026. It is a 13% associate-stake exit of Nil financial contribution sold back to the investee's own promoter, with no stated reason, no scheme of arrangement and no change in plan to trace, because no plan was ever disclosed earlier.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe Route Mobile separating, demerging or spinning off any business — the premise cannot be supported from the documents supplied, and I will not infer one. Across all six transcripts (May 2025 through Jul 2026) and all six filings, the only corporate transactions disclosed run in the opposite direction or are immaterial: an inbound acquisition of Heltar Technologies' AI-led omnichannel business undertaking by wholly owned subsidiary Route Connect Private Limited on a slump-sale basis (board approved Jul 13, 2026; INR 238,845,200 upfront plus INR 97,709,400 deferred at 18 months; funded from internal accruals, supported by an INR 35 crore 9% unsecured ICD from Route Mobile to Route Connect; completed Jul 29, 2026), and the voluntary de-registration of Route SMS Solutions Zambia Limited effective Jan 06, 2026 — a step-down subsidiary that "had not commenced any business" and contributed nil turnover, revenue, income and net worth. The only 'separation' management actually discusses is organizational, not corporate: from the Nov 2025 call onward they split the sales organization into two dedicated units — telco (firewall, CPaaS-in-a-Box, RCS MAP server, Konera network APIs, sold with BICS' 450+/900+ operator reach) and enterprise (omnichannel CPaaS: SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, Viber, email) — with Rajdip Gupta stating "people from telco will not sell SMS and the people from SMS will not sell the telco product." The stated reason is margin visibility and focus, not legal separation: firewall/platform work carries 30%–60/70% margins versus a 20.9%–24.5% portfolio gross margin, while ILD A2P SMS (roughly one-fourth to one-third of revenue) is in secular decline against FY26 revenue of INR 44,082 million (-3.7%), gross profit of INR 10,073 million at 22.9%, and new products at only ~8% of revenue despite a 43% four-year CAGR. A related but narrower unbundling is commercial: management said any future Vodafone Idea engagement will be contracted as two separate deals, firewall and SMS, so the SMS minimum-revenue commitment can no longer dilute firewall margins — a direct response to the ~INR 28 crore exceptional charge taken in Q4 FY25 when a global technology client phased out a platform and the MNO volume commitment was missed. Nobody — no investor, lender or partner — asked for a business separation in these texts; the only structural question from the market was about delisting, which Rajdip Gupta flatly denied on behalf of Proximus Global. Capital-allocation pressure from analysts (Dipesh Mehta, Kunal Ochiramani, on ~INR 1,300-1,400 crore of cash, <4% yield, roughly half of enterprise value) was answered with acquisitions, a dividend raised from INR 11 to INR 16.5 per share, and possible buyback/special dividend — never with a separation or value-unlocking demerger.
verdict.evolution: No separation idea surfaces at any point: May 2025 and Jul 2025 are about the ILD/AIT reset, Proximus COGS synergies and Rajdip Gupta returning as CEO; Nov 2025 introduces the internal split of sales into telco and enterprise teams; Feb 2026 hardens that into "two separate businesses" with separate product roadmaps, denies the delisting rumour, and says future Vodafone Idea deals will be two separate contracts (firewall vs SMS); May 2026's full strategy update lays out five pillars (ELEVATE, INNOVATE, DEEPEN, EXPAND, ACCELERATE) built on acquiring capability, not divesting it. Jul 2026 then executes that acquisition thesis with Heltar, and the only disposal in the record is the Jan 29, 2026 filing on the nil-activity Zambia subsidiary's de-registration. So the trajectory over these 36 months is consolidation and bolt-on M&A, with separation appearing only as internal organizational and contractual unbundling.

points.quote: The acquisition of the AI -led Omnichannel  Business Undertaking of Heltar Technologies Private Limited by Route Connect Private Limited , a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The Q1 FY27 call treats Heltar as capability acceleration, distribution leverage over 3,100+ clients mostly on a single channel, and a push for non-SMS revenue that has compounded over 40% annually for four years — all integration logic, with no separation discussed anywhere on the call.
points.quote: Heltar compres ses what would have been a multiyear internal build into an immediate deployable platform, consistent with our build versus buy framework.

verdict.what_management_expects: Not applicable to a separation — none is proposed. For the telco/enterprise operating split and the unbundled Vodafone-style contracts, management expects protected and higher margins (firewall/platform at 30%-60/70% versus a ~21%-24.5% portfolio gross margin), no dilution of gross profit or EBIT from SMS volume commitments, sharper product roadmaps per segment, and recurring managed-service MNO revenue alongside enterprise CPaaS. FY27 guidance stays mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth at ~12% EBITDA margin.
verdict.gaps: No separation, demerger, spin-off, scheme of arrangement, listed-entity restructuring, segment carve-out rationale, valuation-unlock argument, or lender/partner demand for one appears anywhere in these texts.

verdict.rationale: The premise cannot be supported from these texts: across the three transcripts supplied (Investor & Analyst Day of 25 March 2026, Q4/FY26 call of 12 May 2026, Q1 FY27 call of 21 July 2026) and the two filings supplied (the 29 May 2026 postal ballot notice and the 28 January 2026 Q3 FY26 press release), Sagility Ltd. never announces, proposes, or discusses separating, demerging, spinning off, hiving off, or divesting any business, and there is no scheme of arrangement, NCLT filing, record date, share-entitlement ratio, or appointed-date language anywhere in the material. The strategic direction management actually articulates is the opposite of separation: consolidation and bolt-on acquisition. They bought BroadPath (closed January 2025, bringing roughly 30 mostly mid-market payer clients and onshore, open-enrolment-heavy delivery) and CareSeed (closed 11 June 2026, Kansas City, founded 2012, CY2025 revenue 5.1 million dollars, 95 percent recurring, 31.4 percent EBITDA margin, 30 clients of which 26 new, 14 staff, platforms Forecast and Harvest), and Ramesh Gopalan says BroadPath is now fully integrated to the point that revenue cannot be split out, with Srinivas Mattapalli giving only an approximate 13.5 to 13.6 million dollars for BroadPath clients in Q1 FY27. The two reporting segments an investor might expect to be split, Payer (89.6 percent of Q1 FY27 revenue) and Provider (10.4 percent), are both explicitly described as businesses the company intends to keep and grow, including doubling down on provider-side RCM with an agentic AI layer. Capital allocation is framed as full debt repayment during FY27 (net debt 1,110 million rupees, 0.06x adjusted EBITDA), cash of 9,674 million rupees retained for M&A and AI investment, and a small final dividend of 0.10 rupees per share, with no mention of unlocking value through a separation. The only separation-like event referenced anywhere is historical and appears solely in a press-release footnote: the earlier carve-out of the healthcare business from HGS, cited as the origin of intangible amortisation now adjusted out of Adjusted PAT. The only corporate action actually put to shareholders in the filings is the Sagility Limited Employee Stock Options and Performance Stock Units Scheme 2026 (up to 3,09,10,845 options and 12,36,43,222 PSUs, exercisable into up to 15,45,54,067 shares, run through the Sagility ESOP Trust with an interest-free loan capped at 5 percent of paid-up capital and free reserves).
verdict.evolution: The idea does not surface at all. At the Investor & Analyst Day on 25 March 2026 the plan presented is capability expansion (managed services, Synchrony, MLR-reduction, clinical) plus capability-led M&A, and Ramesh Gopalan rules out even moving outside healthcare. On the 12 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the forward agenda is FY27 debt extinguishment, retained cash for acquisitions in both payer and provider, and a possible dividend review. By the 21 July 2026 Q1 FY27 call the company has added CareSeed and is scouting further clinical, provider and healthcare-technology targets, so the trajectory over the three calls is consolidation, not separation.

points.point: Asked about adjacencies outside healthcare, Ramesh Gopalan rules out leaving the sector and frames any widening as staying inside healthcare, with no reference to carving anything out.
points.quote: No, at this point, we want to continue to remain a healthcare firm.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these texts describes Shilpa Medicare separating a business: there is no demerger, spin-off, slump sale of a division or separate listing of a vertical anywhere in the eight transcripts (Jul 2024 to May 2026) or the three filings, and no analyst, lender or partner on any call asks for one. The corporate actions on record run the other way, toward consolidation into the listed parent: the NCLT Bengaluru order of 27 Feb 2026 (certified copy received 16 Mar 2026) sanctions the amalgamation of Shilpa Therapeutics Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary with revenue of only Rs 2.31 cr (FY23) and Rs 3.07 cr (FY24), into Shilpa Medicare, with no shares issued since the transferor is a WOS, its shares cancelled, authorised capital clubbed, staff absorbed under Clause 7.1 and the appointed date pushed from 01.04.2023 to 01.04.2025 at the Regional Director's insistence; the Regional Director flagged that the loss-making transferor merging into a profit-making transferee means there may be a negative outflow of income tax, and the same tax logic was stated explicitly for the earlier inward merger of INM Technologies (NCLT approval 18 Jun 2025), where Alpesh Dalal said unabsorbed INM losses would lower FY25 tax outflow, taking the Q1 FY26 effective tax rate down to 5.5%. The only genuine separations disclosed are two small exits, neither explained strategically: Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc. ceased to be a wholly owned subsidiary on 14 Jan 2026 when 2,84,21,020 shares were allotted to an individual, Steve N. Slilaty of Quebec, for CAD 2,000 total, a non-material subsidiary contributing Rs 34.33 lakh of income (0.03%) and Rs 46.09 lakh of net worth (0.02%) in FY25, already provided for, so no impact on financials; and in Q4 FY26 the sale of a 31% stake in JV Sravathi Advance, retaining 34%, booking an exceptional gain of INR 30 crores and reclassifying it from joint venture to associate. Management's stated strategic direction is the opposite of separation: Shilpa is described as an integrated one-stop solution across API, formulations, biologics and CDMO, with API deliberately feeding captive formulations because, in Dalal's words, you get end-to-end margins there, which lifted FY26 group gross margin to 70% and EBITDA margin to 29%. The nearest thing to a requested carve-out is presentational, not legal: investors repeatedly pressed for CDMO, captive-API and biologics revenue to be reported separately (CDMO was INR 158 cr in FY25; about INR 110 cr of API CDMO in FY26), and management said it was considering showing CDMO separately, while already publishing an adjusted ROCE that excludes biologics, NBE and albumin investments (4% in FY23 to 17.4% in FY26). The schemes' own rationale clauses are not reproduced in the filings, so no managerial reasoning for any structural change is available in this corpus beyond the tax and capital-clubbing mechanics recorded by the regulators.
verdict.evolution: The idea that surfaces is consolidation, not separation: on the Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) call Alpesh Dalal disclosed NCLT Bangalore approval for amalgamating INM Technologies into Shilpa Medicare and said its unabsorbed losses would cut prior-year tax, cutting the quarter's ETR to 5.5%. The first actual separation appears only in the 15 Jan 2026 filing, when Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc. stopped being a wholly owned subsidiary for CAD 2,000, never mentioned on the Feb 2026 or May 2026 calls. The second scheme was sanctioned on 27 Feb 2026 (intimated 5 and 17 Mar 2026), merging Shilpa Therapeutics Private Limited inward with the appointed date moved to 01.04.2025. Only on the May 2026 (Q4 FY26) call did a divestment get narrated, as the 31% Sravathi Advance stake sale yielding an INR 30 crore exceptional gain and reclassification to associate, prompted by an analyst question rather than by management strategy.

points.point: The 27 Feb 2026 NCLT order amalgamates a wholly owned subsidiary, Shilpa Therapeutics Private Limited, into the listed parent with no consideration and no dilution, the transferor's shares simply cancelled.

verdict.what_management_expects: No separation benefits were stated, because no business separation was announced. For the inward mergers management cited only tax relief from unabsorbed subsidiary losses (Q1 FY26 ETR 5.5%), clubbed authorised capital, absorbed employees and no dilution. verdict.rationale: The premise cannot be supported: nothing in these ten transcripts or the single filing announces, proposes, or explains a separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or hive-off of any Solar Industries business. The only time separation is raised at all is an analyst question in the Q3 FY25 call (Feb 6, 2025), where Rakesh Roy of Boring AMC asks whether the defence business could be spun off in 2-3 years; Aanchal Kewlani answers that defence sits in the group alongside the explosives business and 'that will continue' — a refusal, with no rationale, structure, record date or ratio offered. Management's repeated stance across the whole period is the opposite of separation: 'we treat business as one unit' (May 21, 2025), 'we run business as a whole' (May 15, 2026), 'Like we always say that for us, our business is one' when refusing to split FY27 capex of INR2,050 crores between defence and non-defence, and refusals to disclose segment-level EBITDA margins ('we as a business as a whole, we are achieving around 27% EBITDA margin'). The group is in fact consolidating and integrating rather than separating: defence is run through subsidiary Solar Defence (noted in May 2026 as 'a subsidiary of Solar Industries'), with capex of INR2,700 crores over two years, a INR12,700 crore 10-year MoU with the Government of Maharashtra, nine-plus overseas manufacturing subsidiaries, the Problast (South Africa) acquisition, and a stated intent to move up the value chain into complete 155 mm rounds rather than only supply energetics ('our intention is to make a complete round of 155'). The closest thing to separation language is descriptive, not structural: on May 15, 2026 Manish Nuwal said 'the defense vertical is steadily maturing into a powerful stand-alone platform' — immediately after reporting defence revenue of INR2,634 crores for FY26 (up 94%, 27% of the INR9,838 crore group) and an INR18,000 crore defence order book inside a INR21,300 crore total, i.e. scale and focus, not a legal split. The lone filing (April 24, 2026) is not a scheme at all: it is newspaper clippings of an IEPF unclaimed-share transfer notice; the scheme-of-arrangement text on those same newspaper pages belongs to unrelated companies (Swan Defence and Heavy Industries / Triumph Offshore, plus Tata Chemicals' IEPF notice and BGR Energy's insolvency notice) and must not be read as Solar's. No investor, lender or partner in these texts asks for a separation, and no problem is said to be solved by one.
verdict.evolution: Feb 6, 2025: the only separation question in three years is asked by an analyst and declined — defence 'will continue' inside the group. May 21, 2025 through Feb 4, 2026: management repeatedly reaffirms one-business management (single EBITDA guidance ~27%, undivided capex, no segment margins), while defence is scaled up inside subsidiary Solar Defence under the INR12,700 crore Maharashtra MoU. May 15, 2026: defence is called 'a powerful stand-alone platform' and FY27 capex of INR2,050 crores is again explicitly refused a defence/non-defence split ('for us, our business is one'), so the only trajectory visible is integration, not separation. The April 24, 2026 filing adds nothing: it is an IEPF share-transfer newspaper notice, with the only demerger/amalgamation text on the page belonging to other issuers.

points.point: The sole spin-off question in the entire record: an analyst asks whether the defence business could be separated within 2-3 years. Management declines, saying defence stays in the group alongside the explosives business.
points.quote: Is it possible from solar energy, is it possible to spin off our defence business in the next 2 to 3 years?

points.point: Aanchal Kewlani's answer — defence is held within the group (with the economic-explosives business) and will remain there. No rationale, structure or timeline for any separation is given.
points.quote: Currently, we have defence in our group as we hold for economic exclusives, we have the main defence business. So, that will continue.

points.point: Asked to split net profit margin between coal/explosives and defence, Nuwal refuses on the grounds that the company is managed as a single unit and guides only at group level — the opposite of carving a business out.
points.quote: So we treat business as one unit.

points.point: Asked specifically for defence EBITDA margin, management refuses segment-level disclosure and restates a single consolidated ~27% margin, so no standalone defence economics exist in the record on which a separation case could rest.
points.quote: You can ask such things, but we will answer only one thing, that we as a business as a whole, we are achieving around 27% EBITDA margin, and we should be able to continue with the similar margins.

points.point: The only 'stand-alone' language in the record is descriptive of defence's maturing scale (FY26 defence revenue INR2,634 crores, up 94%; targeting INR4,500 crores in FY27), not of any legal or structural separation.
points.quote: Additionally, the defense vertical is steadily maturing into a powerful stand-alone platform, driving deep tech innovations, enabling significant future growth potential.

points.point: Asked to split FY27 capex of INR2,050 crores between defence and non-defence explosives, Nuwal again refuses on single-business grounds and says capex is allocated centrally by priority and opportunity.
points.quote: Like we always say that for us, our business is one.

points.point: Defence and the international operations are run as subsidiaries (Solar Defence) and consolidated up, and were explained as the drag on, then driver of, subsidiary profits — presented as integration inside the group, not a prelude to separation.
points.quote: So sir, in the first half of this year, since the defense business because defense -- our Solar Defense is a subsidiary of Solar Industries and our international business are also subsidiaries.

points.point: No scheme exists in the record. The only filing supplied is an IEPF unclaimed-share transfer newspaper notice dated April 24, 2026; the scheme-of-arrangement and amalgamation text on the same newspaper pages belongs to unrelated issuers (Swan Defence and Heavy Industries / Triumph Offshore) and must not be attributed to Solar.

verdict.rationale: Management presented the separation not as a fix for a broken business but as the vehicle for closing its biggest admitted portfolio gap and executing its 'Look East' growth engine. On the 23 July 2026 call Vivek Vikram Singh said Sona had built 'one of India's broadest portfolio of electric powertrain products' but 'did not participate at all in high voltage electric as well as hybrid powertrain systems for passenger and commercial vehicles' — a market S&P Global Mobility puts at over 2.3 million Indian hybrid/EV cars and commercial vehicles, about Rs 24,000 crore in 2030 and 'maybe 3 times that' by 2035 — and that DENSO (world's second largest mobility technology company, with electrification revenue above $8 billion a year, and 100:1 better known than Sona) fills it. The mechanics: Sona carved its existing 2W/3W EV business (air-cooled traction motors and generators, traction inverters, eAxles) out of the listed company by slump sale on a going-concern basis into wholly owned Sona Comstar eDrive for INR 8,932 million (INR 8,575 million cash plus roughly INR 357 million in eDrive shares; Deloitte India Valuation LLP range INR 8,694–9,180 million), then sold DENSO 49% of eDrive at an enterprise value of INR 17,500 million while keeping 51%, majority directors and a 7-year transfer lock; separately a new JV2 for liquid-cooled high-voltage 4W+ motors, generators and inverters (excluding eAxles and gears) is 51% DENSO / 49% Sona out of a INR 535 million subscription, Sona putting in INR 262.15 million, with DENSO contributing the technology, IP and management. The stated problems solved: zero participation in high-voltage and hybrid 4W+ systems; a 2/3W business stuck at about 25% India share that Vivek wants above 50% and which is the group's lowest-margin line (FY26 revenue INR 3,855 million, EBITDA INR 405 million, roughly 10.5%, repeatedly cited as dragging consolidated margin); a customer base 'that is in a way not that open to us right now'; and exports 'to other markets where Denso is far more dominant'. Royalties are reciprocal — each partner is paid by its own majority-owned JV — which Vivek called the 'ultimate validation' of Sona's technology and possibly the first royalty income by an Indian auto company from a global mobility technology company. The filings add the corporate-speak version: technology collaboration, long-term product development capability, enhanced market access, 'operational focus' for the EV Business and to 'unlock significant value'. Nothing in the calls or filings attributes the move to any investor, lender or customer demand — Vivek framed DENSO as having chosen Sona ('why Sona Comstar?'), analyst Sonal Gupta instead challenged 'the motivation for putting that in the JV', and Sona's suspension motor and all other non-traction motor businesses were explicitly kept outside the transaction.
verdict.evolution: On the May 2025 and Aug 2025 calls the 4W/high-voltage piece was purely an in-house project ('we are developing high voltage traction motors') and the eastward route ran through a China driveline JV with JNT, which was then 'put in abeyance' on the Oct 2025 call for geopolitical reasons and 'the need to prioritize other active capital allocation decisions'. The Jan 2026 call carried the first real foreshadowing: the 'big boy piece, which is the four-wheeler bit' was being worked on, 'closer than one expected', with a 'meaningful update' promised in 6-7 months and an explicit fallback that 'if we are not able to do it ourselves, we'll... collaborate, partner, do something'; as late as the May 2026 call M&A was still 'nothing that has reached a stage which is worth sharing or reportable'. Definitive agreements were signed 22 July 2026 and unveiled on the 23 July 2026 call, where Vivek revealed the strategy had been worked on 'more than 2 years ago' but deliberately not discussed until there was something tangible. A postal ballot notice dated 31 August 2026 (voting 4 September – 3 October 2026) then put the slump sale, the eDrive share issue and a 29-year Chennai land sublease to shareholders as a material related-party transaction of about INR 8,934.05 million, with closing targeted on or before 31 March 2027.

points.point: Management named the gap the JVs are meant to close: no participation at all in high-voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for passenger and commercial vehicles.
points.quote: We did not participate at all in high voltage electric as well as hybrid powertrain systems for passenger and commercial vehicles.

points.point: The high-voltage prize was sized from S&P Global Mobility data, and Vivek later said the 2035 number could be roughly three times the 2030 figure.
points.quote: If we go by S&P Global mobility, Indian hybrid and EV cars and the commercial vehicle market alone represents an addressable market of over 2.3 million vehicles, which would roughly amount to about a 24,000 crore opportunity in 2030 itself.

points.point: In the 4W+ high-voltage JV Sona is the minority partner and DENSO brings technology, IP and management control.
points.quote: In this JV, Denso will hold the majority stake, contribute the relevant technology and intellectual property, and lead the business from a management perspective.

points.point: In the 2W/3W JV — the business being carved out of the listed company — Sona keeps majority ownership and control and licenses in its own technology.
points.quote: Here we will retain majority ownership and management control while licensing our own technology into the joint venture.

points.point: The stated commercial aim for the carved-out 2/3W entity is more customers and a shift from leadership to dominance; Vivek said 25% India share 'is also not enough. Why not more than 50%?'
points.quote: Today, we have a leadership position in 2 and 3 wheelers in India, and through this partnership, we should hopefully add more customers to the 2 and 3-wheeler JV and extend our leadership position to one of dominance.

points.point: Answering Sonal Gupta's challenge on why a business already doing well should go into a JV, Vivek cited a customer base 'not that open to us right now' plus exports.
points.quote: Third, the export opportunity opens up for us to other markets where Denso is far more dominant.

points.point: Royalties run both ways, each JV paying the partner whose technology it licenses; Vivek called this the validation that Sona's technology has value.
points.quote: JV2 will pay royalties to Denso for its high voltage technologies, while JV1 will pay royalties to Sona Comstar for our 2 and 3 wheeler technologies.

points.point: The business being separated is the group's lowest-margin product line, which management repeatedly blamed for consolidated margin dilution in the same quarter.
points.quote: There was also a product mix impact as traction motor sales grew quite rapidly, and as is well known to you, that product category has the lowest margins relative to our average company margin, so that also dragged it down a little bit.

points.point: Scope was explicitly fenced: only traction motors/controllers for 2W and 3W move; suspension motors and other non-traction motor businesses stay in the listed company.
points.quote: Let me also clarify because we got some calls that our suspension motor business, together with all our other non-traction motor businesses remain completely outside the scope of this transaction.

points.point: Management argued motor and controller businesses are capital-light, with Sat Mohan Gupta putting high-voltage revenue at 11-12 rupees per rupee of capex versus 8-9 in two-wheelers.
points.quote: Sure, capex intensity of motor business and control system businesses is actually low.

points.point: Six months before the announcement, the four-wheeler traction motor move was flagged as live and nearer than expected, with an update promised in 6-7 months.
points.quote: And obviously, the big boy piece, which is the four-wheeler bit, is something that we are working on, and hopefully, we can share something in the times to come.

points.point: The same call pre-committed to a partnership route if Sona could not crack the four-wheeler segment alone.
points.quote: If we are not able to do it ourselves, we'll, of course, figure out a way to collaborate, partner, do something, but it is a segment that we will come to in the end,

points.point: The earlier eastward partnership vehicle — the JNT China driveline JV — was shelved, with capital allocation priorities cited, clearing the way for the DENSO structure.
points.quote: I'd like to add that after careful consideration, we have decided to put a proposed joint venture with JNT in China in abeyance. This decision is based mostly on geopolitical factors and the need to prioritize other active capital allocation decisions.

points.point: Three months before signing, with roughly Rs 1,270 crore of cash on the balance sheet, management still disclosed nothing on the transaction when asked about the M&A pipeline.
points.quote: Nothing that has reached a stage which is worth sharing or reportable.

points.point: The carve-out is a slump sale on a going-concern basis with no values assigned to individual assets and liabilities, for INR 8,932 million (INR 8,575 million cash plus eDrive shares for the balance).
points.quote: The transfer shall be undertaken on a slump sale basis as a going concern, without assigning individual values to the assets and liabilities comprising the Electric Vehicle Business.

points.point: Price was set at the midpoint of an independent Deloitte India Valuation LLP range using DCF and comparable company multiples.
points.quote: Based on a combination of the Discounted Free Cash Flow and Comparable Companies Multiple methodologies, the valuer arrived at a valuation range of INR 8,694 million to INR 9,180 million with a mid value of INR 8,932 million.

points.point: DENSO's 49% subscription was priced at an enterprise value of INR 17,500 million, roughly twice the INR 8,932 million fair value at which the business was moved into eDrive.
points.quote: DENSO will buy 49% equity stake in this subsidiary at an Enterprise Value of Rs.17,500 million.

points.point: The filings' own stated rationale for the separation: technology collaboration, product development capability, market access and operational focus, alongside unlocking value and supporting long-term growth.
points.quote: The Transaction is expected to facilitate technology collaboration, long term product development capabilities, enhanced market access and operational focus for the EV Business.

points.point: The carved-out unit's disclosed track record: turnover INR 1,609mn (FY24), 2,564mn (FY25), 3,855mn (FY26); EBITDA 43/260/405mn; net worth 2,055/3,362/3,471mn; the deal equals 20.07% of FY26 consolidated turnover of INR 44,494.60mn.
points.quote: Note: Based on carved out adjusted financials prepared for the transaction.

points.point: Because the EV business is under 20% of income and net worth, no Section 180(1)(a) special resolution or Regulation 37A compliance was needed — only an ordinary resolution for a material related-party transaction.
points.quote: Based on the audited financial statements for the financial year 2025-26, the EV Business neither contributed 20% or more of the Company's total income nor represents 20% or more of the Company's net worth and therefore does not constitute an "undertaking" nor substantially the whole of an undertaking for the purpose of Section 180(1)(a) of the Act.

points.point: eDrive stays consolidated, so group turnover is unchanged, but 49% of its equity and profit shift to non-controlling interest, reducing net worth and profit attributable to owners.
points.quote: In the consolidated Profit & Loss Account, 49% share in profit/ loss of Sona eDrive will be reflected as Profit/Loss Attributable to non-controlling interest (NCI) along with any other such NCI in the group and Profit Attributable to owners of the Company will be lower to the same extent.

points.point: Ancillary to the BTA, Sona subleases 5.13 of its 10.87 leasehold acres at Keelakaranai Village, Chengalpattu, Tamil Nadu to eDrive for 29 years at a premium capped at INR 1,913,531 and rent of INR 2,077 a year, at no mark-up.
points.quote: Both the Sublease Premium and Sublease Rent have been calculated on a proportionate basis without any mark-up in accordance with the commercial understanding as a part of the overall transaction structure contemplated under the BTA and SSA.

points.point: Approval was sought by postal ballot (voting 4 September to 3 October 2026) as a material RPT of about INR 8,934.05 million, with all related parties barred from voting.
points.quote: In compliance with Regulation 23(4) of the Listing Regulations, no related party of the Company shall vote to approve the aforesaid related party transaction

verdict.what_management_expects: eDrive (2/3W): more customers, leadership extended 'to one of dominance' beyond 25% share, DENSO-enabled exports, royalty income, Sona 51% control and continued consolidation, plus INR 8,575 million cash and eDrive shares to the parent. JV2 (high-voltage 4W+): DENSO technology, IP and management, a Rs 24,000 crore 2030 market, capital-light returns. Group: 49% becomes non-controlling interest.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe a separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any business of Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd., and no such transaction can be reconstructed from them without inventing it. Across the eight transcripts (Jan 2025 through Jul 2026) management discusses one integrated company running three reported segments - domestic solar EPC, international EPC, and O&M - plus newer BESS and wind balance-of-system work, and repeatedly frames them as mutually reinforcing rather than separable: O&M order additions come from the company's own EPC commissioning (18.3 GWp portfolio by Q1 FY27, up from 13.5 GW in FY26 and 8.7 GW in FY25), and the stated aim is a holistic solar-plus-wind-plus-battery offering for hybrid and FDRE tenders. The only entity-level separation in the filings is housekeeping, not a business separation: the single filing (6 March 2026) reports that Sterling and Wilson Kazakhstan LLP, a step-down subsidiary, was liquidated with effect from 2 March 2026, and states in the prescribed disclosure table that turnover, revenue, income and net worth contribution are Not Applicable because there was no business activity in the entity since inception, with no consideration, no buyer, no related-party element, and the scheme-of-arrangement row marked Not Applicable. The nearest thing to a separation rationale in the calls is a ring-fencing and clean-up of legacy overseas liabilities inside the existing structure rather than any carve-out: in Q2 FY26 (Oct 2025 call) the company wrote off INR 580 crores on the Conti LLC arbitration in its US subsidiary SWSS (claims of USD 55.06 million dismissed, USD 6.44 million awarded against it), settled with OEG Inc. for USD 2.25 million (INR 19.95 crores) against a USD 7 million claim, absorbed a USD 7.19 million (INR 63.47 crores) SBLC invocation, and in standalone accounts wrote off INR 600 crores of loans to the wholly-owned subsidiary plus an INR 2,038 crores impairment on the stalled Nigeria project, aggregating INR 2,638 crores of exceptional items that management said would align standalone and consolidated net worth and neutralise the roughly INR 1,700 crores of corporate guarantees. Management framed that as cleaning up the balance sheet so it could focus on operational performance, and said losses come from subsidiaries with no projects - US, Australia, Dubai - that carry only legal costs and overheads of around INR 40 crores a year for another 1.5 to 2 years; FY26 then carried a further INR 611 crores of exceptional litigation items and a reported annual loss of INR 296 crores, with roughly INR 800 crores indemnified by the erstwhile promoters, SP Group and Mr. Khurshed Daruvala, who had paid about INR 180 crores. Nobody on these calls - not investors, lenders, nor the strategic investor Reliance - asks for a separation; investor pressure is instead about revenue guidance misses, lumpy exceptional losses, credit limits and the rating, and the quantum of pending claims. If the premise of a separation rests on a document outside this set (for example a board-approved scheme), it is not in these texts and I will not reconstruct a rationale for it.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaces: no call from Jan 2025 to Jul 2026 mentions a demerger, spin-off, hive-off, subsidiary sale or scheme of arrangement, and no analyst asks about one. What does evolve is legacy clean-up and structural tidying inside the group - Oct 2025 books the Conti, OEG and SBLC hits plus the INR 2,638 crores standalone write-off and Nigeria impairment to align standalone and consolidated net worth; Jan 2026 confirms the Conti matter closed with a further INR 30 crores of legal fees and that it sat outside the promoter indemnity because it post-dated Reliance's entry; Apr 2026 reports FY26 exceptional items of INR 611 crores, an out-of-court settlement with no upside or downside, and O&M reaching an inflection point as a segment; Jul 2026 adds the only new corporate vehicle in the period, a 50-50 joint venture with Hassan Allam Construction for the USD 560 million West Minya project in Egypt. The one filing, dated 6 March 2026, records the liquidation of the dormant Kazakhstan step-down subsidiary - a shell with no activity since inception, explicitly not part of any scheme of arrangement.

points.point: The only corporate separation in the filings is the liquidation of a dormant step-down subsidiary in Kazakhstan, effective 2 March 2026, with no turnover, revenue, net worth, consideration or buyer, and the scheme-of-arrangement disclosure row marked Not Applicable.
points.quote: Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we wish to inform you that Sterling and Wilson Kazakhstan LLP, step down subsidiary of the Company incorporated in Kazakhstan has been liquidated with effect from March 02, 2026 The said Company did not have any business activity.

points.point: The filing's prescribed table confirms the liquidated entity contributed nothing financially, so this is shell clean-up rather than the separation of any operating business.
points.quote: Not Applicable as there was no business activity in the entity since inception.

points.point: The closest stated rationale to a separation is clean-up of legacy US subsidiary (SWSS) exposures within the existing structure - INR 580 crores Conti write-off and INR 19.95 crores OEG settlement - to let management focus on operations, not a carve-out.
points.quote: While these are largely legacy project -related issues in our U.S. subsidiary, the ir resolutions, while financially painful in the short term represents a significant step towards cleaning up the balance sheet and enabling management to focus squarely on operational performance and profitable growth going forward.

points.point: Standalone accounts took an INR 2,038 crores impairment on the Nigeria project plus INR 600 crores of loan write-offs to the wholly-owned subsidiary (INR 2,638 crores exceptional) expressly to align standalone and consolidated net worth and defuse the roughly INR 1,700 crores of corporate guarantees - a ring-fencing move, not a separation.
points.quote: Further, considering the inordinate delays with respect to the Nigeria project, we have made an impairment provision of INR2,038 crores from the wholly -owned subsidiary during the quarter in our standalone financials.

points.point: Management identifies the loss-making units as subsidiaries with no projects left - US, Australia and Dubai - carrying only legal costs and overheads of about INR 40 crores a year for another 1.5 to 2 years; it never proposes separating or divesting them.
points.quote: The losses are from those subsidiaries, where there is no projects, there are certain overheads like U.S., Australia, Dubai.

points.point: The Conti liability fell outside the erstwhile promoters' indemnity because it was a subcontractor case not covered in the due diligence done when Reliance came in as strategic investor - the only place investor-entry structuring is discussed.
points.quote: Conti being a case with subcontractor that was not considered during due diligence and negotiation with Reliance when they joined as an investor.

points.point: O&M is described as a segment reaching an inflection point within the group (13.5 GW from 8.7 GW), fed by the company's own EPC commissioning - management treats EPC and O&M as integrated, with no suggestion of separating them.
points.quote: Fourth, the operation s and maintenance segment, which has till now been relatively a small contributor to top line and profits is beginning to reach an inflection point.

points.point: The only new legal vehicle created in the period is a 50-50 joint venture with Hassan Allam Construction for the 1,000 MWac plus 600 MWh Egypt project worth about USD 560 million - a partnership for one mandate, not a separation of an existing business.
points.quote: In June, this financial year, we received a letter of award for our 50 -50 joint venture with Hassan Allam Construction, one of the leading construction company in Egypt and the wider MENA regions for the West Minya Solar Power Project in the Minya Governorate of Egypt.

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is stated, because no separation is proposed. For the legacy clean-up that is discussed, management expects aligned standalone and consolidated net worth, negligible corporate-guarantee risk, legal costs falling to nil in about two years, roughly INR 800 crores recoverable under promoter indemnity, and attention redirected to EPC gross margins of 8-10 percent and O&M at about 20 percent.
verdict.gaps: Everything: the calls and the single filing never mention a demerger, spin-off, hive-off or scheme, its perimeter, rationale, ratio, timeline, approvals, or any party requesting it.

The only profit line available in the segment notes is 'Segment Results' (a gross-margin-style segment result before unallocated finance costs, depreciation, employee benefits/other expenses and unallocated income — i.e. not EBITDA, EBIT, PBT or PAT), and segment revenue is 'external customers' only, with no inter-segment revenue disclosed.
